Also I learned that “The Twitch Streamer” actually got his start as an influencer on motorcycle TikTok which is pretty cool! “The Philosopher” brought a bunch of Dominoes to bar night which I wish I left a Yelp review for but didn’t :(. I also learned there are different kinds of epi pens some of which are much easier to use than others. Ones in Canada are easier to use you take it out, twist, and inject. The last thing you want with an epi pen is trying to figure out how to use it when you need it. I’ll admit I’ve never been particularly opinionated on epi pens until now :D. Friday I went to Barry’s in the morning. It wasn’t as good as Monday but it still hit. Today after work I went with “The Fisherman” and “Top of the Rope”  to help get signatures on a petition to save public transit in the Bay Area. I don’t normally post politics here but it shouldn’t be surprising to y’all that I am an unabashed public transit stan and very much don’t want public transit to fall by the wayside. We learned some of the basics of how to get signatures on petitions. Some of the stuff is obvious like anyone who signs must be a registered voter, and some things that were less obvious like the fact that there are different sheets for people registered to vote in different counties (SF, San Mateo, Contra Costa, Alameda, Santa Clara) and you can’t have two people from different counties sign on the same sheet or it will invalidate the whole petition :O. We got some sheets so expect me to come ask to you sign (if you meet the criteria expect that I will be badgering you in the near future >:)). While there we had a brief flyby with a Saturday trasher who I don’t have a nickname for. Hmm, lets call him Mr. Roblox Runner or Mr. Double R because I’m sick while writing this and my creativity isn’t at it’s highest right now. After that we all went to a startup party to celebrate the acquisition of a startup two of my old Snorkel coworkers work at. It got acquired by Google and I’m super excited for them! They’re both super awesome people and this is incredibly well deserved. The party itself doubled as a way for me to catch up with a bunch of my old coworkers. Afterwards I had a 1:1 with “The Boxer”. At this point I think I’m almost done with my 1:1s, if I haven’t verbally reached out to schedule something (even if the invite hasn’t come yet) please let me know! Anyways, we went to 4505 Burgers and BBQ and talked a lot about work, hobbies, and other stuff. He asked me what some of my main goals for the year were. You know its funny we’re only 2 months in and I feel like they’ve shifted a lot. The first impression stuff wasn’t something I was thinking about at the beginning of the year neither was the gym bro stuff and yet here we are. As a bit of a tangent it’s funny because both of these were things I started as a way to help me with dating but they’ve both evolved beyond that in ways that I’ve found pretty meaningful. Some of the first impression stuff like being more empathetic has really helped when I’ve wanted to encourage people I’ve been talking with and make them feel better which is a genuine goal of mine but one I haven’t always been the best at expressing in words. One of the books “The Philosopher” gave me to read (“The Like Switch”) really helped me with that in ways that I find meaningful not because it will help me with dating but just because it will help me to become the more ideal version of myself. Similarly going to the gym is now even kinda fun. Way back last year when I went with “The Professor” and “The Quant” I was complaining a lot (some might say too much but I found it funny), and now I somewhat enjoy going to Barrys and I really enjoy how I feel afterwards. Don’t get me wrong I still have dating as a goal but it’s been interesting to see my interest in these steps evolve to being more than just a means to an end. It was really cool hearing about how much he was enjoying his work and his new place as well. He also expressed interest in going for the 7 can record which I want to setup for beginning of April so be on the lookout for that. Afterwards I went back to the party where I hung out for a surprising number of hours. While there I learned that the twin sister of someone I knew from college is engaged to the twin brother of an old coworker of mine. Also I met a woman who works at City Hall and was responsible for hiring “The Politician” to his current role which was cool. At one point the fire alarm went off due to the smoke machine there so I wound up going to a nearby Salt and Straw and chatting with some folks I met there for about an hour. I convinced some people to come to Marina Run Club (SFs 3rd best run club),  got a verbal commit from someone to close one volume of Mooni hoodie sales, and found out about a musical open mic where you can go up and sing songs on Mondays which I am very much looking forward to. I was told if you go early there is less pressure because there are less people but frankly going with more people sounds a lot more fun to me. I didn’t say it would be good for their eardrums mind you but that's a secondary concern here. Saturday The day begins with Marina Run Club with “Top of the Rope”. I was hoping to find Katie the girl I was interested in but sadly she doesn't show up today. On the other hand I did find a guy whose dad owns Bongo Burger! Bongo Burger was a small chain of burger restaurants that I went to all the time back at Berkeley. I can now add him to my esteemed list of people I know whose family owns a restaurant that I know of along with “La Tacqueria Royalty”. In the words of philosopher emeritus Dr. Doofenshmirtz “If I had a nickel for everyone I met whose family owns a restaurant I’ve been to I’d have two nickels. It’s not a lot but it’s weird that it happened twice right?” I managed to get some of the people from the startup party to come to run club which was also pretty fun! I also meet a guy who says he writes Yelp Reviews and his goal is to become Yelp Elite. I offer to nominate him since that is something I can do but he then says that he writes his reviews on a secret account and turns me down. In a bit of high risk fun I tell him about how I become Yelp Elite and he responds by saying that’s really smart but honestly seemed pretty unimpressed. I knew that bit is a gamble to tell people but it was worth a shot. I guess he wanted to connect to talk about AI though which is … something. Afterwards I went to trash pickup with “Not a matcha bitch,” and “The notetaker”. I learn there’s a form of art called paper cutting one of the people at Saturday trash pickup will have an art exhibition showing off her stuff in April. From there I went to a double Barry’s class to celebrate opening their 100th studio (on Wall Street of all places). This double workout proved to be pretty hard but rewarding! They had a DJ playing the whole time which felt very Marina. Also between this and the run club I’m reminded why Marina is the Trash Tales designated unofficial backwards hat capital of SF. Later in the day I went to a party hosted by “The Filmaker” where he made his DJ debut! It was really cool to see him do this and it was great! As always super proud when my friends do cool new things and the show really hit. He mainly focused on 70s and 80s songs and as an extra sweet note dedicated the performance to his mom who is a big fan of the genre! We also did some karaoke as well although at one point the neighbors complained and we had to make our way to Blondie’s. Well, everyone else did while I went home because home is just two blocks from me. Sunday The day begins with trash pickup with “The notetaker,” “The Philosopher,” and one of “The Philosopher”s college friends who isn’t apart of the usual group of Canadians but also happens to be one. Later in the day I took “The Twitch Streamer” and his girlfriend out to Kogi Gogi which was super fun! I learned that “The Twitch Streamer’s” girlfriend is also a bar tender and they both write motorcycles. Talk about birds of a feather huh? We shot the shit and generally goofed off. It had a very unique flavor compared to some of these other small group settings. Sort of like how like you can like all your children in very different ways this one had a uniquely comical energy. I told a joke that I know I can’t tell on the first meeting but I quite liked. I was told during this that its good to compliment small things which was why I talked about “The Twitch Streamer’s” dick :D. Yeah yeah minus however many Humza points I’ll gladly take the hit here.

title: Episode 63
excerpt: Tuesday Just another day at work. Wednesday Today after my stint in the mines I went to Midnight Runners with “Top of the Rope”. Originally I planned to take MR a little bit chill. To give you an idea of how that went I first get this text from her Now natura…
content: Tuesday Just another day at work. Wednesday Today after my stint in the mines I went to Midnight Runners with “Top of the Rope”. Originally I planned to take MR a little bit chill. To give you an idea of how that went I first get this text from her Now naturally of course I had an out here. I could have just said no and I could have had a nice chill time lollygagging around. We did not in fact lollygag around. My competitive side came out and I have to admit I actually enjoyed pushing myself like that. I had to put in some work but it was satisfying. And I finally got below 7 minutes on a mile Sadly I realize I also have more work to do on myself personally at MR. After the 4th mile I was admittedly pushing myself and this guy came up to me and said “You looked pretty out of breath during that last mile”. I was caught a bit off guard by that remark and tried to play it off with a “Oh I wasn’t that out of breath”. He then said “No you were pretty out of breath”. I was kinda stunned at this point and just looked him square in the eyes and said “I don’t really know what you want me to say here”. He then said “Just telling the truth” before awkwardly leaving. It’s been a while since someone could really annoy me like that. I was genuinely ticked in a way I hadn’t been before. So much so that my goal for the last mile was to sprint hard and beat his ass. Looking back I wish I hadn’t gotten annoyed though. One of my personal goals (outside of the whole dating feedback thing) is to try be annoyed as little as possible and this does give me an opportunity to try and improve that and get my personal annoyance at minor things closer to 0. It may never be exactly 0 but I can always try to get it a little bit closer. Thursday After work I went to bar night with “The Mosher” and “That’s nuts”. I learned that the usual bar tender here just got into twitch streaming which is super cool! I really want to check out one of his twitch streams sometime. I think it would be fun! While there I learned more about beer and skiing. On the beer side I learned there is something called dark beer which is called so usually for its color but sometimes for its flavor note. It is malted in water and often pairs well with coffee and chocolate. I also learned that sours can change perspective on taste and if you are drinking multiple beers you may need a palate cleanser lest you want everything to taste like sours. On the skiing side I learned that there is a certain curvature of skiing called bowl shaped skiing where you can ski generally without trees on a wide bowl shaped slope. My understanding here is that this kind of skiing is generally preferable because it's easier and more fun. At the same time we were also watching the Attack on Titan finale (the actual one not finale part 1 part 3 or something). In a rare break from what usually plays on the TV at bar night I actually knew what was happening and served as the main catcher upper of folks for “That’s Nuts” who had seen a lot of Attack on Titan a while back but not what just came before and “The Mosher” who hadn’t seen Attack on Titan at all until now. Friday After work I have another 1:1 with “The Big Youtube short” and his girlfriend “function(get_rid_of_cancer)” at Noe Valley Indian Cusine. I’m not generally a big fan of Indian food but this place was really good! The eggplant pakoras were great as was the garlic and pesto naan. But what was even better of course was the conversation. I really liked learning more about “The Big Youtube short’s” job and how passionate he is about it. He is really into the problem of recommender systems because right now Youtube shorts is not very good at recommending videos. I told him I don’t watch a lot of Youtube shorts because I’m skeptical it's not just a center for brainrot and he told me it's precisely because of the recommender problem. I’m not able to be recommended shorts that I may actually like and enjoy hence I just got the lowest common denominator slop. If the recommender system was better tuned I could get educational things that could broaden my horizon and let me explore more beyond the niches I typically explore. For the first time I had some genuine faith in youtube shorts. And beyond just that I love seeing people passionate about things whether it's work or hobbies. And it was also great catching up with his girlfriend too. She works with patient data and joked that I have some of the best deidentifying of personal data she has seen. This is actually extra funny because at the health care startup I was at I worked on deidentifying patient data for a while which was certainly … interesting in retrospect. “The Pyramid Schemer”, if you are reading this part you should tell the office about this. Some of them might find that funny. I learned she also did bee keeping research for a while wherein she learned that some of the main causes of queen bees dying are pesticides and parasites. The two Ps of the aPocalypse if you will. She also wrote some code for a project to help someone become completely cancer free, hence her nickname I just came up with today for her “function(get_rid_of_cancer)”. Saturday Originally I wanted to go to Marina run club to put my new joggers to use helping me look better but my legs weren’t really feeling it so I skipped. One problem with Marina run club is its awkwardly right before I need to go to trash pickup meaning its hard to talk with people, and at the same time I’m not convinced the conversations go on long enough that its actually worth skipping trash pickup for. Maybe I could skip and just come for the post trash hang? Who knows. Anyway, I went to trash pickup with “The Notetaker” and a bunch of others. It was a fun time as usual. From there I go and get brunch with “The Kpop dancer,” “The Sparkle,” “The Pickleballer," and “The Taco” over at Peacock Pansy. A brunch place I took from looking at my Yelp Elite Mentor (aka “The Dentist’s” yelp reviews) and the place didn’t disappoint. I quite liked the ube french toast there and thought it was delightful. “The Kpop dancer” is getting married in May so it was fun hearing about her getting ready for that. I’m gonna be going to her wedding in L.A which I’m very excited for. Apparently there is a restaurant there called Great Outdoor Restaurant, I really want to go there and sit inside for the irony of it all. The food there is supposed to be good from what “The Pickleballer” told me but that’s not really what I’m here for. It turns out “The Sparkle” started a new job at Zoox but hadn’t rode in one yet so I took her on her first Zoox ride so she can see the fruits of her labor in action. Later in the day I met up with “The Fisherman” and “The Shadow Brigade” and we all went to Detour. We mainly just hung around and talked for a while with the occasional break to play some arcade games. Sunday Today was a trash pickup marked by unexpected faces. I saw “The Trash Queen” and “The Rugby Player” for the first time in a minute there. They came with “The Trash Queen’s” dad and one of her other volunteer friends. It was great to catch up with them. I learned that at “The Rugby Player’s” old job at an autonomous tractor company he went to blueberry and potato conferences to try and sell the tractor he and his company were developing. He said the job really exposed him to all sorts of different people which was cool. I also met a friend of a friend who I last saw back in 2023 during the really old days of trash pickup. Longer term readers who read episode 36 may remember me mentioning that I got a text from someone I hadn’t seen in years who I met up with. This person is a friend of the aforementioned person I met up with. After trash pickup I caught up with one of my longest friends who I’ve known since the 3rd grade. We hung out for a while and watched him get a burrito and chilled in Dolores park. It was cool catching each other up on our lives and seeing some of the different things we are up to. He’s a neuro science  Ph.D student at USC who is going to be doing a post doc at some institute in L.A soon which is quite exciting. Even as a kid he was always more the academic type than me. Being a professor is something I can totally see for him. I remember way back in 2022 I suggested he use ChatGPT and now he is a Codex power user :D. Whenever we meet he always likes to ask me about my thoughts on AI which I am quite happy to give. Later in the day I walk around Duboce park and I see some girls offering lemonade if I tell them an interesting story. I tell them about the time I surprised “The Professor” in Vienna which they were sufficiently impressed by to warrant a lemonade. I turn the question back on them and ask them interesting stories about themselves. One of the girls mentions a time she went mountain biking and went down hard on a slippery mountain and managed to come out of it with minimal injuries. The other girl can’t really come up with a story unfortunately. I also ask them about the most interesting story they heard that day and they mention someone wound up in airport prison after losing their passport which sounds incredibly scary. Finally I have a 1:1 with “The Filmmaker”. He regales me with his trip to Mardi Gras. As a seasoned Mardi Gras attender he knows now which streets have all the action and which ones to go to for the off the beaten path jazz clubs. He even ran into someone he met last year there which sounds like a really fun time.

title: Episode 62- Congrats to my CFAs!!
excerpt: Congrats to my CFAs!! Shoutouts It’s rare that I make the shoutouts the title of this newsletter but today is a rare week! Congrats to “The FIsherman” for signing her new job offer! I’m super excited that she is gonna be making more $$ and working on a team t…
content: Congrats to my CFAs!! Shoutouts It’s rare that I make the shoutouts the title of this newsletter but today is a rare week! Congrats to “The FIsherman” for signing her new job offer! I’m super excited that she is gonna be making more $$ and working on a team that she is super excited about. Anyone who has talked with her knows how passionate she is about housing so I’m super excited she gets to work on something that excites her so! Also congrats to “The Quant” for getting a raise after his perf review!! I know he really deserves a raise as well and am super happy he is getting one! Both my CFA friends are kicking major ass this week and I’m here for it! Announcement I’m continuing my series of doing 1:1s where I treat people to dinner who I couldn’t get to come to the KBBQ event I held a while back. Unfortunately I’m a bit bandwidth bound in scheduling so I haven’t reached out to everyone I wanted to. If you're interested in getting dinner courtesy of the first national bank of Humza and I haven’t reached out please hit me up! I promise if you’re reading this newsletter I wanna treat ya and have a 1:1! Monday Today after work I continued my 1:1 series and caught up with “The Juggler” at Brenda’s French Soul Food. He told me all about what it's like to do a bikepacking trip in the desert. I learned that if you have too much water to carry around while biking you can dig a hole in the ground near a plant and store it there and it will be waiting for you when you come back. That’s a life hack right there. He also told me that if you go to small towns in Nevada everyone knows everyone in really interesting ways. Apparently at the general store there the cashier and someone buying something were both complaining about some woman named Jenny who will leave her kid at their doorsteps at night (I think to go gambling). Also this small town used to have a bunch of donkeys in it until they moved them out which according to “The Juggler” meant they took the one interesting this about this small town and completely got rid of it making it a completely unremarkable small town. I’m not generally a fan of sea food but the fried shrimp they had there was a banger! He asked me the typical question “What’s been the most unexpected thing you learned during these 1:1s?” Given how some of these have gone I don’t think I can post the actual answer publicly but I am somewhat kicking myself for not asking myself the question until now. He also told me some great new offensive jokes that I love. They’re definitely not jokes I can use for the pristine first impression but man they’re good! Tuesday Just a day at the office. Wednesday After work I went to MR today. Surprisingly there were no named characters there today but it was someone's birthday today which was cool! The run itself was fine, I took it pretty chill for the most part. After the run I met up with “Mr. Greenflag” for our 1:1 at The Port of Peri Peri. This is the same restaurant I went to with “La Tacqueria Royalty,” “The Climber,” and “Sergeant Sassy” 27 weeks ago. (The fact that I have these episode numbers means I can now give the exact number of weeks which is fun). It was great catching up with him and hearing about how his trip to China went and hearing more about his journey to learn Chinese which I love for him. I’m super glad I caught up with him when I did since he will be traveling a lot in the coming months which I am also very much excited for. Unlike the last time I went to this restaurant I actually ate something here and I must say their brisket burger is quite good! Sadly I couldn’t leave a Yelp review for it of course. I tried one of the spicy chicken wings that “Mr. Greenflag” got and I was promptly reminded that I am a poor Asian when it comes to spice tolerance. If you only knew my spice tolerance without any other knowledge about me you would probably confuse me with the average midwesterner. When I got home from work I went on this reddit rabbithole where I found this subreddit called r/suicidebywords which is just hilarious. I don’t usually do this but here are some screenshots of some memes I found there that legitimately made me laugh out loud. I don’t complain about my friends photography skills but I resonate with the second half of this Thursday In the morning I do Almost Friday Run Club for the first time in forever which was quite nice. While there I meet someone who works as a journalist and covered stuff about the state of prisons in SF. Sadly I don’t remember what she said for the life of me but I do remember it was quite interesting. Also I say that I met this person but apparently we met before. She remembered me because I brought Franklin to run club once but I totally forgot who she was, which is fun. After work I go to bar night with “The Quant,” “That’s nuts,” “The finer things,” and “The Best”. I talk with “That’s nuts” a lot about winter sports in the Olympics and I learned there is something called ski ballet. As the name implies its a type of ballet done on skis and according to her its a quite interesting and difficult sport. It also happens to be her favorite sport to watch, sadly its no longer in the Olympics which is unfortunate. I also learn about something called the Calgary Stampede which is a big county fair / music festival / pancake breakfast / day drinking event. I never knew Calgary had such character to it! Friday In the morning I do another Barry’s class. For fun I wanted to try logging the treadmill parts of the class on Strava. It didn’t go to plan but the results were pretty funny. Today after work I found myself with no real plans and thought that it might be a good time for a good solo adventure. Unsure of what I should do though I asked Claude for some suggestions and it came up with some bits I was curious to try Take a random bus all the way to the end and walk all the way home from there Go to a restaurant and point to someone randomly and say you will have what they are having Go to the worst restaurant you can find and enthusiastically try it Commit to going to a few different restaurants and only talking in an accent (Wow I didn’t realize until I wrote this now how many of the bits I mentioned were food related). I decided to frankenstein this into a combination of all 4 where I take the first bus that comes outside of work, ride it all the way to the end, find the worst restaurant I can near there, and order in an accent while I’m there, and get what the person across from me gets. I wound up taking the 22 bus to the Marina and I ended up at a 3.6 star fancyish restaurant.. It so happens the person sitting across from me got a burger which wasn’t terrible but certainly not worth the $34 I paid for it. All in all  I found the bit to be a lot less fun than I thought it would be. On my walk back home left with nothing to do I decided to stare into the abyss and think about life for a while. One of the first things I thought about was why I feel the need to do the bits I do. I think the answer to that is simply that if I don’t do them I risk feeling bored. Sometimes I find day to day life to be mundane and I like any extra way I can spice it up somehow. I remember reading something as a kid where someone was complaining to their grandfather that they were bored and the grandfather rebuked them saying it was their job to entertain myself and I suppose my bits are my own way of doing just that. Why run when you can run with an air purifier? Why simply put your name down at a restaurant when you can put a name thats so obviously fake everyone knows it is (like nobody is looking at me and thinking my name is Dairy or Wuhan but those are names I’ve put down at restaurants). Of course I wouldn’t say all those bits are gut bustingly hilarious or anything but any little bit I can do to make life that much more interesting feels worth it to me. From there my thoughts turned to the first impression stuff I’ve been doing. Thanks to my training I have a much better sense of what I should / shouldn’t mention to people when I’m trying to optimize for the perfect first impression. But I thought to myself “Why do I like to introduce myself to people the way that I do?” I think the answer to that comes down to not wanting to seem fake. I’ll take a brief tangent here and talk about something I don’t seldom mention and that is what annoys me in other people. Throughout the training we’ve certainly talked a lot about what *I* do that annoys others but the other way around has largely been untouched for the most part. I think in general I do get annoyed less than average but I will mention something that can do it and that is fakeness. I remember at a previous job I was at I worked with some salespeople who seemed so obviously fake and it really rubbed me the wrong way. I’ve occasionally met people like that outside of work and whether they were really fake or I just read the situation wrong it irked me in a way that other people seldom do. Like you could straight up insult me and I wouldn’t mind as much because I know you’re being genuine with me. And in turn when I meet other people I want them to see who I really am as much as possible. I like my personality and I don’t want to hide it. I don’t want people to think that I’m something I’m not and that they can trust me. Of course thanks to my training I’ve also learned that even if I intend to be genuine the way I say things off the bat can lead to people getting a different impression of me; I understand that and don’t want to belabor the point here as this is more meant to talk about why I act the way I do and less on whether it is optimal. As I got home I continued to stare further into the abyss and confront the fact that I really hate feeling bored / lonely and desperately try to keep myself busy to avoid confronting those feelings.  I don’t think it’s a stretch to say that I feel like I always need to be doing something and the fact that I didn’t have anything planned for a time when I really should (a Friday night) hit me hard. I lean on Claude a bit here as I actually find LLMs to be surprisingly good to talk to about this kind of stuff. I asked Claude to ask me some more “Stare into the Abyss” questions and I chatted with it a bit about my life. If anyone is interested, here is the chat. I mentioned this in one of my other newsletters but one of my other fears is what I would be without my humor, what would I really be. One of the themes which I think that chat gets into is that for me time that doesn’t feel “productive” in some way can feel like a moral failure if it goes on for too long. It doesn’t have to be productive in the work sense of course but anything fun or interesting qualifies. I tie myself a lot to whatever outputs I am interested in producing and if I don’t have any then I can feel pointless. Amongst my many areas of self improvement I’ve outlined I honestly think working on this would probably be one of the best for myself. I don’t want to stop doing interesting things as I genuinely like the things I do but I don’t want to feel as much of a *need* to do them or tie my own moral value to them. Thanks you all for staring into the abyss with me. If you exit out the hallway to your left you can pick up a complimentary “I stared into Humza’s abyss with him and all I got was this lousy hypothetical t-shirt” t-shirts. After staring into the abyss I crashed and went to bed. Saturday I went to Marina Run Club with “Top of the Rope”. The run itself was fine for the most part except at the very end when my shin splints acted up again and we stopped early but thankfully it was only about 0.1 miles before the run finished so we didn’t miss too much. I realized at this run that if I want to meet people I’m interested in romantically I need to get new running clothes (I don’t think my Snorkel sweatpants are fashionable). Amusingly since this run was on Valentines day they gave everyone a different colored wrist band to wear based on relationship status. Even more amusingly they ran out of singles colored wristbands so other single people had to get an “It’s complicated wristband”. I look out and see this one girl at the run club who I talked to once had an “It’s complicated” wristband. My goal for next week is to get new running clothes and work up the courage to talk with her some more. I talked with her once before and she was the one who indirectly inspired me to start going to Barry’s since she’s a gym rat. Next week I will definitely be chatting Katie up. After run club I go to trash pickup with “Top of the Rope,” “The Writer,” “The Notetaker,” “The Politician,” and “The North bay trasher”  amongst others. After trash pickup I have a 1:1 with “John Wick”. We go to Boogaloos and have a lovely brunch with some fun toothpicks in the matcha latte . We have a really nice heart to heart. I can’t really say much about it but I found it very warm and fuzzy. Later I meet up with “The Fisherman,” and one of her mutual friends to celebrate her new job! We go to Emperor Norton’s Boozeland over in the Tenderloin. For anyone who is a fan of SF hero Emperor Norton I highly recommend you go. For anyone unfamiliar I highly recommend you watch this video about him. Later me and “The Fisherman” go to Haru’s and hangout. She’s never been before so I’m glad I got to take her to the usual Thursday night stomping grounds. We catch up some more over duckfat fries and popcorn chicken :D. I go home and work on a new design for a hoodie. I lean more in the transit theme and decide to be more aggressively anti car in this one Shoutout to “The Writer” for the idea to make the car being beaten up a cyber truck. Sunday The day begins with trash pickup with “The Notetaker” and other unnamed folks. The turnout was a bit dampened by the rain but thankfully not too much. After trash pickup I meetup with “Mirandom thoughts,” “The Picklebaler,” and “The Taco”. I catch up with them over at Sofia and treat them as part of my goal. It was great catching up with them. Apparently “The Pickleballer” has been on a crochet grind and can now crochet her own beanie which is super cool. Also the bread at Sofia is apparently really good as it passes “The Pickleballer’s” high bread bar being her favorite bread in the city :D. Later I host a game night with “The Taco,” “The Pickleballer,” “The Pasta Prince,” “The Menace,” “The Writer,” and “The Beekeeper". We play some Coup and Avalon. More and more I’m liking Avalon over Secret Hitler since I can really lean into and customize the roles we play to give either the good or bad side an advantage depending on the situation. There are still a lot of roles I have yet to play with and I am very excited to keep expanding. Monday Well since I’m already late on the newsletter may as well get another day of content here. I start by going to A Runner’s Mind with “Top of the Rope” to get new running shoes. My old ones are pretty beaten up and may be contributing to some of the injuries I’ve been getting. This running store is elite. The people working there are super helpful in terms of recommending shoes based on how you run and what injuries you may have. As part of the shoe trying on process you try on shoes and jog around the store. I thought it would make for a funny Strava to log that and in the process I logged my worst mile pace of all time 😂 We also go to an athletic store in the Marina where I get some new joggers as well in preparation for Saturday. Hopefully with the new running shoes and joggers I should be ready to hit run club hard with no injuries and look reasonably well dressed enough to try my hand at talking to Katie again. Afterwards  we go to a cafe where “Top of the Rope” also teaches me how to knit! I think an indoor hobby would be cool and I’ve never learned before. It turns out if you're me learning to knit can be quite hard. I spend a lot of time learning to make a slip knot as for whatever reason I find it surprisingly hard to wrap my head around. Part of it probably comes from the fact that I’m not a very visual person and have a harder than average time grasping how to do something from a visual demonstration. Usually I need to try a whole bunch to get all the details right and considering it took somewhere between 40 minutes to an hour to learn how to do this knot today was no exception. Once I learn how to do the knot I learn another basic trick of taking stitches and putting them on the needle which is actually pretty easy. Finally she attempts to teach me another trick of taking stitches on one needle and putting them on another but sadly I haven't made it past here just yet. She did say learning to knit takes a lot of patience and I think I’ll try again with her another time but for now at least I learned how to make a knot so that’s something! I go home and finally write the newsletter. I decided to prioritize this over going to Mission Run Club considering both the weather and the fact that I really want to get this newsletter out :D.

title: Episode 61
excerpt: Shoutouts Shoutout to “The Fisherman” for getting her fishing business off the ground. She’s offering urchin foraging classes in the fall and crabbing all year round. If you wanna learn more I highly recommend visiting her website if you’re interested in lear…
content: Shoutouts Shoutout to “The Fisherman” for getting her fishing business off the ground. She’s offering urchin foraging classes in the fall and crabbing all year round. If you wanna learn more I highly recommend visiting her website if you’re interested in learning more! Happy birthday to “John Wick!” You’re a great guy and always a real treat to hang out with! Announcement I’m continuing my series of doing 1:1s where I treat people to dinner who I couldn’t get to come to the KBBQ event I held a while back. Unfortunately I’m a bit bandwidth bound in scheduling so I haven’t reached out to everyone I wanted to. If you're interested in getting dinner courtesy of the first national bank of Humza and I haven’t reached out please hit me up! Monday I start off by going to Barry’s Bootcamp at 6:15AM in the morning. I got the inspiration to do this after seeing a gym rat girl at Marina Run Club on Saturday who I thought was pretty cute. I realized if I wanted to attract that kinda girl maybe I should go to the gym. Either way doing something painful like that is probably good for my character arc so regardless of outcome I figure this would be good. Getting out of the house at 5:30AM felt like a miserable slog. The workout itself was a mixture of weights and cardio. The way these workout classes work is you either do weights -> cardio -> weights -> cardio or cardio -> weights -> cardio -> weights. Either way the class is basically half weights and half cardio. The weights part you do a whole bunch of different lifts and such. I don’t know a good way to articulate this other than they yell out random things and you do them with the weights. Naturally you get to pick your weights so you’re not overwhelmed. The cardio part was actually pretty fine for me considering my running experience. The way they do the cardio is they have you turn the intensity on the treadmill up and down and do X for however many seconds. The numbers on the treadmill correspond to MPH so the lowest people would typically do is 3 (casual walk) all the way to 12 (5 min/mile). They said the advanced people should do 10-12 which I was able to. Woo! The weights were significantly harder but sadly I don’t remember enough to articulate it well. It was a whole bunch of random lifts followed by some core work. I actually felt kinda good after that! Unfortunately I learned later that when I went urchin foraging the week before I made a bit of a mistake with regards to my first impression training. When I was out on the rocks someone asked me if I liked sea food and I curtly said no and inadvertently ended the conversation. For a bit of context this was likely asked when I was trying to climb the rocks and I was super nervous trying not to slip and fall. I wasn’t really focused on the conversation so much as I was focused on not falling. Nevertheless I can totally understand how it comes off as rude if I just curtly answer the question and show no interest in engaging or following up. Also while I admit I don’t like urchin I should try to couch my reaction to urchin a bit more when everyone there really liked it. Like I shouldn't be so open about the fact that it doesn't taste the greatest to me :(. I really did hope I would like it the second time I tried it but sadly it seems urchins and I just aren’t meant to mix. After work I continue my 1:1 series with “The Menace". We go to Anatolian table which he thought was really romantic :D. This is good to know if I ever have a date at some point and want to take her somewhere. Perhaps this place could be the move. We have a real good time catching up talking about career stuff, dating stuff and other random things. Speaking of romantic things, the view from Dolores Park looked great. If this was with a date I think it would have been the perfect time for a kiss or something. If I was feeling cheesy I’d say the view is almost as nice as she was but I get the feeling that wouldn’t go over well most of the time. Tuesday Today after work I continued my 1:1 series with “The Slosher”. We went to good ol Abu Salim. For this 1:1 we talked a lot about traveling. Since she travels a lot we talked about some of the pros and cons of traveling a lot. She mentioned that she’s gotten to meet a very wide variety of people, really grow as a person, and gain a lot of confidence in solo traveling. Now she can travel to places that she normally wouldn’t have felt comfortable not knowing how to speak any of the language like Vietnam and Taiwan for example. On the other hand because she is always traveling she doesn’t really get to build community or cultivate any of her other interests like running or art. Whenever she catches up with friends its always big life updates because she doesn’t have time for the small moment to moment interactions which aren’t grand trees in and of themselves but are the seeds that can grow into them. She really liked the way I framed the and joked that I should charge for these which is extra funny considering that I’m paying for em :D. I told her about some of the big life updates such as my goal to find a parter and the first impression training  and my goal of going to the gym more and she said as a muscle mommy in training she supports me. We joked on what the gender bent version of a muscle mommy would be and came up with some suggestions Pectoral Pappi Deltoid Daddy Hammy Habibi I personally like 2 the best but you all let me know you’re favorite in whatever form of communication I use to send you this newsletter. Or even one you don’t if you wanna be crazy. Wednesday I did another Barry’s class in the morning. This class I definitely pushed myself more than the last and I can feel it (in a good way I think). Today after work I attempted to do Midnight Runners with “The Quant”. Sadly my shin splits aren’t as healed as I thought and I can only do a mile before wanting to give up. I think all the Barrys I was doing probably didn’t help. Instead I just walk around with “The Quant” along The Embarcadero for a while and do what is commonly known as shooting the shit. While this isn’t one of the 1:1s as part of the series I guess it’s a bit of a bonus. Thursday Today after work I continue my series of 1:1s with “Granola Girlie”. We go to a vegan sushi place where I’m surprised to learn vegan sushi is actually pretty reasonable. I still don’t think its as good as regular sushi but I am pleasantly surprised. I learned in addition to trash pickup and tutoring she also volunteers at a suicide hotline which is crazy to me! Of all the volunteering that has to be one of the wildest I’ve ever heard of. I really wanted to ask her more about it but it only came up at the end of our 1:1 so I didn’t have the chance. From there I go to bar night with “The Philosopher,” “That’s nuts,” “The Finer things,” “The Juggler,” “The Juggler’s girlfriend,” and another guy. We went to  a bar in Northbeach called Comstock Saloon. I was told this could be another chance to work on my first impression so I dialed in when I was there. I made sure not to make any potentially risky jokes or even any somewhat lame puns. I’ll admit that I was constantly in my head a while here because of that and I might have gone a bit overboard but I was told it went well so that tells me I’m making progress towards my goal. I wanted to further ratchet it up by trying oysters. After Comstock we went to a different bar where they had raw oysters for a happy hour deal. Since I never had oysters before I had two different plans here. Plan A is I try them for the first time and wind up liking them. Plan B is I do a good job hiding my negative reaction. Either way it should be a win win so long as I get it right.  By the time the oysters do come I am incredibly sleepy so I am holding on to dear life trying to stay awake. I try the oysters and … well let’s just say we put plan B into action here. I think I do a reasonably good job couching it. Since those reading this already know me I’ll tell you that in my personal opinion they tasted very briny. And it stuck around too. When I went home I had a few spicy Plantain chips to get the brine out of my mouth. Friday Originally I was gonna go to a Barry’s class today but I wound up being too tired from last night :(. Today after work I went to a concert with “The Quant,” “The Writer,” and “The Notetaker”. One of my friends “The North Bay Trasher” is in a band who played over at Gestalt. It was really cool to see. Major shoutout to stickdefinition go check them out on insta if you are interested! I generally don’t go to that many concerts but this one was a lot of fun! You know it’s a good concert as well when there is a drunk guy who stumbled onto the stage when one of the songs finished and had to be escorted out. Afterwards we all went to “The Politician’s” bar crawl. We started off at The Sycamore where we met up with “Not a matcha bitch,” “The Fisherman,” and “The Philosopher”. Because I came from the concert I wasn’t at this bar for very long before heading over to Southern Pacific Brewing Company. This bar was a lot of fun! A lot of open space and a good mixture of indoor and outdoor seating is perfect for a bar crawl like this. In my opinion it's up there with The Savoy Tivoli as the best bars ever picked for the bar crawl. A few of us headed out a bit early though. Me, “The Philosopher,” “The Notetaker,” “The Fisherman,” “The Writer,” and “The Beekeeper” all went to El Farlitos and hung out for a while. Saturday I woke up with a bad stomach ache. It definitely sucked but it wasn’t so bad that I couldn’t go about my day. I thought I might even be able to run so I went to Marina Run Club where I was disabused of that notion after 0.1 miles. Running with a stomach ache like that was incredibly painful no matter how brief the duration. I talked with interesting people there including a guy who had a lot to say about seed oils and a guy who when I asked if he was into running flatly said he hated it. Props on him for coming! Afterwards I went to trash pickup with “The Grandma,” “The Notetaker,” “The Writer,” “The Beekeeper,” and others. Unfortunately my stomach ache was really bad at this point so I just sat and guarded the stuff while everyone else picked up trash :(. People could definitely tell I wasn’t looking my best but I thought I could still come to trash pickup for the vibes. Sadly since I picked up 0 trash I couldn’t count myself for this one meaning “The Notetaker” is closing the gap and is only 70 trash pickups away from beating me now.  Huge thanks to everyone that got me water, or tums during the pickup including “The Notetaker,” “The Writer,” and “The Grandma”. Yall are real ones! At this point I decided I needed to go home because I really wasn’t doing too great. When I got home I harkened back to Shrek as one does and remembered a great like from the movie “Better out than in I always say”. I proceeded to do that with the aid of my toilet and I could feel the El Farlito burrito coming back. Yeah and the sad part was that even the first time the burrito wasn’t one of the better lengua burritos I ever had.  I will say that while getting food poisoned wasn’t ideal I was glad to be apart of it for the vibes ;). I was actually feeling a lot better after that so I decided I could go ahead with the rest of my plans which included meeting some friends over at The Botanical Gardens to go see the Magnolias. This group of friends is interesting because I met them while practicing my first impressions and one of them said I had a way with words and should consider being a consultant (she herself is one for context). As a result I’ve significantly tempered down my quirkiness to the point where they actually think I’m normal. Maybe if we hang out again we can go to a restaurant and I can leave a Yelp review for the bit. Anyways back to what we were talking about here, the Magnolias. I liked them, they were nice! We learned that there are a wide variety of different species from all over the world. From Mexico all the way to Japan and there were many species on display. We also took a selfie where they all roasted me for having the photography skills of a boomer. The curse of being the one with the best phone After hanging out for a while I went home and wound up taking a 3 hour nap. By the time I woke up the house party hosted by “Top of the Rope”  I was planning to go to already started. Sadly my stomach was feeling a bit queasy again and I really didn’t want to get out of bed so … I didn’t :(. I’m bummed I had to miss this party but sadly it may have been for the best. Sunday Today my stomach is feeling better and I can go about my day like normal again. I start with trash pickup with “The Notetaker,” “The Raja of Rhythm,” “The Yogi,” and others. After trash pickup I planned to meet up with “The Fisherman”, her Russian dissident friend, and a friend of hers that I met back in Hawaii almost a year ago and haven’t’ seen since. There was a bit of a communication error with Hawaii friend who didn’t quite time her date beforehand properly and we wound up waiting a little bit. In the end it all worked out but I did actually go to where her date was to try and  find her and tell her she’s running late. She already left at that point and when I tried showing her picture to the staff at the restaurant they all said they hadn’t seen her. We later speculated that may have been because I was a guy and they thought I was sketch. In any case once we all met up we went to Camera Obscura over by Ocean Beach. It was pretty cool to see. For anyone unaware its basically a giant pinhole camera where light travels into a dark room and inverted on a lens so you can see the outside. Essentially it’s a giant camera showing what Ocean Beach looks like and you can get a live view in a dark room! Afterwards we walked around the sand dune park, ran into a family crabbing which naturally piqued “The Fisherman”, and we went to an Irish bar to see the half time show. It was super cool because one guy made a bunch of food for the whole bar so we got to eat courtesy of this dude. You can tell this bar is a real community type vibe.  The half time show was pretty good. I’m not a huge bad bunny fan but I like him and thought it was catchy. I’ll admit I thought the choice to fly the Puerto Rico flag was pretty bold. And it got bolder still when they had a whole bunch of other Caribbean flags. In my head I wonder if he was predicting Trump’s foreign policy agenda for the rest of his term. From there I went to another Superbowl party hosted by “The Filmaker” and “John Wick”! Since it was “John Wick’s” birthday I got him this birthday card that I thought was pretty good We watched the rest of the Superbowl lamenting just how screwed the Pats were. Im not a big Pats fan but considering how the Seahawks crushed the 49ers I was definitely anti hawk. Perhaps even a dove. After that we did karaoke for a while which was great. “The Filmaker” has a karaoke machine at his place which is a lot of fun! At one point I decided to a bad bunny song and I think it was pretty apparent that I got a 1 on the AP Spanish exam here. “Mr. Socksessful” said he supported me for trying :D. Afterwards I went home and didn’t actually write the newsletter because I was incredibly tired.

title: Episode 60
excerpt: Monday Today after work I continued my goal of treating all my friends to dinner and caught up with “La Tacquiera Royalty”! We went to Cole Valley Tavern and caught up on all manners of things from JJK, running, and a bunch more. While I’m glad I treated ever…
content: Monday Today after work I continued my goal of treating all my friends to dinner and caught up with “La Tacquiera Royalty”! We went to Cole Valley Tavern and caught up on all manners of things from JJK, running, and a bunch more. While I’m glad I treated everyone at Kogi Gogi a while back, hanging out like this made me realize how much fun it is to catch up with people 1:1 which I haven’t been doing a lot of. Tuesday After my shit in the mines (I mean to say shift at first but thought it would be funnier to leave as is), I went to a Marina run club social with “Top of the Rope”. We went to a bar and all just hung out. To help us socialize there was bingo where we had to find people who did certain things or met certain conditions. Examples included “Having the same # of siblings as you,""Newest to SF,""Never had an espresso martini at Balboa cafe”. I rate the experience a solid “OK”. It was perfectly fine but for whatever reason I didn’t find many people I really clicked with. It got to the point where I was so bored I almost broke my first impression training just to give myself a sense of satisfaction. An example of such that I didn’t say but wanted to was when someone asked me if I read and I wanted to say “I’m learning to read the room”. I think that joke is reasonably funny but I knew it wouldn’t go over well. I decided instead it would be better if I just leave and chill in the Humza cave instead. Wednesday In the evening I went to Midnight Runners but I didn’t go alone. I brought Boris the penguin with me. Last week at MR someone said she wanted to see Boris after I mentioned him so I figured I could bring him with me. Unlike Franklin it's not as much work to explain so I figured I could even bring him to work as well. Most people enjoyed seeing an inflated penguin at my desk. My manager was a bit confused but I think it was fine. After work I ran and finally after a couple weeks of slow runs I ran at a reasonable pace :D. It felt great to run at a reasonable pace again! I was joined on this run by animate characters like “Sergeant Sassy” as well. I met what I believe were a bunch of Muzzies or at least people from the middle east which is relatively rare around here and warrants a note. Thursday Before work I went to a special volunteer trash pickup event with “The of the Rope.” Unlike most trash pickups we don’t have bags and grabbers, instead our job is to walk around and call the department of public works (colloquially known as 311ing) any big pieces of trash. For us this essentially amounted to just walking around Haight Ashbury for just under an hour which was a nice way to start the day. After work the company went for a team dinner to celebrate something I can’t quite disclose but was super cool. We went to Foreign Cinema in the Mission. I felt like a true wealthman having such a fancy meal This meal had two forks! It was quite the good meal! I still maintain that the quality certainly does not scale linearly with price, perhaps logarithmically at best but the food was still great and I really like my coworkers so hanging out with them was great as well! After dinner I went to the usual bar night with “The Philosopher,” “The Bartender,” “The Mosher,” “The Finer things,” and “That’s nuts” along with some cameo appearances from folks that I’m not close enough to to give a nickname. Friday To kick off the weekend I got dinner with “The Raja of Rhythm,” “The Yogi,” and a couple other friends from Mission run club. We went to a place called Roosters Peruvian Rotisserie which I highly recommend! They have some real good and real big portions of food! Afterwards we went to a couple bars and hung out. Saturday The day begins with Marina run club with “Top of the Rope” and her boyfriend who is visiting from the great city of Philadelphia. The run itself was good. While I was able to do the run I’ll admit it was a bit harder than Wednesday so maybe I’m not 100% recovered yet but hopefully spacing my runs out by a couple days at a time should help. I wound up getting a big oversized sweater since apparently they were doing a merch drop that day. You didn’t even have to pay, they just handed them out. I think there is some optional membership you can pay for but they didn’t ask if I was a member, they just threw out shirts and sweaters so who am I to ask too deeply. There was a girl I was interesting in talking to there but it was hard to get the chance to approach her since she was with her friends the whole time and I had to book it after the run to get to trash pickup. On the way to trash pickup I learned that “Top of the Rope’s” boyfriend works at the building with the world's largest mobile which is cool. We were also talking about books and he recommended the book called “Thinking fast and Slow”. From what I gather the book breaks down two types of thinking. The first called Type 1 thinking is fast intuitive quick thinking while Type 2 is more slow methodical and deep thinking. For those in AI perhaps you can think of Type 2 thinking as thinking step by step. We think we do more Type 2 thinking than we actually do when most of our thinking is Type 1 thinking. I am actually curious so I may look into this book. He mentioned it has a bunch of research and feels more grounded than a lot of self help books which take inspiration from this book. After the run we have trash pickup with “The Notetaker,” “Granola Girlie,” among others. I met some new people today who were both born in Japan but came to the states around high school which was cool. Sadly I couldn’t stay at trash pickup long as I get picked up by “The Quant” to go urchin foraging with “The Fisherman,” “The Trash Queen," “Granola Girlie,” and “The Rugby Player” amongst others. I haven’t been shy about the fact that I don’t particularly like the taste of urchin so it begs the question why I decided to come along. Back in episode 51 I had this to say about the experience On this trip I made a discovery about myself that I have a real fear of losing my balance, slipping, and falling on rocks. While the rain boots did help my feet to not get wet they did unfortunately make moving around harder and I didn’t have as much tactile sensation in my feet which made me uneasy. Unlike the other two who took to it like a fish (urchin?) to water, I took to it more like a software engineer to water, that is to say I short circuited. I realized I didn’t want to be afraid of this anymore so my main goal on this trip was to conquer my fear and forage the whole time and go out as far as everyone else. I’ll be honest, it was tough at first. Huge shoutout to “The Quant” for helping me out. He pointed out what rocks would make good footholds and helped me get my balance a couple times. Eventually though I managed to get the hang of it. I was still scared while doing it but not so scared that I couldn’t keep going. And in the end I made it all the way out to the main urchin foraging point. As we were foraging I thought to myself that perhaps the thrill of making it all the way out would make some of the raw urchin taste better. Unfortunately it still tasted like Satan’s turd but nevertheless it’s the journey not the destination that counts. Once we got back we cooked up the urchin and made some uni pasta and uni sushi. At this point I realized I wouldn’t l wouldn’t like urchin whether at a church in, if I’m searchin or even off her chin but it was still fun helping to chuck dead urchin off the rocks and lighting everything up with my great jokes and occasionally a lantern. Later me and “The Quant” headed out and got some In-N-Out on the way back which was the perfect way to end the day! Sunday The day begins with the usual trash pickup. I learned one of the regular trashers does a bunch of search and rescue volunteering which was super interesting to learn about. Tricks for searching and rescue: look up, down and all around. They could be dragged by a mountain lion. Make sure to look backwards as you are walking; you may miss something  otherwise . Lots of people get lost in Marin, Santa Cruz, Sierra Nevada mountains. A perk is you can volunteer in Yosemite almost any weekend helping people with sprained tangles get down and then you get free campsite and a day to enjoy to yourself On my bus ride back from pickup, some guy wanted to stick a match sticker in the bowl of sorbet I had. He kept trying to stick it in and I moved the bowl. Eventually he tossed a match next to me and I panicked and moved across the bus. I was a bit flustered at the moment but thankfully nothing else happened. The guy was laughing as I moved which confirmed he did this specifically to annoy me. I was tempted to go back and sit next to him to prove he couldn’t get under my skin but sadly I couldn't quite do it. Later in the day I had dinner with “The Raja of Rhythm”. We went to an Uzbek place called Sofiya which is really good!! I *HIGHLY* recommend it (it’s the kind of place I could never leave a Yelp review for :D). Talking with him made me realize I need to up my AI tool usage and stop using an IDE like Cursor and go all the way and try Codex or Claude Code. I’m excited to start them tomorrow. On my way back home I had a brief run-in with “The Filmmaker" who mentioned the film he’s been working on is almost done. I’m really excited to see it once it’s finished! Once I got home I just chilled and wrote up the newsletter.

title: Episode 59
excerpt: Monday Over the long weekend I decided to do a bit of shopping at Uniqlo in preparation for the pitch a friend event happening on Wednesday. I dragged “The Quant” with me to go and get some of the items recommended by a friend of “The Fisherman”. I’ve leveled…
content: Monday Over the long weekend I decided to do a bit of shopping at Uniqlo in preparation for the pitch a friend event happening on Wednesday. I dragged “The Quant” with me to go and get some of the items recommended by a friend of “The Fisherman”. I’ve leveled up since the last time I came to Uniqlo back in episode 25. Back then I wrote this about the experience To say Uniqlo was overwhelming was an understatement. It really forced me to use every bit of willpower I had left. Now I would only describe the experience as a mildly annoying waste of time. It didn’t feel like a hellscape so much as a paper cut scape. I walked away with some jeans, a shirt jacket kinda thing, and some shirts. Thanks to “The Fisherman” for joining via facetime to also give some opinions. Later I went to Mission Run club featuring “The Raja of Rhythm”. My legs weren’t 100% but they managed to get through the run pretty reasonably. Originally I told everyone I was gonna go in the back of the pack and take it slow but someone requested I be her run buddy and I obliged which took closer to the front than I was anticipating. It still worked out though. Tuesday Today I went to work and then I went home and called my younger sister. We hadn’t talked in a month so it was great to catch up with her. Wednesday Originally the pitch a friend event that “The FIsherman” prepared was gonna happen today but it got canceled :(. After some time in the mines I went to MR with “The Quant” and “Sergeant Sassy”. Sadly the run was far from smooth sailing as my shins and knees really started acting up. “The Quant” could tell that I was hobbling despite my admittedly not best efforts to fool him. They were still efforts mind you just more half hearted ones. After 2 miles I realized running just wasn’t it. I needed to preserve my strength for Marina Run Club for … reasons we will get to in that chapter. In order to win the war I throw the battle and walk the last bit. Along the way though I meet a girl from Toronto who claims Toronto chinese food is better than SF Chinese food. I’m a bit skeptical of this as she is a Canadian I only just met so I ask a group chat with the true Canadians (“The Mosher,” “That’s nuts,” “The Philosopher,” “The Juggler,” “The Best” amongst others).  They certainly don’t defend the claim as vehemently as she does so I’m a bit less than convinced. Thursday After work I go to an alumni event for the company I was working at from May 2021 - March 2025 Snorkel AI. It was great catching up with everyone again and seeing the majority alumni along with the smattering few of people actually working there. Amusingly enough one person said he almost didn’t recognize me without my trusty unicorn hat. I was reminded of some of my antics like when I would eat mayo with every meal (which was delicious!!). Back in those days I ate mayo with everything from ice cream to thai fried rice and I loved every bite of it. Though that was probably at least part of why I was fatter back in those days but man was it good. Once you leave Snorkel you have 2 years left to exercise your shares. When I asked people currently working there if I should I was met with a resounding awkward silence. Not all bets can pay off I suppose. Originally I wanted to split my time between this and a Yelp elite event before going to bar night but I figured quality beats quantity so I caught up with a bunch more alumni instead which was a lot of fun! From there I went to bar night with “The Philosopher,” “That’s nuts,” “The Mosher,” “The Best” and some other folks who don't have newsletter nicknames. Originally there was someone I met at the regular’s party last Sunday who I tried persuading to come today by promising to give a gold star. They didn’t come but they wound up being used to persuade “The Best” to come through I think I’ll start telling people if they do things I’ll give them a gold star and then actually give them one :D Friday “The Fisherman” is looking for a website to advertise her upcoming crabbing and foraging lessons. It was a tough market but in the end she went with an offshore team. Specifically off the shores of SF. And the team is one Paki who knows how to vibecode with Claude. And unrelated the team member is a guy who was once recognized at a party for scarfing down a burrito on the 33 bus. After work the team starts to work on the first version of the website and send it to “The Fisherman” for review. A couple days ago I got an invite from “La Tacqueria Royalty” to come to an event Originally I thought this was a game night of a sort. Clearly I didn’t read this message thoroughly enough. I also didn’t read this follow up message Before the event starts I get dinner with “La Tacqueria Royalty”, and two other folks that don’t have newsletter nicknames. I see them all dressed to impress while I was dressed in my standard Mooni hoodie and jeans (not the new ones I bought from Uniqlo mind you). When I realized this was meant to be a dating event I shuddered that I’m already neglecting the fashion advice I got from my council :( . Nevertheless I’m still down to go if for no other reason than to practice the first impression advice I got. Huge props to “La Taqueria Royalty” for offering to wing man me :D. When we get to the event it turns out to be quite crowded with a wide variety of folks from all walks of life (though mostly Google, Berkeley, and UCLA because SF I guess). I talk with a wide variety of folks including a guy who got inspired to volunteer at Red Cross after meeting with a Red Cross volunteer at 4AM at Market St, some other people into social deduction games including Blood on the Clock Tower (or BoTC as it's apparently called). To help break the ice there is a bingo sheet to get you to meet people that fulfill different conditions including “Went to Berkeley," “Works at a Startup”, along with different things like “Compliment a stranger” and so on. This works well enough to start with and I get Bingo reasonably quickly. It turns out there is another square on the Bingo called “Meet someone you matched on Hinge with”. I thought surely that wouldn’t apply to me until it did. Out of the corner of my eye I saw a girl and did a double take. It was in fact someone I matched on Hinge with. Hold on could it really be <her> could it?! I pulled up Hinge and went through my matches and confirmed it was in fact her. What do I do now? Well I asked myself what would make for a more entertaining newsletter and the answer was clear. We talk to her team. We wound up talking for about 10 minutes during which I not only employed all the advice I got from “The Fisherman” and “The Philosopher” but even some advice I got from “The Quant”. One thing he observed from the Costco dating event I went to is that sometimes when meeting people in these situations I tend to rapid fire ask questions without giving the conversation a chance to breathe. I’m pretty sure the reason I do this is because I’m worried if there is an awkward silence the person I’m talking to may try to leave. But this time I notice the pauses and let them breathe a bit. It was fun talking to her, she likes games, walks, is a bit nerdy and overall seems like a fun person. I suspect she may be a bit introverted but ya gotta go for it. Surprisingly she asks me for my number and then I ask about meeting up. Considering that some of my other text asks haven’t gone anywhere, this is progress. I know I probably should have asked in person but I think she needed to leave the event and I figured we had a good rapport so I may as well. Slightly later in the event the bar really starts to fill up and I start getting nervous. And then one guy comes down the stairs and stumbles onto me causing me to fall down a bit. At this point I was mildly worried about a crowd crush scenario if I then tripped onto somebody else. I have flashbacks of when I went to Westwood a month ago and got overwhelmed by the crowd. I thought to myself “Yeah I really hate crowds”. “Yeah I may as well leave”. But then I remembered that I need to push past my limits if I want to improve. I don’t want to let this thing beat me. I can’t improve if I just stay where I am right now.  So I take a deep breath and decide to stay. This winds up being the right call as I talk with many more people including the BoTC people at this time. Periodically I tried to enter  some groups to talk with a few select people but they weren’t really open to outsiders. One tip I got from a book that “The Philosopher” recommended was to look at the way people's feet point. If it looks like someone (either in a 1:1 or group conversation) has their feet pointed somewhat outwards it means they are open to outsiders joining the conversation. If not it means they aren’t. This can be a good visual tell before approaching. Towards the end of the night I try to talk to one more girl. This really cute really tall girl. I’m with her and a bunch of people in a group and she asks what we like to drink. I respond with the truth that I don’t drink and she looks at me like I’m some kind of idiot. I don’t really know what to make of this and in retrospect this probably should have been my first cue that she wasn’t interested but don’t worry things go from bad to slightly worse. Not a lot worse mind you, but slightly. Later I notice her by herself having a drink so I go up to her and ask her what she’s drinking. She says water and I respond “Ooh the drink of champions”. She says “Yeah ….” and then she just walks away from me. I was kinda put off by that so I decided that's my cue to leave the event and go home. Saturday I start off with Marina run club with “Top of the Rope”. While my shins were still splinting it was critical that I preserve my strength so I can come to this run club. Not because I really liked the run but because there was this one really cute girl I wanted to get to know better. I started talking with her for all of 2 minutes before the run started and she put her airpods in which made it pretty clear she wasn’t interested in talking during the run. The run itself was quite nice. Normally I would have rather gone to the top of Tank Hill as is my tradition but this run was a close 2nd During the run me and “Top of the Rope” meet this guy who is trying to build a social media app centered around posting videos of yourself doing things and the only way to see what other people post is to post something yourself. He mentioned that 90% of traffic on a social media app are lurkers and this can be a way to mitigate that. He wants social media as it's more originally intended (i.e. folks engaging with others in their own local communities) without grandiose things like Br. Meast or the like. After the run we went to trash pickup along with “The Notetaker,” “The Ravenkeeper,” “The Writer” and others. I skipped out on the usual post trash brunch in order to save room for KBBQ coming up later tonight. I then go with “Top of the Rope” to a party celebrating Wikipedia’s 25th birthday. It was over in the SF public library and it was pretty interesting. They had presentations about different topics such as what it's like to be a Wikipedia editor, how to contribute to Wikimedia commons, and they had a place where you could get the Wikipedia logo printed onto things like shirts, bags, and the like. I met one of her friends who is very similar to me in that we both despise the South bay and have minimal furniture although surprisingly I think this guy has even less furniture than I do :O. They had nametags and I decided to be a bit cheeky with mine Occasionally when I introduced myself I would say that I’m Cite for short and a surprising number of people believed me. I guess this goes back to some other feedback I got that the first 15 minutes of a conversation are intended to be purely factual. Granted I knowingly broke the rule here but it’s interesting to observe. I got to do a coloring sheet which made me feel like a kid in the best way possible One of the presentations was a game where we had to guess which Wikipedia article had more characters than the other in a 1 v 1 format. Let’s play the game here! I’ll give you two Wikipedia articles and you guess which one is longer. I’ll reveal the answers at the end. Note that length is defined as the character count in each article. San Francisco Fog vs Lombard Street List of Hills in San Francisco vs Mission Burrito Emperor Norton vs Charles M. Schultz Sourdough vs Dungeness Crab At the event I ran into one of “The Ravenkeeper’s” friends (Nitu) who introduced me to some of her friends who wound up being really cool. I wound up making a really good first impression on her as she said “You should work in consulting. You have a way with words. You say everything in a packaged up way.” For context she works in consulting herself so I guess some of the tricks I’ve learned have been working. She was also really cool and I love how both her and Nitu are down for really random events like this. I definitely need to invite them to stuff as they seem really fun! I then go home and the off shore website development team gets to work and iterates on the website based on the feedback “The Fisherman” sent and delivers a second version. From there I go to Kogi Gogi for the big KBBQ event. This is the largest group I ever brought to Kogi Gogi with me, “The Quant,” “The Fisherman,” “The Philosopher,” “The Writer,” “The Mosher,” “That’s nuts,” “Not a matcha bitch,” “Top of the rope,” “The Pasta Prince,” another friend who doesn’t have a newsletter nickname, “The notetaker,” and even “The Shadow Brigade”. I wasn’t sure how best to mention this but the whole reason I had this event was to celebrate the fact that a startup I was at previously got acquired and I wanted to treat my friends. It was a great time and I’m really glad everyone could come! Sadly I can’t put the above pic on Hinge but man does it slap. Afterwards we went to Hometown creamery and got ice cream. The cranberry and orange sorbet was surprisingly good! As great a time as it was  I feel bad I could only treat a few of my friends. I’m gonna be reaching out to y’all either 1:1 or in different groups if y’all couldn’t make it. If you don’t hear from me within a week want a dinner courtesy of the first national bank of Humza please reach out and let’s get something on the books. If you 're reading this newsletter it means you’re a friend I want to treat as a celebration! Sunday The day begins with trash pickup with “The Notetaker” and for the first time in a minute “The Yogi”! It was great hearing about all her travels from Tahoe, Chile, Argentina, Dallas, and Toronto! After pickup I went to Crissy Beach to play Spikeball hosted by “The Menace” which I dragged “The Quant” to. I didn’t know he and his group of friends were so into the game! One of them keeps track of every game he has played since high school and has a website with everyone’s ELO based on all the games played. I generally consider myself an average spikeball player but these people were all mostly quite above me :( :( . Sadly my old Tuesday evening training was not serving me as well as I thought. I ingested some copium and told myself its because of the wind and the sand since I usually play in a park rather than a beach but facts are facts and ELOs are ELOs. After this event for the first time in a while I felt tired. “The Quant” even noticed I basically checked out of one of the last conversations I had at the event and gave an out for us to head out. Originally I was planning on inviting “The Taco” over for lamb pasta but I had to cancel because I was low on energy which sucks. I hate canceling things but with my headache and brain feeling fried I felt out of it. I need a way to get more energy so if any of y’all have suggestions that would very much be appreciated. This can’t happen again :( I can’t remember the last time I chose to chill at home instead of doing something social.  I really hate cancelling and feel pretty bad about it (worse than pretty much any bad first impression I made except for one in particular I won't be getting into in this newsletter which did come with some consequences for me). I finally go=]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]=]\===]\===]\===]\==]====]====]==]==]==]==]==]==]==========]=]=]=]=]=====]=]=] around to writing the newsletter after way too much lazing around. Wikipedia Answers Round 1 Winner Round 2 Winner Round 3 Winner Round 4 Winner

title: Episode 58
excerpt: Shoutouts Shout out to “Tightly Knit” for doing her first Midnight Runners run! Also it's her birthday today so extra shoutout for that! Monday Another day at work. We’re getting to the point where the days will mostly blend into each other as I acclimate so…
content: Shoutouts Shout out to “Tightly Knit” for doing her first Midnight Runners run! Also it's her birthday today so extra shoutout for that! Monday Another day at work. We’re getting to the point where the days will mostly blend into each other as I acclimate so nothing too interesting. After work I go to Mission Run Club where I learn a brutal lesson about the importance of bag drops. Unlike Midnight Runners this club doesn’t have one of those meaning I either can’t bring a bag or I have to carry it myself. Before when I did this run club I didn’t have that whole job thing so that wasn’t a concern for me; now I learn what its like to run with this backpack and let me tell you its not fun. If I run with it  on my backpack all the bouncing around will cause the zippers to come undone meaning I have to stop every so often to rezip it. On the other hand if I run with it up front where I can rezip it more easily it feels like I’m getting punched in the gut every 5 seconds and with my laptop, clothes, headphones, and portable charger it hurts :(. I don’t think I’ve run a more brutal 3 miles before if I’m being honest here. On the plus side I brought “The Enabler” to his first Mission Run Club and he said he enjoyed it so there is a chance my already great Mondays may become even greater :D. Of course “The Raja of Rhythm” also joined at the end as well to sweeten the deal. Tuesday Just work. Onto the next Wednesday Today after work I do Midnight Runners with “The Enabler,” “Tightly Knit,” and one of “Tightly Knit’s” friends who I promised chicken tenders to. “Tightly Knit” did such a good job for her first run! Sadly this was in the pre newsletter days but the first time I did this run club I nigh on gave up and only kept going because I saw a Hinge date who I ran next to for a while and my pride couldn’t let me back down.
