As a brief aside I learned recently that this old Hinge date is on Strava and now I can definitely say after almost 2 years of running I have in fact closed the gap between us Bringing chicken tenders proved to be a bit of a conversation starter which was cool. And everyone loved them! Definitely a very fun and wholesome bit! Thursday Today after the mines it's time for bar night with “The Mosher,” “The Finer things,” and “The Bartender”. For the most part it's a pretty chill night. At one point I ask “The Philosopher” if he is coming and this is what he says in response Well given what he said here I can’t not give Riley (the person who actually bartends at this bar) a kiss right? Friday Today after work we have the grand debut of the meme song “The Fisherman” wrote! She will be singing / guitaring this next Wednesday at a “Pitch a Friend” event which will be a lot of fun. Between the song and the practice I’m doing to improve my first impressions I’m quite looking forward to seeing what will happen. I got “The Writer,” “Top of the Rope,” “The Quant,” and “The Pickleballer to all come over and watch the splendid performance! It was awesome! Mad props to “The Fisherman” for doing this. Once the song was presented we hung around while I converted more people to the coveted church of Plantain chips. Our numbers are small but growing! We’re what big potato chip doesn’t want you to know about! Later me, “The Writer,” and “The Fisherman” hung out and did a bit of a Hinge party where we all sent likes on each other’s Hinges which was fun :D. Saturday The day starts off with me going to Marina Run club with “Top of the Rope”. To be perfectly honest my legs were kinda sore from all the running I was doing before but that wasn’t really why I came here. No, I came because the last time I came to this run club I saw a super pretty girl. I wanted to get to know her more and I wanted “Top of the Rope” to act as my wing woman. As I saw her come with a group of friends though I’d be lying if I said I didn’t get nervous. I knew I just needed to reach out and break in but I stood right before the wall unwilling to burst through it. I thought if I had someone else with me it would have been ok. I thought I would have figured something out. I thought wrong. Interestingly in parallel someone came up to the two of us clearly intending to flirt with “Top of the Rope”. While it didn’t work out she did use this to reassure me that even if it doesn’t it’s still fine. At this point the run started and I figured maybe I would get a chance later. Unfortunately my leg was really acting up at this point and “Top of the Rope” noticed I was hobbling during my run. She suggested we stop and honestly the prospect of running 3 miles with the state of my leg right now made me agree. I wasn’t interested in doing this run for it’s own sake and it’s not worth suffering through like this just for a chance to talk to ms. pretty girl (I’m sure I could come up with some better way of referring to her but I have a serious case of can’t be bothered). So me and “Top of the Rope” instead go for a nice walk from Marina to Mission for trash pickup. Big thanks for ditching run club to walk with me instead :D. We get to trash pickup where we have quite the crowd including “The Notetaker,” “The Politician," “Not a matcha bitch,” “Granola Girlie” amongst others. It was a great time as always and given the good weather it was awesome seeing so many people out and about. Afterwards I meet up with my Dad and we go for a walk. I mentioned in a previous episode I wanted to connect with him more so I proposed we meet up for a walk. We go through Crissy field up to Golden Gate bridge and back. Along the way my Dad tells me stories of when he was young in SF and would come down to Crissy field to watch the waves from his car. He told me how some of the guard railings around the area weren’t always around and it was more dangerous. It was really nice to hear a bit of history from his younger days like that. The little stories. He doesn’t live in SF anymore so it kinda felt like passing the torch down. Which reminds me, my house in Mill Valley is right near the bus stop and that location was chosen specifically because my Dad liked to take the bus to the city. Now he doesn’t do that anymore as he just drives but whenever I go home to visit I take the bus to the same bus stop so it also feels like passing down the torch. That doesn’t have anything to do with the above but I quite like the story and wanted an excuse to share it. From there I go home and work on my presentation of “The Fisherman” for the “Pitch a friend” event on Wednesday. Once I make sufficient progress on that I go to an Irish bar over in lower Haight to try talking with people. It goes over ok I guess. The bar definitely leans older and while I commiserate with a few people about the massacre that was the 49ers vs The Sea Hawks it certainly wasn’t as successful as my usual Thursday night romps. One of my friends says “We need to get you a new hobby that doesn’t involve going to bars and not ordering anything. Perhaps board game cafes”. I would love to but there really aren’t that many of those :(. I am of the opinion we need more places where you can socialize at night where drinking isn’t the default 😤. Sunday A trash pickup a day keeps the cigarette butts away. Today we have “The Raja of Rhythm,” “The Notetaker,” “The Philosopher,” “Cool friend whose newsletter nickname is admittedly a work in progress” and others. Not much out of the ordinary but when an ordinary trash pickup is a continual source of joy that is not a bad thing by any means. After trash pickup I go to Dolores park because a spikeball acquaintance is hosting some public event involving opening a bottle of jam. It’s a really tough bottle to open and I fail miserably at the endeavor. He tells me about this new AI agent app he is making which while I’m not exactly enamored by, I do respect his enthusiasm and hustle towards it. If it gives him meaning and makes him happy then I’m happy to see him do it. He asks me some questions about getting AI models to run on small devices and I share some tricks about how he might do that which he was quite keen to adapt. He also roasts me for my filler words while I’m speaking. He asked me how old I am and I said “I’m like 29” and he responded “Like? You don’t know your exact age?”. This was another (albeit smaller) piece of feedback on the first impression that I have. The way I come off can make me sound unconfident and uncertain. I haven’t been indexing on this as much but it is worth thinking about how I can reduce filler words. Perhaps more …. Pauses. Perhaps phrases to indicate I’m gathering my train of thought. I’m also elated to say I have a long form bit that I’m doing. I can’t say exactly what it is but here is an encrypted message U2FsdGVkX19me1qWzwWl+e3wHenZLp2KHa3NatHsjPZ2CKMvvhAGIP/w7h0WpEAZfVSeZ5WUJK9tG/knH+nZM3sD5+yINii1Ybbve0EUgA9jwDOMZek8utK+U/7LmGN0 The decrypted message will be revealed once certain conditions are met. As to when that will be, well that depends on *you*. I look forward to playing this game with you. Later in the day after a brief stint at the Iqbal cave I go to my usual Thursday bar for a regulars special. Since this bar is very community driven with a lot of regulars they are hosting a special party for the regulars so we can all get to know each other. Naturally the Canadian pack that I roll with including “The Philosopher,” “The Mosher,” “That’s nuts,” “The Best,” and “The Finer things”. I also invite “The Quant” as my +1. It was a really good time! A lot of the regulars there are pretty cool and I got to talk with folks I already know and meet some new people. I met this one girl who is big into F1 and just moved to the city recently. I’m trying to get her to become a Thursday night regular and I told her I would give her a gold star if she comes next Thursday. The event continues for a number of hours until the bar winds up closing and we help clean up. I get to see behind the kitchen for the first time which feels a little bit like peeking into Narnia. There is an after party but at this point I’m tired and decide to head home. I’m so tired I don’t even write up the newsletter :(.

title: Episode 57
excerpt: Shoutouts Happy birthday “Dentist”! Hard to believe we only met on Christmas around a year ago because as we and “The Enabler” often say it feels like we’ve known each other our whole lives! Monday Today is the first day of my new job! So far it’s mainly just…
content: Shoutouts Happy birthday “Dentist”! Hard to believe we only met on Christmas around a year ago because as we and “The Enabler” often say it feels like we’ve known each other our whole lives! Monday Today is the first day of my new job! So far it’s mainly just onboarding and various trainings. I don’t know if y’all knew this but sexual harassment is bad actually. I also have started reading some papers that are going to be relevant to what I will be doing. One cool trick I found that makes reading papers better is I upload them to Claude and I ask Claude to go through them with me section by section and quiz me on each section before we move on. Kinda like a teacher. I think this way it forces me to explain in my own words what I think is happening and it can point out what is going right and wrong. Originally I was planning on going to Mission Run Club but it got cancelled due to rain so I just went home and chilled. Tuesday Another day of reading papers with Claude as my teacher. I’m starting to understand a little bit more about GPU programming now but without hands-on experience I think I still have a lot to play around with. I’m hoping once I start on my actual projects I’ll get to play around with more concrete stuff and really nail down the intuition here! After work I go to a potluck hosted by one of “The Raja of Rhythm”’s coworkers. I was invited as +1 by one of the coworkers friends who I met at trash pickup! It was a really good time. The main dish was beef pho which was quite good and convinced me that maybe pho as a food isn’t as beyond redemption as I initially thought. Afterwards we all just hung around and had a conversation that could best be described as “Very straight male esque humor”. It was amazing and I highly enjoyed it. I met someone else there who writes a substack about his life which I read when I got home. Wednesday I got my first real task at work. It was a small bug designed to better acquaint myself with the codebase. It's a simple bug whose solution is more about me getting familiar with running things than actually identifying the fix. I come up with and validate a basic fix by the end of the day. In the evening I do Midnight Runners with “The Quant” and "Sergeant Sassy”. The run itself was fine without too much to note. I wound up talking with some folks afterwards and heard some stories of truly terrible first dates. I don’t think it would be right for me to say them here but wow they actually made me feel better about myself which will be relevant later. Thursday I merged my first PR today only to later find out I now technically introduced my first bug because the fix turns out to be more complicated than we originally thought. Back to the drawing board :D. Later I go to bar night with the Canadians including “That’s nuts,” “The Philosopher,” and  “The Juggler” amongst others. It was great to be back after the new year! I learn from “The Juggler” that Gough street was named after a milkman (Charles H. Gough) who got onto the SF street naming committee and named it after himself and Octavia was named after his sister which is pretty interesting! We met a nurse there who does kidney and heart transplants. He described some stories of having brains hanging out over a patient which were pretty wild. Mad respect to him that is not an easy field to be working in!! Friday Today I properly fixed the bug and brought my first week here to close. After work I get dinner with “The Philosopher" and “The Fisherman” where they give me some very helpful feedback for dating (and just personal relationships in general). One of the big overarching things they told me was that I can sometimes make a bad first impression on people for a variety of reasons. Part of it is that I take a “one size fits all” approach to social interaction and use a wide variety of jokes and bits that don’t really make sense right away. For example some of my terrorist jokes are not good to say right away (especially to a woman on a date) but even in general may unnecessarily put people on the backfoot. Another example of this would be a time when I went crabbing with some people and they asked if I would be eating any and I made a joke along the lines of the following “Oh I can’t I’m allergic … I don’t eat anything I don’t like”. I meant the joke in a light hearted way but from what I was told their reaction was not the best. This brings up two points. The first is that a first conversation with someone (especially the first 30 minutes or so) should be mainly factual and making jokes like that can be highly disruptive to forming the first impression, and the other (which I have noticed in retrospect) is that I’m not the most aware of how others perceive me. I don’t always pick up on subtle grimaces or turning away as a response to things I may do or say. Being able to pick up on and recover from that with things like “Oh sorry did I make you uncomfortable” can be quite useful in the event I do fumble the ball. Along those lines smiling more can be good. I don’t really have a very good “smile on command” smile (this is part of why my Hinge profile is also bad). We did a little bit of practice here as well to nail down some of the components. I should make sure that I squint my eyes, raise my eyebrows a bit, and fully use my cheeks. :D. I also need to be mindful of my tone of voice and distance when asking questions. For example, sometimes when I’m meeting people and I ask the question “What’s something cool or interesting about you that people wouldn’t expect?” I do it in a dry tone and upclose distance that gives off the vibe that I’m sizing someone up or evaluating them rather than genuinely trying to get to know them I can also sometimes have awkward silences when I speak due to me needing some time to think of what I’ll say next so adding in phrases like “Oh sorry I lost my train of thought one second” can be helpful. There was also some really good and thought provoking feedback on things related to religion and materialism specifically in terms of what it is I want in a partner. I’m Muslim but I realize I don’t entirely know what I should want or expect from a partner. Someone who is already Muslim? And if so, how devout are they? For example they were telling me about some Muslim women they know who to put it bluntly are more devout then I am and for example would not be ok with me going to my weekly bar nights with the Canadians even though I don’t drink alcohol. Would I be ok with someone who was raised Muslim but doesn’t really practice? Would I give up the woman of my dreams just because she isn’t Muslim? These are questions that upon thinking about it I don’t have a clear cut answer to since to be honest I don’t really have the relationship experience to say. Originally my intention was to have a long term relationship that can lead to marriage but given my inability to answer these it may be better to have some more short term relationships that can teach me more about what it is I really want and be able to answer these hard questions. Of course it's possible I go in with the intention of dating for experience and find something that works but it’s no guarantee. Another less hard thing I need to figure out is materialistic expectations. Anyone who has been to my apartment can probably guess I’m not a very materialistic person but that’s not generally the kind of expectation I can have in a partner. As such I may need to consider things like upgrading my apartment or buying fancier things to meet somewhere in the middle. This one obviously isn’t as big as the point above but still something to think about. I am really grateful for the feedback it has given me a lot to think about along with some tips which if applied should even boost personal relations of all kinds. And of course super grateful for friends taking the time to give me this kind of feedback! After the feedback session I wound up going on a late night trip to El Farlito’s because a college friend of mine was in town and we met up for a while over burritos and hung out. Saturday I did Marina Run Club for the first time today with “Top of the rope”. All in all the run itself was good, it was 3 miles with a break in the middle so somewhere in between Mission Run Club and Midnight Runners. The people there were definitely friendly and I talked with some cool folks. I also tried putting the advice from last night into practice and not saying any weird jokes off the bat. When someone asked if I come here regularly for example I resisted my impulse to say I’ve been coming every week … since today and just said straight up (but with enthusiasm) that this is my first time and it seems great so far. I also saw a cute girl that I wanted to talk to but didn’t have time. On the plus side this motivates me to come back next week. Since I don’t know many people at this run club compared to others it's a great training ground for first impression work. Afterwards we went to trash pickup which was poppin with such folks as “The Writer,” “Not a matcha bitch,” “The Notetaker,” and “Granola Girlie” amongst others. It was great to see so many folks back after the new year! From there I went over to the Moscone center to sneak into a biology conference. My college friend from last night was presenting a poster at this conference (his whole reason for visiting in the first place) and I wanted to come support him! Now when I get to the first floor where I see the posters a security guard says I have to have my badge out. I then awkwardly walk away and look around other floors since my friend never specified where exactly he would be presenting. When I get to the third floor and see he is not there I walk back only to find a security guard saying on the radio “Yeah I found him … he is wearing a green jacket”. Turns out I was caught and I was being escorted out of the building. To his credit the security guard doing so was really chill and we wound up talking on the escalator ride down. I explained my situation to him and he said “Yeah I get it but I can’t let you in here either”. I told him that makes sense and that its my job to go see my friend and its his job to stop me and in the end he won and I can’t really blame him for that. It’s not whether you win or lose after all its how you play the game which got a laugh out of him. Apparently he thought he might have to tackle me given how fast I was walking around :D. I chilled for about an hour and my friend came out of the Moscone center and we caught up for a bit longer before he needed to leave for the airport. I am glad I got to see him and I do really hope his poster went well! Funnily enough after I saw him off I ran into the same security guard again. We talked for a bit longer and I asked the question “What’s the craziest thing about your job that people wouldn’t expect?” and he told me that he sees all kinds of shit as a security guard and knowing how to deescalate can be huge so he doesn’t do anything that can get him fired or sent to jail. You never know if the people you are talking to are in their right minds. He also says it pays really well and that he enjoys it and I should apply to be one. Who knows maybe if this whole Software Engineer thing doesn’t pan out I’ll consider a pivot :D. Afterwards I go and audition for some Improv teams. It’s been a while since I’ve done improv and the place I do it at is hosting auditions for teams so I thought this could be a good way to get back into it. I haven’t really done improv in a while but getting back in there felt a lot more natural than I thought. Maybe it's all the bits and stuff I do when talking to people which feels kinda akin to improv. Hopefully I get on a team but we shall see. Finally we end the night with the birthday party for the one and only “The Dentist”! We have a get together in the community room in her apartment with the two of us, “The Enabler,” “La Tacqueria Royalty” and a bunch of her other friends. “The Enabler” came up with a plan to surprise her with a cake which was really funny for two reasons. The first was she also got a cake from the exact same bakery because she has a very particular cake she likes. The second was he realized we didn’t have a candle for the cake and needed to quickly come up with a solution. Now keep in mind we’re already in the party so I come up with the idea to door dash a candle because these days what can’t you door dash right? I prioritize whatever will come here the fastest which winds up being a scented candle Now you might be thinking “Well how do you put this on cake?”. The answer is you don’t. You hold it alongside the cake and hope for the best. Look this was a gametime decision that had to be made while not letting “The Dentist” know  meaning communication was lower here. I did what I had to do and in the end she liked the candle so it doubled as a birthday present so I guess that means it all works out. Of course it wouldn’t be my take on a birthday without a custom birthday card and this is what the folks at the lab came up with this year (Ignore the low resolution part that doesn’t actually print on the card itself that was just Walgreens warning me). Sunday Today I did the SF Hot Chocolate 10k. Originally I was not planning to do this but last night I got persuaded by “The Enabler” and “La Tacquiera Royalty”. I had a bit of a problem though. The race started at 8:15 in GGP and I needed to make sure I got to trash pickup by 10am in The Mission. This means I sadly couldn't go at the more chill pace everyone else in our group was going at and I kinda had to gun it a bit. All in all the race was fine. I actually felt the first 5k was great. I was able to PR on the mile there with 7:17 which was pretty good and gives me hope I may by the end of the year be able to break the 6 minute mark. Sadly the next 5k was a bit harder for me. Sadly I couldn't stick around for the post race festivities. There was hot chocolate befitting the name of the race but I can’t have that anyway. I really wanted to stick around for the brunch to hang out with folks and of course write a Yelp review about it but I already told folks earlier I would be going to trash pickup and running this was a last minute decision for me. I head to trash pickup and catch up with a bunch of folks. It was great hanging out with everyone. After trash pickup we hang out for a while longer and wind up chatting at Ritual. I was discussing some of the feedback I got and mentioned that I started reading a book I was recommended about increasing my likeability. One tip in the book is you should tilt your head in conversations because it shows warmth and vulnerability. The evolutionary roots of this are apparently because it exposes your carotid artery. I was met with some skepticism on this particular tip but it is actually a thing!. Some guy who was sitting next to us at Ritual commented and asked if he was doing it right with a really exaggerated head tilt. He was a fun guy, he said he really liked the laughs we were having in our conversation, that my friends are awesome (which is unequivocally correct of course), and that they will shepherd me through this. Later I went to Panchitas only to see a bunch of my old coworkers at the job I got laid off from which was kinda awkward for me. I got over that though and said fuck it and chatted them up and it winds up going better than I thought it would. It was kinda nice to catch up with them and hear about how they were doing. They had to leave though because they had to Uber back to the office to do something that a deadline that night which sounded intense. I went home and chilled and got dinner with “The Enabler” at a JBBQ place called Gyu Kaku which is quite good! I don’t hang out a lot with him 1:1 so it was nice to catch up and talk with him for a while. Then I went home and started writing the newsletter.

title: Episode 56
excerpt: Monday Since the weather was nice I wanted to celebrate my last week of funemployment by going on a big walk. I went from my place -> Twin Peaks -> Ocean Beach -> Land’s End -> my place -> Duboce Park. Afterwards I went on a Christmas tree run with Midnight r…
content: Monday Since the weather was nice I wanted to celebrate my last week of funemployment by going on a big walk. I went from my place -> Twin Peaks -> Ocean Beach -> Land’s End -> my place -> Duboce Park. Afterwards I went on a Christmas tree run with Midnight runners with “The Enabler” and “La Tacqueria Royalty”. For this run we started over at Fisherman’s Wharf and ran to Chase Center stopping at a bunch of different Christmas trees along the way. The run itself was pretty good! Once again “La Tacqueria Royalty” and I had wildly different Strava paces despite running next to each other for most of the run which continues to baffle the mind. It turns out one of “Granola Girlie’s” friends also does Midnight Runners which was a fun coincidence. Tuesday The weather proved unexpectedly good so I decided to get out and do something I never did before and hike to the top of San Bruno mountain. Overall I found the views to be reasonable but admittedly not my favorite in SF. That being said I am glad I did it seeing as I never actually made it up here before. The way down though proved more treacherous than I expected. I went far enough along the mountain that it made sense to go down a different path than I came up and every path down was incredibly narrow. Much like when I went urchin foraging my fear of losing my balance and falling really came back to bite me here. It took me three tries to find a path that wasn’t too narrow but the tradeoff was that it was really rocky and slippery. Funnily enough I trudged through really slowly at first but then got motivated to pick up the pace when I saw a Coyote behind me. I know Coyote’s aren’t the most dangerous wildlife to encounter but if it came towards me on uneven terrain I knew I wouldn’t be a happy camper. After I eventually got down I went home and kinda just chilled the rest of the day. I meant to go to game night at Detour but wound up getting engrossed in a manga instead in what I’d call pretty uncharacteristic fashion but oh well. Wednesday The weather was quite bad today so I mainly stayed inside and did a bit more flight school and chilled. In the evening I started to prepare my lamb pasta for “The Enabler” and “Tightly Knit”s NYE party. Thanks to “The Mosher” and “La Tacqueria Royalty” I got some good feedback on improving the pasta. “The Mosher” told me I should season more and he gave me a number of recommendations. The one I decided to go with was pesto. “La Tacqueria Royalty” told me that when I’m boiling the water for the pasta I should add salt to it. He said to make it “salty like the Pacific Ocean” which is to say it’s really hard to add too much salt. I followed both of those and was pleasantly surprised by how it turned out The party itself was great! “Tightly Knit” took all the food and beverages and made quite the aesthetic table spread the likes of which I would never be able to replicate on my own. It was great to catch up with a bunch of the Google group that I don’t really get to see and I got to see “The Dentist” after a while along with other members of the dental pack. After a while we all went around and shared what some of our accomplishments were for the past year. I think this was a pretty standout year for me between leaving a job I didn’t like, getting another new job when that one didn’t work out, the half marathon, the long walks among other things but I thought it would be funniest to highlight the whole Yelp elite bit. Eventually the clock struck midnight and I surprised everyone by popping out in a bear onesie. To explain we need to rewind the clock back to Monday during the Christmas tree run. I wish I had some kinda fade back effect like they have in TV shows so just imagine one in your head please and thanks. During the run we saw someone wearing a bear costume and “The Enabler” said “Humza I’d like to see you in a bear costume next year!”. Of course little did he realize that I would be at his NYE party two days later which would enter into “next year”. So naturally I made sure to order a bear onesie that same night and when the clock struck midnight I put it on post haste :D. Thursday The weather was pretty bad today so I wound up just chilling inside. I did a bit of admin and flight school and then wound up just chilling for a while. In the evening I decided to get out of the house and go to the SF MOMA free day. In general I’m not the biggest fan of art museums but I hadn’t been in a while and thought it might be fun to check out. After all, it's free. When I got there the first thing I saw were some pictures of nature which at first glance didn’t look that much more impressive than anything I could take a picture of. Upon reading the description this is apparently the border between the U.S and Mexico photographed over some time period I don’t remember. I guess it’s meant to be symbolic but even still it just felt … lacking to me. I know it's a bit of a cliche to say someone doesn’t “get art” but that was how this made me feel. Like could I just go over a single day and photograph a bunch of views in SF and put that together and it would be worthy to display in an art museum as “Views of SF”? I don’t know but it did get me wondering. Thankfully my faith in art was restored when I saw some stuff below that looked genuinely sick! CE And finally no art museum would be complete without the piece of modern art that looks like a child Is this money laundering? After the museum I wound up going to Downtown First Thursday which was livelier than I would have expected given all the rain. I wound up stopping by the Civic Joy Fund booth only to find both the people there are untangling a giant mess of disco balls which I decide to help them with. It takes us the three of us about an hour and a half to properly untangle the monstrosity fully but it was a fun community effort that I think reflects the spirit of the Civic Joy Fund Friday Overall a pretty chill day. I host a board game night in the evening with “The Taco,” “Top of the Rope,” “This little piggie didn’t go to the slaughterhouse,” “The Politician,”  “Not a matcha bitch”, and the friend of “Granola Girlie” I met at Monday MR. I realized that I play Secret Hitler a lot at board game nights so earlier in the day I bought a new boardgame called Avalon. It’s also a social deduction game which is pretty similar to Secret Hitler at its core but allows for a lot more customization and special characters which I’m hoping will give it some more shelf life. If anyone reading this has board games they like let me know! I want to have a bigger selection of games that are still somewhat involved beyond party games without being too onerous. So maybe something where a round can take something on the order of 20 minutes or so. Another game I’m heavily considering is Hanabi for this sort of thing. Saturday First trash pickup of the new year! We’re off to a rainy start this year but great to see everyone back at it. I met someone at pickup today who does competitive marching band for fun. I learned that competitive marching band is judged based on a few criteria including music, consistency, and artistic composition. Also tempo is king! A lot of inconsistencies can be masked by everyone moving at the same time. This guy did it a lot in high school and college and now he instructs highschoolers on how to do it! Also a small but potentially relevant PSA is if anyone out there is annoyed that the Contacts app on the iPhone sorts by last name rather than first name you can change that in Settings by going to the Contacts app -> Sort order -> First, Last. It may just make your Contacts easier to organize :D. We then went and helped “The Politician" pick out a birthday gift and card where we had a flyby with “The Enabler” and “Tightly Knit”. I learned that “Tightly Knit”’s sister really appreciated the bear onesie which made me happy! Sunday Today started off with trash pickup as per usual but it was also pretty rainy! “The Quant” and I hightailed it back 10 minutes early because of how bad the rain had gotten. After chilling for a while I went to a board game event over by Sports Basement. It was a lowkey but fun time. It reminded me of some of the boba buddies meetups I used to go way back in the day. Then I went home and wrote the newsletter.

title: Episode 55
excerpt: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The Pickleballer”! Monday Today I headed home to spend Christmas with my family. We take it chill and just hang around and talk which is nice. My younger sister ordered a 500 piece jig saw puzzle which she started working on. Its…
content: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The Pickleballer”! Monday Today I headed home to spend Christmas with my family. We take it chill and just hang around and talk which is nice. My younger sister ordered a 500 piece jig saw puzzle which she started working on. Its her first time ever doing a puzzle like this so I’m curious to see how it goes. Tuesday One of my best friends from college is in town so I go back to SF for the day to hang out with him. He’s a big foodie / bakerieie so we go on a tour starting from the Arsicault by Oracle Park over to Ashas for the boba, then to Al Carajo for their breakfast burrito and finally to El Gallo Giro (a Mexican food truck). While at the food truck I overheard a bunch of teenie boppers who were in the midst of a very intriguing conversation. These were the snippets I could hear. “He thought WE hooked up … He’s short and a midget … He came to class and said I hooked up with this Asian girl. … He was IN LOVE WITH ME”. Afterwards we checked out some shops in the Mission one of which had some interesting art Last week I said that if a certain TikTok “The Fisherman” made got to 350K views I would buy some wall art and based on what she’s been telling me that’s likely to happen quite soon (maybe it already has at the time of this writing) so the above could be some strong contenders. I also took my friend in a self driving car for the first time which he liked! We ended the day by going to a thrift store and then to Detour to play some games. It was really good to see him after not seeing him in over a year and I’m glad he’s kicking ass in his residency program! Wednesday Overall a pretty chill day hanging out with the family. When I have some time to myself I try to make flight school progress but really a lot of hanging around and talking and watching my sister continue to work on the puzzle. In the evening though I do take my Dad to Kogi Gogi. I mentioned last week that I should do more stuff together and this winds up being quite fun! It helped that the waiter there knows me quite well (he also bought Pokemon cards from “The Quant” which is an interesting side fact). I show my Dad all the best cuts of meat, how to cook them, and so on! What isn’t cool though is the MASSIVE RAIN which really sucks. When we get home we follow a Christmas tradition my younger sister is really into of watching Elf. It’s a perfectly fine Christmas movie. Thursday Merry Christmas! I read a description of Christmas once that basically said something to the effect of “Its the perfect time to cozy up indoors with friends and family”. Anyone who knows me should realize that the “cozy up indoors” part is something I quite detest and is a large part of why Christmas is one of my least favorite holidays of the year. The fact that the rain continued to keep us inside most of the day didn’t do any favors. Thankfully in the morning before everyone else in the family woke up I did go for a few hour walk with what little sunshine there was in the day. Part way through I decided to turn that walk into a run because I hadn’t run in over a week and needed to keep it up. Considering I was wearing 3 layers and had rocks in my shoes I’m reasonably happy with this. Once I got home it looked like my younger sister was finally about to finish the jigsaw puzzle. At this point we were all jumping in to help since we all got invested in seeing this finished. In terms of overall puzzle skills I would probably rank our family as follows Mom Younger Sister Older Sister Dad / Me I was able to fit in 4-5 pieces of the jigsaw puzzle but even with the vast majority of it completed I was still struggling. I do have to give my younger sister props for working on this for 6+ hours. Eventually the puzzle came to a close and she finished it off in dramatic fashion! I later learned that apparently “The Shadow Brigade”s mom is capable of finishing a puzzle like this in under 3 hours which boggles my mind. We hung out some more and later in the evening I watched the Jujutsu Kaisen 0 movie which is a prequel to the main Jujutsu Kaisen story. Since the final fight of the movie takes place on December 24th that means it’s a Christmas movie since if Diehard is a Christmas movie then this should be too! Friday In the morning I went for another walk which I turned into a run part way through Sadly after this the rain picked up again so the family stayed inside today. It was still a good time though. Saturday Today I headed back to SF. I went to trash pickup where we had a low of 6 people. I think this is the smallest trash pickup I’ve seen in a while but it was still fun. One of the trashers works for a  works for a pharmaceutical company called Eli lily I want to email someone from their marketing team with a slogan for their drugs “waist not want not”. I looked up the CEO on LinkedIn but it turns out I need LinkedIn premium to be able to message him. Later I’ll try to track down the email of the marketing team or something. I really think this would be a great slogan for them! I walked around for a while and wound up at the farmers market over in the Ferry building. There was one butcher that was supposedly selling pigeon meat but they were all out. Unlike dogs pigeons are actually halal in Islam so I could have made some pigeon pasta which I think would have been cool. I also had a flyby with “The Philanthropist”. Later I met up with my family in the city. We went to Compton’s for some coffee then to Union Square. Most of my family thinks Union Square is “The ghetto” which to be honest it kinda was a few years ago and as my family’s #1 SF fan I am glad to report that Union Square is no longer “The ghetto”. While we were there, a Waymo was stuck at a traffic light for over 30 minutes. I felt bad for the guy inside who couldn’t really do much about the situation.  Afterwards we went to Anatolian Table where I got to show off my trash pickup and get us a 30% discount on dinner which wound up being quite substantive. Then I parted ways with the family and went to Detour with “The Fisherman,” “The Quant,” “The Philanthropist,” “Sergeant Sassy,” her boyfriend “Trivial Pursuit,” and another trasher who doesn’t have a nickname. While there I learned that “The Philanthropist” was once a part of future farmers of America. She raised a pig which is normally supposed to go to a slaughter house but she couldn’t bear to see it go so she found it a home at an adoption shelter instead. As a result I am immediately changing her nickname to “This Little Piggie didn’t go to the slaughterhouse” because honestly “The Philanthropist” was not my best work in the nickname department. We played a bunch of games from 4 player Pacman, to Killer queen, but the surprising highlight wound up being Jenga. I never would have thought this myself considering I’m usually not that good at it but we wound up playing for quite a while and got quite good. I think a large part of that was because we shifted the goal from setting the next person up to lose to actually trying to build the tower as high as we can. When thought of as the former Jenga is perpetuating the cycle of abuse we all wrought on each other, but when thought of as the latter we’re like the CCP with a shared objective. While I don’t think we quite reached the heights of Babel I think we got pretty close! Sunday The day begins with a surprise birthday party for “The Pickleballer”! Me, “The Quant,” “The Taco,” “The Sparkle,” “Mirandom thoughts,” and of course “The Pickeballer” all go to Plow. For the bit I put my name down as Wuhan. Later when the person calling the names came for us she came up directly to us and said the name in a bit of a whisper unlike normally when they would shout it out which I thought was kinda funny. As per usual I made a custom birthday card And we got her some Tartine cookies since those are her favorites. From there we went to Game Parlor to play some games. One of the games we played was called “Bad People”. In this game there are different questions and you are supposed to vote on who is the most likely to answer yes. This is an NSFW game so questions can include things like “Who is the most likely to die in a horror movie?”, “Who is the most likely to be a dirty cop?” and other such things. I got voted unanimously for “Most likely to be committed to an insane asylum,” “Most likely to have a secret sexual fetish,” and least surprising of all, “Most likely to appear on the no fly list”. After the birthday party me and “The Quant” met up with “The Fisherman” and "This little piggie didn’t go to the slaughterhouse” to catsit as part of “The Fisherman”’s side hustle. This was a much more pleasant experience than when she was watching the dog as the cat wasn’t a yappie little shit that would pee everywhere. I’m not much of a pet person but even I could start to see the appeal of this cat.

title: Episode 54
excerpt: Monday Today I had a chat with the person whose team I would be joining at my new job. He walked me through the project I would be working on and it seemed quite exciting! He gave me a paper to read which I’ll go through during the holidays before I start. In…
content: Monday Today I had a chat with the person whose team I would be joining at my new job. He walked me through the project I would be working on and it seemed quite exciting! He gave me a paper to read which I’ll go through during the holidays before I start. In the evening I went to Mission Run Club. There I met someone who created a fan account to talk about Bojack Horseman which got big enough that she was invited to come to the studio for a shooting which I found to be pretty cool! I tried a new burrito placed in the Castro afterwards called El Castillito which had some really big but admittedly just ok burritos. I do wish they had lengua meat tho that would have elevated the burrito in my opinion. I learned that one of the guys who comes to run club regularly has a brother who opened a restaurant in France with a dish called Hamza which was funny :D. Tuesday I worked through some groundschool stuff in the morning and then in the afternoon I went poke pole fishing with “The Fisherman” over in Half Moon Bay. This was the same spot we went clamming several episodes ago but unlike then here I could focus on the good parts AKA beating fish with rocks and walking around the beach on a nice sunny day. For the first time I was actually able to catch and kill a fish entirely on my own which means I’ve grown into a level 2 fisherman. I was hoping with the level boost I would get some kind of increase in drop rate for rare fish but sadly life doesn’t seem to work that way … yet. Ultimately what I value most in fishing is being able to hang out on a nice day and chat with everything else being a bonus so by that logic this was a great trip! The last thing this fish sees There was even an extra bonus that some other people that were fishing there recognized me and “The Fisherman” from some of her TikToks! In case you're curious it’s this one! I never thought I’d actually get recognized from a TikTok video in real life considering I don’t even have a TikTok but here we are. By the way, the video above has 300k+ views. If it gets to 350K within a month then I’ll buy a decoration to hang on my walls of some sort since I’ve been told my walls are lacking in things to put on them. I’m counting on y’all to help me get my walls adorned via social pressure :D. Wednesday Aside from walking around, not much interesting happened in the early part of the day. I couldn’t muster the motivation to do anything productive. The one thing I started to notice is that I’ve become less dependent on listening to music or watching youtube videos while walking around. One of my goals is to become less dependent on constant stimulation (more of this to come in my New Years newsletter in a couple episodes) but the fact I can routinely walk for 40+ minutes with nothing but my thoughts feels like a strong step (well more like a couple thousand really) in the right direction. On my way to run club I encountered a guy in the MUNI who oddly liked my shoes and jeans and say they were much better than his “ugly ass khakis”. He was being unusually friendly towards me asking if we could hang out and go to a bar right after I met him. When I told him I had things to do he said he would even pay for my drinks which honestly raised some alarm bells. On the one hand I don’t like being aloof towards people but on the other my danger sense started to sound so I kept my distance and gave a fake name when asked. If he ever meets my twin brother Imran he may think he’s me. Thankfully he left after a couple stops though so it wasn’t that much of an issue. Also on my way there “The Filmmaker” hopped into the MUNI and we caught up and we talked more about his film and I gave some more of my thoughts based on the preview he showed me last week. I’m excited to see how it shapes up into the full movie! At the run club I saw “The Quant” and “La Tacqueria Royalty”. It had been a while since me and “La Tacquiera Royalty” talked about One Piece so it was good to catch up on the latest chapters. One weird thing though was that despite the fact we ran next to each other for most of the run Strava was giving us very different paces which makes no sense Wtf we should not have been a full min/mile apart when we were Deep in the midst talking about *that flashback* We also met someone who just ran a 100 mile Spartan race after only running for a year which was inspiring as all heck. Apparently she offers coaching now for long runs advising runners on how to pack for food, electrolytes, and so on. It makes my goal of doing an ultramarathon next year feel somehow more achievable. Wait crap do I actually need to start training for that?! My main training right now has been for sprinting up to Twin Peaks. Thursday Originally I wanted to go to Almost Friday Run Club but I came down with a bad case of not waking up in time having woken up at 7:14. I really hope they come out with a vaccine for that someday but the day is not today. I went to the post run hang in Flywheel which was still something though. I made my way through more of ground school today and later I went to meetup with “The Bartender” at Last Rites. For those unaware its a charming Tiki Bar over in The Castro with airplane seats being used for the bar seats. We hung out for a while and he told me some interesting tidbits on Brazilian history. One thing I didn’t know was that in the 19th century a lot of Syrian and other Middle Eastern immigrants came to Brazil followed by a second wave during the collapse of the Ottoman empire. Apparently Brazilians liked them because they looked “white passing” (note these were his words not mine).  As a result there is actually a reasonably large Muslim population in Brazil which I didn’t know until now. He also told me growing up that he played with both Muslim and Jewish kids playing soccer in a 3 school soccer league featuring the Muslim school, the Jewish school, and his (the Catholic school). Also interestingly Brazilians think every Muslim person there is Lebanese by default which is interesting since Lebanon has quite a sizeable non Muslim population (looking at you “The Juggler”). He also told me more about the difference between Knitting, Crocheting, and Quilting. Basically knitting is chaining fabrics linearly by knots. Crocheting is more non linear with the chaining and quilting is more about adhering things together via a loom. They are kinda like different building blocks for building similar things. I also learned that he knits and even made the sweater that he was wearing that day. I think knitting could be an interesting hobby as something to do while on the bus or just going around and I need something to keep my hands occupied. They said idle hands are the devils workshop after all and maybe my hands can be more of the angels playground instead. Later we went to the usual Thursday night bar and met with “That’s nuts” and some of the other usual Canadians. Friday Today I finally got off my butt and did something I told myself I would do for a while and message someone who works at MUNI about doing a collab with my MOONI hoodie. I sent a message to one Erica Kato head of media relations. Not sure if she will respond but I figured I may as well shoot my shot. One thing I’ve been told is that there may be some ethical qs considering the fact that I did use ChatGPT to make the actual design based on the idea that I had along with feedback steering it in the direction that I wanted. To be honest I didn’t think about it until after I messaged her and I still lean on the side of it being OK but there could be a chance I made a mistake and should have only kept it to me + friends considering I did use AI but I guess we shall see. Later I attended the holiday party of the company I’ll be joining at the start of the new year. For the party we went to a fancy restaurant called “The Progress” which is normally way out of the Humza budget but considering the company is paying for it it’s suddenly ok! It was slightly awkward at first since I showed up in my MOONI hoodie only for everyone else to be dressed relatively nicely (collared shirts and so on). Nobody told me there was a dress code 😓. I assumed since it was SF most everyone would just be wearing casual stuff so I felt slightly out of place at first but its not like I could suddenly go and change so f it we ball. The party itself was great. All the people I talked to were super nice and I could definitely see myself being excited to come into work every day to hang out with them which is a good sign culture wise. I also got the chance to validate a long standing theory of mine that fancy food isn’t really that much better than normally priced food. Despite being really fancy I can’t say I was overly impressed by the food I had. We had a 4 course menu that looked something like the below I guess the waiters there were very attentive and the aesthestics of the room were nice and all but to be honest most of the courses were ok except for the beef which was actually pretty good but not better than most other beef I get. Like I’d put it maybe slightly above my lamb pasta. One thing I did learn that was interesting was the idea of grilling some meat and having a passion fruit based thing you dip it into to combine the meat with a sweet flavor which actually did work pretty well I think. I’m sure these platings would look impressive if I cared at all about aesthetics After we toasted to the end of the year and how excited we were for the next, the party wrapped up and I went to The Marina for “The Politician’s” final bar crawl of the year. There I was joined by “The Fisherman,” “Not a matcha bitch,” and “The Notetaker”. We started off at Bar Darling which was a pretty good place for the bar crawl. It had plenty of space for us and we had a good time chatting. Out of the corner of my eye I saw a girl who I saw on Hinge a couple times and has been to Midnight Runners before. We’re definitely not a match based on her profile so I wasn’t really interested but I thought I’d point it out. Bar Darling was a great time for talking with people and catching up with some of “The Politician’s” friends who I only see at these bar crawls! Afterwards we went to Westwood where I rode a mechanical bull for all of 17 seconds. One thing I learned from “The Fisherman” who lasted 44 seconds was that you need to hold the bull with your legs so you stay on. In retrospect I should have remembered that from when I rode an actual horse with “The Shadow Brigade” but here we are. Sadly after that I think I started to get overstimulated at Westwood. One thing I’ve come to realize is that I’m not really that much of a club person after a while as all the people, music, and everything gets to be too much for me. I suspect this is an area where having alcohol would actually help me to be able to handle it all but since that isn’t an option I think I may need to skip the clubs and come more for the earlier parts of these bar crawls. A good rule of thumb I think is that how good a time I can have strongly correlates to how well I can have a conversation. Put another way fellow Jujutsu Kaisen fans may understand is that being in the club after a while felt like I was being hit by Gojo’s Infinite Void domain expansion as so much sensory information was flowing into me that I felt overwhelmed. Sadly I couldn’t counter with my own domain or use a domain protection technique like simple domain since I am sadly not a fictional character from the JJK verse. At one point I was standing around while the DJ was playing “Not like Us” and some woman came up and started dancing near me and expected me to start dancing with her but sadly I was really overwhelmed at that point so I basically just looked her in the eye and said “No thanks”. I do feel a bit bad about this in retrospect though. Eventually I head out roughly half an hour after I already should have but better late than never. Ultimately I still had a good time overall and I am definitely glad that I came, it was great to see everyone! Saturday The day begins with the usual trash pickup. Due to the bad weather and people being out of town we definitely see lower than usual numbers but its still a good time regardless. Afterwards, “The Quant,” “The Plower,” and I got brunch over at Plow. I learned the tea there is actually pretty good which means I don’t have to go there and get literally nothing. I can go there and get $5 worth of stuff instead. From there me and “The Quant” went to play badminton over in South SF. He’s a lot better than I was but over the course of our play time I think I leveled up to the point where I could get a few points in on him per game and not be a total pushover. I quite like badminton so this was definitely a lot of fun! At point he thought I looked “tired” which sure as hell motivated me to keep playing 😈. By the time I got back to SF proper I learned there was a huge blackout that affected a lot of the city. My neighborhood was among those affected meaning my apartment and everything around it had no power. A bunch of grocery stores were closed, all the lights were off and everything was dark. Thankfully I wasn’t super impacted as I could just hole up and hotspot and more or less chill just like normal except in the dark. Apparently a bunch of Waymos got stuck causing huge traffic jams which is kinda funny. After about 4 hours my neighborhood got power back and the first thing I said was “Fiat Lux”! For those who don't know, that’s the Berkeley motto which means “Let there be light”! I am grateful the outage only lasted a few hours for me considering other neighborhoods like The Richmond fared much worse. Sunday Today we had the smallest Sunday trash pickup in history with only 22 people showing up. The holidays really did a number here but the people I did meet there were great! I met a high school German exchange student who is wrapping up next week. She had come for about 5 months from a small town of 20K people about 3 hours away from Berlin. She really liked it here which I’m glad for! Apparently the part that surprised her the most was how friendly the relationship can be between students and teachers. At her exchange school (Mission High school) the precalc teacher is super friendly and best friends with a bunch of her students. On the other hand she described German teachers as having a much more professional relationship with their students which definitely sounds less fun by comparison. I also met a couple people who work at an electric plane company where they are designing an electric airplane and trying to get FAA approval to sell it. Who knows, maybe once I get my pilots license I could try flying it. They currently have test pilots but they are all people with 20+ years of experience who have flown F16s. Afterwards I had a group call with “The Professor,” “The Taco,” “The Game Master,” “The Sparkle,” and  “The K-pop dancer” to catch up. “The Professor” has been thriving in Vienna which we love to see! I got home and kinda just chilled. Later I had a call with my Mom who told me I should do more father son things with my dad. To be honest we don’t really do a whole lot 1:1 and she said it would mean a lot if we did and since I’m now an adult I should be more proactive in driving and initiating these things. To be honest she is right and it hadn’t really crossed my mind to seek this out in particular. While he would never ask for it she said it would mean a lot to him. I suspect that it's because growing up there was never really a hobby we both did that we could keep doing together but no better time than the present to start changing that. I thought for a bit about what kind of things make sense. He’s not as active as I am and can’t really run, somehow I don't think he would be that into trash pickup, and then it hit me! KBBQ! I called and suggested we go to Kogi Gogi and walk around in GGP and he was quite excited! This could become a good father son ritual for us! On a more serious note, I have heard that people regret not spending time with their parents and such when they are around my age and regardless of past circumstances I’m the one who can choose to change things now. From there I wrote up the newsletter!

title: Episode 53
excerpt: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “Mr. Green Flag!” You’re a really great friend and I appreciate your thoughtfulness and your flair! Hope your travels are really fun and looking forward to hearing your leveled up Chinese when you come back Monday The weather was n…
content: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “Mr. Green Flag!” You’re a really great friend and I appreciate your thoughtfulness and your flair! Hope your travels are really fun and looking forward to hearing your leveled up Chinese when you come back Monday The weather was nice so I mainly drove the lambrofeeti around today in the morning before going to Mission Run Club with “The Raja of Rhythm” in the evening. Thankfully unlike the last few weeks I went there weren’t any hills which I greatly appreciated. Even better despite running ahead of the pack I did not in fact trip and twist my foot in the dark. I am ON IT. After the run club we went to Fort Point for a beer. I learned that the bathrooms in Fort Point have an audio track playing facts about marine animals which I found to be a really fun and unique touch. I really wish more restrooms played animal facts or something fun. I’d like one that plays one of my favorite One Piece youtubers but I don’t think that would be quite as popular. One of the people I met at run club today is a consultant from Deloitte working with Anthropic on financing their planned 2027 IPO which was pretty interesting Tuesday I started off with some flight school where I’m now about a quarter of the way through the lectures. To be honest my slow pace is largely because I somehow find it hard to get through lectures despite being interested in the end goal of flying the plane. I’m hoping it will get more interesting once I get to that part. In the evening I go on a long walk with “The Philosopher”. We have a tradition now where if one of us gets laid off the other will buy a burrito at the time of it happening and once a new job is obtained so I cashed in on the latter to get the finest burrito El Rancho Grande had to offer. On the walk he asked me an interesting question “What are your goals / what do you want?”. I’m actually going to delay what I said here because I think it fits more into things I’ll be talking about tomorrow. The walk itself was great with a bunch of usual bullshit being exchanged. Nothing else too notable for the newsletter but I just really appreciate any sort of long walk where I can just talk with people about whatever. It truly is one of life's greatest pleasures. Along the way we ran into one of his other friends who was going on a different walk around the Ferry Building. Wednesday Today I wanted to try taking a Judo class. I’ve done a bunch of Krav Maga in the past but never Judo and I hear its pretty popular around here so I found a place offering a free lesson and decide to head over. The Judo instructor looks really intense given his eye patch, man bun , and gauze around his leg. Kinda like this Upon talking with the guy he actually wound up being super nice and friendly so maybe a bit more like this It turns out by accident I wound up signing up for an advanced class rather than the intro I thought I was so I couldn’t exactly participate in the class. Thankfully the instructor was nice and gave me some training on the side for a while in fundamentals. I learned the Judo stance which is a little bit different from Krav Maga. Interestingly you want to keep one of your hands close to your face and the other far out from you unlike in Krav where you may keep both medium far from you. In the evening I went to another “pitch my friend” dating event where this time “The Fisherman” pitched me with “The Quant,” “The Taco,” and “The Philanthropist” coming for support. The pitch was great! “The Fisherman” did an awesome job selling me! She even brought the plushie I got her for her birthday to show how thoughtful I am :D. The pitch got a lot of laughs and applause. To paraphrase some of her words the pitch was actually written by a woman who understands what women want as opposed to being written by a straight guy writing what he thinks is funny. Afterwards I met some interesting people but nothing that ultimately went anywhere. I spent a while talking with this one girl and a guy who I can tell was also trying to talk to her. To be honest the social dynamics of this sort of situation feel a little bit odd to me. On the one hand I suppose in terms of results I’m mainly trying to get to know this girl and see if I can get her number and try to get a date with her. On the other hand, it feels like I have to play a weird sort of dance where this guy and I are both talking to each other and trying to get to know this girl in a way that … I don’t know if it entirely makes sense. Maybe this is just not something I’m used to or anything but it doesn’t quite feel right to me. Perhaps I’m overthinking this. It also didn’t help that I made my usual terrorist joke which I could tell the woman wasn’t interested in. After debriefing later with “The Fisherman” who watched that exchange she gave me some good advice that I should not use that joke right away because women are especially tuned to avoid unsafe situations and anything that could come off as weird or uncomfortable may fit in with that. In other words I shouldn't use it when she is still trying to get a base read on me to determine if I’m a safe person, instead using that on a second or third date. Towards the end I could kinda tell she liked the other guy more but nonetheless I still got her number and asked her out. Perhaps predictably she never responded but ah well. Remember earlier when “The Philosopher" asked me “What are your goals / what do you want”? At this point in my life I have a lot of the things I really want like hobbies, friends, a good job, and an overall sense of satisfaction. One of the few things I don’t have though is a path to finding someone and getting married and potentially starting a family. At this point I’d call myself open to kids but not 100% sure. Nevertheless it does feel like this is one of the few areas in my life where I’ve had relatively little success really finding what I’m looking for. In almost every other area of my life I feel incredibly fortunate to say that I’m quite satisfied with what I have. I’m sure I’ll get there with this too but not quite yet. On the plus side I met a guy who does psychedelics research at UCSF which was pretty cool. He told me a little bit about the medicinal impact of shrooms but sadly I don’t remember any cool findings :(. I do want to hit him up though he seems like someone I could be friends with if nothing else. Thursday I did a Krav Maga class today which was quite fun! Unlike the Judo class I was definitely in my element here and since I’ve gone before I made sure to sign up for the right class. This class was a whole lot of striking from straight punches, to hooks to uppercuts. My worst of these was definitely the hook which also explains why my intro sections for each day of the newsletter are so cut and dry :D. I was better at uppercuts than I thought I would be and now I think  I’m ready to knock some chins up. Later I went to a flying trapeze class at the Circus Center. I had done this way before in the pre newsletter days of 2023 but sadly I never figured out how to hang upside down on the trapeze. Lets see if anything changed this time. For context the whole idea of a Flying Trapeeze is you swing on a trapeze and you do tricks kinda like this Unlike most hobbies I partake in, this one was mostly girls with me being the only guy in class. There were 5 women and me here. The class basically consists of us lining up to go on the trapeze and attempting whatever we’re taught. It starts by learning to hang upside down, and then you do learn to do a flip as you fall from the trapeze, and finally you swing from the trapeze into the arms of someone else. Well before any of that you have to climb the ladder up to the top where you get onto the first trapeze. I found this to be pretty scary, especially the first couple times. Thankfully unlike with urchin foraging I conquered my fears and climbed up the ladder and was able to start swinging. Sadly this is where my successes ended as I was unable to hang upside down even once. Everyone else in the class got it on their first try while I couldn’t do it on any of my 5+ attempts. Every time I tried I couldn’t quite get both my legs over to actually hang onto the trapeze. The best I could get was one with the other awkwardly dangling close to it. Between my failures and the rope burn I was getting on my hands I took a break for 20 minutes because I found myself running out of motivation. One of the students in the class was super nice and kept encouraging me to try again saying I was doing great. Considering how much better everyone else was doing I was impressed she could say that with a straight face but I nevertheless found it encouraging and tried again. I still failed but I’m glad I tried. I think I’ll go again next week to see if I can get it. Afterwards I went to “The Philosopher’s” Christmas party. The usual Canadian suspects including “The Juggler,” “That’s nuts,” and “The Mosher” were there along with a bunch of other folks. Since I got there first I won the “un lottery” as “The Philosopher" put it to be the doorman which means I got my steps in which was good. “The Juggler” told me a lot about the drone delivery problems he was working on Zipline which I found super interesting. Then “That’s nuts” nerdsniped me with an interview question she got from a friend. The question setup is given an n x n matrix containing the natural numbers 1 through n^2 sequentially in order, prove that if you chose 1 number from each row and column and sum them up you get some closed form formula. It was actually a pretty interesting problem but my brain was a bit overclocked at this point and I don’t think I made meaningful progress on it. The key idea I focused on was trying to prove that no matter how you do it the result will be the same. Lets look at the example where n = 3 and we have a 3 x 3 matrix 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 Suppose we pick along the diagonals and do (1, 5, 9). Then you get the sum is 15. Now suppose I want to change things up and instead of doing 1 from the first row I do 2 instead. In this case since we can’t do 5 since its in the same column as 2 we have to pick 4 or 6. If we pick 4 then we can still do 9 as in the first case. This also sums to 15. Actually proving that its the same requires some bashy math which my 11pm brain didn't quite have the capacity for expanding out polynomial bashes. She did solve it though by the end which was great. Interestingly she told me the last time she got an interview question from a friend like this she wound up getting the same question in an interview later so if it happens again she will definitely be prepared. Friday As soon as I got out of the house I tried to do a sprint with 132ft of elevation gain up to Tank Hill. Despite it only being 0.23 miles I felt like I was dying going full pace for that long with a 13% grade. I think my time was around just under 9min/mile pace which isn’t too bad but still not quite my goal. Ideally if I could run all the way up to Twin Peaks at 8 min/mile then that would be awesome. But progress is encouraging! Later in the day I hosted board games with “The Raja of Rhythm,” “The Quant,” “Mr. Greenflag,” one of his old college roommates, “The Sparkle,” and “The Pickleballer”. For whatever reason when we play Secret Hitler I tend to get fascist which led “The Raja of Rhythm” and “The Quant” to suspect I rigged it which I definitely did not do :D. We all know I’m an honest lad that would never rig the game. Thankfully when “The Quant” handed out the roles and I got fascist I managed to beat the allegations. Sadly though I made one of the funnier blunders anyone has ever made in the game where I accidentally said “If Hitler is elected as chancellor we win” rather than “If Hitler is elected as chancellor the fascists win” which I meant to say. Thankfully we still won but my god that was kinda hilarious. Saturday The day begins with trash pickup as per usual. Sadly the post trash hang goes longer than I’d have liked and I sprint to make it to a joint birthday party for  “Mr. Greenflag” and another friend from the Hopkins crew. I manage to keep at a 6:45 min/mile pace for 0.33 miles which isn’t too bad and gives me hope I can do that for a full mile and finally break below 7 min as my best these days seems to be around 7:28. The birthday party had a fun theme which was to dress for the wrong event! I wore a hazmat suit I got off of Amazon which was fun but I do wish it had pockets. I had to carry my fanny pack around with me instead which opened my eyes to what it's like to have clothing without big pockets. I made him this custom card It features a bunch of his favorite things: His favorite national flag (Seychelles), a bowl of soup, and a leather jacket! While there I met someone who told me there is a kind of fish that is blind and learned to walk on walls. It’s called the Waterfall-Climbing Cavefish (Cryptotora thamicola). Afterwards I met up with “The Historian” and we got KBBQ at a place in Oakland called Ohgane which taste wise is even better than Kogi Gogi but at the price of being a lot further as it’s out in Oakland. Funnily enough he’s the first person I ever got KBBQ with and the one who got me into it. We walked around in Rockridge and SF for a while seeing a fair number of Santas along the way for Santacon. Along the way he regaled me with SF history about the dockworkers and the places they would frequent along The Embarcadero that are still there today like Red’s Java house. We tried going in to see if we could get a beer old dock worker style but sadly they were closed for private events. Boo corporate Christmas parties! Sunday Today starts off with the usual trash pickup. Afterwards one of my friends has a Christmas party so I go and catch up with “The Quant,” “The Game Master," “The Mushroom Hunter," and “The Sparkle”. They really pulled out all the stops for this party including renting out a house to fit all 70 people, hiring some folks off Craigslist to help out, and having cookie and ornament decorating. Here are some decorated cookies, want to guess which one was mine? During the party we were told there would be an ugly sweater contest and the winner would get a lap dance from Mrs. Claus. I assumed that was one of the friends who was dressed up as Mrs. Claus only to learn later that they hired a stripper for this. The winners ended up being a pair of friends who wore matching light up Christmas sweaters and I have to admit the lap dance was truly a sight to behold I don’t usually try to represent actual anatomy in these doodles But I think its warranted in this case Afterwards the host gave a heartwarming speech thanking us all for coming and celebrating the 1 year anniversary with his boyfriend which was touching. From there I went to a second Christmas party hosted by “The Filmmaker” featuring “The Raja of Rhythm,” and “Mr. Socksessful” where we played board games, watched a preview of his upcoming movie, and did Karaoke. He has his own karaoke machine which is pretty cool! Low key I kinda want one now because I think doing karaoke at home could be really fun and then I can show even more people Rap God! I wanted to write the newsletter when I got back but sadly I was tired and decided to go to bed.

content: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Announcement This is the 1 year anniversary of trash tales! Hard to believe I’ve been writing this for 52 weeks now! Attached with this newsletter is my attempt at a one year anniversary special. Stay tuned after the regularly scheduled content Monday Today I had two interviews. One of which was with a company I was really interested in technically and thought could be a really strong fit. Sadly though I underperformed in this interview and mind kinda froze for a while which really sucked. Interestingly though after the interview I was able to solve the problem within like 5 minutes a fact of which I told them about in the slim hopes it would change things. Naturally it didn’t but you miss 100% of the shots you don’t take right? Afterwards I had another interview with “The Raja of Rhythm’s” company. The interviewer was one of the nicest interviewers I ever had. He was super cool and really enthusiastic! I got through the question quite easily and we talked for a while about MUNI since he noticed my MUNI sweater :D. Small shoutout to David for being such an awesome interviewer. After a bit more walking around I met up with “The Shadow Brigade”. We walked around some more and made another attempt to go to Haru by Sam’s only to learn its closed on Monday :(. Tuesday I was inspired by “La Tacqueria Royalty” on Strava and decided to do a run up to Tank Hill from the Humza cave. I have a goal of being able to run up to Twin Peaks at about an 8 minute pace which sadly I am still far from but I guess being able to go up that kind of elevation at just over 9 isn’t objectively bad in and of itself. Later in the day I got a formal offer from the company I did an onsite with a few weeks ago! To be honest the package looked quite compelling in and of itself but at the moment I told the co founder who gave me the offer I wanted to interview with other companies first and get back later which she was very understanding about! From there I go to Fatboys run club over in GGP and run for a few miles where I learn a very crucial life lesson. Specifically, never eat 3 burgers an hour before running. During the last part of the run my stomach was really hurting so I had to stop early :(. Afterwards I go to The Detour for the weekly game night with “The Writer”. We play a really interesting game called The White Castle which is basically a game about managing resources, moving Samurai and a few other things with a feudal Japanese aesthetic. Wednesday Today was all about foraging for urchins. “The Fisherman” took me and “The Shadow Brigade” up North to forage for urchins. Way back in episode 3 I went for the first time to this spot and tried foraging for all of 5 minutes or so before my feet got wet and I gave up. But not this time! This time I brought rain boots and I was ready to rumble! Well for all of like 20 minutes anyway. On this trip I made a discovery about myself that I have a real fear of losing my balance, slipping, and falling on rocks. While the rain boots did help my feet to not get wet they did unfortunately make moving around harder and I didn’t have as much tactile sensation in my feet which made me uneasy. Unlike the other two who took to it like a fish (urchin?) to water, I took to it more like a software engineer to water, that is to say I short circuited. Unlike last time I did actually do some foraging and grabbed around 20 urchins before heading back. Thankfully it was a nice day on the beach so I did some impromptu dance choreo and hill repeats. In order to get to the beach you have to go down a hill so I figured I’d run up and down the hill in order to level up my speed. Sadly the best pace I got was just around 8 min/mile when I was really hoping for something more like 7:30 min/mile. Like many things related to foraging for urchins here it did not go my way. When they were coming back over the rocks with the buckets full of urchin “The Fisherman” asked me to take one of the buckets back to the beach and what followed was a good 2 minutes of me freaking out while slipping a bit with the bucket being really panicked about trying to make it back. On my way back I stubbed my foot against a rock and hurt my hand a bit. Not a lot but it didn’t exactly put me in the best headspace either. “The Fisherman” asked if she should take the bucket back but I figured I should do at least something on this trip and not be a totally limp noodle so I persisted and earned the rank of only a mostly limp noodle. After collecting urchins we went back to “The Fisherman”’s place to cook and prepare the urchins for dinner with the help of “The Fisherman”’s mom. I guess this is where I shined (relatively speaking) because unlike “The Shadow Brigade” I had no qualms with killing urchins. While it wasn’t as much fun as the time I beat an eel with a rock there was still something satisfying about cutting them open and taking out the gonads that we ate :D. Sadly the satisfaction did not extend to the taste. As someone who generally doesn’t like seafood it shouldn’t be too surprising  that I didn’t really care for the urchins or the mussels. When “The Fisherman”’s mom asked me why I wasn’t eating more I tried to politely say it was because I was already full but somehow I don’t think she really bought it when I only ate about 3 bites total.
