Also to continue the streak of me really messing up today I fumbled with the chopsticks I was using to eat the uni pasta. “The Fisherman”’s mom asked if I needed help and while I said no the next minute of me fumbling caused her to override said answer and just get me a fork. I could feel her judgement on my soul which “The Fisherman” did later confirm. Although apparently she also found it funny so oh well I guess. As it turns out I’ll be coming back here on Saturday because a Muslim girl “The Fisherman” knows who is interested in doing this so “The Fisherman” set up another trip so we could meet which I quite appreciate. This time I’m going to use “The Fisherman”s helmet to alleviate my fears of falling. Thursday The first thing I do today is change my mind about interviewing with other places and accept the offer I got! I realized I was already really into this place anyway and my Dad gave me some good advice that while keeping options is good it’s also important to trust my gut. So I did! Huge thanks to “The Raja of Rhythm” and everyone else who gave me referrals and provided help throughout the process whether it was the offer of a referral, taking me out to Kogi Gogi, or just being a good friend! With this I’m now finally done with job interviewing and will be starting my new role at the beginning of next year! I’m a little bit nervous but quite excited too! I go to Downtown First Thursday with “The Fisherman” and “The Shadow Brigade” where we check out a men’s choir that is almost certainly gay. Afterwards me and “The Shadow Brigade” head over to Haru by Sam’s and I finally get to show her where I spend my Thursdays with the gaggle of Canadians. We hang out with “The Philosopher,” “The Bartender,” “That’s nuts” and “The Mosher”. A pretty solid time as per usual with a slightly amusing incident where “The Shadow Brigade” assumed that the person who runs Haru by Sam’s is “The Bartender” from the newsletter when they are in fact different people :P. Sadly “The Shadow Brigade” had to leave before she could meet “The Mosher” as I think they would have hit it off as they both do space related stuff for either a work or hobby. Friday Today I head over to Berkeley to go see two of my friends from college give their Ph.D dissertations. As it happened both of them were on the same day! One of these friends reached out and asked if I was attending either over Zoom or in person and since I’m still in the unemployed arc I said I would love to come in person. I reached out to the other who said she was finishing around now and lo and behold same day! What great timing! Dissertation 1 (Packing up them genes) The first dissertation I went to was from my old college floormate who is graduating with a Ph.D in microbiology. For her Ph.D she studied proteins that pack genes. One thing I really appreciated about this talk was that she started by giving a high level overview of the concept for people without a background in Biology. She likened packing genes to intelligently putting spools in a basket by first wrapping them up and then putting them all as opposed to just chucking all the spools in the basket. Personally, this talk took me back to my childhood as I imagined myself packing a suitcase by chucking clothes in and my mom telling me to neatly fold them so you can put more clothes in. The talk itself ran for about 40 minutes with 20 minutes worth of questions. I kinda wanted to ask some questions too but considering the caliber of questions being asked I figured it was best to not ask my rudimentary level questions like “Can you explain those last 5 slides again?”. After the talk we went to go get lunch at Mendocino farms and I caught up with her some more on her research and the different things she’s doing now. Now I have a couple hours before the next dissertation so I walk around the campus for a while and chill in Memorial Glade for a while where I wind up overhearding a surprisingly morbid conversation about a girl whose mom died when she was 13 and her sister attracting bad men. Since they didn’t realize I was listening there's a part of me that feels like I should have found a different spot to sit but I’ll admit I couldn’t help myself here Dissertation 2 (Models + Application layer) After that I head to the next dissertation that a friend of mine from an ML club I was in in college did. Unlike the last dissertation I could actually understand this one pretty well. And good thing too because unlike the last one he didn’t really try to add intro level analogies for people who weren’t already familiar. This dissertation largely centers around combining pretrained models with applications like Cursor, Lovable etc. for domain specific models for maximal performance. Sadly unlike the last dissertation there were only 5 of us in person with most people (including this guy's Ph.D advisor) remote on a Zoom call. Granted this was the week of a major ML conference but still the contrast felt pretty stark. This talk also lasted about 40 minutes but there weren’t really many questions afterwards. It seems in CS there isn’t really a culture of asking questions. From there me, the guy giving the dissertation, and a couple of our other friends walked around Berkeley a bit more. I went back to SF to meet up with “The Shadow Brigade” at a pasta restaurant which she was very interested in taking pictures and videos of for her Nudge which if you aren’t familiar with is an app where people put up videos of fun activities to do and she is something of an influencer on. I get some olives at the restaurant and they wind up being worse than I thought but that's fine because the vibes were good. Originally our plan afterwards was to go to a comedy show but it turns out the venue accidentally double booked so the show got cancelled. “The Shadow Brigade” decided to slink back into the shadows and I met up with “The Fisherman,” “The Trash Queen,” and “The Rugby Player” at “The Trash Queen’s” apartment and we hung out and talked for a while which was great. I learned that the Muzzie girl may not be able to come on the foraging trip which I was both disappointed and relieved by. The relief came from the fact that to be honest I’m not really that keen on going foraging again since as I mentioned I didn’t really enjoy the experience and it is a 2+ hour drive each way so it’s not really my thing. Saturday As I leave the Humza cave I learn that someone else cancelled on the fishing trip which really sucked. For a bit of context it is a 2+ hour drive each way and there are few enough people that one of the drivers (either “The Fisherman” or “The Quant”) would have to drive alone which is quite annoying. I figured since “The Fisherman” did initially set this up in part to help me meet this Muzzie girl I should go anyway to boost the numbers so nobody has to drive alone. To be clear I don’t dislike fishing in general or even the concept of urchin hunting. It's just that particular spot which combines a long drive with fear inducing rock climbing that leads me to classify it as a spot of horrors. Before I get into what that entails today at trash pickup we wound up having the largest in Saturday trash pickup history because by chance both a local girl scout troop and a local Questbridge alumni network along with a bunch of regulars for a record breaking 77 people in attendance. Afterwards me and “The Quant” go to Plow to meet up with “The Taco” and “The Kpop dancer” and get on a call with “The Professor” to catch up on how his life in Vienna is going. There are other cameos including “The Sparkle,” “Mirandom thoughts,” “The Mushroom hunter,” “The attorney,” and someone else I don’t know well enough to have a newsletter nickname for them. It was nice to catch up with a lot of the meetup gang and see what kinds of cool and interesting stuff they’re up to. From there me and “The Quant” head off to urchin hunting land. While little miss muzzie wasn’t there it turns out that one of the people that “The Fisherman” met off of tiktok is actually a coworker of “The Raja of Rhythm” (it was Justin btw).  Unlike last time I made no attempt to go out on the rocks since I don’t really have intrinsic interest, it's darker which adds a whole new complexity, and most importantly there are no girls I want to impress. So instead I decide to sit on the beach and see how long I can last without any external stimulation like music or phone which winds up being an hour and a half which I guess is something in its own right. I was also supposed to guard “The Quant”s In-N-Out with my life but due to the bag getting wet the burger fell in the sand :(. Once the urchin gang returns we help a bit with cleaning urchins and dumping seawater on them. While doing this someone using one of the spigots at the place sprays me a bit with water and I make a growling sound. It wasn’t a lot of water but it gave off vibes that this place really doesn’t like me which is why I growled in a bit of resentment. Sigh. I don’t have much luck at this place. It’s going on the list for things that annoy me which are as follows Settlers of Catan Hadestown the musical This particular foraging ground for urchins Originally as this was happening I was looking forward to going on a long hyperbolic tirade about this place for the comedic value but now I’m just like well hopefully I never have to come back here. I’m definitely down for a wide variety of other fishing things that are both closer and less rocky but I really don’t want to come back here :( and it seems this place doesn’t want me back either. I’m down to be mutual enemies and hate this place if that's what it wants. Also I know “The Quant” really wanted to go on more fishing excursions so I am glad he came here and liked it at least. “The Fisherman” and a bunch of other folks stay to camp overnight while me, “The Quant” and someone reading this who I really should have a nickname for but don’t at the moment drove back. On the way “The Quant” doubted my left handedness which wasn’t helped by the fact that I can only snap with my right hand despite me writing with my right. Sunday Nothing like a good ol Sunday morning trash pickup to soothe the soul after going to that urchin spot. I pick up trash with “The Raja of Rhythm” and a bunch of other people for a while which was exactly what the doctor ordered. Afterwards I get brunch with “The Enabler,” “Tight Knit,” and “La Tacqueria Royalty” over at Kitchen Story where surprisingly enough I actually ate. It was great catching up with them and I tried an interesting combination of grapefruit, ketchup, and tabasco which I highly recommend you all try. From there I head home and write up the newsletter. Anniversary special Normally the above would be all there is to it and I’d send it out. But we’re doing things a little differently today. I knew I wanted to do something to commemorate 1 year of me doing this. For a while I was thinking about what it would be and I decided on a two parter. Part 1 I figured I’d start by answering a question nobody really asked but feels spiritually fitting which is “What’s been the most unexpected thing about writing a weekly newsletter?” Good question, thanks for asking! I think the answer would have to be how much I think about the newsletter throughout the week when I think about events as they are happening. I’ll have thoughts like “Oh the readers will like this!” Or “Man this is gonna suck to write about.” I’ll also go through drafts in my head as something is happening in real time. I definitely wouldn’t have expected that at the start but now that the newsletter has become a weekly staple I now find it all but inevitable. Part 2 I want to take a moment to really thank all of you for being part of this with me. Originally when I started this I certainly wouldn’t have expected that people would actually enjoy this or that I would keep it up consistently for a whole year. And to be honest without all of you engaging with it in some way shape or form I probably would have stopped long ago. I’ve mentioned a couple times throughout this newsletter how important y’all are to me and to show that I thought I would do something interesting and go through every character in the character list and share my favorite memory with ya over the last year. It just felt like a fitting thing to do so why not right? “The Professor” Interestingly enough I think you moving away really pushed me to try to come up with unique things I could do to celebrate ya like getting Garden Creamery to bring back the Mugicha or the surprise party. But I think my favorite would have to be when I showed up at your apartment in Vienna and surprised ya! That might just take the cake for best bit I ever committed to! “The Quant” I consider you my left hand (yes I am left handed goddammit and the next time I have a pen and paper I’ll prove it to ya) for how down you are to always do a bunch of random shit with me. Sadly that makes it hard to nail down one particular memory but perhaps the one I’ll go with is the time we went from Crissy Field to Engagement Hill. It was a really good walk! “The Taco” Your birthday over at Terra Mia was pretty cool. It’s not often I make ceramics stuff so it was a nice change of pace. Of course I still haven’t picked up the dogshit thing I glazed but thats besides the point “The Plower” I was really touched by the unique gifts you came up with for my birthday! The Will commit to the bit shirt is one of, if not my favorite shirt. And the funko pop is hilarious! It really fits what I value in a gift of being something unique that you can only get by really getting to know someone. It’s awesome just like you! “The Driver” Definitely that one time when were in Lyon and we went to that cafe before everyone else woke up. Only time we talked 1:1 and reminded me how cool you are! “High Entropy” I liked the time a couple months ago we hung out with “The Taco” and “The attorney” and got poke. Its not often ya tell me so much about yourself considering how quiet you usually are :D “The Kpop dancer” That time when I surprised everyone that you were coming back to the Bay for “The Plower’s” birthday was awesome. It was really funny seeing everyone's look when you showed up. Sadly when you came back recently you let the entire group chat know which was a rookie mistake really. Next time just let me know and we can run the good shit back. “The Game master” There was one time when I finally beat you in a game of Dune Imperium with both expansion packs. Its the one and only time I ever beat you in that dang game and I will hold onto that despite what the overall win loss ratio says :P “The Pickleballer” I remember when we went to that ping pong place over by The Fillmore and played ping pong. One of these days I’ll beat ya. “The Notetaker” and “Mr. Greenflag” You guys get a bit of a dual memory as I remember the time when you both came to my powerpoint party and since you both made powerpoints about flags you guys were able to present each others perfectly. It was amazing! “The Politician” The north beach bar crawl that you hosted was really good! Tivolis wound up being the perfect bar for a bar crawl and it singlehandedly boosted my opinion of the North Beach bar scene which before I mainly associated with strip clubs. “Not a matcha bitch”: I really liked going to the manga museum with you!! It was super cool and the discount you got us certainly didn’t hurt either ;). “The Fisherman” Definitely the urchin foraging :D. Sike! I really appreciate all the fishing trips we went on since we were both free during the day. Perhaps my favorite was the one where we went to The Presidio and then got dinner and stuff for your birthday party. It felt like the perfect mix of random stuff and talking about the efficacy of protesting. Your birthday party was also pretty awesome! “The Hombre” I’m really glad we met up that one time the day I learned “The Climber” died. I definitely needed someone to talk to around then and it was also the last time I saw ya before you moved to the U.K. Hope that's going well by the way! “The Climber” You didn’t think you were getting out of this by dying on me did ya? I really liked the time you, me, “La Tacquiera Royalty,” and  “Sergeant Sassy” went to that Portuguese restaurant after Midnight Runners and the two of us went on that long improv skit about being co-parents of a duck. And of course we all debated the very important question of would you risk drinking titty milk if the choices were between a rich supple person and someone from the Tenderloin with 50:50 odds or would you not drink it at all? Unexplored but very important territory! “Sergant Sassy” I remember when I first met ya and we were all deliberating over what texts you should send to that guy that you liked. The whole exchange was as funny as it was satisfying when he said he was down for a date! And I still really like the trivial pursuit joke I made since you guys had earlier gone to trivia together which may or may not have been a date depending on who you asked :P “The Shadow Brigade” That 35 mile walk we did was pretty legendary not gonna lie. 14 hours is the longest I’ve ever walked with someone so that's one for the history books. And it was really funny when we went down that slide despite having no child supervision :D. “The Raja of Rhythm” I remember that one time after yoga when we talked for a while and you helped me when I was feeling really down after the fight I got into with my sister. You’re a real one man! A close second would be your birthday party where I brought Franklin the air purifier and got to use him both for sitting and for purifying the air :D. “The Ghostbuster” Definitely the time when we went to Señor Sisig and we talked about that one place in Rhode Island which from what you described may or may not have been haunted. “Always Causing a Racquet” I’m glad there was the one Thursday bar night that coincided with your birthday. It was a lovely time! “The Slosher” I think the time when we were both fighting on that Google form to see who would be the chicken at your birthday party was awesome. It is a little too bad that you cheated to win by pushing back the vote time but it was fun nonetheless. And in everyone's hearts we know I won. “The Filmmaker” True to your name, getting to be an extra in your film was quite fun! I never did a film while in a MUNI before and it was pretty cool dancing around. It was also really funny that one take we did when the MUNI jolted and I wound up veering onto the stairway. Oh and when those old people were staring at us like “What the heck are the youth these days doing?” “John Wick” I think the time when you got really into karaoke at my birthday party was stupendous. You were killing it, especially when you were sloshed! “The Yogi” Remember when we played that really long elaborate dungeon game “The Raja of Rhythm” brought? It was one hell of a game and you and “The Taco” squeezed out a pretty impressive win! “The Philosopher” I knew one of our walks would make it for this but I wasn’t quite sure which one. Ultimately I think the one where you wound up surprising me with Kogi Gogi was the best :D . I really appreciated that gesture after I got laid off. It was super nice. “That’s nuts” I think the time when you came to trivia and I was really banking on ya getting the question about the bar we go to every Thursday was pretty funny :D “The Mosher” This one goes to the time when it was just us at Haru and I learned a lot about Kerbal Space Program. It was really cool seeing you talk about the mods you were doing and how you got into the super elite modding discord! “The Juggler”  This one is shared by both you and “The Philosopher” but I’d have to go with the night walk we did from 10:30PM to 7AM the next day. It was quite the legendary achievement!! “The Bartender” That BBQ you hosted at your place was great! I love Brazilian meats and it only makes sense a native born one would know exactly how to cook it! “The Enabler” Doing the amazing race that you and the others put on was really fun! I hadn’t done an event quite like that before and it got me quite excited for next year! “La Tacqueria Royalty” To be honest what I really want to put here is the general vibe of us discussing a new One Piece chapter whenever it comes out. I really like making random segues from other conversation topics like “Oh wow look at all those rocks. Say … speaking of Rocks , about that God Valley flashback …”. If I had to put a specific memory maybe the time we got dinner at that burger place in Richmond and we first talked about One Piece a lot! “The Dentist” The birthday party you hosted was awesome. I remember that me and “The Enabler” peer pressured you a bit into having one when you weren’t originally planning to so score 1 for us! Also I remember how happy you were when you set up the Partiful since you described yourself as being a grandma when it comes to technology (your words not mine). “Tight Knit” It was great when you helped me surprise “The Enabler” with the birthday card I got everyone to sign at his birthday party. You both helped me get people to write in it and you gave it to him right at the moment when the cake was being cut. 10/10 execution! “The Big YT short” It was really fun teaming up with you and your gf for The Amazing Race “The Enabler” put on. Definitely a great way to get to know someone and only together were we able to figure out all the clues and get that clutch 5th place with the harrowing Jenga at the end! “The Writer” I really liked your Halloween party where you laid out all the skulls for people to find and did the gator competition. It was a really fun activity especially early on when not many people had shown up. And the stickers I got from it were awesome too! “Granola Girlie” Ok technically I wasn’t here for this but the time you ate 6 cans of beans has gotta go on here. If not that, maybe the time you won my trivia contest. “The Ravenkeeper” The time when you met my “twin brother Imran” was pretty funny. Not gonna lie I really hoped my using a Google voice number would fool you but I didn’t expect you to make the expert play of actually calling my phone and trying to exchange contacts using the tap method. “The Spiker” I remember that time at Spikeball where we were talking and you told me that great quote “The question is the way”. Its something I think about and reminds me to question why I’m doing what I’m doing to make sure its really the right thing as opposed to the default “The Boxer” Probably the time when you, me, and “The Quant” got KBBQ! “Olives” I really liked chatting with you at the going away party that you had (a couple months after you actually moved to NY but thats neither here nor there). It’s awesome to hear how you’ve taken to the city and how you’ve built up a community from not much! “Mr. Socksessful” Probably the time when we played poker and you absolutely cleaned up. It was a little heartbreaking to see the humza bucks move on to become socksessful bucks instead but it was fun! “The Grandma” I think the time when I learned that you and your now husband got engaged was pretty cool! “Fortnite mocap dancer” Definitely the poker night you hosted at your place which also happens to be when I first met you and learned about your fortnite lore! “The Pyramid Schemer” I remember when we first met and were about to go rock climbing and you asked if  I was ready to be emasculated by you. Little did you know thanks to my history with “The Fisherman” getting my butt kicked by a woman is just another day in the life at the Humza factory “Pasta Prince” The time when you finally tried my pasta after trying and failing to get a time when you were free for me to make it! Well that’s it for the 1 year anniversary special. Here’s to another year of me mass messaging everyone every Sunday!

title: Episode 51
excerpt: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The Shadow Brigade!” Its rare that I meet someone right off the bat and immediately we do a bunch of random stuff like coming to help me shop in Stonestown. You’re also the person I’ve spent the most time going on a continuous wal…
content: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The Shadow Brigade!” Its rare that I meet someone right off the bat and immediately we do a bunch of random stuff like coming to help me shop in Stonestown. You’re also the person I’ve spent the most time going on a continuous walk with! :D. Not to mention I really appreciate your banter, you’re an awesome friend! Also I totally didn’t write this because you told me you’d cry if I didn’t put a birthday shoutout for ya in the newsletter. Totally. Monday Today I was supposed to talk to the CEO at a startup who incidentally I saw and liked on Hinge a year or two ago. Small world. We didnt’ end up talking because she said the company had a security incident so she needed to reschedule. In response I told her to SOC em good. Much like my Hinge like … no response. I also interviewed at “The Raja of Rhythm”’s company and I managed to not shit the bed enough and got a next round interview. Once that was done I went to Mission Run Club with the aforementioned “The Raja of Rhythm” along with “The Italian Stallion” and some other folks. Today there was a new guy who joined and was definitely the fastest person there. I did my best to keep up with him and solidified myself as a solid second place but I knew I wasn’t really beating him. We did an uphill run up to Kite Hill which definitely beat me up a bit. Thankfully I never dipped below a 9 min/mile pace even on the uphill but it was definitely a struggle bus. Enjoy this picture from the top of the hill which symbolizes me running up the hill As clear headed as I was :D During that run I met someone and I asked my usual question “What’s something cool or interesting about you that people wouldn’t expect?” and in turn I got asked the question “What’s the coolest response someone ever gave you?”. In all honesty I’ve gotten a lot of good responses to the question and I’ve only remembered a handful of them. To that end I decided to make a google doc listing all the notable responses I’ve gotten which I’m going to try to update so I can look back and remember all the cool things people have said. I’m also gonna share that at the top of the newsletter now each week in case any of you want to see just how cool some people can be :D. Tuesday I started off by walking from SF to my home in Mill Valley to see my family for Thanksgiving. When I got dinner with friends the week before I told them I would do this and I’m definitely not backing down from the bit :D. The walk was pretty smooth tbh. It was a nice day so I got to see some great views of Presidio, the Golden Gate Bridge, Sausalito, the Mill Valley Marsh Hat tip to “The Slosher” for inspiring this All in all I managed a 14:33 pace per mile which isn’t bad for speed walking for 12+ miles IMO. Once I got home and told my family how I got here we chilled for a while and watched Great British Bakeoff. In all honesty I’m not a huge fan of the show but the rest of the family likes it and it is a good bonding experience. For those unaware its a cooking competition show where every week a bunch of bakers compete to see whose the best baker. As each week passes a different baker is eliminated until only one stands. Personally I kinda wish the show was more exciting in its pacing and atmosphere. It feels very mellow and subdued which doesn’t really jive with me all that well. Although it is pretty cool to see all the different things people can bake up. Wednesday Today was honestly a pretty chill day. To make sure my step count doesn’t totally atrophy I go for a walk in the morning before my family wakes up and then I mostly hang out with the family or chill by myself and continue watching flight school lectures. Thursday Mostly the same as yesterday except its Thanksgiving! This may be a hot take but personally I’d rather eat out or do something which involves less time spent cooking and cleaning and instead just hang out and do something fun with the extra time. While I definitely like Thanksgiving food I don’t think its that much better than anything else we could get outside. Sadly the rest of my family vehemently disagreed with my visionary take so we do the standard thing of making a Thanksgiving meal. Accounting for the skillsets we have and the limited kitchen space we divide the labor so that my Dad and I go get the stuff, my sisters do the cooking, and me and my dad do the cleaning. All in all its a functional system and I suppose we do spend a lot of time hanging out in the kitchen while stuff is happening but you know I’m still biased towards other systems. The meal itself admittedly is absolutely delicious with everything from the stuffing to the pies being amazing. We don’t have a turkey because we all agree that turkey is easily the worst part of Thanksgiving. I mean seriously, it's terrible. Instead we have steak which is quite good! I suggested I make some ground lamb patties which I think would have been even better but that idea also got shot down :(. The Iqbal family just isn’t ready for what could elevate Thankgiving to the next level. But again, it is worth repeating that the meal we had ABSOLUTELY SLAPPED. Friday Today is a lot like Wednesday except with a bit more walking with the family. Not a lot more mind you but a bit more. I do notice that whenever I go home I tend to take things pretty chill which I guess isn’t a bad break from all the different things I could be getting up to in San Frisco. Perhaps the most notable thing is I realized a restaurant right near by me called Cole Valley Tavern has some really good food for pretty cheap if you order it from the window. Saturday I head back to SF today (not by walking) and start off with a trash pickup with “The Shadow Brigade” and “The Fisherman”. After trash pickup I walk around for a while and then go home to watch more flight school lectures. At this point I’ve finished 2 of the 12 ground school lectures. Right now the material being covered is important but somehow a bit dry. A lot of it is basic airplane physics along with knowing how the internals of airplane engines work. This is important especially since unlike with cars we can’t pull over and call a mechanic we need to know this stuff ourselves. That being said however I still can’t say I’m enjoying this part of the process however and I do need to push myself more in order to really get through it. Once I finish the second lecture and do some homework problems I can’t muster any more attention towards it. From there I ask myself what I should do next? In theory there are infinite things I can do either on the productive side or the non productive side. I could use the internet to learn about literally anything. Or I could indulge myself in an endless amount of movies, TV shows, or Youtube videos. And somehow nothing really appeals to me. I feel bored and listless. I ask if some friends are available and since nobody is at the moment I decide to walk around go to The Detour to play some arcade games. I get there to find it surprisingly empty for a Saturday night. Usually the place is rowdy and crowded with games being played, merriment being made, and a feeling of liveliness running through the place. Today instead it seemed less like a bar and more like a cafe in terms of its energy and excitement. I play a couple games there and leave instead deciding to just sit outside and think about life. I resolve to just sit alone with my thoughts for sometime and think about anything and everything that passes through without resorting to my phone. One thing I realize is that while I’m at home chilling I tend to have a really hard time doing a long form activity for a while without switching to something else even if it is just for a 5-10 second break. I guess I have gotten brainrotted from the need for constant stimulation. When I don’t have any competing source I tend to be fine but at home I might be writing this newsletter then quickly switch to Twitter or Instagram or something else. This definitely makes it harder for me to do more productive things like get through flight school lectures faster. As a test I’m going to resolve to write the rest of this newsletter without being distracted. Lets see how it goes 😤. My mind also ruminates on regrets that I’ve had over the past year and things that had me feeling down. Surprisingly getting laid off isn’t really on that list. I tend to think more about personal situations where I wish I stood up for myself more and didn’t let others walk all over me. I’m generally pretty good about this but there was one situation which I won’t be getting into in this newsletter where I do wish I had the guts to say “Hey you can’t just treat me like this and it’s you that’s wrong”. After thinking about and letting the feelings wash over me I feel better, like I’ve made progress of a sort. On a more light hearted note I also looked at the night sky and thought how nice it was out. The serenity felt incredibly peaceful and I felt a warm feeling run through my body. After this time to think, I  check my phone to find a message from “The Shadow Brigade” and we meet and walk around for a while. I try to show her the bar I go with all the Canadians every Thursday only to find that my favorite bar tender isn’t there which makes me not want to go anymore. While we’re talking I mentioned one of the rare downsides of writing this weekly newsletter which is that it’s sometimes hard for me to feel like I’m doing enough and could always be doing more interesting things. If I find that my life as of lately hasn’t been that interesting than it does fill me with a bit of dread to write about it. Like I’m imagining texting 50+ people to basically tell them that I’ve been doing nothing which doesn’t feel all that great. There’s a tension where on the one hand I do want this newsletter to be an authentic account of my life from the good, the bad, to the in between foundations but on the other I worry about what will happen if I don’t have interesting stuff to say. Is it still worth sending? She said that she actually thinks I’m doing too much stuff sometimes and that its ok to spend time rotting in bed. I really appreciated that, so thanks! She also asked if I’m one of those people that feels the need to be productive all the time and while my gut response was to say no I realized the answer may actually be yes. While not “productive” in the sense of work per se I do often feel the need to be doing something of note whether its a hobby, hanging out with a friend, or something that I feel like people would be interested in. Maybe I don’t need to think that way as much. Maybe I can slow down a bit more. Granted I don’t want to most of the time but perhaps I can start by not feeling bummed or worried if there are times where my life isn’t as interesting as I think it should be. Back to the matter at hand we walk around for a while through GGP and then she watches while I eat a burrito. From there we part ways and I head back home. Sunday Today begins with another trash pickup as per usual. I made a bit of a small world connection as I learned that someone “The Writer” knows who was at one point interested in buying one of my Mooni sweatshirts is also friends with one of “The Raja of Rhythm”’s coworkers. Funny stuff! From there I go crabbing with “The Fisherman,” “The Quant,” a trash friend who doesn’t have a nickname, and a couple “The Fisherman” met through TikTok. The couple was really cool! I learned one of them was a diplomat in the Obama administration and lived in a  bunch of places for work like Costa Rica, China, and London. Also she now works as an insurance broker for Civic Joy Fund and knows Manny! Small world! We catch some crabs and watch them play around in the bucket. I’ve heard from past trips that sometimes the crabs will have sex with each other which leads me to ask the important question of whether or now crabs can get crabs. These are truly the questions that drive our society forward. Its also cool to see “The Fisherman” teach this couple how to fish. She has been growing her fishfluence to 1K+ followers on fishtok and now she has met randos online interested in learning fishing from her 😮. Once that wraps up I go home and fill out an application to be an SF walking tour guide. Every year you can apply to give walking tours with SF City Guides. Given my interests in walking, meeting people, and learning SF history this feels like the perfect opportunity for me. And as luck would have it the applications are due December 1st so I’m just in time to apply! I write up a quick application and send it off. Interviews will be in January and there are trainings afterwards so I won’t start giving tours for a while but I’m excited! Then I write the newsletter. Also in case you were wondering I managed to write the rest of it from Saturday onwards without being distracted!

title: Episode 50
excerpt: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The impersonator!” Your accents are really awesome and I always get a kick out of hearing them. I do really need to start watching your tiktok :D Monday Today was a pretty even split between interviews and walking. The interviews…
content: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The impersonator!” Your accents are really awesome and I always get a kick out of hearing them. I do really need to start watching your tiktok :D Monday Today was a pretty even split between interviews and walking. The interviews themselves were fine with nothing too much of note. In the evening I went to Mission Run Club with “The Raja of Rhythm,” “The Filmmaker,” and “John Wick”. Since I twisted my foot the last time I came I decided to take it chill and go at a nice casual pace so as to not wreck my foot on the unpaved streets which thankfully worked out. It turns out that one of the organizers was moving out of SF after this run so this doubled as a goodbye run for him. In his honor we did an especially hilly run up to Bernal Heights which I thought was thoughtful since now I certainly missed him less as I was going up that big hill. Tuesday Today I had an all day onsite with a startup I’m interviewing at. Unlike last week’s onsite this one I had to work on a single project for about 8 hours or so and then present it. The problem was actually a pretty interesting Computer Vision task with some messy data that definitely reflects the kinds of challenges you see in the wild. One thing I did note as I was at this company was that the vibes just seemed … off. Its hard to say exactly what it was but I noticed that I didn’t really click with the people as well as I normally do at these things. As the day went on I was more interested in solving this problem to see if I could rather than because I was excited about working here. In the middle of the day I had an “informal” chat with one of the ML engineers there who asked me what I was looking for in a job. Usually I might think to tailor my answers to whatever company I’m talking to but here I basically just said that I want to work for a company I think will actually be a net positive for society and can do something to help everyday people. I’m not honestly sure this company meets those conditions but I didn’t care enough to really think about it here. Around the end of the day I went to present my solution and explain it to a few different people. From my perspective the presentation seemed to go well. I walked through what I did and there weren’t as many questions as I was expecting. A couple sure, but not really a lot. I then talked with the CEO who basically asked what it would take for me to say “Yes” and I mentioned standard stuff like comp aligning and then I basically gave the same answer I did above. From there I walked out and stopped by the bar I usually go to with the Canadians every Thursday and caroused with some of the locals. Afterwards I  went to The Detour for a game night that happens every Tuesday. I haven’t gone to one of these in a hot minute but it was a good time even in spite of the fact that we started with Codenames. I got to find this cool new cooperative game where we all have to work together to roll different kinds of multicolored dice to meet certain conditions (like all 3s, all different colors) within 10 minutes which kept us on the edge of our seats. When I got back home I learned I was rejected from the company I did my onsite with today. Unusually the CEO said he was happy to give feedback if I was interested. Naturally I said yes and I learned that it came down to my communication. Apparently there were times where my reasoning and ideas were strong but didn’t come through the clearest. If that's the case I’m surprised they didn’t ask more questions during the presentation. Ah well, like I said I’m not that interested in this company and the fact that the CEO told me working 12+ hour days was normal certainly didn’t make me feel any worse about not getting it. Wednesday Yet more interviews abound today including one that I messed up due to some really stupid bug which kinda sucked. After the interviews I went to Midnight Runners today with Franklin the air purifier. It was my first time with him since I twisted my foot so I was happy to see that I could not only hold my own but I finally got a sub 9 mile while carrying him :D. Look at me go! And with a not terrible smile too :D I will admit that as the run went on my increased pace did start to weigh on me a bit :(. By the last mile I had to drop down to like a 10 minute pace which was a bit less than great. There was also a bit of irony at play here because normally I love when people ask why I’m carrying Franklin but today people were doing it when I was running my last mile out of breath and in my head I’m like “Please just wait til I’m done. I’m dying here 🫠”. Ideally I would have stuck around at Underdogs for the post run hang but due to most of it being booked for a private event what little was left proved to be too crowded so I went home. When I got home I learned that my air purifier run got more traction than normal this time :D. From a discord “The Game master” is on From a big Whatsapp group chat I’m in Thursday In addition to my normal interviews today I finally decided to start ground flight school. A few episodes ago I decided to try flying a plane and resolved I’d start taking more lessons and today I finally did that by starting ground school. In order to get certified you have to do both flight training and do an online course. I’m starting with the online course right now and working my way through the lectures. Currently I’m learning the basics of aerodynamics and some more of the physics behind flight. In the evening I went to a pitch my friend dating event with “The Quant” and “The Philosopher”. Unlike last time I made sure to sign up for a slot ahead of time and “The Quant” prepped a presentation! Huge shoutout to both “The Quant” and “The Philosopher” for getting up on stage and pitching me. I could definitely feel the love and in the end isn’t that the most important thing? Regardless of how the actual results of the event the love was there! Sadly the actual results were … not the greatest. I’ll admit that maybe there were a couple typos in the presentation In all fairness 90% of my name is spelled correctly here It didn’t help that I also wasn’t interested in most of the other presentations. Amusingly some of them mentioned the ARRs of the startups they founded which was truly an “Only in SF” moment. The way the event was structured was there was a set of presentations, a 15 minute break, and then another set of presentations. Mine was one of the last ones in the first block so my plan was to stick around until after the break and then bounce. I figured that as more presentations happened the mind share for me in particular would go down and whatever interest I got in the first half would be it. There was one girl I was interested in but sadly I didn’t get much time to talk with her during the intermission so I figured I would send her an insta message instead. During the presentation she mentioned the fact that she was related to Alfred Nobel so I thought I would send her this In case you didn’t know Alfred Nobel invented dynamite Everyone told me this would be a bad idea though so I opted not to. It was one of the few times I ever heard “The Quant” give such an emphatic “NO!” So instead I decided to send her something more generic After the presentation we all headed over to bar night to meet up with “The Mosher,” “That’s nuts” and a couple of the other Canadians. It was a good time but in the back of my mind I did feel a bit bummed I wasn’t really able to talk with as many people as I wanted. Friday I started off by doing a special Mission Run Club pastry run that happens one Friday morning every month. For this one we went up to Tank Hill and got some great views Later in the day me, “The Quant”, and “The Plower” went to an event called “Fall of Freedom” over at Green Apple books in inner sunset. This was basically an event raising money for Palestinian folks via art, tarot card readings, and soap. I met a guy there who got really into soaps and now imports olive oil soap from Palestine. I never knew someone could be so passionate about soap and here he was telling me how this  olive oil soap thats been made for one thousand plus years is some of the best hes ever had whether its for skin or hair. And in all fairness his hair is quite lush so perhaps there’s some truth to that. I wound up buying Donkey Milk soap mainly because the name intrigued me and I figured the novelty was worth the $5. After hanging around there and making my usual bomb jokes (or Humza joke #1 as “The Philosopher” would put it), I went to a Friendsgiving hosted by “The Enabler” and “Tightly Knit” which included some other Google folks like “La Taqueria Royalty” and “The Big YT short”. Those two did an amazing job cooking! The turkey thighs were quite good and the carmelized pear with pecans slapped. It did give me a slight sense of foreboding as I thought about the Friendsgiving I would be hosting tomorrow and realized there was definitely gonna be a big gap in food quality here. It was a really good time, we all hung around and talked for many hours before playing a team based board game where we all had to keep a bunch of multi colored timers from running out. This proved to be a pretty intense game as we were all frantically scrambling to turn over hourglasses. I think we won one of the ten times we tried and even then that win may have been a bit disputed. Saturday Another Saturday morning another Sisters trash pickup. Nothing out of the ordinary here really. Afterwards I tried and failed to run up Twin Peaks. Granted I was doing it with jeans and a jacket but I still feel like I could have pushed myself harder. I ran for a few minutes and a couple hundred feet of elevation before I felt like collapsing. This sadly means I’m not as cool as “Top of the rope” who did that run earlier today, but I suppose thats to be expected :D. Once my heart recovered I prepared for the Friendsgiving that I would be hosting.  This wound up being quite fun as I had a large group of people come including “The Quant,” “The Taco,” “The Pickeballer,” “The Mosher,” “The Philosopher,” “The Enabler,” “Tighlty Knit,” “Mirandom thoughts”, “The Boxer” (and his girlfriend), “Top of the rope”, and “The Fisherman”. I made my usual lamb pasta, “The Mosher” brought mashed potatoes and a french dish and “The Quant”  brought some Korean Fried chicken from Aria. And “Top of the rope” and “The Fisherman” brought some sparkling water and wine. I’ll admit without y’all we would have had to subsist on lamb pasta, water, and pies so y’all definitely were the MVPs of this whole event. This event broke the record for most people I had in my apartment at once. We had to use all the chairs, Franklin, my bed, and I had to take a cushion from the papasan chair and put it on the floor. I’m quite glad we had such a good turnout, it may just be one of my favorite events that I hosted yet. For dessert I made a deal with “The Quant” that he got to choose the pie I brought with the condition that he has to eat it with pepper which he did! He says it tasted fine which I certainly found to be quite informative :D. Sunday On my way to trash pickup today I ran into a homeless guy who kept gesturing at me with the come here motion I wasn’t quite sure what to do in this situation so I kept walking forward until I passed him at which point he proceeded to follow me for half a block. At this point I planned for the worst case scenario that he was after me and sprinted for a block to make sure I lost him. Trash pickup proceeded as normal which was good. From there me and “The Raja of Rhythm” checked out a cookie picnic event in Dolores Park. I found this event by looking at Partiful and seeing what events my mutuals were going to and lo and behold this popped up. The lesson here is that Partiful can be an interesting source for events you didn’t know were happening and now I’m going to check it periodically to broaden my horizons. The picnic itself was pretty good! A bunch of people brought cookies and we all just stood around and talked. Since we heard about this at the last minute we didn’t bring any cookies but there were more cookies than people by the end so the host was practically begging us to take some regardless. Amusingly I ran into a bunch of people I hadn’t seen in a while like “The Writer”’s roommate, a friend of “The fisherman”, some people I played Spikeball with, and someone I met at the meetup where I met “The Quant”, “The Professor” and that group of people.  Truly a small world. I also met one guy who I noticed as being distinctly awkward. He was quite keen on connecting with me even though we only talked for a couple minutes and most of that time I don’t think he was really paying that much attention to what I was saying or really reacting to much. Its a bit hard to explain but I just got weird vibes from him. Nothing bad, just not really the vibes I wanna hang out with again. Don’t get me wrong though, the event was still great. I went home and watched some more flight school lectures and then went to KBBQ with “The Italian Stallion,” “The Raja of Rhythm,” “The Quant,” “La Tacqueria Royalty,” “The Boxer,” and “The Mosher”. It was my first time bringing “The Italian Stallion” and “La Tacqueria Royalty” so I’m glad I got to introduce them to the good stuff :D. From there I went home. I should have worked on the newsletter but I just chilled and went to bed so I’ll have to pick up the slack tomorrow.

title: Episode 49
excerpt: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The Writer”! You’re a super down to earth and outgoing guy! I also really like the way you say “very cool!” Its an iconic catchphrase of yours that really reflects your nature. I hope you enjoyed your birthday weekend! Another “Th…
content: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The Writer”! You’re a super down to earth and outgoing guy! I also really like the way you say “very cool!” Its an iconic catchphrase of yours that really reflects your nature. I hope you enjoyed your birthday weekend! Another “The Writer” shoutout! He is looking for beta readers for his book! If you are interested, here is a summary of what he’s working on. In Southeast Asia, rising chef Saka watches his new life crumble when his criminal past resurfaces. With Rani - an ambitious cop and his closest friend - the two of them take on the island’s ever-changing underworld to shut away his demons for good. But a deepening conspiracy exposes the parts of Saka that Rani wished were gone. Soon, Saka himself must choose - will he let the past within him lie dormant, or will he let it loose to confront the demons of his past, even if he risks losing everything he loves? Sample with a link to his discord! Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday The day started off with a couple of interviews which went well. One of them I’m moving onto the final stage which will be an all day onsite happening next week so look forward to that. Afterwards I hung out with “The Fisherman” and we went fishing over by Heron’s Head Park. We didn’t really catch much in the way of fish but I accomplished my main goal of touching grass (rocks) and hanging out so I considered it a successful fishing trip nevertheless. Afterwards we went on a walk over by Tank Hill and Kite Hill. Long time readers may know that I have quite the fondness for Tank Hill, but she had never been before so I figured now was as good a time as any to show her. We also went over by Kite Hill to collect the full list of panoramic viewpoints in the area. I think they say purple sky is a good sign. Or not. Idk. From there I went to Mission Run Club with “The Raja of Rhythm”. Sadly because my foot was still on the mend from last week I couldn’t run so I just went and hung out with folks afterwards which was still quite fun. Tuesday Today I went and got coffee with the person I met last Thursday who was protesting MUNI. At first I thought we would immediately talk about her anti Waymo stance but instead we talked about a wide variety of different social causes she is a part of like freeing Palestine and streamlining the MUNI budget and making SF more safe. I also learned that she wants to move to Thailand with her partner which I found a bit funny considering that she moved to SF for the ease of being able to organize protests and the country she wants to move to has some of the strictest Lèse-majesté laws in the world. I do hope she likes the current monarchy there or she may not have a good time. Eventually we did get to discussing the merits of Waymo which was initially prompted this meeting. She is very anti Waymo for reasons of taxi driver displacement and safety. I’ll admit the displacement angle isn’t really something I can argue but I can definitely argue the safety piece. She brought up the Kit Kat story as an example of why Waymos are unsafe but if I’m being honest thats a pretty weak argument considering that human drivers have certainly done worse. I pressed her on this and she conceded that even she herself feels more safe crossing the street when Waymos are driving versus humans. While I do admit that there are societal implications we need to considering when rolling out self driving cars more I do think safety is pretty solidly in favor of the Waymos here and she did budge there after that. From there I went to the manga exhibit at The DeYoung with “Not a matcha bitch”! He texted me last night asking if I was down for any fun sidequests and I proposed this which he was very down for. For any of y’all who haven’t gone and may be manga fans I highly recommend! It was a bunch of fun to see the different exhibits. The way it worked was there were different exhibits for different authors. Each exhibit had a brief bio of each author along with some of their work. The below is only a fraction of the photos I took. Taniguchi Jiro Ito Junji This will be a new manga coming out in 2026 I think Depicting Moby Dick! Yamazaki Mari TIL there is a manga adaptation of Steve Jobs! These were quite cool but now we finally get to the two manga artists who make stuff I’ve watched before and I am quite excited!! Remember before when I said what I’m showing is only a small fraction of the photos I took? Yeah this is really where this kicks in. First we have Araki Hirohiko I’m a big Jojo’s Bizarre Adventure fan! Its definitely one of my top 10 anime / manga of all time so this was a real treat! New Hinge pic? One of the security guards actually called me out because apparently you aren’t allowed to take pictures of the individual manga panels, you can take a picture of groups of them but not individual ones. We asked why and he said he himself didn’t really know but that was what he was told to enforce. We looked it up and apparently its because you can enforce copyright on individual panels if they are uploaded but a group of them is considered more fair use. A bit of a weird corner case in copyright law I guess but ah well. Oda Eiichiro For me this was the crown jewel of the whole exhibit! One Piece is my second favorite anime/manga of all time. If Yoshihiro Togashi the creator of my favorite Hunter x Hunter was here I’d have a hard time resisting the urge to upload every photo I took. I’ll admit in the One Piece section I may have knowingly broken the rule about not taking photos of individual panels. Unlike in the other sections I knew what a bunch of  the panels were saying despite being in Japanese because a bunch of these were such iconic ones. It was also really cool seeing a bunch of people from 20 somethings like myself to young kids to older folks going around and appreciating it. At one point a young kid and his mom were talking about One Piece and he was trying to explain to her what was happening with some of the latest arcs and who the “reindeer” guy was. “La Tacqueria Royalty,” “The Writer,” and “The game master” I know y’all will really appreciate this section! A man’s dream will never die! Put a pin in this one, I’ll use it later for something Ding dong! When you’re at sea, you fight pirates! After fanboying to only a mildly excessive degree we went to a bonus exhibit which had some stuff on how manga itself is actually made. They showed stuff on the plating of the pages and how things are printed on. There was even a whole video on the process from inking to submission to making all the magazines that go out across Japan each Monday morning! The examples here were all One Piece which unfortunately for you all means I have more One Piece pictures to show you! Alright I promise that's actually the end of the One Piece glazing that took up the last 6 pages of this thing :D. Once we wrapped up at the museum we got some coffee and I headed over to FiDi for an in person interview. The interview was a pretty short coffee chat so basically an in person version of recruiter calls  I typically do in the first stages. From there I went over to Crissy field to fish with “The Fisherman”. Unlike yesterday we (she) actually caught something. It took our tag teaming efforts of her to catch the fish and me to record the video of her explaining what she caught for her growing fishtok account. I introduced her to Abu Salim for dinner which is now sitting in her top 3 Middle Eastern places in the Bay Area. A high bar indeed. Wednesday Today I made the grave mistake of interviewing with 5 different companies in the same day. Granted these weren’t all technical interviews but by the end I got really sick of explaining a project I worked on in the past that I’m proud of. On the one hand you could say that doing this a bunch helps me remember but at the same time giving the same answer 5 times drained my soul more with each answer. I think the rate of draining can be modeled by this exponential graph here The interviews themselves were fine but man did I feel dead after going through all that. I walked around afterwards to breathe some life back into me. After what can only be described as aggressively dicking around I went to Midnight Runners with “The Quant” also featuring “Sergeant Sassy” and a brief cameo from “The filmmaker”. This was my first run since twisting my foot last week so I didn’t want to risk it by bringing Franklin. I PRd this week and finally broke sub 8 in the mile getting a best of 7:28 and  7:56 for close to 3 miles. Unfortunately my foot was hurting a bit more so for the upcoming half marathon on Sunday I figured I’d stop now and conserve my energy instead of running the last 2 miles. Instead of running those last two miles I went to bar night with “The Mosher,” and “That’s nuts”. It was a nice chill hangout. One Piece was playing on the TV there so I filled them in on whats happening since they were understandably confused about stuff happening around 500 episodes in. Thursday The onslaught of rain today sadly meant that Almost Friday Run Club was cancelled :(. I was looking forward to going at a chill pace today and not trying to PR like I did yesterday. The main event of today was going down to Redwood City to pick up a friend from a hospital appointment. It was an odd time and since I have flexibility with my schedule right now I figured why not. And I got In-N-Out on their dime afterward which definitely sweetened the deal. Afterwards the gloomy weather meant I kinda just sat at home and watched TV. In the evening I had a video call with one of my friends from college. We hadn’t talked in 10 months or so and the first thing he told me was that he got a new job. And it turns out it's at the place I’m doing an all day onsite interview tomorrow! I don’t talk a lot about specific companies in this newsletter because it usually doesn’t matter all that much but for some context this place already employs 2 people I went to college with that I knew about and now it turns out hes joining for a total of 3. To be honest this made me a bit nervous since the 2 people I already knew spoke positively about me so if I bungled this interview I didn’t wanna look bad. I know that seems a bit silly but it did give me a bit of anxiety. The fact that a 3rd is there too didn’t really help. Nevertheless the call was great, I’m glad we caught up and he said we needed to end the call so I can get some good rest before my onsite tomorrow. Friday The main activity today is of course the aforementioned onsite. The onsite was structured into 4 technical rounds and lunch. The exact schedule was Coding (1.5 hours) Lunch System Design (1 hour) New Framework (1 hour) System Design  (1 hour) I won’t really go into too much detail on each specific interview except to say that the coding interview actually was kinda a combination of system design plus coding. For those unfamiliar with a typical system design interview a lot of the interview involves getting a vague set of requirements and being expected to ask a bunch of clarifying questions to understand specifics and tradeoffs you can make depending on the set of assumptions. You can’t really blindly go and start building something because what may work for one set of requirements may not work for another and part of the interview is being able to understand different tradeoffs. Once you do that you propose a solution and then the interviewer will say something like “Ok this solution works for X but lets say I now want to introduce Y new complexity. How will you adapt your solution?” I’d probably say the coding interview was about half clarifying the requirements for the problem and half coding it. The two system design interviews were pretty much exactly what I described above and I think they went alright. The last interview was a new framework interview in which I had to solve a problem I never really did before with the idea that the interviewer wanted to see my thought process as I looked stuff up, ingested information, and worked with frameworks. I think all the interviews went alright but in each there were definitely things I could have done better. Of course that doesn’t mean I failed but as someone who tends to be pretty cautious in assessing interview performance I’m not 100% I passed either but we shall see. During my last System Design interview I could definitely feel my throat get sore from all the talking I was doing. During that interview I think I drank water at least 7 times 😅. Once the interviews finished up I got dinner with “The Quant” at a Caribbean restaurant near my place I never tried which was good. If anyone wants Caribbean food I recommend Cha Cha Cha over in Haight Ashbury. I don’t have a Yelp review of it though which should tell you something :D . We then walked around and talked about a bunch of random bullshit as we are wont to do. Saturday Another day another trash pickup. It was a solid pickup but nothing too notable to report here. One of my other trash friends is also running the Berkeley half tomorrow so I’m looking forward to seeing him and others there! After the pickup I went to the slums of Berkeley to pickup my bib for the half marathon. There was an option to customize the bib and this is what I went with Once I went home and dropped my stuff off I went to “The Fisherman”s birthday party! I was recruited to come early to help with setting up stuff so I helped out with that for a bit  and then enjoyed the party. This was a house party hosted at one of her other friends’ apartment. One thing she did was she sent out a Partiful text blast giving most of the big updates in her life so that she didn’t need to say them a bunch of times and save on catchup chat. This is a tradition that has particular meaning for me since “Mr. Greenflag” doing this for his birthday almost exactly a year ago is actually the impetus for how this newsletter was born! Another thing she did as an icebreaker was compile a list of fun facts for everyone and invited people to guess whose fun fact was whose. Mine is that I regularly run with the air purifier. There were some pretty cool ones including someone who did a whole year of study abroad in China from his home in the East Bay, someone who is near fluent in Arabic,  and someone who made dental floss out of recycled plastic. At my suggestion she also included a fun fact about herself and invited people to try and guess it based on the process of elimination. For the curious it's that she had an anticlimactic encounter with Bill Nye the science guy. During the party I also went around getting people to sign a custom birthday card I made for her. Ideally I wanted people to sign it and then I would slip it into her jacket pocket without her knowing as a fun surprise. As the card was making its rounds I was keeping track of where the card was and where she was and I think to the best of my knowledge she didn’t notice until the card was already in her jacket pocket. After a few hours the house party wrapped up and folks went to some bars nearby. I would have loved to join but I needed to get up early for the half marathon tomorrow. Unfortunately the sore throat I got on Friday hadn’t fully gone away at this point and I was starting to get worried. Originally I assumed I got it just from talking and that it would go away within a day or so. I have a bunch of interviews coming up next week and I’m not sure if running 13.2 miles would be good for my throat Sunday I got one of the worst nights of sleep I got in a while. I was anxious about the whole half marathon thing and whether I would really be able to run it. My throat still wasn’t better and at 4:30 AM I was debating what I should do. Should I skip? Should I go? I really wanted to run this thing! I had the custom bib! “The Enabler”’s girlfriend even made a shirt that had the names of a bunch of people in our group that were running including mine. I couldn’t let all those people and the readers down! Sadly that was what I decided. With all the interviews next week I really can’t risk my throat getting worse. Right now I can still go out and do stuff but if I push it for 13.1 miles at reduced breathing I thought there was a significant chance of deterioration. So I lied in bed instead :(. This sucks! “The Enabler”, if you’re reading this thanks for adding me to that half marathon group chat and sorry I couldn’t make it :(. To be honest this did really bum me out throughout the morning. I’m pretty sure I made the right decision here but I’m not 100% sure and it still wasn’t a fun decision to make. It didn’t help seeing the Stravas of the people who did though. The FOMO was real. Thankfully there was still trash pickup to lift my spirits. Today I saw “The Trash Queen,” “The Rugby Player," and “The Trash Queen”’s younger brother. Also today I met someone at trash pickup yesterday who said “Oh you’re Humza?! I was at a party yesterday and when I mentioned I’m going to trash pickup tomorrow they said you should try to meet Humza”! Unfortunately she didn’t remember who this person was but I still found that cool. This person is also friends with “The Ravenkeeper” (not the person who said the above) so that was also cool. During the post trash pickup hang I got to ride in a Zoox since one of my trash friends works there! I’ll admit that now that I’m used to riding in Waymos some of the initial novelty had worn off but it was still cool to see. I did like the experience of getting to ride in this car that was built with self driving in mind from the ground up without needing to have a seat with a steering wheel in it and no front / back either. Its just 4 seats next to each other with 2 rows. You can tell that Zoox is still newer than Waymo with less miles driven because it wasn’t as graceful at making unprotected turns. It needed to break and accelerate in a more clunky way than either human drivers or Waymos would but who knows where it will be in a year from now! It really does say something about SF that now you can look around and see self driving cars and not even blink anymore. Once that was done I went home and checked instagram only to find out that “The Fisherman” knew that I was the one that made the card for her! This was my reaction when I saw this story. I told you that One Piece shocked expression Would come back Then I went home and wrote the newsletter.

title: Episode 48
excerpt: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The Fisherman”! I really love bantering with you as I think our senses of humor are very aligned and you are one of my only friends who does both standup AND improv :D. And I really appreciate your very thoughtful political takes…
content: Shoutouts Happy birthday to “The Fisherman”! I really love bantering with you as I think our senses of humor are very aligned and you are one of my only friends who does both standup AND improv :D. And I really appreciate your very thoughtful political takes which have definitely taught me a lot especially about urban development based YIMBYism and cultures abroad. Happy birthday to “The Slosher”! You are an absolute powerhouse of energy and as much as I give you shit for running being like 90% of your personality you are an absolute beast and you do have some of the better Strava activity titles of any of my friends Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday The day started off pretty alright I suppose. After some interviews in the morning I tried running with Franklin the air purifier up to the top of Twin Peaks and boy was it painful. The best I could do was go up to Tank Hill before giving up, and even then I stopped for a 20 second break. The moral of the story here is I am out of shape cardio wise and have a long way to go of reaching my goal of running to the top of Twin Peaks with Franklin. I had the first session in my new Volo Volleyball league 20 minutes after this run was supposed to end so I was booking it in order to make sure I made it back on time. Not only was I the first one but I was well and truly ahead of the pack. Sadly about 0.3 miles into the run I twisted my foot around Shotwell and 23rd street on some uneven terrain. Due to the adrenaline that was coursing through me I didn’t notice how bad it was at the time. Sure it hurt but it was nothing terrible and the run otherwise felt REALLY good. I PRd and got my fastest mile and 2 mile time finally going sub 8 on a mile. Once I finished and said adrenaline wore off the pain hit me HARD. I could tell based on how I was limping already that I was in no shape to play Volleyball. However since it was only a few blocks away I figured I would at least go and introduce myself to everyone and watch from the sides. I got there and everyone was quite nice but boy was it painful. I couldn’t put any weight on my left foot which was searing out in pain. After about half an hour I couldn’t take it anymore so I went home and iced my foot the only way I could. Using a frozen veggie packet of Squash I had in the fridge. Tuesday The pain in my foot was even worse than at the end of yesterday. I woke up in the middle of the night and going to the bathroom felt like stabbing 1000 needles into my foot. Needless to say I would not be moving around a lot today. Perhaps today is the day of the Sloth. I commemorated Sloth day by staying in bed all day and bedrotting. While I did some work and educational stuff at various points the vast majority of the day was unproductive bedrotting. Come evening I finally have the energy to leave the house so I go on for a little walk just to get some fresh air and not be a total potato. Sadly this is the first day in a long time that I walked less than 20K steps a day and it shows :( Wednesday Today I can actually start to walk around a bit more and leave my house like a normal person. While walking around I see this in a window in a shop near my house This caught my eye since “The Fisherman” has the one on the left so I thought she may like the one on the right to go with it and since it's her birthday this week it's the perfect opportunity for me to get it for her! As luck would have it she invited me to go clamming with her today so the timing worked out nigh on perfectly. For anyone like me before this who may not be familiar with clamming it basically involves going to a beach and looking for (small) holes with water coming out of them and digging to find clams. You use an instrument called a clam gun. Despite the cool sounding name you don’t actually shoot clams out of it and instead you use it to help you quickly extract large amounts of sand to get to the clams. I couldn’t stand on my left foot while using the clam gun meaning my pull out game was pretty weak so I focused primarily on getting it in there while “The Fisherman” took it out. Over about 1.5 hours of doing this we managed to get 5 living clams which wasn’t too bad all things considered. One other thing I didn’t realize with clamming is you needed resilient clothes as some of the holes involve getting in some muddy places up close and personal. Since I don’t own any much less bring any with me I served in more of a supervisory role while “The Fisherman” handled the main extraction. I’ve done a number of different fishing types with “The Fisherman” and while I enjoyed clamming over all I would say it's my least favorite. The complete list is as follows Poke pole fishing (Based) Crabbing by Ferry Building (What she calls crabbing on easy mode) Sea Urchin hunting (A little of this, a little of that) Clamming (I mean I guess) Since I’m not that interested in catching fish what I mainly value is something which lets me hang out and talk with minimal actual work required. Clamming was the exact opposite of that as we were continually digging and refilling holes the whole time which wasn’t quite what I was looking for in a fishing trip. My heart went out for Stanley Yelnats  here. From there we went to Costco and got some hotdogs for dinner. I was debating going to the post MR hang but opted against it when learning some folks I wanted to see weren’t gonna be there. Although in retrospect I learned some folks I did were gonna be there so I should have gone but ah well. Thursday Normally I would have gone to Almost Friday Run Club in the morning but given the state of affairs I joined them afterwards at Flywheel. While talking with someone I posed my usual question “What’s something cool or interesting about you that people wouldn’t expect?”, and unlike most times when I answered back the person who asked wanted to hear every answer I had and ranked them according to how good the answer was. The ranking she gave was Becoming Yelp Elite at restaurants without eating The 45 mile walk Going to Vienna to surprise “The Professor” Bringing back the mugicha at Garden Creamery Personally I would probably go with this ranking but it may be less based on the raw aura farmed and more on how personally attached I am to these stories so ah well. Going to Vienna to surprise “The Professor” 45 mile walk Yelp Elite Mugicha at Garden Creamery After run club I had some more interviews and then I walked around for a while. While walking I ran into a woman who was putting up posters for some sort of MUNI protest. Apparently she is protesting the idea of being able to force fare evaders of the MUNI. I asked her a bit more about why she was doing this and one time while riding the MUNI the fare officer didn’t realize how her day pass worked based on timing and thought it expired subsequently chucking her off the MUNI. She fought and won later but that prompted her to push back completely against fare evaders being forced off. Given how amenable she seemed I tried debating her on the matter and highlighting the differences between actual fare evasion and mistakes like what happened with her. It was actually quite an interesting debate and we talked a lot about public transit in general and how to make it work the best. Ultimately we both agreed that in an ideal world it could be free and this wouldn’t be an issue but I was a bit more skeptical that could happen than she was. She mentioned that Luxembourg has free public transit which I didn’t know about until today. We were about to get into discussing Waymos which she was adamantly against and I wasn’t but she had to go. She did invite me to get coffee with her some other time to continue the discussion which I would be pretty down for as the discussion was entirely civil and I could tell how passionate she was about the issue and as someone who thinks a lot about public transit and different ways of getting around in the city I love to see that! Later in the day me and “The Quant” went to a Costco dating event. Some or many of y’all may have seen instagram reels about this since I think it became a bit famous after the fact but for those of you who haven’t there was a dating event at a Costco where the group running it gives every participant a pin so people know they are with the event and let them loose in a Costco. The idea was supposed to be that you would go shopping in whatever aisle interested you and you would meet others in the same aisle and start talking. Realistically what wound up happening instead was most of us congregated in the area between the aisles and a bunch of people were all talking at once. To be honest I was kind of hoping for more 1:1 conversation and while I got some of that most of it was big group conversations. It's not the worst for meeting people in general but harder to see if I should ask out folks. I did try to ask out someone by getting her insta which she deflected by saying she needed to go pick up her friend and then quickly got out of there. I found that particular deflection method kinda funny but I guess in her situation I don’t see how she could have more smoothly extricated herself from the situation. Interestingly I found someone who reminded me of “The Writer” since she wrote both books and screenplays and has even published a book! Ironically the only woman’s insta I got out of this event was someone I wasn’t interested in all at romantically but I just went on this whole bit about “The Quant” being China’s Mozart because he was playing the piano and I was basically just messing around which she found amusing. I guess there could be a lesson in that somewhere? After the event I went to bar night with “The Philosopher,” “The Mosher,” “That’s nuts,” and “The bartender”. When I recapped the event to “The Philosopher” he said it went about as well as he would expect a dating event at a Costco to go which perhaps was true.
