Friday A while back I found out there is a service called HeyThereNeighbor in which you can sign up for 10 minute coffee chats with people in your neighborhood. Since I don’t actually have many friends in Haight Ashbury I thought it would be cool to try and meet some folks. Around lunch I met with a guy who wound up being really cool! He’s gonna be trying improv for the first time tomorrow so I gave him some tips. He’s also trying to meet more people so naturally I advertised trash pickup which he said he would come to next week. He’s another Canadian and my experience with those led me to predict where exactly he was from when he said “Toronto” which he was surprised by. Later in the day I went to a chicken chase birthday party for “The Slosher”! For the uninitiated a birthday party like this consists of someone donning an animal onesie (usually a chicken or a fox), and going to a random bar from a list of bars and everyone else has to go and find them. There were 3 birthdays being celebrated at this party so there was a Google Form put up where people could vote on who they wanted to be the chicken. There was “The Slosher,” a guy named Hunter (a former trash pickup leader!!), and a 3rd guy named Angello. Angello is a swell guy but spoiler alert he sadly won’t be relevant for the rest of this story. Initially in the poll “The Slosher” had a reasonable lead and it looked likely she would be the chicken. Personally I was gunning for Hunter because I wanted Hunter to become the hunted and thought the wordplay was too good to ignore. An under reacted Partiful comment I did my civic duty and casted my vote and was originally content to leave that alone until “The Slosher” updated the Partiful So I can vote as many times as I like huh? Well I certainly can’t ignore that now can I? I immediately preceded to go hard and vote 70 times ensuring that Hunter would be chosen. Sadly I didn’t capture the exact breakdown before the party started but Hunter was now comfortably winning with around 60% of the vote. When I got to the party I was pretty assured of my (err I mean Hunter’s) victory. I told “The Slosher” what I did and she said “That was YOU?!”. For some context the party started at 8 and voting was supposed to close at 9. One of her friends wanted to try closing the gap and making it closer to 50:50. I wasn’t gonna let that happen so I kept voting at the party and he did the same. Thankfully my votes per minute was pretty fast so he gave up once he noticed the gap wasn’t shrinking. At this point my (wait I mean Hunter’s) victory should have been assured. Sadly as the clock struck 9 and things were all set she cheated by changing the rules a bit and pushed the voting time back to 9:30. She also got a bunch of her friends to vote for her multiple times as well. While I probably had the highest votes per minute out of any individual person, the sheer quantity that she employed overwhelmed me and in the end “The Slosher” became the chicken. In case anyone is interested here is the final breakdown. In total we got 1741 responses which wasn’t bad considering 40 people went to the party. Once that was settled we all left to go track down “The Slosher”. Throughout this I got a sampling of some of the finest bars North Beach had to offer like Spec's which had a bunch of cool knicknacks and other things inside which was lovely, and there was also Hawaii west which had a bunch of cigarette smokers in there who assaulted my lungs all at once. So you know, you win some you lose some. Eventually after some searching I tracked her down to a bar called The Showdown which was somewhere in between those two in terms of how cool it was but it worked out well considering our size. I hung out for a while and chatted with all 3 of the birthday people. At one point I thought “The Slosher” could use some water and given how packed the bar was I was worried it would take a while so I tried going to a corner store and getting her some water but the bouncer wouldn’t let me bring it in (I did try albeit not so well to sneak it in). Also “The Slosher”  forgot her own nickname in the newsletter and thought it was “The Sloshballer” instead as if I would give her such an unelegant nickname. She was so sure however that she bet me a drink on it. Naturally she lost so now she owes me a drink at some point in the future. Finally to round off the night I noticed “The Slosher” had her phone beside her on the Partiful unlocked so I decided to give her one last gift before heading out via a text blast on Partiful. I told her exactly what I did after I think she was a bit too deep in her cups to remember ;). Saturday The day begins with trash pickup as per usual. After pickup I went to a memorial picnic for “The Climber!” It was a joint effort organized by “Sergeant Sassy” and a few other folks. It was a lot of hanging out and chatting with some volleyball in the beginning. I really think “The Climber” would have loved to see everyone come together like this and have fun so I think it was a great tribute to him. What made it even better was we were joined by some random people who were playing Volleyball separately and wanted to play with us! “La Tacqueria Royalty” was also there and he was quite the good volleyball player! There was also a run that happened since many people including myself met “The Climber” through Midnight runners. Sadly my foot prevented me from participating so I mainly talked with “La Tacqueria Royalty” and another guy about One Piece instead. Originally I thought the picnic would end around sundown but we wound up talking in the dark for even longer. Needless to say it was quite a good time! After the picnic me and “La Tacqueria Royalty” got dinner, talked more One Piece, and I mentioned that I saw one of his and “The Enabler’s” friends on Hinge which was pretty funny. She is cute so maybe I should send her a like and see what happens. On my way home from the picnic I was having a phone conversation on the bus and some guy said I was disrespecting everyone else by doing so and started cussing me out and dropping the f bomb which was certainly surprising. Regardless of what you think of having a phone conversation on the bus I do think that was over the line. Looks like I became someones nemesis today. Sunday This is the first Sunday in a while I did trash pickup as somehow I was busy with something every Sunday for the past while now so it felt good to get back to the basics. After trash pickup I hopped on a call with “The Professor,” “The K-pop dancer,” “The Taco,” and “The Quant”. Since “The Professor” moved to Vienna we’re doing once a month calls now to keep in touch and it was cool learning about his life in Vienna and some of the new things he’s doing. Once that was done I got Garden Creamery with “The notetaker,” and “The Raja of Rhythm”. “The Notetaker” asked me what my default emotion is and I said happy. But then he posed an interesting question back to me and said “Is happy your default or is happy the word you use to describe your default?” In general I think I’m happy by default. I might not be radiating joy each day but I find happiness in a lot of little things that happen to me all the time which generally makes it the default. Others said numb was their default and I don’t think thats true for me? From there me and “The Raja of Rhythm” went over to “The Ravenkeeper’s” abode to play Blood on the Clock Tower. Finally this meant I got to see “The Ravenkeeper" in her natural element.  It was fun playing the game as per usual! Given how the game goes we only got through 2 games after playing for about 5 hours but they were some good games. I went home and started to write the newsletter but decided to do some interview prep and instead and elected to finish tomorrow.

title: Episode 47
excerpt: Shoutouts Happy birthday “Aquaman”! You’re a powerhouse of energy and you bring 110% of it to everything that you do! Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday Today is a pretty chill day for the most part. After…
content: Shoutouts Happy birthday “Aquaman”! You’re a powerhouse of energy and you bring 110% of it to everything that you do! Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday Today is a pretty chill day for the most part. After the 35 mile walk “The Shadow Brigade” and I did last week I wanted to recover for a bit. I think my legs are definitely getting stronger because the last time I did a walk of this magnitude I would not have been able to do a run club the next day but towards the evening I felt good enough to go to Mission Run Club with “The Raja of Rhythm" which was great! Not that it matters much but I was the first to finish so I wasn’t dying the whole time :D. Along the way I met a really cool guy who turned out to be one of the main people behind the no dancing sign that used to be in GGP. He talked a lot about his different art installations and some of the cool underground art parties that he went to which were quite interesting. After the run we went to a bar at Alamo Square Drafthouse, a movie theater in the Mission. I hadn’t been there til now and honestly it makes me want to. It was a very aesthetic movie theater where you can order food directly to your seats. As some of you know I’m not a big movie guy but honestly I kinda want to go for the experience. Maybe on a cloudy day I may just make it out. Tuesday The day begins with a bunch of interviews, most of which go well. After the interviews I go for a long walk from my apartment through Presidio to the Ferry Building. Put another way, I do most of the Roundabout Trail that was not finished last week. After the run I go play Spikeball with “The Spiker” and some others in the Panhandle. Since daylight savings time is ending this will be the last spikeball tuesday we have until the daylight savings starts again. I hadn’t played much spikeball in a while and it definitely showed since I was not that good but it was still a lot of fun as always. After a few games of spike we went to “Aquaman’s” house and hung out for a while. I didn’t get to participate in this season for long but it was fun while it lasted! Wednesday Today I did a fair amount of personal project work. There was an aspect of deep learning I really wanted to understand which I only had superficial knowledge of so I spent a while staring at equations and playing around until I got it. I wouldn’t say I’m at 100% understanding now but I am better than I was before. In the evening I went to Midnight Runners with “The Quant,” “La Taqueria Royalty,” and "Sergeant Sassy”. On top of that I got to meet a reader of this newsletter I hadn’t met until now being "Sergeant Sassy’s” man friend who I heard was a fan. They say you shouldn’t meet your heroes so hopefully he wasn’t too scarred by the experience. I realized earlier today that I want to make air purifier runs a normal thing for me as they do help me to get stronger so naturally I brought my air purifier with me this time. Amusingly everyone thought it was part of a costume of some sort so when asked what my costume was I said I was a guy named Humza from a weekly autobiography series called “Trash Tales”. Technically I wasn’t wrong but they admired my dedication to the character which I guess was technically true. I feel like if Humza were here right now he would be ok with how I depicted him in the run. This was definitely my easiest air purifier run yet as I was actually able to run the whole way and at a decent pace. Towards the end of the run “The Quant” declared that he wouldn’t lose to a guy carrying an air purifier so he sprinted hard to try to beat me. I raced him to the finish line and I ended up winning. He claimed afterwards that he let me win but I think we all know that that's cope. After the run me, “La Taqueria Royalty,” "Sergeant Sassy,” her man friend, and another person went to Kayah nearby. I wrote a yelp review here Thursday In the morning I went to Almost Friday Run Club which was good. During the club they asked us an icebreaker question “Whats your hottest take?” The leader said that we shouldn’t over think it and I should go with whatever came to mind. The first thing that came to mind was that I’m not ethically opposed to eating dog meat and kinda want to try it to see what its like. Sadly fear kicked in and I went with a safer opinion that I find travel to be overrated in our cultural zeitgeist but honestly I wish I just went with my first answer as I think that would have been more interesting. To be honest for most of the day afterwards I honestly just bedrotted. For whatever reason I didn’t really have motivation to do much else. Thankfully in the evening I did a Horatio Alger and pulled myself up by my bootstraps to go get some cooking lessons from “The Fisherman”. She offered after reading my last newsletter where I mentioned not having indoor hobbies and offered to teach me some basic cooking recipes. For this cooking lesson we went over how to take chicken and marinade it to make chicken tacos. I mainly focused on cutting up the chicken, cooking it on the pan, rubbing in the marinade, and finally heating up the tortillas. It's not a lot but I did learn things I didn’t know before so now I’m that much better at cooking. Look out world! She was dog sitting a new dog via Rover so I got to play with a dog whose breed I’m not sure about but gave off more cat energy on account of not being as active as most dogs. Though like any small dog it did bark quite a bit which was funny. Additionally said dog was peeing all over the floor resulting in some creative solutions for absorbing said run off. Once we finished eating our tacos and walking the dog I headed off to bar night. Not a lot of folks were there today so I mainly chatted with “The Mosher” for a while. He taught me a lot about Kerbal Space Program,a game about making and launching rockets. Apparently a lot of the fun comes in decompiling the source code and modifying the game to make it play the way you want. He told me a lot about the different mods he was working on like changing how the physics engine works and how certain objects render to cut down on weird rendering issues. He even got invited to a secret Kerbal Space modder discord so he is one of the elite modders. Friday Happy Halloween to all who celebrate and a happy fright to all who don’t! Before all the festivities I mainly did a bunch of admin work like reading over the contract I got for my startup acquisition which told me less than I would like about the exact specifics of the money and when I would get it a but a little bit more on how much I could expect. Tldr is I won’t be a fat cat but it's at least something. For this Halloween I decided to dress up as a penguin since I already had a penguin onesie. And for extra fun I carried around my inflatable penguin Boris with me. When people asked why I had Boris I would give a variety of answers based on how much of my bullshit I thought they could handle. For the less initiated I said that Boris was meant to be just a kid penguin. For the more initiated I brought up that penguins have been known to commit necrophilia and that Boris is actually dead, further implications being left as an exercise to the listener. I started my actual festivities off by going to a party hosted by a friend of “The Enabler” and “La Taqueria Royalty” both of whom were there. “La Tacqueria Royalty” dressed up as Ash Ketchum and in that spirit he asked people to give him challenges so he could earn gym badges. I gave him a challenge but I won’t say what it is now because it is something I assigned him to do on Sunday so look forward to that in a bit! The party itself was great but sadly I had to leave earlier than I wanted because there was another halloween party happening for which 3 people were my +1s so I couldn’t exactly leave them hanging. I did delay leaving as much as I could so I could also see “The Dentist” with whom I overlapped for all of 2 minutes before making a non ceremonious departure. The next party was hosted by a different friend I met via trash pickup. I invited “The Fisherman,” “The Quant,” and another guy I met through Mission Run Club. There were a lot of trash friends at this party like “The Writer,” “Granola Girlie,” and “The Yogi”. Things were definitely more packed here than at the previous party which came with the usual plusses and minuses that that would entail. “The Fisherman” killed it with her Toph costume, it was easily the most popular costume I saw that Halloween night. The party we were at was explicitly meant to end at 9:30 as a place to pregame before your final destination so then I wandered around with “The Writer,” “The Quant,” “The Fisherman,” and some other folks we met at the party for a while. We first got some street hotdogs and I have to say I thought street hot dogs in The Mission would taste better than they actually did. Mine and “The Fisherman’s” hotdog touching tips We went through Dance-O-Ween for a while which was a lot of fun! In my opinion it had all the party vibe of a club or bar without the long lines. Seriously for any bar we saw around here there was an hour+ line to get in which made it very not worth it. Along the way we ran into “Aquaman”, “The Spiker”, and “The Yogi”. After a while there I got a ride home from “The Quant” which came in clutch as public transit was very delayed and Ubers were $50. I went home and played a choose your own adventure Halloween game for a bit before going to bed. Saturday The day started off with trash pickup as per usual. We picked up a large amount of candy wrappers in the aftermath of last night. I chatted with “The Ravenkeeper” who contends that she could probably walk longer than “The Quant” and believed I should have put her above him on my walker list from last week. I think this is probably true but since I haven’t gone on a long walk with her I can’t personally put her on the list. After trash pickup, I along with “The Quant” went to “Aquaman’s” birthday party in Panhandle. We played spikeball, kan jam, and tried to cut pieces of candy exactly in half. The best I could do was take a 17g snicker bar and cut it into pieces which were 8 and 9 grams respectively which was alright enough. We also had a challenge to estimate how many jolly ranchers were in a jar. There were 101 total and I guessed 107 which was the 3rd closest guess out of roughly 15 or so which was pretty good. From there “The Quant” and I headed over to Green Apple books to hang out with “The Plower,” “The Taco,” and “The Pickleballer". I’m not generally a fan of books but I hadn’t seen “The Plower” in a while and she really wanted to go to a bookstore so here we are. At first I didn’t know how I was gonna take down a challenging beast like a bookstore which would chew me up and spit me out alive but it turns out that she was the only one interested in perusing so the rest of us all sat in the back with the cooking books and chatted. I tried to help some random person who came through find a book she was looking for which was the most interesting part of the book store. Sadly “The Plower” needed to go home early so the rest of us got dinner and went to my place for boardgame night where we were joined by “The Raja of Rhythm” who got a new motorcycle, “Mirandom thoughts,” and a new friend I met a trash pickup for some good ol Secret Hitler which was fun. Afterwards I did briefly try to come up with some other Halloween plans after being inspired by “The Fisherman” but after failing to come up with any I just crashed and went to bed. Sunday Today started off with a run with “La Taqueria Royalty” and “The Dentist”. Remember when I said on Friday I gave “La Taqueria Royalty” a challenge to earn a gym badge that would be happening today? The challenge was to do our 5K run while carrying Franklin the air purifier. Unfortunately when I showed up to his apartment with Franklin to start the run he turned down the challenge. This meant I wound up doing the run with Franklin instead which still worked out because if I want to meet my goal of doing a half marathon or running up to Twin Peaks with Franklin I need to be able to do a 5K like this. All in all it wasn’t the easiest but certainly not the hardest either. I remember way back in the beginning of the year (January 1st to be precise), I did a run with “The Dentist” and “The Enabler” and got my butt kicked. For any One Piece fans, imagine Luffy vs Kizaru on Sabaody. Since then I’ve gotten a lot better at running and this run was more like Luffy vs Kizaru on Egghead Island. This time I could keep pace with the both of them while carrying Franklin! The run itself was beautiful since the day was nice and we ran through The Presidio and got to see Mountain Lake which was delightful. What was less delightful was when I awkwardly took off my jacket and had it slipping around Franklin before we stopped and I tied it around my waist but I persisted through that. After the run we walked around a bit before meeting up with “The Enabler” and some other friends for brunch. During the walk I gave “La Taqueria Royalty” another chance to earn the gym badge by carrying Franklin until we got to brunch. In a way this is like how Ash earned his Kanto gym badges by not doing the original task and instead doing something slightly different so perhaps it fits. We got brunch at Rice and Shine which was great. I wrote a Yelp review here. From there I went fishing with “The Fisherman” at Horseshoe Bay which was a lot more fun than I expected. Going into the fishing trip I wasn’t expecting to catch anything I just came for the vibes. Little did I know I would be able to catch a big af Eel and some crabs. Since we were actually taking the Eel back home to eat I killed the Eels with a rock since they can survive without water for 36 hours which is pretty crazy. Killing the Eel with said rock felt a bit like playing whack a mole as the little guy would continually slip around as I tried to cave its head in. Me catching my first fish! Once we finished fishing we went back to “The Fisherman’s” place to cook and eat said fish. I learned more about how to clean and gut fish which was certainly informative and by the end we had a meal that tasted like a fishier version of chicken which was interesting. This was the first time I ever caught and cooked my own meal which was honestly pretty cool. I felt kinda like a real hunter back in the day except with less day to day dread and more existential dread instead. Cool! While we were preparing the fish, the rover dog she was watching hung out with us. In order to distract the dog while she was finishing up the cooking I talked a bunch with the dog as if she was a person. I dove deep into her backstory about her original owner who according to my improv was so fat he needed 3 seats on airplane, got a divorce because of his 30 sidechicks, and a son who was so stupid he tried deep frying and eating weights in order to become stronger, and the dog herself was a fan of Andrew Tate. It was actually a pretty fun form of improv, all things considered. What said fish turned into! After that I went home and wrote the newsletter.

excerpt: Shoutouts Shoutout to “The fisherman” for passing level 3 of the CFA and becoming one of two accountants that I know along with “The Quant” Correction 11/2: I know an actual accountant “Sergant Sassy” who I did not account for above. The above two are Charter…
content: Shoutouts Shoutout to “The fisherman” for passing level 3 of the CFA and becoming one of two accountants that I know along with “The Quant” Correction 11/2: I know an actual accountant “Sergant Sassy” who I did not account for above. The above two are Chartered Financial Analysts which are different from accountants. I call them that as a joke but since I know an actual accountant I should issue this correction Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday Today starts off pretty chill. I write up last weeks newsletter in GGP, do some personal work and then walk around for a while. As I’m walking I come to the realization that I don’t really have a lot of interesting indoor hobbies. I mean sure if I’m relaxing I may watch TV, youtube or whatever but nothing really fulfilling or newsletter worthy. Previously this was never really an issue for me as when I was working after work I’d either have my other hobbies like improv or running and on the nights I didn’t I’d usually be tired enough that I’d just want to chill. Now with this time the question becomes, what should I do? Ideally I want something that isn’t just consumption. I guess writing the newsletter itself could count but what else could I add? Maybe I could take some online classes? Maybe I could sew or crochet? The possibilities are endless in theory but in practice there isn’t anything that really sticks out to me. After I think about this while walking I go to a new run club in the Mission appropriately called Mission Run Club. I heard about this from “The Raja of Rhythm” who mentioned that he started going on Mondays. I figured I’d check it out and honestly it was quite good! The run itself was alright. There was a reasonable enough spread of paces that I could have taken it chill if I wanted to. Unfortunately it turns out one of “The Raja of Rhythm”’s friends is really good at running and I made it a goal to keep up with him for the whole run which meant I actually had to try. Don’t get me wrong I could do it just fine and I wound up beating him but it did mean I actually had to put in effort. After the run we all went back to a bar and hung out. I learned that this is where the Mission Run Club really shines. The post run vibes were some of the best I had seen in a while. It's much smaller than Midnight Runners which makes it much easier to talk to people. For people who do trash pickup imagine the difference between Sisters and Mannys. I met some pretty cool people there and it cemented Mission Run Club as my second favorite run club in the city. Here’s the current rankings Midnight Runners Mission Run Club Almost Friday Run Club Tuesday Today I flew a plane for the first time! I got inspired because “The Juggler” is learning how to fly a plane and I thought it would be a cool thing to try. There's a flight school over in San Carlos where you can learn to do this so I went and checked it out. When I got there I met with my flight instructor who got me situated in the plane and explained some of the different controls and panels. So many things. Such fancy. One thing I took for granted was how much pre flight work there was before the flight itself. Not just the taxi and take off but continually radioing into the control tower to make sure you are cleared for flight, checking the fuel, and a bunch of other preflight checks I have a hard time remembering. Once all that was done and we were in the air that was when I got to take over. Let me tell you flying a plane was SUPER SICK! I remember as a kid I used to play a bunch of videogames and I’d always love the ones where I got to fly in all directions and this is basically a real life version of that! I got to go up, down, and even turn! Sadly I couldn’t quite do a barrel roll but maybe someday. Thankfully I picked a sunny day to go out and do this so the views were great! Once the flight time was over the flight instructor took over and we landed back at the airport. An interesting detail I didn’t expect was that the controls for steering an airplane on the ground are different from in the air. In the air you use the thing I’m holding in the picture above to steer the plane. Kinda like a steering wheel for a car. On the ground you use pedals to move the plane left or right. After landing I took the plane back to its original position and found myself confused when I wanted to default to using the handle but needed to pedal, a confusion the instructor said is pretty common. Honestly this flight does make me want to sign up for more lessons and try flying again. Gosh darn was this fun! Upon coming back to SF I originally went to check out Tuesday Spikeball over in the Panhandle only to find nobody there. On a whim I decided to fill the spikeball shaped void in my heart with another run club in the form of Fat Boys run club. Naturally anyone who ever met me wouldn’t question my qualifications for this particular run club. This run club meets in the area between Panhandle and GGP and runs along GGP for a while and then the perimeter of the Panhandle. I’d rank this run club solidly below Mission Run Club based on the vibes. There was a bit of socialization in the beginning but didn’t quite seem as fun. The run itself was alright I suppose. As the run was finishing up in the Panhandle I saw the spikeballers playing in the distance and decided to ditch the rest of the run and join them. I only had a couple blocks left anyway. With that here is the new rankings of the run clubs Midnight Runners Mission Run Club Almost Friday Run Club Fatboys run club Sadly spikeball itself was wrapping up by the time I got there but I did find “The Spiker” and talked with him and some other people for a while. We wound up going on a bit of a deep dive on what hobbies we want to do and why and he brought up an interesting point I quite liked that “The question is the way”. In other words you always want to start with the most fundamental questions on why you are doing what you are doing as well as breaking things down by starting with the simplest questions. An example he brought up was how the journey of 1000 miles begins with a single step. Wednesday Today after some work and walking I went to Midnight Runners. Sadly due to some MUNI delays I miss the first 30% or so but its still a good time. I saw “The Filmmaker” there for the first time in a while which was great. Turns out one of his friends does Krav Maga just like I do so we spent a while talking about that. We did this run at a pretty chill pace which was nice for relaxing and the post run vibes at Underdogs were great. Thursday Originally I wanted to get up and make it for the 7AM run club but my body chose sleep instead. I still joined for the post run hangout which was fun but nothing particularly notable I suppose. In the evening I went to bar night with “The Philosopher,” “That's nuts,” “The Juggler,” and “The Mosher”. It was a fun time as per usual. “The Juggler” was very interested in hearing how my flight went and I too was interested in how I can continue my flight journey. One of “The Philosopher’s” friends is a self proclaimed small C conservative and we had a pretty interesting discussion around the tradeoffs of building housing and preserving SF. I tend to be more on the YIMBY side of building more housing even if it is ugly (think what China does for example), while he leaned more on the side of having a city that inspires and the aesthetics as an important human need. Friday Today I went over to Berkeley to catch up with one of my old floormates. It was my first time really wandering around Berkeley since 2019 so I got some real nostalgia for my college days. I even got there an hour early and spent a while wandering around the campus. I checked out my old computer science building Many nights were spent in this basement Just some CS stuff I also went up the clocktower known as the Campanile. You get free admission if your currently a student and since I had my old student ID I wanted to see how carefully they would check it. The answer was not very :D. I haven’t aged a day since this photo right? Legend has it if you step on this seal you don’t Get a 4.0 this semester. Guess I’m cooked. After reliving my college days I met up with my former floormate and it was really good to catch up with her! Unlike my meeting from last week there wasn’t really any tension going into this and it was a straightforwardly nice catch up. Apparently she walked 40 miles from Berkeley to Napa once making her the second biggest walker I know, a fact that will become more relevant later in this episode. We agreed that once she finishes up her PhD in December we will go on an even longer walk to beat my current 45 mile record. I spent a bit more time walking around in Berkeley after this. I checked out the student centre which was around when I was there but now requires you to be a current student to enter. Thankfully just showing them the ID above did the trick again. Apparently this student center now has an air hockey machine and skeet shooting which were not around in my day. * Shakes fist in the air*  these kids today don’t know how good they have it I got boba from Sharetea which used to be one of my favorite places back in college but is honestly mid now. It just tastes like sugary slop. I was jittery for a while after that. From there I got back and hosted a trivia night at my place. We had “The Raja of Rhythm,” “The Sparkle,” “The mushroom hunter,” “That’s nuts,” “The Taco,” “The Quant,” “Granola Girlie,” “The fisherman,” and “Smokey the bear”. I had never hosted trivia before so I wasn’t sure quite how it would work out but all in all I think it went quite well! I had questions spanning 3 categories: General SF, MUNI, and famous people in SF. Most of the questions were pretty general questions but being me I did throw in a few that were tailored to my friends because why not right? In the end “Granola Girlie” won which means that in addition to being the bean king she is also the trivia titan now. She won an incredible prize of a random thai bill that “The Juggler” gave me from his trip to Thailand. I entered the contest myself not to win of course but to shake up the rankings and keep things interesting. Saturday The day begins with trash pickup. It was raining so we didn’t get a huge attendance but it was still pretty sizable. “The Shadow Brigade” was in town this weekend so she stopped by as a bit of a guest appearance to the pickup. After the pickup the two of us went to Daly City to go ride horses. I had never done it before but she suggested it and I thought it could be fun for both me and you my dear reader. It turns out it was quite fun. Riding a horse (at least a well trained one), is a bit like playing a video game where you move a character using some reins. The video game is a bit laggy though so you may need to pull the reins multiple times or occasionally course correct. Oh and sometimes the character randomly wants to drink water by the beach so you need to pull it back. In all seriousness though it was pretty interesting seeing what horses react to. One of the horses got spooked by a paper bag and needed to be taken back to the stable. Going downhill was a bit scary at first but once I got used to it it was alright. I just need to remember to lean back on the downhill and lean forward on the uphill. “You look like nerd/horse girl with that helmet” - “The Shadow Brigade” After riding horses we went back to the mission and walked around for a while and wound up at an olive oil store because apparently her boyfriend wanted some olive oil from a particular place in SF. While we were walking around she read my last two newsletters in front of me and provided live reactions which was pretty entertaining. My favorite of which was when she read the part where I described my 20’s arc here and she said “I knew you were a loser in the past”. Thanks love you too “The Shadow Brigade”. From there we split off and I went to go get KBBQ with “The Philosopher,” “The Mosher,” “The Sparkle,” “The Quant,” and “The Raja of Rhythm”. It slapped as it usually does. From there me, “The Philosopher” and “The Raja of Rhytm” went to the usual Thursday night bar spot to hang out with the bartender a bit. While at the bar I tried some snacks that “The Shadow Brigade” got me from her trip to China. Here’s a sampling I found the Oridian (matcha Oreo) to taste pretty good. The Pineapple cake was pretty mid. There are many others I have yet to try though! Sunday Today I spent the whole day doing The Roundabout trail (a trail meant to be the perimeter of SF) with “The Shadow Brigade”. About a year ago I walked roughly the perimeter of SF with “The Quant” and “The Philosopher”. “The Shadow Brigade” mentioned wanting to do a long walk of some sort and I suggested the one above which clocks in at about 38 miles. To be honest I didn’t think she’d actually say yes but she did and I thought why not right. It turns out when I did the perimeter a year ago we cut a lot of corners on the south east part of the city so I figured now would be a good chance to go and fix that. In honor of the walk I wore my lambrofeeti socks that I got from “The Quant” Ferry Building -> Candlestick park We start at 9AM at the Ferry Building. As with many of these long walks part 1 is always the time when we are the most optimistic and upbeat. We think we can conquer anything and are ready for everything. In my opinion the first part has the most sketchy areas considering we have to go through Bayview, Hunters point, and Candlestick park so I decided to get that out of the way during daylight hours. This part is alright. Nothing too crazy really. The sketchy parts are predictably sketchy but we remain in good spirits. Along the way we stop at a slide and slide down. I can read but the sign still             I wish I could include the video of me going down Can’t stop me                                  this slide Candlestick park -> Los Trinos Now that we’ve gone as far south east as we possibly can we head westward. We go through Visitacion Valley, Crocker Amazon, Excelsior, and get close to Daly CIty. Energy wise we’re both fine here but as we pass through the “purgatory of houses” as Shadow put it it does get a bit boring. This isn’t helped by the fact that it starts raining here. It's raining, it's cloudy, and my spirits are starting to go here. We are no longer in the optimistic phase 1, now we are solidly in phase 2 where we start to realize just what we signed ourselves up for. Every long walk this always happens to me. Eventually I get hungry and so we stop and get lunch at an El Salvadorean place. While we’re getting lunch we take a phone break and “The Shadow Brigade” said “Are you reading manga you FUCKING WEEB?!”. At the moment I was not but I read some afterwards since she got the idea in me. To be honest between the cold and the rain and the boredom I was tempted to give up. Los Trinos -> Ocean Beach Thankfully after lunch the rain subsided and my spirits came back. At this point we were joined by “The Quant” who tried his best to sneak on us but I thwarted such chicanery. We were still in house purgatory around here which subsided right around the time we got to Ocean Beach. Ocean Beach -> Geary St Sadly “The Quant” left us to go back home. This sucked especially for “The Shadow Brigade” since it meant she was stuck with me again for a while. We walked through Ocean Beach and got to see some of the sunset. There were hammocks along the way which looked kinda nice. This was pretty uneventful for the most part until we got to Lands End. Unfortunately the sun had set at this point so we were doing a straight night time hike. Apparently “The Shadow Brigade” has really good night time vision as she didn’t need a flash light to navigate Lands End. Sadly what I have in walking skills I lack in night vision so I definitely needed one. To be honest now we’re getting into the part of the perimeter trail that I really dreaded because doing this at night is definitely suboptimal. Originally after Lands End we would go up the Presidio by Baker beach and go to Golden Gate Bridge. However I decided against that because we get quite close to cars and I’ll be honest I really don’t want to get right next to cars driving by when it's night time. So I organized a strategic pivot to have us instead walk along Geary St and get to Ferry building and go that way Geary St -> Tenderloin At this point I’m honestly pretty bored. One thing I realized about myself doing long walks is past a certain point. It's less because it's fun and more about achieving a goal. For example when I did the 45 mile walk I would not have persisted as long as I did solely because I thought it was fun. I did it because I wanted to achieve my 45 mile goal. But I’ve already walked to the Ferry building before. I’ve done the perimeter trail. There is nothing really new for me to achieve here. With that I suggested to “The Shadow Brigade” that we stop the walk and take pride in what we achieved so far. “The Shadow Brigade” was not having it though. She was adamant that we finish. I think because she hasn’t done this before she was still chasing the novelty of achieving the goal. She also reminded me (multiple times) that it was my fault for suggesting this in the first place. I’ll admit she has a point. If we did the double cross like she originally suggested we would have been done many hours ago. But the past is in the past so it was time to persist. As we walked along Geary St we first set an intermediary goal of getting her boba like she wanted. By this point it was 8PM on a Sunday so many places were closed. I found Little Sweet was still open so eventually we made it there but sadly it didn’t meet her particular boba standards (i.e. that the place has seats). One interesting thing to note here is that while she had more mental energy than I did I certainly had more physical energy. We reached the point where she wanted to sit down roughly once every 10 minutes or so. Most of these sitdowns were at bus stops where I tried to not so subtly suggest we stop to which she with as much subtly reminded me of who it was that suggested this walk. After a certain point we get to where Geary st meets the Tenderloin which brings us to … Tenderloin -> The Ferry Building This is the final part of the walk. Originally “The Shadow Brigade” didn’t want to walk through The TL so the plan would have been to stop right before. However just as we were getting to The Tenderloin she wanted it on the record that I gave up before she did. I refused to admit such things and said I”d be down to go to The Ferry Building if she is. And with that our battle of pride led us to walk straight through and finish. To be honest this was the best thing that could have happened for me. I didn’t have a clear motivation for this last part but a battle of pride was exactly what I needed! With that I was back to almost prime form. I could feel a clear boost as I was determined to finish what we started. We walked straight through TL dodging many cases of vomit on the street and eventually made it onto Market street. Honestly even 30+ miles in I feel like I could have run there. It's like I got a second wind! Eventually we made it and finished our walk. The final route looked like this (ignore the breaks I paused and forgot to restart) Come to think of it this is now the second longest walk I’ve ever done! Before today here was my list of SFs best walkers as I knew them Me “The Philosopher” “The Juggler” “The Quant” Now we have this Me “The Shadow Brigade” “The Philosopher ” “The Juggler” “The Quant” I can now also say for both “The Shadow Brigade” and “The Quant” I got them to walk the longest they ever have. Once we got to The Ferry Building and celebrated our post walk a bit we parted ways and I headed home, ordered some McDonalds and went to bed.
