content: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Shoutout to “The Plower” for organizing a fundraiser for Gazan families affected by the conflict there. She’s really been spending quite a lot of time on this and its pretty impressive that over a couple days she’s already raised close to 4K dollars. Additionally she’s been very transparent about the exact families that she’s going to be sending the money to and has been quite clear and methodical with the exact ways that the money will be transferred. If you are interested she wrote up a lot of details here. Another one for “The Filmmaker” for starting production on his film! Looking forward to seeing it when it comes out! Also, this film involves some big dance scenes both in GGP and at his apartment for a running scene and a house party scene and he is looking for extras. He said the more the better and to bring everyone you can find so in that spirit I’m linking his two shoots here and here if interested! They’ll be this coming Saturday and Sunday at 11am. Monday Today was a pretty chill day. I spent some time doing a bit of reading but didn’t really do much else. The weather was pretty bad so I didn’t have too much of a reason to leave my apartment. Tuesday Today I started work on a personal project of mine. One thing I realized while working is I don’t really get a lot of time to dive deep on certain things that can be quite useful but I don’t have the time to learn so I figured now is as good a time as any to do so so thats what I did. Mainly getting things started. In the evening I went to a Blood on the Clocktower meetup. For anyone unfamiliar its a social deduction game somewhat like Mafia except A LOT more complicated. There are a whole bunch of special roles which make the game pretty interesting. A whole round takes about 2 hours to play so we only got through one game but I greatly enjoyed it. One of my friends got her nickname “The Ravenkeeper” through this game actually. If you’re reading this you should come to one with me sometime! Wednesday Today certainly proved to be quite the rollercoaster of a day. I woke up to a message from my college ex who I hadn’t spoken to basically since we broke up asking if I was free to meetup today since she would be in SF. I’ll admit that message surprised me more than anything had in quite a long time. I won’t go into all the details here but we had a pretty bad breakup and she certainly wasn’t interested in talking. I did try to reach out once back when we were both in college and that meeting was incredibly awkward. I saw her on graduation day and then opted not to talk to her. So what do I do now when faced with this message? I thought for a moment and decided I would meet with her. In my mind I expected this to be a half hour meeting at most. Worst case its slightly awkward but you know whatever. Today I also learnt that one of my previous startups may be acquired. This was a startup I joined shortly out of college back when it was just getting started. As a result I got a reasonably large number of shares for a new grad. This is public knowledge but what I don’t actually know is exactly what my upside would be here. I did some math which if true would make it reasonable, enough that I could extend the Humza unemployment arc for quite a bit if I wanted to. Between the two things above I was far too distracted to do any work on my personal project instead choosing to dive deep into hypothetical futures where the acquisition makes me bank and also what exactly this conversation with my ex would be like. Eventually the time comes to go meet with my ex and honestly the conversation went much better than I thought it would! What I thought would initially be a 30 minute meeting wound up going for 2 hours and even then we only stopped because we both had plans afterwards we had to do. We spent quite a bit of time catching up talking about life after college, travel, and occasionally AI. Amusingly she thought I was C suite at some AI startup and would either be too busy to meet or all I would want to talk about is AI. As it turns out she finished her PhD and is doing her own unemployment arc traveling around before she looks for jobs and happened to come here to visit people. Since we hadn’t spoken to each other since college we talked a lot about what we had been up to since college. Since we’re both nearing the end of our 20s she asked me a pretty interesting question “What adjectives would you use to describe your 20s?”. I thought for a moment and couldn’t come up with any specific words. After thinking a bit more though I did describe in great detail the overall arc of my 20s. One thing I realized is that most of you reading this have only known me for the last 2-2.5 years and thus don’t really know the whole arc so I figured I may as well share what I told her (slightly cleaned up) here because why not. Humza’s 20s in an arc After college I started working at a startup (the same one that may be acquired). At this point I didn’t have a very clear idea of what I wanted to do other than something in Machine Learning (the term AI existed but wasn’t thrown around as much as it was today) and I didn’t really forge out as much of my own identity. I didn’t really have too many hobbies to speak of. To be honest after work I mostly just chilled at that point. My work life balance right now was pretty bad with me working a lot of weekends. I didn’t like it but it was what it was. I remember back in those days I would panic if anything seemed like it was going even slightly wrong. If QA ever filed a bug with my code or time estimates were off I’d freak out and frantically try to fix it with far more stress than I should have. Experience definitely taught me when and when not to freak out :D. Come to think of it before the pandemic I barely had any friends (not just outside of work but in general). Boy is it weird for me to think that given my current situation. Around a year and a half after graduating college we got into the pandemic. I remember I went home right around when it started for what I thought would be a couple days for my dad’s birthday only to be there for several months and then come back to my apartment in SF just to move out since paying rent in COVID seemed dumb. Interestingly I had more friends early on in the Pandemic since I reconnected with some people from college since everyone was online anyway we were all as far or as close as anyone else. It was actually during the Pandemic that I started going on long walks. After a few months I’d come back to SF on the weekends and just go for a long walk. In those days I’d do a reverse bay to breakers and walk from Ocean Beach to the Ferry Building. Also around that time I started doing stand up comedy via online classes at the same place “The Enabler” currently takes stand up classes. This was really where my hobbies started to cultivate and I got a much clearer sense of what I liked to do and could feel myself carving out a more distinct idea of who I am. Work wise some big projects I was on gave me my innate belief that as long as I work hard things generally work out. Not always the way I might expect and with some roadblocks but more so as a general point to not stress too much about work. It also taught me that I’m definitely more of a work to live person than the other way around. A year later I’d get a new job and did some digital nomading. It was my first time solo traveling and I learned how to manage an evolving trip and how to start making friends in a completely new city. I went to Miami as part of it and started breaking into the local standup scene. I got to know some of the folks there who were mostly cool. There was also the guy my dad’s age who invited me to go on a cruise with him 1:1 but that's neither here nor there. One year from there I moved to SF. Because of all the time I spent walking in GGP I really wanted to be in Haight Ashbury specifically because it was close to there which wound up being a pretty good decision (I’m writing this newsletter from GGP as we speak). At this point I was doing some casual improv but I didn’t really have much of a community in the city. From 2023 to now I started to build that up first via a meetup where I met “The Professor,” “The Plower,” “The Quant,” “The Taco”, trash pickup where I met too many people to name here and finally run club. I only realized after I said all that just how much detail I went into. To summarize I guess my 20s were essentially an arc of developing more confidence that things would work out and finding more of what I really want to get and cultivating community. Well now I have a much more succinct answer to the question that doesn’t involve going through my whole 20s but sometimes you only know the path after going through all the detours. I won’t give the full description of what she said but the broad themes were largely similar in terms of understanding more of what she wanted to do and now having a bunch of fun new hobbies. Back in college I always thought of her as the work to live type always grinding on something to get ahead and now here she is talking more about her cooking club and bike backpacking trips than anything else. We wound up spending a lot of time talking about travel which was interesting. It turns out she also travels about as spontaneously as I do (ie not booking return flights, quickly finding hostels) and so on. This conversation actually inspired me to travel a bit more and placed Central Asia near the top of my bucket list after remembering how much I like Uzbeki food. I still want to spend a bit more time here after my last trip but who knows what lies in the future of the Humza unemployment arc. After 2 hours we did unfortunately have to end even though we could have kept talking for quite a while. It really is crazy just how much people can change. To be honest I didn’t think the two of us would ever see eye to eye again but I think we both became better people than who we were back in those days and now we can start over and the fact that such reconnection is possible made me really happy. It inspired me to reach out to an old friend from college who I certainly wasn’t on bad terms with the way I was with my ex but who I still hadn’t seen in quite a while and we’ll be reconnecting later this week which I’m quite looking forward to. Once we wrapped up I met up with “The Fisherman” and another friend from that group to cook dinner. We made some eggplant and pork which I’m told was delicious and some pasta which I can confirm for myself was good. Given the personality of me and “The Fisherman” we made a bunch of eggplant jokes but I told myself I’d limit myself to one here so the one I’ll go with was normally her boyfriend would be the one to give her eggplant but since he wasn’t around I guess I had to do it. Amongst the 3 of us I was definitely the least experienced chef so if “The Fisherman” was the head chef, the other friend would be the sous chef and I was the intern. I learned quite a few things from this including how to use a can opener which I never did until now. I may not have skill but I have a *can do* attitude Once we wrapped up cooking I headed to Midnight Runners to catch the last part of socializing. I caught up with “The Mamacita” and hung out for a bit before heading back. A meme comes to mind that I think perfectly encapsulates today Thursday Today I did some more work on my personal project and did an interview with a company I don’t really care about just for the practice. I then went on a walk and then went to bar night with “The Philosopher,” “The Mosher” and “Thats nuts”. Bar night was fun as usual with standard activities like “The Philosopher” rage baiting me about One Piece. Amusingly the bar had almost no beer which would really suck if I actually drank the stuff. Friday Today I did some more personal work and had another interview which was fine. In the evening I went to a pitch a friend dating event where friends get up on stage and present a power point presentation describing why you should date their friend who is also on stage. I made a presentation and was all set to have “The Quant” pitch me! Unfortunately I didn’t realize that the pitch tickets were separate from normal spectator tickets which already filled up. This was a bit of a setback since I was hoping the pitch would get me some attention. Sadly this meant I had to go out and talk to everyone myself which if you know me you can already see the problem here. There were about 24 of these presentations that I watched. Most of them were reasonable enough. One girl went who I thought would be cool although apparently she said to not go out with her if you’re weird which I realized was a bit of a disqualifier for me. “The Quant” even mentioned that I wear weird like a badge of honor which is usually true :D. As the presentations went on you could see people get more fatigued which is a good reminder to go early to stay in the zeitgeist. After the presentations concluded I kept a note of the people I liked and tried to find them. One of the girls was always with some of her friends which is a situation I didn’t exactly know how to penetrate. I mean if I’m trying to ask out a girl I can’t exactly do that with her friends around.  With her I settled on cold messaging her on insta since I found her on insta and we have some mutuals. This went about as well as you’d expect but I figure you miss 100% of the shots you don’t take. I had to scout around for a while until I found one such girl who was alone and I talked with her for a while. Interestingly she grew up in Prague so my recent trip there gave me some stuff to say! Eventually I did get her number and I need to message her at some point. While we were talking some other guy awkwardly came up and tried to ask her out. He commented on the fact that she mentioned biking in her presentation and asked if she’d be down to go on a bike ride tomorrow. She then said her bike was broken and wasn’t sure when it would be fixed. Honestly my heart goes out a bit to that guy. Its tough. Saturday The day starts off with trash pickup as per usual. I hadn’t been back at the Saturday pickup in a while so it was great to see everyone again. After pickup I get lunch with “John Wick,” “The Raja of Rhythm,” “The Yogi” and a friend of “The Yogi”. It was good to see them all again since I hadn’t seen them in quite a while. The friend of “The Yogi” is one of the few people I’ve met who I think is a troll in similar ways to me which was pretty cool to see. He spent a while doing a bit about how stuck up people from private schools are specifically because “The Yogi” was the only one amongst us who went to a private school but it was done in a pretty tasteful way :D. He also apparently has someone convinced for 8+ years that he doesn’t know what Disneyland is, which was just great. From there I went to a brief pregame at “John Wick’s” house and  then to a halloween party hosted by “The Writer”! One thing he did which made the party quite fun was he hid a bunch of toy skulls around the apartment with clues to where each one is. It was quite fun to solve these and the first 25 people to do so get a sticker. I had an advantage arriving early (read on time) and spent a bunch of time looking before anyone else got there and did it before anyone else. Sadly I started getting tired around midnight and headed out around then and got a bit of food with “The Raja of Rhythm” before heading home Sunday The day begins extra early today as instead of trash pickup I help “The Filmmaker” with his movie! I’m an extra in one of the dance scenes he has. Since its a dance scene I don’t have any lines to learn, instead I mainly spend time learning choreo. Despite having the least to do I’m pretty sure with my lack of coordination it takes me the longest to learn but nevertheless it was a good experience! For a bit of context we’re doing a scene in a MUNI where we dance across the length of a MUNI car. Given the challenges of doing this in a MUNI we first practice over in Dolores park until we have the moves down which takes a few hours and then we do it in the MUNI itself. We get lucky as there are very few people in the MUNI when we do it which makes the actual filming easier. The moves we do require a bunch of space which would have been really awkward in a large car. As it was I’m pretty sure we got some confused looks from the people in the car with us while we were doing this which I find kind of funny. We did this dance number to “The Subway” by Chapel Ronin. I never heard this song before and now I’ve got some pretty distinct memories dancing to it. In my opinion it's the kind of song that I can see why its popular even though I don’t really like it. It's too sad for me.  For extra irony the place where we got lunch after filming was playing another song by the esteemed Chapel. From there I caught up with “The Quant,” “The Taco,” “High Entropy,” and “The Lawyer” and watched most of them eat Poke and hung out in Dolores park. Afterwards I went to “The Mosher”’s for movie night with “The Philosopher,” “That’s nuts,” and “The Juggler”. We watched Airplane. It had been many years since I saw it and I forgot just how absurd the humor was, which was great! If you haven’t seen the movie I highly recommend it! We also watched Naked gun which ostensibly had a plot but if so I couldn’t find it amidst all the shooting and sex scenes. To be honest I was getting pretty tired after the long day and wanted to leave in the middle of this movie but I stayed because another friend was supposed to eat a whole bunch of bandito eggs which I wanted to see. It turns out the bandito eggs tasted horrible. I had a bite and was brought to tears with “The Mosher” concerned if I was ok. The friend had two bites before throwing the rest in the trash. Once that was done I made my eggscape and went home. Sadly by this point it was 10pm and didn’t have time to write the newsletter so its getting delayed a bit.

title: Episode 43-44
excerpt: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Belated birthday shoutout to “The Politician!” Hope your birthday bar crawl was fun. The birthday party (mentioned below) was! Request for content I’m going to be goin…
content: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Belated birthday shoutout to “The Politician!” Hope your birthday bar crawl was fun. The birthday party (mentioned below) was! Request for content I’m going to be going to a dating event next week where a friend makes a power point about me and pitches me. I’m having “The Quant” do this but if any of y’all have suggestions of things I should put in here let me know. Like if I were to make a powerpoint about me what do you think would be the best things Tuesday Today was a pretty chill day in Vienna. I wanted to mix things up and go on a hike in the nature surrounding the city. Granted Vienna is no SF but there is still at least a little bit to do. The best view I could find looked a little something like this A solid 5.7 out of 10. If I didn’t come from the Bay Area I might have rated it higher All in all the hike wasn’t the greatest but it was a change of pace so I’m glad I did it. When I got back to the main city I found they were shooting a movie in part of downtown Vienna I can’t quite tell what the movie is supposed to be about from what I see here. This looks to be a love story of sorts. My head cannon is that the woman is the scion of Vienna’s biggest hotdog industry and the man is a washed up smash bros champion who now works at Vienna’s retro gaming museum and against all odds they find a way to make it work. But who knows I’m just guessing here. After some more wandering that results in no noteworthy content I meet back up with “The Professor” and we find a cafe that actually has some good mango matcha latte and we hole up for a while and play Gomoku. When we get back to his apartment I lay down on the couch bed and after asking if I’m going to bed I say no I’m only making myself more comfortable and according to him I was soundly snoring two minutes later. Wednesday Since this is my last full day in Vienna I decide to do some of the more random stuff I thought about but never actually did. I went to Danube tower which has Europe’s tallest slide. I meant to take a video of myself riding down it only to realize I forgot to start the video so instead heres a doodle Also here are some views from the top of this tower Much like yesterday these views reinforce my opinion that Vienna is a city best viewed at ground level where you can look up at the imperial towers rather looking down on generic skyline with a couple interesting things if you squint hard enough. I got a slightly better experience when I went to a tower in St Stephen’s cathedral in the center of Vienna. Since this tower wasn’t as high up it wasn’t as disappointing Amusingly the elevator ride to the top of the tower was playing Sabrina Carpenter which definitely wasn’t the vibe I was expecting for a centuries old cathedral. I’d have gone with more Gregorian chants myself but hey if that's what the people of Vienna want than who am I to judge. What I will judge on the other hand was the labubu store that I saw. It's bad enough that I see these things in normal stores but to have a whole store for them makes me wonder if the arguments that civilization as we know it has morally rotted may have more merit than I initially anticipated. I won’t be showing any pictures here to save both your and my eyes from looking at them but it was a whole store of the little shits. At the request of “The Professor” I’ll highlight a bit he had going on for the last 3 days. Whenever we would meet up after he finished work he’d always send me a message to indicate that he was on the train headed my way. These would include things like Things are in motion that you couldn't possibly comprehend Events have been set in motion that cannot be undone The cards have been dealt, and the wheels of fate approach an inevitable end He was quite proud of this bit and at his request I included it here so you may all bask in his brilliance. We go to the same cafe as yesterday so I can performative male it up and get a strawberry matcha latte and after that its time to turn in and say goodbye to Vienna! Thursday I head to the airport early in the morning to catch my flight to Dubrovnik where I’ll be meeting up with my family. Funnily enough the Vienna airport actually had Switch games you could play at the gates to pass time :D. Not gonna lie this was possibly the most fun I’ve had at an airport waiting for a flight! Once we get going and start getting close to Dubrovnik I see scenery like this I’m excited for a nice change of pace from imperial city life! Curiously after descending for a while I notice we start ascending again. A minute later I hear an announcement in German which gets a bunch of people in the crowd laughing and applauding. The same announcement is said in English a moment later. “We will be going back to Vienna and landing in about an hour”. Wait what?! We’re going back?! Why?! The pilot doesn’t really give an answer for a bit so I come up with a list of guesses as to why A  weather issue A medical emergency An issue at the airport Eventually after looking at the forecast in Dubrovnik I find evidence of severe wind. Eventually the airline informs us that wind was indeed the issue. We land back in Vienna and its a mad dash as everyone goes to the airline counter to figure out what the airline is gonna do to help them out. When I finally get my turn I’m told that they can put me on a flight to Warsaw tonight and then catch a flight from Warsaw tomorrow. Initially I’m leaning towards this option but decided against it. Thankfully “The Professor” lets me stay at his place again and I instead decide to take a direct flight via Ryan Air the next day. Once I left the airport after traveling so far to get nowhere I met up with “The Professor” again and I got some really good orange chicken which was the perfect way to lift my spirits after the above. In the spirit of his bit above I figured I’d play along and send a message of my own in the format like so “Fate has unlocked a new canon event the consequences of which will ripple throughout the multiverse”. Incidentally my family who I’d be meeting up with was flying from London to Dubrovnik today as well. They hit the same issues I did only worse. While we flew directly back to Vienna they landed in a different city in Croatia and then after a bunch of people got off from there then they went back to London. Not only did they have a longer flight in both directions (2.5 hours for them vs 1 hour for me) they also waited a couple hours at the airport for the people leaving from there to do so before the plane went back to London. And of course they didn’t have a Professor to stay with so they had to work out hotels and stuff with the airport which sounded real fun from how they described it. Friday Alright its take two will our hero, protagonist, dude bro make it to Dubrovnik this time? We start off on the wrong foot (wing?) knowing that the flight will be delayed by 20 minutes. I do get some good news though that my family’s flight which left before mine did land in Dubrovnik so there is hope. Eventually my flight does take off and much to my surprise we do indeed land in Dubrovnik! Once I get settled I go out and start exploring the city and I have to admit it is actually cool. Maybe the wait was worth it? One fun fact about Dubrovnik is that its where Westeros was set in the Game of Thrones TV show which the town really leaned into with some of its stores. Admittedly the town itself while cool does feel a bit touristy. Its kinda like Venice in that the majority of the people here are tourists rather than locals which aren’t generally my favorite places to go to but its still got some cool elements. Once I got into the city I caught up with my family and we hung out for the rest of the day and got some dinner and sorbet. Saturday I started off the day with some solo travel. Unfortunately I tend to wake up about 4-5 hours before the rest of my family so my family trips often have at least 15% solo travel at the beginning of each day. Today I got away from the main city and went on some hikes. The nature here is much better than in Vienna with some actually nice views Unlike the places I went to yesterday I saw a bunch of people with their pets which made it feel more local which I appreciated. I walked around the area and at one point went to an ice cream place which was cash only. When I told him I had no cash he curtly said “Goodbye”. I found his matter of fact attitude pretty funny and after I left I wished I said something back like “Goodbye our meeting was as brief as it was memorable” to see how he would have reacted. Afterwards I went to a mountain nearby where you can overlook the entire area around Dubrovnik These views were great even by my standards! The hike itself was moderate, certainly not challenging especially for any of y’all seasoned Bay Area hikers or walkers but it was a great change of pace and it was the first sort of challenging walk on this trip. By this point my family had awoken so I went and caught up with them. We explored the city some more. I think there was a wedding here Today there were at least 4 different weddings that we had seen either on a boat or just around town. There were roving processions of people going around taking pictures and what not which was cool. Some of these weddings had a bunch of people dancing outside the church afterwards as a post wedding celebration and I figured it was only right I join in and dance along with them for the vibes. I also joined a tour of what looked like German old ladies at some point and looked like I was participating in it which my mom found pretty funny. A side story while I’m away While I was away I thought it would be a fun bit to host brunch and a boardgame day at my place without me being there. I tasked “The Taco” and “The Quant” with being my proxies. Ideally if anyone asked why I wasn’t at brunch they would keep saying I’m in the restroom for a while and we’d see how long it takes people to realize I’m not actually here. Sadly people caught on quick from what they told me. Also they all drove over to my place and for once couldn’t find parking and left. Sadly some bits just weren’t meant to be but thanks y’all for trying. It would have been great tho! Sunday I kicked things off by doing a wall tour of Dubrovnik and seeing the city from its massive walls. These walls were so nice it made me wonder if Mexico paid for them. Unfortunately it started raining as I was finishing up the walls which is extra unfortunate in an area with slippery cobblestone streets as it makes slipping quite easy. I had a couple close calls but I made it through without slipping. I caught up with my family and we walked around for a bit but in the spirit of Dubrovnik’s Game of Thrones lore you could say that Winter had come and a bit of a storm picked up and we all retreated to the AirBnB my family was staying at and hung out there for a while. We all kinda just chilled and didn’t really go out much after that. I played some Gomoku with my older sister which to my shagrin she picked up much faster than me. I was hoping based on my bouts with “The Professor” I could stay ahead of her for at least a day but she got good after like 5 games. Thankfully at this point I had seen pretty much everything I wanted to in Dubrovnik so if there was ever a time to be rained on this is a not terrible time for it. The one thing I wish I could have done was take a bus since I never got to see any of Dubrovnik’s public transit. The one time I didn’t walk I Ubered to meet up with my family which while probably efficient felt like one of the less Humza choices I could have made. Ah well. Monday Today we leave Dubrovnik and head to Istanbul. Unfortunately as we are taking a taxi to the airport it turns out my sister may have caught a bit of food poisoning which is really unfortunate especially on a travel day :(. To make things worse we learn before getting to the airport that the flight we were going to take got delayed by 1.5 hours. We don’t know why yet but when we get to the gate I learn its because the plane had a hard time landing because of … wind. Here we go again, right? Thankfully this gets resolved after only another half hour so it seems leaving Dubrovnik is not as bad as entering but its still a tad annoying. After landing and getting to Istanbul most of my family except me is pretty tired and stays in the hotel. I walk around for a while and check out a number of areas including The Grand Bazaar, downtown, and others. Hey “The Fisherman” I see your people here Perhaps most surprising of all I see a store that has the world record for largest unisex luxury perfume company which I didn’t think was a thing but here we are. I immediately rectify my mistakes in Dubrovnik and buy Istanbul’s version of a clipper card. Unlike in Prague and Vienna here you buy a physical card and tap on to get through turnstiles kinda like you would the BART. In Istanbul a lot of the public transit is bus and light rail which is pretty good overall except for if there is heavy traffic which there can be. At that point I think walking may actually be faster than bussing. Thankfully towards the end of the day my sister is starting to feel better from her food poisoning so hopefully things should be back on track tomorrow. Tuesday Today starts off interestingly enough when I wake up at 1AM and feel a strange lurch in my stomach. Initially I try to go back to bed but this feeling continues. I worry that I myself need to throw up which is what my sister did yesterday and unfortunately I realize I may be right. I make a beeline for the bathroom where I indeed do so. Oh fiddlesticks. Looks like what my sister had may not have been food poisoning and it may be a bug instead. I called my mom where I learned that my dad also threw up just 10 minutes before me. What timing, right? This confirms a bug and after some searching I suspect norovirus. Based on the fact my sister recovered so quickly I’m inclined to believe it. For those unaware norovirus is a bug symptomized by vomiting and diarrhea which typically goes away in 24-36 hours. In other words, it’s a day-long bug. I go back to bed and wake up later. It seems my sister is almost back to normal while my Mom and Dad are both feeling pretty weak :(. At this point my energy levels are actually fine and other than not feeling that hungry I don’t have that many symptoms so I actually head out albeit I can’t walk as fast because I notice when I walk fast my stomach feels a bit queasy. I also can’t really eat all that much :(. I meet up with my sister and we go through the bazaar together and then I chill for a while in my room. I then walk some more and get dinner with my sister and my Dad who is feeling well enough to make it outside while my Mom is not :(. All in all it definitely could have been worse. I easily had the most mild case as other than the vomiting episode in the morning I was pretty much ok today and I still got 18K steps which by Humza on vacation standards is low but you know you win some you lose some. Wednesday Thankfully today my whole family is now back at it. Of course the morning is still solo time which I spend going over to the Asian side of Istanbul where I go up a tall but disappointing tower and getting some really good lamb and eggplant in a less touristy neighborhood. At this point I catch up with my family and we walk around some more and take a ferry over to another neighborhood in Istanbul with some nice mosques. For those unaware Saltbae of the Saltbae meme is from Istanbul and has a chain of restaurants here that I saw There is a “Saltbae burger” which costed $28. I wanted to try it for the bit but I didn’t wanna pay that much for it. Thursday Today my vacation comes to an end and I come back to the U.S. Things are generally pretty uneventful on my journey back here. The only somewhat interesting thign was the fact that Istanbul happens to be one of the most security intense airports in the world which I learned by the fact that to get to my gate I had to Go through a screening where I take out my stuff and put it through a conveyor belt Go through passport control Repeat step 1 Have my passport and boarding pass checked and stamped 3 separate times right at the gate In case anyone was wondering why step 4 has 3 of the same checks I asked the people running the checks and they gave me a pretty vague answer. I looked it up online afterwards and apparently its because these checks are run by different agencies. Also apparently these checks are requested by the country you are flying into and because of terrorist activity in Turkey the U.S requests a lot of these checks. Thanks unc Sam! After a 13.5 hour flight I made it back home! Originally I was planning on going to bar night and catching up with “The Philosopher” and the usual gang but I instead crashed :(. I think this year I’ve travelled more than any other in recent memory having been gone for 4.5 weeks. Generally I only travel 2 weeks max a year. Some of you may know that I go on record as finding travel to generally be overrated. Don’t get me wrong I don’t dislike it but I think people tend to make it out as some amazing life changing experience and while I think it's fun I don’t strictly speaking think it's that much better than any other hobby. It doesn’t help that people list it generically as a hobby in a way that tells me almost nothing about them and kinda becomes a buzzword. I will concede though that when I think back on the trip it did feel like a lot more happened in these 2 weeks than generally does. Usually when I think back over a 2 week span I’m able to mentally compress a lot of it as I generally do a lot of the same things whether it's the same old work, same old trash pickup and so on. It was also cool being in a different environment. With that being said though I did also definitely get fomo especially as the trip went on. I missed out on stuff I would have liked to be here for like trash pickups, poker night (with Leo coming back no less), “Granola Girlie” eating her six cans of beans and other things too. Granted I’m sure a lot of these things will still be here when I’m back but nonetheless as someone who greatly values community it did start to weigh on me after a bit and I was definitely excited to come back. One other thing I find interesting as well is that after spending 3-4 days in a city I generally get bored and want to move on and start walking around somewhere else. SF on the other hand I still enjoy walking around even now. Maybe it's the fact that with SF I get a kind of joy I only get being somewhere for a long amount of time, but I also think its just because SF is a pretty great city and being away makes me appreciate some of the things I might otherwise take for granted here. Friday This winds up being a pretty chill day. I start by going to my favorite view in Tank Hill shortly after sunrise and looking at the city. I see someone walking their dog and I get treated to this lovely picture I do some admin stuff like laundry and so on to ease back into being here and then I go to a nightmarket in Chinatown which winds up being pretty reasonable. I have a mochi and chicken riceball which winds up tasting better after the fact. It turns out “Olives” is back in town for her actual going away. For anyone unaware she made a soft exit to New York a few months ago but said she was coming back to have a proper going away party which happened tonight. One of her friends was moving to L.A so they did a split theme party with half New York decorations and half L.A. The party itself was great. I wish I could have stayed longer but I have something early in the morning tomorrow so I call it around midnight right as rage cage is going. Saturday Unlike most Saturday’s back in the Bay I don’t start off with trash pickup today and instead do Diplo’s run club. This is a 5K in GGP followed by a Diplo concert. For this endeavor I’m joined by “The Shadow Brigade,” “The Enabler,” “The Dentist,” “La Tacqueria Royalty,” and a friend of the dentist. The 5K itself is pretty straightforward. Amusingly the friend of the dentist wonders if we will see Daniel Lurie since he is pretty involved in community events like this and not 30 seconds later we see him running considerably ahead of us. He manifested that one :D.  Afterwards there was a Diplo concert. Well ok first there was an Austin Mills concert followed by a Diplo concert. I’m not a huge follower of this genre of music but honestly in my opinion there wasn’t that much of a difference between the two in terms of quality. They both generally seemed about the same. I think it was a cool experience but I’m not sure I would do it again. By the end I was pretty ready to leave considering it was a 2.5 hour concert in total. One thing which helped was that “The Professor” was hosting friend office hours on a teams call which I joined in the last half hour of the concert. This helped both in terms of dealing with Diplo fatigue and just general noise fatigue.  It looked kinda like this It was honestly a pretty good setup as I could still hear Diplo just at less noisy levels and I could hear “The Professor” and “The Kpop dancer” in the friend office hours. The one downside was I couldn’t actually speak in the friend office hours all that much on both sides since I didn’t wanna be that guy talking at the concert and on the office hours side there would have been a lot of background noise. From there we went to get brunch at a french place which I left a great Yelp review for. Amusingly while we are at brunch somebody texts “La Taqueria Royalty” and asks him if his family actually owns La Tacqueria. Turns out the reason that person texted him is because he is dating someone who reads my newsletter and learned indirectly about the lore that way which I found quite amusing. Through “La Taqueria Royalty” I learn that this person wants to meet me and thinks I seem fun. If you’re seeing this I’m down to meet you too. Come to Midnight Runners some time! :D . Afterwards I went to Game Parlor for “The Politician”’s birthday party. It turns out one of his friends also has a birthday so it wound up being a joint birthday party which was pretty cool. We played a bunch of games including a Clue like murder mystery game, a redneck based game of life, and others. I see Settlers of Catan setup but everyone is just sitting around the game chatting which is in my opinion the best way to play Settlers of Catan (that is to say you don’t). I would have loved to stick around more but me and “The Writer” head off to go to a bonfire hosted by “The Ravenkeeper”. It had been a while since I went to a bonfire so it was cool to see. We wound up getting a bunch of free pizza because someone else was having his own party and none of his friends showed up after an hour and a half :(. We invited him to come join us but he decided to go home instead. After a while it started getting quite cold which greatly diminished my will to stay. I was having a great time but man was I freezing. Sadly because I was out all day I layered more for the early morning activities than the evening ones which feels like a mistake an SF veteran like me shouldn’t be making. Big oof. On the outside I probably looked like this On the inside it was more like this though I began to get intrusive thoughts. What if instead of being here I was in bed eating lamb pasta. This is fun and all but rawr I’m cold. Eventually  I made my decision that I needed to leave when I realized I spent more time thinking about being cold than actually having fun. At that point I decided to head out (once “The Ravenkeeper" got back from the restroom so I could actually say goodbye). It took about another 15 minutes for that and then I headed home. Sunday Today for the first time in weeks my day actually starts with trash pickup. Since I had been gone for a while I managed to get “The Quant” to join me. It was also “Olives” last trash pickup before her hard exit so I hung out with her along with “The Notetaker”. On the whole this was one of the more lowkey Sunday pickups I had been to in a while which was nice. It was great finally being back at a pickup after so long. I did the math and I realized I hadn’t missed this many trash pickups in over 2 years. At one point we were all going to go to a club called El Rio but when I learned there was a $35 cover I opted not to since it didn’t seem worth it to me since I don’t drink nor would I want to pay that much to go clubbing. I go home and finally write up the newsletter. I really hope I don’t delay a newsletter this much again :P.

title: Episode 42
excerpt: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Shout out to “Granola Girlie” for being able to eat 6 cans of beans and become the new bean king. I previously tried to eat 6 cans of beans twice and failed miserably…
content: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Shout out to “Granola Girlie” for being able to eat 6 cans of beans and become the new bean king. I previously tried to eat 6 cans of beans twice and failed miserably in both cases :(. To be honest I wasn’t sure if someone would do it but glad to see I was wrong! Monday Today starts off as a pretty normal day. I do a bit of reading and walk around but nothing out of the ordinary. In the evening though I meet up with “The Philosopher,” "That's Nuts,” “The Juggler,” and “The Mosher” to go for a walk. “The Philosopher” and “The Juggler” planned a route specifically with me in mind which I really appreciate! Thanks y’all for doing that, it was a lot of fun! We wound up starting in the Mission and going up to Buena Vista Park and then down to inner Sunset for … Kogi Gogi! Y’all really do know how to do something for me <3. Didn’t realize how good Buena Vista Looked in the Sunset Tuesday-Wednesday Today I boarded a flight to Prague. Since I got laid off and had some extra time I thought it might be fun to go back to Europe. Part of this is also because my family happens to be in Europe for a vacation I originally turned down. On top of this “The Professor” moved to Vienna so why not pay him a surprise visit? There are no direct flights to Prague so I wind up going SF -> Frankfurt -> Prague. The flights themselves were long but relatively uneventful. When I was transferring in Frankfurt I had to go through multiple buses to get to where I needed to go which makes the shuttle system in SF and many other airports look like magic in comparison. While on the flight I finally decided to nominate myself for Yelp Elite. For those unaware I got inspired by “The Dentist” and have wanted to become Yelp Elite for a while. My reasoning being that there are Yelp Elite events you can go to and I’m trying to make more friends so I figured this could be a good way to do that. One thing though is I hate food reviews as a concept so to make it more palatable to me I only leave food reviews at places I don’t eat at. In other words I go with friends, take pictures of their food, and go off of vibes to write a review. Now that I have 20+ such reviews under my belt I figured I’d nominate myself. Let's see how this goes! After a short flight I land in Prague and start to check it out. I quickly go over to my hostel and check in and start going out for drinks with some other travellers. Far and away I’m travelling for the shortest time at only 2 weeks. Everyone else seems to be traveling for a month plus with many people going for multiple months. To be honest I don’t know how people travel for so long without getting sick of it. If I was away from home for that long I’d be pretty sad. While this trip has been fun I have missed out on many things including “The Hombre’s” going away party, “Granola Girlie” eating 6 cans of beans and many more. If I extended this trip too long, who knows what else. I met an interesting cast of characters including one guy who had “every job you can imagine” including building construction, bar tending, landscaping and more. He’s one of those who is travelling until a fixed budget has ran out. I met someone else who was very coyish about saying where she's from. Generally at hostels the standard ice breaker is to say where you are from but she refused instead asking us to guess. We all put our racial profiling hats on and guessed everything from Vietnamese, Canadian, Netherlands and more. Apparently the answer was Indonesian which was a hard fought struggle. There were some other folks too but I can’t remember anything notable about them at the moment. After a while we all go out and walk around the city. We wind up going to St. Charles’s bridge which is a famous bridge in the city with a whole bunch of statues on it I didn’t realize how blurry this picture was until now yet Here we are Less blurry version of the picture above with AI Thursday Sadly today begins at a temperature of 40 degrees and raining. Its dreadful weather yet I can’t waste a good Prague so venture out I must. Naturally I didn’t bring an umbrella with me but thankfully the hostel I’m at has one I can borrow which winds up being a life saver. I go to a breakfast place which has a small serving of pancakes that winds up being perfectly ok. It didn't spark joy but it wasn’t terrible either. After walking around for another 10 minutes the rain picks up and I go inside to another place in part just to escape the weather. The pancakes here are absolutely terrible and I get through about one bite before deciding to leave. Thankfully though the waitress doesn’t make me pay for them on account of only eating a single bite. I go back to the hostel and meet up with some of the gang and we go to a 3rd place where I get a beef goulash that is actually pretty good. They thought I was joking when I said it was the best meal I had today though. Apparently the cafe I went to was one that both Einstein and Kafka regularly went to which they were not shy about advertising. Sadly I think the average IQ of the cafe just went down after I went though. Chameleon the cafe had. Looked so serious I thought It was a German chameleon After breakfast I split off and went to Prague Castle which actually looked really cool. I’m a sucker for very elaborate architecture I walk around a bit more and get to a good vantage point and get some views of the city. The views are nice but the weather certainly dampens them :(. After a bit more walking the cold and jet lag demand I take a nap so I make a strategic pivot to conserve energy. A few hours later I do a bit more walking, get some food, and then I go out to another bar with some of the folks from the hostel. Sadly this bar lets people smoke indoors which is terrible for me. I lasted all of 2 minutes before promptly doing an American exit. When I get back I chat with some new folks who moved into my room. Among them I meet a pair of 18 year old British boys who have been traveling on their own for around a month now. I’m intrigued as its rare in the U.S to find 18 year olds who are already traveling by themselves and are well versed in the “adult arts” (smoking, drinking, gambling etc.). I think this is because the drinking age in Europe is lower than the States (16/18 vs 21, and underage drinking is less of a big deal). Come to think of it, I wasn't carded once when I went to bars in Europe which was interesting in and of itself. I also met another pair of female British tweens who wanted my opinion on whether what they were planning to wear for their night out was too slutty. Considering that it was 40 degrees out and just rained earlier I was impressed they could wear short shorts and a tank top out. Personally I thought they were built different. Friday The weather is finally not raining and I’m ready to seize the day! One of my favorite parts of Prague is the fact that you can find towers like the below just randomly scattered throughout the city. I never really looked too much into the history of the city but I like to imagine these were used in case invaders came and they needed a place to take them out from. Maybe not, who knows but that's the Humza canon anyway. These steps were narrow af I went to the Old Square in Central Prague after this to see some more towers and views Did I mention Kafka lived here? Some of my favorite interior art I’ve seen On this trip From there I go get banana pancakes at a place that would put Plow to shame (yeah I said it “The Plower”), and then go and find a view of the whole city at Petrin tower which is sick. I wandered around a while longer and found a store that sold medieval armor. I actually considered buying the helmet above until I realized it cost $112. I’m not paying that much for it. If it was $10 I think I actually would have done it. When I get back to the hostel I find that I finally became Yelp Elite! Big thanks to everyone who I went to a restaurant with where I didn’t eat. Couldn’t have done it without y’all! I’ll check out some Yelp Elite events and see how it is. If I don’t like it I may have a spectacular crashout where I say what I did and see how the other Yelp Elites react. I’m hoping there will be some good events. Saturday Today I wrap up Prague by getting breakfast at the same place I did yesterday and then going to one last tower to end my stay. This tower actually had an art museum with some pieces I quite liked What a beaut For fun I decided to imagine myself in the same style as above with Chat GPT What I got was something that I really want to put on my Hinge profile but I know I shouldn’t So cool! From there I head off to the train station to go to Vienna. Interestingly this train station had a book store with its very own Manga section which I wasn’t expecting. After a 4 hour train ride I find myself in Vienna. I get quite excited here as my plan to surprise “The Professor” is finally underway. For those unaware, “The Professor” recently moved to Vienna for a job and part of my motivation for this Europe trip was to come and visit him. He isn’t aware of this at the moment which makes it all the more fun. I got his apartment address from his younger sister and plan to show up there when we have a group call scheduled to make sure he is home at the time. As I make my way through Vienna I have to be extra cautious to ensure I don’t run into him before I’m ready. I camped out at a Five Guys for a bit since a pescatarian like him would never show up there. Eventually I make my way to his apartment and with about a half hour before the call I park myself right outside the door. The anticipation grows ever more. I’m really excited to see the look on his face and waiting the last half hour is torture. I almost break early but thankfully “The Quant” keeps me on track Eventually the call starts and I’m finally ready to make my move. To make the bit even better I specifically asked “The Quant” to start the call by asking “The Professor” how he has been liking the city and if he has gone to any meetups. This would prompt “The Professor” to say we should all come visit him and then right on cue I would ring his doorbell. This works exactly as I imagined it would and when he opens the door his exact words  were “Humza … what the fuck?! … Well come in I guess.” Not gonna lie this might be one of the best bits I have ever done. To help lay the groundwork for this me and “The Quant” made it look like I was still in SF when I was in Europe. For example we posted some photos in the group chat that were taken last week but posted them on Wednesday This was actually taken at Midnight Runners last week not this week I also had to be sure not to look at any messages outside of normal PST hours to avoid suspicion here. Once I filled “The Professor,” “The Taco,” and “The Plower” in on the joke, we played a game of online Dune which I lost but I won the war here. Sunday Today I largely hang out with “The Professor” as he shows me around. We get food and then go to a gaming history museum. This museum has games from all different types of consoles such as the old sega genesis, arcade games like Streetfighter, all the way to the modern switch. It was pretty interesting playing the OG version of Mariokart and seeing just how far we’ve come. We vibe around some more before going to a carnival in the evening. Vienna has a standing fair over in a park which is certainly … something. I wind up going gokarting in which I have exactly as much fun as I look like I’m having. Can you feel the joy? Monday Today while “The Professor” was at work I had a relatively chill day wandering around the city and taking a nap in the park. I saw some more of Vienna’s architecture which actually looks pretty sick. After that I decided to go to a run club. Yesterday I actually saw a run club running around and wanted to find one to do. The one that I found tended to attract a lot of locals which was kinda cool except for the fact that by default everyone was speaking in German and I had to really fish to find people speaking in English. Even I couldn’t imagine myself being like “Yo mind if I disrupt this whole conversation and y’all speak in an entirely different language here”. The run itself was pretty good. We did a 6K run through the perimeter of Vienna’s city centre that hit up a bunch of fancy buildings. One thing I noticed about this run is that people were running at their own pace, meaning if you didn’t know where you were going it might be a bit difficult. Thankfully I was keeping up with someone who did. This made me appreciate how good a job Midnight Runners does of having captains throughout the run guiding people. After the run I hit up the bar and tried talking with people. As mentioned a lot of conversations defaulted to German which made them impenetrable to me. I did find some English speaking folks and chatted with them for a while. A couple people doubted I did the run since I was wearing jeans and a jacket which forced me to whip out the Strava shown above (for what its worth out of ~40 people I was the 4th person to finish which meant I definitely finished before the doubters 😤) When I’m mingling with some of the runners they ask me if I run before and I reply with one of my usual retorts (Humza joke #5 as “The Philosopher” might put it), “only from my problems” and I get stone silence followed by a … “thats great”. Clearly that joke didn’t land. The Austrian mind can’t comprehend. I catch back up with “The Professor” and we get dinner and try unsuccessfully to find a good ice cream place. Interestingly a lot of the places here don’t like it when you sample. At one place he asked the lady working there glared at us and asked if we were actually gonna buy something. I was almost tempted to respond to such pettiness with pettiness of my own by making sure to sample and *not* buy something but thankfully cooler heads prevailed.

content: In Honor of The Climber Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday Today was a pretty chill day. I enjoyed the nice weather and walked around. I didn’t go anywhere or do anything of particular note. Perhaps the best part was when I went to Tank Hill early in the morning and enjoyed one of my favorite views overlooking the city. Tuesday Today after meandering for a bit in the morning I thought it would be fun to spontaneously do The Double Cross trail. I start off around Pier 23 and make my way towards Lake Merced. I make it a goal to go as aggressively as I can without running so I wind up going at about a 16 min/mile or 3.8 mph pace On the way to Coit Tower A nice view of the Embarcadero View from Mt. Olympus. One of the more Slept on SF views Tank Hill Twin Peaks                                                            West Portal Stern Grove Random lake at Stern Grove It was a fun hike but overall nothing particularly notable. Between this and the regular Crosstown trail I think I like the regular one more but it's pretty close. At this point I had done hikes of this distance enough that I didn’t feel like I was breaking new frontiers here. Perhaps the most interesting part was towards the end when I was at Stern Grove and a bunch of dogs came up and barked at me. One of the dog owners informed me I was at a dog park and I just sighed and moved on. I think at that point 5 or 6 different dogs were barking at me. Maybe it was because I was walking fast, maybe they didn’t like the cut of my jib, maybe they sensed some demon aura inside me. Who knows. It certainly did dampen the walk for all of 3 minutes. From then on I got a bit spooked whenever I saw a dog on the walk. The same thing happened when I finished the walk and was headed back. At that point only one dog was barking at me but it was doing so quite aggressively and blocked my main way down since I couldn’t overtake the dog and its owner. I entered a Mexican standoff as I stared down the mutt and shot it my fiercest look of annoyance. After a minute I backed down and waited for the scamp to walk on by which it eventually did as I wished for the dog equivalent of stepping in gum to happen to it. On my way home I took the bus; going through the south west part of SF I shared the bus with a bunch of teenyboppers who talked about classes and clubs they were doing and it took me back to my time in high school. It was kinda amusing reminiscing on my time taking classes and doing clubs like that. I think in my time living here I never had a bus with so many kids on it. Sometimes you have a few but never a whole bus full of them. Afterwards I went to a Krav Maga class which was fun. This one taught a different style from the one I’m used to so the class was mainly reviewing fundamentals but with slight twists. It was a good time. Wednesday Today was another chill day. I walked around and laid down in Duboce Park for a while. Then I went to Midnight Runners with “The Quant”. Thursday I started off by doing Almost Friday Run Club. I tried to make it a bit harder by carrying my air purifier with me. Back in episode 24 I did this at Midnight Runners and actually succeeded. Unfortunately this club is smaller and tends to run at a more homogenous (and faster) pace which I couldn’t keep up with so I just ran by myself for a while while carrying the air purifier and caught up with everyone afterwards. Sadly after the run club I received some horrible news that one of my friends “The Climber” had passed away. When I first read the message I was shocked. It seemed so surreal. He was pretty much my age. How the hell does something like this happen? To be perfectly honest I wasn’t going to write about this given the subject matter but for reasons I’ll get into later today I ultimately figured this was the right thing to do. I felt a sense of despair that hung over me for quite a while. Throughout the day I imagined him next to me as I shuffled along.  Conversations we had would flood back to me. I had to resist the urge to cry in a Whole Foods as I reminisced. I didn’t really leave my place much after that. Later in the day I got myself up and met with “The Hombre” for gelato in Mission Dolores. He would be moving away to the UK for a job and I wanted to make sure I saw him before he left. Best of luck man, I know you’ll kill it in your new role! From there I went to a service for “The Climber” at his old apartment. As part of the service people brought things for an apartment shrine that was being set up. I wasn’t sure what I should bring for the shrine. Flowers seemed like a standard choice but when I got the message that he passed I was told “he really loved your newsletter and sense of humor” so I knew there had to be something more personal I could leave. I thought about it for a while and what I ultimately landed on was leaving some of my six of hearts playing cards along with some flowers. For those unaware I have a “magic trick” I like to do in which I ask someone to pick a card and I try to retrieve it after shuffling the deck. The joke of this trick is they are all 6 of hearts and thus it is very easy to pick. Its the easiest way to have a tangible form of a joke and I never got to do the trick with him unfortunately so I wanted to leave a little bit of it behind because this is one of my personal favorite jokes that I do, while the cards themselves aren’t special in general they are special to me and I want to give a little something to him, and finally to wish him six-cess in the after life. I am Muslim and believe in an afterlife afterall (I prayed for him before this as well but that's separate). The service itself starts off understandably pretty somber as we all gather around and share some of our favorite stories about “The Climber”. Throughout the event it's heartwarming to get reminders of what I already knew: How kind he was, how funny he was, how down he was to do anything, how he was really good with kids. I met his mom, sister, and brother at this event. To be honest I can’t imagine what they are going through with all this. As the event goes on the mood becomes a bit lighter as the ice breaks and we share more stories about him and even start laughing a bit. One of his apartment mates makes a toast and reminds us that he wouldn’t want us to feel sad and we toast to him with a bit of a smile. Throughout all this I’m reminded of a quote from one of my favorite mangas called One Piece When does a man die? When he is hit by a bullet? No! When he suffers a disease? No!  When he ate a soup made out of a poisonous mushroom? No! When his heart stops? No! A man dies when he is forgotten! I won’t forget you “The Climber’. As part of the event we all went around and shared some of our favorite stories with him. Unfortunately most of y’all reading this newsletter never got to know him, or what an amazing person he was so I want to share some stories here. Some of these may be in previous newsletters but I want to write them all out here anyway. Climber Story 1 One time I did Midnight Runners with “The Climber,” “Sergeant Sassy,” “La Taqueria Royalty,” and one of our other friends and we went to a restaurant afterwards for dinner. While there we were talking about hobbies and I mention that I’ve done improv in the past and “The Climber” and I do some impromptu improv for a while centering around a white sauce condiment we see on the table and a fictitious duck that we co parent after our divorce. A lot of times people will be interested when I say I do improv but very rarely will people be so down to do it with me spontaneously. Afterwards we got into a discussion regarding titty milk and answering the age old question of whether you would drink the titty milk of someone rich with really good genes. To be perfectly honest even amongst all my friends there are very few who I think I can truly go full unhinged humor on. He was one of them. I could take the conversation in any unhinged place and he could match me titty milk for tatty milk. Climber Story 2 One time after Midnight Runners me, him, and another friend were sitting around a table and discussing our biggest dating failures. At one point I bring up the dating posters I made He found this so amusing that he asked everyone around what they thought about it which led to a whole bunch of interesting conversations. He had this childlike enthusiasm, energy, and excitement that felt downright infectious. I couldn’t help but laugh as he eagerly showed everyone this poster. I mentioned this earlier but originally I wasn’t going to write about this. In part because I was worried it was wrong to do so, and in part because I wasn’t sure I wanted to write about this myself. Ultimately what convinced me to do so was as the event was ending I talked with "Sergeant Sassy” and she asked me if I was going to write about it. Originally I responded “I don’t know” because I wasn’t quite sure at the time. She said I should as he would have wanted it. I thought back to how excited he was to first read one of these newsletters and realized I should do so for him. As I said I believe in an afterlife so if somehow you’re able to read this up there I hope you like this “The Climber”. I really do. You truly were an amazing friend, there were so many more adventures I wanted to have with you. You had authentic, radiant energy. You had one of the best smiles and laughs. Rest in Peace. When the event ended I kinda wanted to just go home and chill. There was a bar night planned but at first I wasn’t feeling in the right head space to attend. Ultimately I decided to go because I remembered that he was the kinda guy who would always be down for something and always bring positive energy and the vibes. If I truly want to remember him, if I truly want to keep him with me, that's what I need to do now. Of course I’m still quite sad but I need to be there for the people I have in my life right now and so I decide to go. We go to a bar we don’t usually go to over near Union Square. It's not as homey as The Fermentation Lab that we usually go to but it's a nice change of pace. As usual I don’t drink but I did get a raspberry from the collection of raspberries that they top some of their drinks with. The owner said he wanted to charge me but one of the other bartenders slipped it my way. Apparently they throw out most of their raspberries at the end of the night so really I’m doing them a favor. Before we conclude this section I want to say that given the recency of what happened I still think about “The Climber” a lot this week but I won’t be writing about it any more. Both because there isn’t really anything I could say that I haven’t already, and because in the spirit of what I can best do I want to focus on what I’m doing for everyone I have in my life right now. And finally I want to thank all of you who are reading this right now. I’m grateful to have so many amazing friends in my life. Another thing I was reminded of throughout the day was this xkcd comic about saying final words. Of course, there was no way I could have known that the last time I saw him would be the last but it did come to mind. Friday The day begins with a walk followed by another Krav Maga class. In this class I learn a lot about how to escape from a chokehold if someone wants to do a head choke so I’m that much more ready for the streets of SF. Or sex. Either one really. Afterwards I do a pilates class which I thought would be pretty easy but winds up kicking my tooshie. The whole class I have to run back and forth on this stupid machine doing plancks, squats with a leg extended, and various other exercises which suck. The class is also incredibly fast paced. Its “do this random exercise”, “ do that random exercise”. Does the instructor ever explain what they are? No. Also I have to take these red and yellow pins and alternatingly place them in the machine for various reasons I don’t quite understand. My glutes are still feeling it a bit as I’m writing this. I can’t say I really loved it but I guess I’m glad I did it. Perhaps I’ll do it again at some point. Afterwards I met up with “The Quant” and “Mirandom thoughts” and we walked around and got dessert at a cafe over in Inner Richmond called Sweet Mango Dessert cafe. According to “The Quant” apparently the place ripped off of some place in Hong Kong down to having the same menu items.  I had the nothing which is as delicious as it always is and I left a yelp review here Saturday The day started off with trash pickup which was a good time. From there I go to a bbq hosted by “Granola Girlie” which is a great time. I tried a grilled carrot for the first time which was better than I thought it would be. Not quite as good as grilled beef but still this could do in a pinch! Her house has a narrow spiral staircase which reminds me of going up some old towers in Europe. Not the better parts of going up the old towers in Europe but part of that experience nevertheless. Afterwards one of my other trash friends has a 30th birthday in Dolo that I go to which is good fun. Finally I get dinner with a friend over by El Farlito and we go on a walk from Mission down to Oceanview over in Southwest SF. While in Mission we pass by the low rider festival thats happening As we walk through Oceanview I see some discounted Painted Ladies Are these the painted ladies we have at home? Sunday Another trash pickup another fictitious dollar. After trash pickup I get brunch over at Cracked and Battered with “The Taco,” “The Plower,” “The Sparkle,” “The Quant,” “Mirandom thoughts,” “The Mushroom hunter,” “The pickleballer,” and a couple other folks. I get my usual which is as scrumptious as one can hope for. Review here. I’m wondering if now is finally the time I try to apply for Yelp elite. Can I finally crack through the gates of Valhalla? From there we go back to the Humza cave and play some board games. We play a game called “Trial by Trolley” from the people who made Cyanide and Happiness. This game centers around two teams creating absurd trolley problem scenarios and a judge picking which group of people to run over. You can put people that you don’t want the trolley to run over (a group of kids, someone who made the cure for cancer), and people the trolley should run over (someone who spoils movies and tv shows, corrupt pharma executives). Generally people try to judge based on what would save lives but when its my turn to judge I give everyone a little surprise by judging based on what would kill the most and I decide to save the group of people that has an assassin on it as a form of future investment. Then we play Secret Hitler in which I manage to get trounced in every game. For whatever reason everyone thinks I’m always suspicious no matter what I do. Completely baseless naturally but what can you do? Afterwards I write up the newsletter.

content: Water Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday After just coming back from Europe I wake up in the middle of the night trying and failing to sleep. Ultimately I get up and go to work with a bit of a headache but fine enough. It was nice being back and seeing everyone. A lot can happen in startup land in a week so I start off trying to get my bearings back. After a bit of catching up I settle in and work proceeds normally. Around 7 or so I can start to feel the jetlag coming so I head home and a short while later I crash. Tuesday My jetlag still persists as I wake up intermittently. This bout is a bit interesting as I wake up to see a message from my manager asking me to meet outside a cafe in Hayes Valley around 8:15. For some context we generally have standup at 10 so this is definitely abnormal. I’m too tired to question what it means at the moment so I think nothing and go back to bed. When I wake up I head off to this meeting wondering if I’m getting fired or something. I hadn’t gotten any sort of warning or PIP so I discounted this and headed over to the meeting. I get there and my manager immediately opens with “I want to keep this conversation short because it won’t be easy for either of us” and my heart sinks. Turns out I am in fact being laid off. I won’t go into full details here but the short version is that the skills that I’m strongest at aren’t the ones the company needs. I won’t go into the full details here but perhaps a short version is that originally the assumption is the company would be going deep on a particular set of skills which was originally what I interviewed for. While I could work on other projects it evidently wasn’t up to the standard they wanted and so chose to let me go. My manager did say some conciliatory stuff with this like “When this happens it's generally the fault of the employer” and so on. If I’m being honest here my one complaint was I wish I was given more warning as I did feel pretty blindsided by this. I’m also not sure how I feel about this having been done early in the morning at a random spot outside of work. Interestingly my manager explicitly said it wasn’t because of the vacation I took and that he said he was glad I took it and that it was well earned. I didn’t even think about that at the time but some other people asked me about that when I told them given the timing so sharing that here. For a while I’m just sorta stunned. Its really. Wow. There have been times where I’ve been stressed and I’ve thought about, fantasized even, about this sort of thing happening. In those fantasises I’d always respond with some sort of witty retort, laugh, maybe do something cool. Here I was closer to a deer in the headlights. Ok thats not entirely accurate I follow along enough in conversation but I certainly didn’t have the confidence I did in my fantasies. Once the conversation wraps up I walk home. I’m stunned enough that walking home kinda feels like I’m walking through water. Steps feel slower and more measured. The mental burden I’m carrying in my mind translates to a slow and dreary gait. To get myself out of a funk I start by just doing the things I normally couldn’t do at this time. I do laundry, I get some groceries, anything really to feel a bit more productive and keep myself moving. In what I guess is the job equivalent of a rebound I finally respond to a Meta recruiter who had been emailing me for the last while and set up an intro call. I spend most of the day doing nothing of any real value as I process what has happened. If I’m being objective there is some truth to the fact that this job probably wasn’t the best fit for me. There were times when I thought about the fact that while we use ML for the problems it is ultimately pretty surface level and not really related to the things I had been doing prior.  Also I’ve certainly had to work longer hours than I had before and dropped some of the hobbies I used to do as a result. Where do I go from here? What's next? I feel like I’m staring out into a sea of open possibilities. Thankfully I have saved enough that I don’t need to scramble immediately to find something which I am deeply grateful for. As of writing this newsletter I don’t have a solid next plan. We shall see what happens. Later in the day I have a call with the Meta recruiter (“The Rebound”?) and it winds  up being an incredibly soulless exchange where she asks me how many years of experience I have along with my programming languages with the same level of passion I have towards cleaning my apartment while I respond in turn with the passion I only reserve for clipping my toenails. Afterwards I plan to go home and visit my parents, an activity which again I don’t normally have time to do during the week. I have an unusually hard time getting out of bed which generally seldom happens to me. Lethargy getting out of bed isn’t generally amongst the Humza demons. Its almost like I had to fight someone else's demon. Or maybe the demon was loaned out to my collection. Nevertheless I get out and go home. It's nice seeing my family and they definitely appreciated the chocolate I brought back from Switzerland. We catch up for a while only for the jetlag demon to promptly one shot me around 8. Wednesday I’m still at home so I decided to go for a walk around my hometown which I haven’t done in years. Generally I’m either too busy to come back home, or spending time with my family when I am. In the morning everyone but me is working so I take the chance to go for a walk to Tiburon which I don’t think I did since high school. Back then a 1.5 hour walk to Tiburon was on the upper end of what I’d do, and a 3 hour walk to Sausalito was the height of my powers. Oh how things have changed. After going home and spending a bit longer with my family I head back for run club. The run itself isn’t too notable except for the fact that I see "Sergeant Sassy” who mentions that I bungled the origin story of her nickname in the newsletter when I first introduced her and requested an addendum. For the first time in newsletter history I made an addendum which can be found here. She even added the request for an addendum as part of her Strava for the run Sadly I can’t stay for the whole run as I have other fish to fry. Or perhaps more accurately “The Juggler” does as I go to his place for a fish fry. There I saw “The Philosopher” and appropriately enough “The Fisherman”. I really wish I liked fish more as it looked delicious but sadly did not taste that way to me :(. Big thanks to “The Juggler” for putting together was fun! Thursday I go to run club in the morning and for the first time I actually decide to do the whole run. Usually I either show up at the end for the post run hang or I try but fail to keep up since my legs are still sore from Wednesday night run club but today I managed the whole way through. Once I go home I decide to start testing the water by applying to jobs that I’m not really that interested in but figure may as well apply for / interview with to shake off any rust I have. After some time of this I decide to do a trash pickup in the middle of the day over in the Marina. Only me and the organizer actually show up to this so I wind up spending an hour and a half picking up trash by myself which is actually a pretty relaxing experience.
