Its essentially just walking around which I enjoy anyway. I chat with the organizer for a while after its finished and then head to Dolores Park for pickup Volleyball. A number of friends play Volleyball and I thought it would be fun to try but never really got around to it until now. I never really played before but I have something better than experience … I watched all four seasons of the volleyball anime Haikyu! I was ready! I knew all the positions! I knew the jump serve! The volleyball world was about to be reckoned with! Ok maybe that's not quite what happened. Instead I was the one who was reckoned with. Honestly I think Haikyu should have come with a disclaimer that watching this show will not make you an expert in the sport. My receives were awful. My serving was … actually ok. My elbows and fingers got hurt like nobody's business. But it was a lot of fun! There were people there with more experience than me to show me the ropes but not so much more experienced that I was abnormally bad. We were all just having fun playing around. In Volleyball everyone rotates being either in the front and close to the net or in the back further away. I definitely prefer being up front as I have a better chance of getting the ball over the net rather than receiving a serve and passing well. Interestingly “The Juggler” was also there playing Volleyball as part of a separate league. From there I go to bar night with “The Philosopher,” “The Juggler” and others. Twas a fun affair but nothing of too much note. Friday Today I take it chill and don’t do a whole lot of anything until the evening. Since I’m going to be hosting people soon I decided to decorate my walls a bit. I’ve gotten feedback that my walls are rather barren and I’m pleased to report I’ve now taken a first step towards fixing that with this! My walls are oozing character When that rolls around I host a game night with “The Taco,” “Always causing a Racquet," “The Pasta Prince,” “The Writer,” “The Raja of Rhthym,” and “The Film maker”. It's a fun time as always. From there I go to a special late night run hosted by Midnight Runners. Whenever I tell anyone about Midnight Runners I’m always asked if I actually run at Midnight only to respond in the negative. Today though that finally changes since Midnight Runners hosts their once a year city of lights Midnight run. We go down to the Marina and run through The Palace of Fine Arts and the Marina Green for a roughly 3 mile run. Its a party alright!                                       I did not realize how cool the Palace of Fine Arts looks at Midnight The only catch was when we finished the run near a grassy field and got blasted by the sprinklers which certainly built character. I’ve always enjoyed Midnight Runners but this was the first time it got me wet. Saturday Today starts off with my usual trash pickup. We got a pretty group of people today including “The Philosopher,” “The Writer,” “Granola Girlie,” “The Notetaker,” “The Politican” and many more. Along the way I got “-1 Humza points” for repeating a standard joke of mine when a stranger thanked me for picking up trash and “+1 Humza points” for saying something novel that I don’t remember. I’m technically neutral but I think my Humza stock went down a bit. Afterwards I went home again to see my family since they’re going on a Europe trip starting on Sunday. They actually asked me if I wanted to come since I’m now free but I decided to stay since I do have some stuff I wanted to do during their trip window. After seeing my family off on their European trip I come back and go to a bar crawl hosted by a friend of “The Fisherman” over in Hayes Valley. Here I hang out with “The Fisherman,” “The Writer,” “The Hombre,” “Mr. Green flag” amongst others. We have a good time hanging out and catching up. Outside one of the bars there is some line dancing which I decide to get in on. My line dancing skills are about up there with my Volleyball skills and my not getting laid off this week skills but nevertheless I hop in and I also find it pretty fun. Hat tip to both “The Fisherman” and “The Writer” for capturing this glory At one point we stop for food over at The Bird where I get a fried chicken sandwich which tastes great at first but gives me a bad headache and anxiety afterwards. While at the restaurant we watch a boxing match between these two guys named Crawford and Canello which is supposedly historic for reasons I don’t know enough about boxing to articulate. I never watched a boxing match before this but it was interesting. I didn’t realize that boxing exchanges were short and bursty. The actual blows exchanged tended to only happen for around 5-10 seconds at a time with most of the time being spent prowling around looking for an opening. It was definitely cool to see and while I probably wouldn’t watch boxing by myself I think it would be a bunch of fun to watch with friends. By this point I’m unfortunately getting quite tired and opt to go home. Part of why I decided to go home is that I get really anxious in ways I haven’t gotten in many years (decades is probably more accurate).. I’m quite in my head, I have a bad headache, and I feel distressed. I suspect it's because of something I ate as this has happened in the past when I eat things I shouldn’t such as food high in dairy. Thankfully this gets resolved by going home and sleeping so this isn’t too serious but I don’t think I’ll be eating at The Bird again. Sunday The day starts with trash pickup where I pick up trash with some new folks. Nothing really eventful here but it was good. Afterwards I hang out with “The Quant” and we walk around for a while. We try to go to Plow to meet with “The Plower” while she’s eating brunch but we’re kicked out of the restaurant since there isn’t enough room for us and its quite busy. From there I hang out with “The Plower” and “The Taco” and we go to Tartine. We catch up for a while and then I go home to write this newsletter.

title: Episode 39
excerpt: Tuesday This issue picks up with me getting into Lyon. Upon arrival we quickly check into our hotel and get some lunch. As we walk around we’re greeted with some gorgeous sites right outside the hotel At this point we’re pretty hungry and desperate so most of…
content: Tuesday This issue picks up with me getting into Lyon. Upon arrival we quickly check into our hotel and get some lunch. As we walk around we’re greeted with some gorgeous sites right outside the hotel At this point we’re pretty hungry and desperate so most of the group goes to an Italian place while I go to a Mickey Ds. This starts a bit of light bullying where the rest of the group gangs up on me for wanting to go to McDonalds. In my defense I only eat McDonalds on vacation since I try to eat healthy when normally so this is my only real chance to do it. But apparently eating it every day is considered “wrong” for reasons that continue to allude me. I did learn an important lesson though that a maple bbq burger does not in fact taste good. Afterwards me and “The Quant” go up to this big castle pictured above and it looks pretty cool. We also got a great view of Lyon from the top of the castle I walk around a bit more both with “The Quant” and by myself before dinner time. We all (minus “The Plower”) go to a french place where I get some steak and fries which is perfectly ok. As we wrap up dinner I ask the waiter for the check and he comments that “The Pickeballer” is still eating to which I respond “So?” The European mind can’t comprehend the American mindset of wanting to get the check so quickly. Generally dining here is a more leisurely experience unlike in America where folks are generally rushed more to finish. The waiter was definitely taken aback by my flippant remark. We then head back to the hotel and sleep. Wednesday Today me and “The Driver” go out and get some coffee / pastries before everyone else wakes up. Considering that we get a coffee and a matcha and stay there for about an hour and a half we truly get the European experience of sitting around a cafe for a while which was actually pretty nice. By that point the rest of the gang had woken up and we met them over for brunch at some place where I got both pancakes and waffles. The waitress gave me an interesting look and everyone else piped in and said I was American :P. Yeah once I get back I go back on the diet hard. Afterwards we go to the station and take the train to Zürich.  All in all Lyon was a cute city which we picked at random so we didn’t have a really long train to Zürich but it wound up being a keeper. I do think that one day and one night was the perfect amount of time for it. By this point I had seen pretty much everything worth seeing. After 4 hours and one 12 minute transfer at Mullhouse we get to Zürich. If you ever find yourself there one of the first things you need to know is that it is EXPENSIVE. And I mean more EXPENSIVE than SF. To give you an idea, a typical meal at a restaurant may wind up costing you 36 USD. Yes you read that right. 36 USD. Never before have I thought to myself “Oh SF prices are pretty reasonable compared to city X”. But I guess that day is today. While on the train to Zürich “The Professor” tries to get us all to download the app for managing Zürich public transit which brings us to … Humza reviews foreign public transit Zürich edition Hey there you numtots! We’re back it for another foreign public transit review. This time taking on the center of Switzerland itself Zürich. As a recap here are the criteria used. 1. Frequency of trains 2. Coverage of transit 3. Ease of paying 4. Reliability of transit Frequency of trains This one gets an A. I never found myself needing to wait more than 5 minutes for a train to get me where I needed to go. Coverage of transit This one also gets an A.  I was able to take public transit all the way out to the feet of mountains I climbed back to downtown and all around. Ease of Paying Alright this is by far the most controversial but I’m giving this a B-. In order to pay for public transit here we used an app called SBB Mobile. The reason for this is that if you tried buying a ticket based on where you are and where you want to go you have to calculate zone based fare with a zone map that looks something like this Imagine yourself frantically trying to find the right zone right as the train approaches What the SBB app does is you give it your location plus a credit card and you swipe on the app to say you are starting public transit and swipe again when you finish and it takes a look at your start and end location and calculates the fare for you and charges your credit card. That seems like a pretty fare system except for the fact that almost all our credit cards couldn’t be saved due to an error in the app. I know this technically isn’t the transit system’s fault itself but when we’re all trying for like 40 minutes to connect credit cards and only two people can manage that is really saying something. Shout out to “The Driver” for somehow having his credit card not give some app error which we could all then copy and use for our time here :P. Reliability of transit This one gets an A-. Not quite Japan level but pretty solid. Generally I had to wait at most a minute or two after expected time. Once we got into the city and settled in we got dinner and walked around for a while. After dinner we walk along the river and sit down to see some PHAT SWAN No this isn’t a bad photo the swan just moves EXTRA FAST Thursday I start today off with a solo walk in the morning while everyone else is sleeping. I go to Lindenhof hill and get some really nice views Once most of everyone else wakes up (me, “The Quant,” “The Professor,” and “The Pickeballer”)  we get breakfast and go to the Lindt museum of chocolate. For those who don’t know Lindt is one of the big chocolate makers in Switzerland and they have a whole museum dedicated to the craft. The museum itself was pretty cool! I had learned some of this before but I always forget how intricate the process of making chocolate is. It's also pretty wild that people were able to figure this out thousands of years ago. Afterwards we meet up at the hotel and we all split off again. I decide to try going shopping with “The Plower” and “The Driver” to see what its like. Humza reviews shopping with The Plower I know from what she has told me that “The Plower” likes to shop a lot but since I generally hate shopping I don’t usually witness it. I thought today I may change that. Going shopping with her is kinda like walking a dog with the intention of going to see a particular squirrel only for said dog to get randomly distracted by random squirrels every 3 seconds and you’re getting aggressively dragged as you hold onto the leash. We originally intended to go to a sunscreen store (for the Korean stuff) and some other random store I can't remember but along the way got distracted by an Aesop, a book store, a knick knack store (for the magnets), and probably other things I’ve forgotten. It’s mildly amusing to watch for about 30-45 minutes before I realize I need a break to walk around and see random towers so that's what I do in the middle. I go to a random tower and climb up it for a view that's pretty reasonable Windy staircases sure are popular here After taking a break I resume shopping with “The Plower”  watching “The Plower” decide whether to buy a book for 15+ minutes before running into “The Quant” who joins our little show.  Sadly at this point it starts raining and pretty badly at that so we beeline for the hotel. We then go out to dinner at a Singaporean place where I get some of the worst Mongolian beef I ever had. It looked very nice but tasted like ice. The rain is still pretty bad and here I fumble by not renting an umbrella from the hotel. I thought I wouldn’t need it but boy was I wrong. I wound up crowding under an umbrella with “The Plower” which was a miserable experience for all involved. We attempt getting gelato afterwards which the rain really transformed from an outing to an ordeal. I then go back to the hotel and doordash McDonalds because I was put off from dinner. Friday The rain is still bad this morning so in order to get my early morning steps I do the unthinkable and go to the hotel gym. It was ok, I got some steps but certainly not as fun as walking around. Once “The Quant,” “The Pickleballer," and “The Professor” are up the rain comes back to walkable levels and we go and get some breakfast and walk around. We go shopping for a while but in a way that has more direction and less indecisiveness than yesterday. “The Quant” wanted to go and get some gold so we went to a gold shop and watched him get a gold coin. While in the shop I see a whole bunch of coins which make sense to me, but in the back I see a Texas license plate. I’m not sure why its there so I ask the guy working there who tells me that apparently someone who brought a bunch of stuff to the shop had it in one of the boxes. I was greatly amused to see a Texas license plate in Switzerland so I decided to buy it for the bit. Afterwards we got some lunch and I decided to peel off from the group to go on a solo hike to the top of Zürich. Specifically I go to Uetilburg. The views here were some of my favorite from the whole trip. It was seriously stunning! There was also a wedding happening below me that I caught a glimpse of Many congratulations! Some bonus views on the way down After finishing the hike I regroup with everyone and we all go to get dinner and walk around a bit. Saturday Today before everyone else is up I go on an early morning hike to a random view point close to the hotel. This one isn’t as pretty as yesterday but still reasonably nice Then I meet up with everyone else to go get breakfast. This breakfast place C.R.E.A.M is really good and I wind up getting 2 sets of pancakes and a crispy chicken burger. “The Plower” also really likes the fries at this place. Afterwards we take a train down to the lake front town of Meilen where we chill by the lake for a while. Originally me and “The Quant” were planning to go on a hike but given we had to wait an hour for the bus to take us to the start we opted not to and instead just relax which was nice in its own way. We then went back and had some dinner. Me, “The Professor” and “The Quant” chilled by the river a bit more and walked around and then went back to the hotel. Sunday Today is the last day of my trip. Everyone else will be staying longer for some degree but I needed to be back for work on Monday. So I walk around a bit more in the morning and then we head off to the last meal we all have together. We went to the same place we went for breakfast yesterday C.R.E.A.M which “The Plower” likes so much I almost decided to change her nickname to “The Creamer”. At this point I say my truly final goodbye to “The Professor”. I already shouted him out quite a bit in other newsletters pending his move so I won’t repeat myself but man this trip was a lot of fun and thanks for organizing!! As a joke I made an unofficial energy ranking based on who had the most energy during the trip. Who was able to walk the most, who slept in the least and so on. The final rankings are as follows Me “The Driver” “The Quant” “The Plower” “The Professor” “The Pickeballer” Since I know y’all were talking about this, any information that comes out after I leave is not part of the ranking :P. That being said from what I heard “The Plower” did sleep in big after I left so maybe that can be asterisked. I then head to Zürich airport where on my way from going to the airport to my plane I get asked for my passport 5 separate times which is absurd. I first had to go through passport control thats required for leaving the Shengen area, then while at my gate I was asked twice before boarding and then at boarding I was also asked twice. The flight itself was alright. I get home, chill for a bit and start to write the newsletter but don’t finish. I get about 5 hours of sleep on and off which isn’t bad for a first night home.

title: Episode 38
excerpt: Shoutouts Happy birthday “La Tacuqeira Royalty”! You’re an awesome friend and I hope you had a great birthday. Wish I coulda been there. Monday Today is a slightly but not too stressful day conjuring up the code as we have a deadline to hit. We keep going tow…
content: Shoutouts Happy birthday “La Tacuqeira Royalty”! You’re an awesome friend and I hope you had a great birthday. Wish I coulda been there. Monday Today is a slightly but not too stressful day conjuring up the code as we have a deadline to hit. We keep going towards it Tuesday See Monday we are closer but need a day more. Wednesday Today at work our code conquering gets us to the deadline. After work I go to Midnight Runners. Today it turns out that I forgot to wear my Brook running shoes so it looks like I’m doing the run in AirForce ones. On top of that I was too lazy to go to the bag drop so I am also doing the run while wearing my backpack which has my laptop, sweater, jacket, and headphones. I figured it would make the run somewhere between 5.1 to 5.7% more interesting. It certainly wasn’t as hard as the time I ran while carrying an air purifier people were still pretty surprised I ran while carrying my backpack. Personally I didn’t think it was that bad. The hardest part was at the end when I was trying to be competitive with someone who was regrettably much faster. He also didn’t wanna lose to the guy running in a backpack so he really picked up the pace. After the run I chilled with “The Climber” and one other friend for a while. We were talking about our worst dating fumbles and I share a story about one of the first ever dates I went on. I know some of y’all have heard this story but not all so let me take you back to a time with a younger and more naiver Humza as he goes on one of his first dates Humza’s epic dating fail The year was 2018 and I was a young and naive dater. We met over at an arcade bar called Coin-Op (now rebranded as Thriller Social Club). When I got there my date bought me a drink which seemed like a promising start. A promising start turned into a great fart when I found the drink to be very not good. It seems my acting skills could use some work as a few sips when she said “You don’t have to finish that”. Relieved, we talked and played some arcade games. I don’t remember much about this meaning it must have gone not terribly. After the arcade games we went to Oren’s Hummus for dinner. We were talking for a while and bonded over the fact that we found travel to be overrated (ironic considering I’m writing this part of the newsletter on a train from Barcelona to Lyon). The check came and I had a bit of a deer in the headlights moment as I looked at the bill. I was also in my frightfully frugal era and I stared at the bill for a minute deciding what to do. What was probably only 20 seconds in real time felt like 2 minutes as I stared at it. Nowadays I’d just pay the bill without really thinking but sadly the Humza of yesteryear didn’t possess such common sense. Eventually I think we split it. We then went to see “Us” , the sequel to “Get Out”. I think the movie was fine but I fell asleep for most of it. When I woke up I tried to pretend like I didn’t but from what others who heard the story have said she could tell I fell asleep. The date ended and she said “see ya bro”. From that day on I learned that when a girl says “see ya bro” it means you’re not getting a second date. As part of the dating fumbles I also share my dating poster that I made. In case any of you haven’t seen it here it is for reference. “The Climber” said I looked performative picking up trash which I found funny considering I’ve been doing this for 2.5 years. I must be really devoted to my performance :D. He showed the poster to a number of friends. One said she liked the picture. The most prominent of these friends is one who described herself as a “Hot mamacita.” She mentioned that at her age (32) she doesn’t have time for anyone playing games and wanted something serious. For example she mentioned that in my biography section I should just say what I do rather than make a joke out of it. The “hot mamacita” said I definitely needed some help and thats what she was for which was nice in a funny sort of way. We hung out for a while and went to a cabaret show over in North Beach afterwards. I had never gone to one before, for anyone curious it was a bit like musical improv with a lot of scatting. Thursday Today was a relatively pedestrian day turning code into shareholder value. After such fruitful activities I go to bar night with “The Philosopher,” “The Raja of Rhythm,” “Always causing a Racuqet,” “Thats nuts,” and “The Mosher”. “The Philosopher” gives me an old projector of his which may well bring new life to the Humza cave. Perhaps now I can host new kinds of events. Also it turns out the bartender at this bar also rides motorcycles so now “The Raja of Rhythm” has a new riding buddy. Separately I also promised that I would buy a terrarium and show it to the bartender. If I do I get free drinks that night which will be great for the zero alcohol I always get at these. Friday-Saturday Today is a relatively short day at work as I head to the airport to fly to Barcelona. I meet with “The Plower,” “The Quant,” “The pickeballer,” and “The Driver” at the airport and we fly off. The flight itself is relatively uneventful. At one point we see what looks to be Greenland here I told myself I would be productive on this flight and start writing up the newsletter early. I also told myself I wouldn’t let my vacation delay sending out the newsletter but you can see how wrong that was :(. I instead spent the flight rewatching The Office and playing 2048. Best I could do on that was 512. After 11 hours of that and napping we land in Barcelona! The first thing we do is go over to the hotel everyone but me is staying at to meet up with “The Professor.” View from the hotel I elected to stay at a hostel to save money and meet new people. As for how that went well we shall get to that later. By the time we land in Spain and get settled in its about 4pm so we go out for a lunch / dinner type meal. We take the public transit there which means that its time for the brand new segment called “Humza reviews foreign public transit” Humza reviews foreign public transit Hey there all you numtots! Its time for the foreign public transit review. In todays episode we go over Barcelona. Since this is our first episode we’ll go over the criteria used. 1. Frequency of trains 2. Coverage of transit 3. Ease of paying 4. Reliability of transit Frequency of trains I’d say Barcelona gets an A- here. I don’t find myself needing to wait any more than 7 minutes for a train. Definitely better than SF but worse than London or Japan. Coverage of transit This gets an A from me. I was able to use it to go all over Barcelona (for the times I didn’t decide to walk places to boost my step count) and it was quite easy. I never needed to walk more than 5 minutes or so to get a station and I could take the transit all over. Ease of Paying This one gets an A+ from me. I can pay using my credit card at any point or I can buy a clipper card and keep using that. I’m glad BART is finally letting you pay by credit card. Take notes MUNI. Reliability of Transit This one gets an A. Its not Japan levels where things come exactly on the dot but generally the difference between when public transit comes and when it says it will come is at most 40 seconds. One thing I liked about a lot of the stations in Barcelona was that they had a minute and second counter of when the next train would get there. I found this to be a small but nice quality of life improvement. The trains also came much more frequently as to be expected from Europe. The food itself was a solid thumb sideways. I noticed the prawns tasted fresh in the sense that I could taste the “pier” in them which I don’t think I quite liked. Form there we split off with “The Professor” and “The Pickleballer” going back to the hotel, “The Driver” and “The Plower” going to shop and me and “The Quant” walking around. We go to a LEGO store which was much nicer than any of the ones you would see state side. At the LEGO store I decide to get a little birthday gift for “La Tacuqeria Royalty” since I won’t be there for his birthday.The LEGO store has this thing where you can make  custom LEGOs with One Piece bodies so I get him this We walk around some more and check out downtown Barcelona. After a while I head to my hostel and meet some new characters. As is typical while traveling I meet a bunch of people from Australia. I guess they really have a culture of traveling around which is cool. I meet plenty of people from the U.S including someone who will be joining the army soon doing intelligence which gives off some real “The Shadow Brigade” vibes. I meet someone who has a life goal of wanting to teach fashion design in prison which is certainly out there in a cool way. One of the people I met was an 18 year old who thought I was 22-23 which at my age of 29 I’ll take. Apparently the culture of this hostel is to do drinking games so we played Kings Cup which was interesting with 20+ people playing. As part of the game we all went around and introduced ourselves by saying our name, nationality, and what we thought was the hottest nationality. I learned that statistically speaking Italian and Colombian were considered the hottest by hostel dwellers in Europe. Who knew. It really felt like being back in college in ways that I’m not sure how to feel. Maybe I have gotten older but I don’t quite know if thats the vibe I want. I’m def down to meet people but maybe not like that. After a game of rage cage with an even spicier ice breaker “Favorite sex position” it was time to go clubbing. I thought I’d go but ultimately decided to sleep. Sunday I go to everyone else's hotel to enjoy the free breakfast with “The Driver” and “The Quant”. They have a wide variety of breakfast foods including everything you could possibly want. The food was reasonably good but it really won on variety of options. Afterwards while everyone is chilling in the hotel I decide to take a solo trip up to Temple of the Sacred Hearts. It was certainly quite the hike :D Imagine this but repeated 30 more times and thats roughly what I needed to do And some great views! I regroup with the rest of the gang and we go get brunch somewhere. Originally I wanted to leave a Yelp review but I wound up eating something. I have a goal of leaving one Yelp review in every country I go to. Hopefully I can do this soon. We then go to Montjuic castle for some more views We then went to the Gothic quarter and had some Paella that was pretty good, only complaint that there wasn’t as much Oxtail as I would have liked. Sadly I did have some jet lag today so after some light bullying from my friends  I decided to go home rather than go clubbing like I originally wanted. Lets see how many of these things I’m able to do tomorrow. Monday I once again take advantage of the hotel my friends paid for to get some free breakfast. It didn’t hit the same the second time but it was still pretty good. While everyone else is resting up I decide to go to the Sagrada Familia which was amazing. I saw it from a distance from the hotel I was not prepared for how intricate the artwork would be up close. The inside also definitely did not disappoint There was an actual service happening here I took the elevator to the top of one of the towers for some more views While I took the elevator up I had to take these incredibly narrow spiral stairs down Everyone was holding the railing as the stairs were narrow and felt quite slippery. Just going down them was an act of type II fun. I walk around a bunch more with no real destination in particular to try to get to my 40K step goal. At one point I go down to the sea side and sea the port of Barcelona which was pretty nice. Eventually I met up with “The Professor,” “The Quant,” and “The Pickleballer” and we check out one of the local markets and get some Italian food for lunch. Since I didn’t eat here I checked off my goal of leaving a Yelp review and here it is! We walk around a while more and eventually find ourselves in a McDonalds that I do eat at. Unfortunatley since I went out and started my day before everyone else I wound up getting a bit tired first leading to this. Generally in our friend group I have the most energy and am not likely to get tired so everyone was relishing in lightly bullying me now that I’ve been nerfed by the combo of jet lag, starting earlier than them, and having a step count for today thats probably more than all of them put together. While chilling at the hotel “The Professor” took this picture which he decided to make the group picture for our WhatsApp chat. After dinner, “The Quant,” “The Professor,” and “The Driver” go to the hotel spa for a while and do a combo of sauna and cold plunge with a bit of steam room to spice things up. It was my first time doing any of those things and I have to admit it was better than expected. At first the cold plunge was nigh on intolerable but after a couple iterations I could jump in and do it with only a little bit of whining on the inside. From there we met up with “The Pickleballer” and went to dinner and gelato.The dinner was pretty good. I got a bunch of meat with some steak tartare and another dish with steak cooked less raw. My fatigue was beginning to show which resulted in more light bullying. I swear I could adopt a shelter with all the strays I was catching here. Afterwards I went home and slept. Turns out my dream of going clubbing in Barcelona didn’t quite work out. In retrospect that may have been for the best considering I was up and atem at 6am each day so I couldn’t quite pull it off. I thought perhaps I might find “the one” at a club like this (there was that song by Ed Sheeran after all) but maybe not. Tuesday Today we break tradition a bit as I end the newsletter not by day but by leg of the trip. The day starts with me getting breakfast with everyone and catching the train to Lyon. I’m on the train right now writing the newsletter. Unfortunately due to the hecticness of the trip I didn’t get a chance to write this all up before and I figured a train ride would be a good time to. I don’t want to keep folks waiting for too long so I figured I’d send this out now. In the next issue we will finish up the trip sharing Lyon and Zurich :D.

title: Episode 37
excerpt: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Huge congrats to “The fisherman” for finishing CFA level 3! An awesome achievement and you’ve now joined my mental pantheon of two, count them, two CFA level 3 finishe…
content: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Huge congrats to “The fisherman” for finishing CFA level 3! An awesome achievement and you’ve now joined my mental pantheon of two, count them, two CFA level 3 finishers. Monday Today starts off as a pedestrian day shuffling code through when I’m informed that we will have a big deadline on Friday for a customer push. Bring it on :D. After work I go home and do nothing of particular interest. Tuesday The code caboose keeps chugging as we make our way towards the deadline. We make good progress and have established strong footing but we definitely have a lot more to do. After work today I met up with “The Shadow Brigade” and we walked around for a bit. I show her the Nintendo store which she seems to generally like. She astutely notes that there isn’t really a lot of Pokemon there. I suspect its because Pokemon is so popular they have separate standalone Pokemon stores. It is the highest grossing media franchise after all. We then head to the last supper for “The Professor” before he leaves the Bay Area. Its me, “The Shadow Brigade,” “The Professor,” “The Taco,” “The Plower,” “The Game Master," “The Sparkle,” “The Quant,”  and “Mirandom thoughts, We go to Nakama sushi and Naya dessert cafe where I leave some Yelp reviews. After today I earned a Yelp recognition in “The Dessert” category which should bring me one step closer to becoming Yelp Elite. Hey “The Dentist,” once I become Yelp Elite we should go to some Elite events together :D. Its a bitter sweet moment when we all part ways. I think back to my friendship with “The Professor” and remember a lot of things. I’m really gonna miss ya but congrats on everything! Looking forward to all the amazing stuff you’ll do! I give him a big hug and head back home to the Humza cave. I head back to my apartment only to realize the callbox to let myself in isn’t working. Thankfully someone else lets me in. I suspect it's a one off thing and everything will be fine tomorrow. I”m sure this won’t be a plot point later. Wednesday Another day of turning matcha lattes (of the non performative male variety) into code awaits. As I get to the N-line to go the office I get greeted with this For context I usually have to wait at most 11 minutes for the N with the median wait time being much closer to 6 minutes so this is quite the shock. I wonder if an accident happened. As a comparison I look at the Uber price and see this utter monstrosity. Perhaps an accident happened leading to surge pricing? Generally an Uber from my office (in the Fidi) to Haight Ashbury should only cost around $11 typically perhaps $16 with surge pricing. Thankfully the 7 bus is still running and my commute is only slightly suboptimal. Theres a lot to be done today so I skip Midnight Runners and stay at the office until 10pm at which point I’m told I should leave since I wrapped up the main stuff I needed to do. There isn’t an N running for 20 minutes so I decide to Uber. I get in my Uber and after a couple blocks he asks me to input my address. I’m confused by this as I thought I already put in my address the first time. I put it in and he complains about it adding 14 minutes. He asks what happened and I don’t know as I’m very confused. It doesn’t help that its evident English isn’t his first language so articulating isn’t easy here. I look at my Uber and it turns out I accidentally called it from my office to my office! When I checked the Uber price from my apartment to my office this morning it locked in my office as the destination. I give him a big tip and he takes me back to my apartment. Somehow I don’t think he and I became besties during that ride. I get back to my apartment and once again my callbox isn’t working and once again someone lets me in. I guess this isn’t as much of a one off thing as I thought. Oops. Thursday-Friday I’m fusing these days together for reasons that will make sense later. Its full steam ahead today as we go towards that deadline. Me and 6 other people stay at the office until 4AM. Yeah you read that right we were there til 4AM. I got to the office around 8:30 or so meaning I was in the office for close to 20 hours that day. It was definitely crazy and a bit stressful but also kinda fun in the type II way. I am very thankful to work with folks who I can joke with while being at the office at 4AM. We get a lot done and manage to meet our deadline. Another thing worth noting is unlike my last job here I’m actually working on things I’m excited will help real people. The work I’m doing is helping to get insurance to approve drugs for patients faster meaning quicker turn around time. I don’t think I need to tell any of y’all that health insurance in this country is bloated and awful and I’m glad I can do something to make it slightly less awful :D. Since I’m leaving around 4 and I’ve come to the conclusion that my callbox not working isn’t a one time thing I initially think I”ll sleep at the office but one of my coworkers generously offers his couch. Thanks man it was indeed comfier than the office couch! I sleep there for 2.5 hours til 7 or so then head back to the Humza cave and lie in bed and not really sleep until I get into the office later than usual. Its a relatively chill day today as I code until about 4PM and leave so I can say I left the office at both 4s. From there I hosted a poker night at my place with “The film maker,” “The Raja of Rhythm,” “Mr. Socksessful,” “The Raven keeper,” and a few others. As has usually been the case for me, Poker is a form of charity where I give to the more fortunate. It was a fun night with some crazy hands and well worth the $10 I donated to the cause. Congrats to “The Ravenkeeper” for winning big and “The Filmmaker” for having a really big winning hand where he went all in and won two buy ins worth with a single hand. After poker night “The fisherman” comes over and we catch up and talk about life. For a while I had been planning to do a 24 hour walk starting Saturday at midnight and going until Sunday at midnight. However I asked a bunch of people whether I should still do it given I got so little sleep Thursday night and out of the 8 people I asked they all said no. I’m trying to get better at listening to advice from others and I hate to admit it but if they all said the same thing perhaps they have a point. Here are some of the testimonials I got about the walk As much as it was the right decision I did feel a little pained by it. After all I’m the guy who commits to the bit. Does this mean I’m going soft? Am I a quitter? I was also told that my motivation of beating out those guys who posted their 100K step walk on the SF reddit wasn’t great motivation. Saturday-Sunday The day begins with me sleeping in but still making it to trash pickup. I go with a couple other folks and we pick up trash around Tadaima, the matcha place near 20th and Valencia. One of the people I’m with is annoyed by the attitude and littering of the people sitting down there and calls the people over there “matcha bitches” which I thought was too amusing not to put in the newsletter. After trash pickup I go to Golden Gate Park and go to “The Slosher’s” bi annual game of Sloshball. For those unaware Sloshball is essentially kickball but with drinking. The rules are that you have to always have a can in your hand and when you get on 2nd base you have to finish your can and take a new one. I wind up deciding to captain one of the teams. Naturally due to my lack of skills in the kicking department and catching department I’m really more of a personality captain. When I got my team I almost told them “Do you guys wanna win? If so you picked the wrong team :D”. This wound up being correct as we did lose but only by a couple points. It was still quite fun. Interestingly at this event I met 3 separate people I knew from very different circumstances. I met someone from the chess club I went to a couple times who turned out to be high school friends with “The Slosher,” someone else who is a coworker of “The Juggler,” and a 3rd person who I met through run club. I also met some people who all went to high school in Davis and told me some pretty interesting stories. Apparently when they were in high school there was a girl who brought some cookies and asked people to guess what was in them. The natural guess for many people was weed but it turns out it was her grandmas ashes. Yeah, that was weirder. It got weirder when they told me about someone called “the cat girl” (not a newsletter nickname) who would go onto the roof and hiss at people. There was also a group of people called “the clusterf*ck” (definitely not a newsletter nickname) who were all in relationships with each other and traded around as a combination of monogamy and a polycule. I can’t say that my impression of Davis as a city soared after this. I talk with “The Slosher” a bit more and before I leave she mentions that she will try to come to trash pickup. She has said this many times and very seldom comes so I jokingly give her flack for it and mention that she is better at comedy than I am. She then says she will actually come this time and I tell her that if she actually comes I will apologize in this newsletter and say I’m wrong. Will that happen? Stay tuned. From there I went to The Detour to celebrate “The fisherman” finishing her CFA exam. I got to catch up with “Mr. Greenflag” and “The Trash Queen” as well. Congrats again on finishing the CFA! We played a bunch of Killer Queen and some big buck hunting. While there we run into Scott Weiner and talk with him for a bit. He says he really liked my Mooni sweater which was great to hear. Me and “Mr. Greenflag” also got a pic with him It was fun but I was getting tired around 11pm and decided to go home. Well what I thought was going home anyway. I got back to my apartment and my callbox still wasn’t working. I tried calling a bunch of other people and nobody was awake or decided to let me in. I tried calling my apartment management 24 hour hotline and explained the situation to them. They told me there was nothing they could do. Oops. Now I’m on my own and don’t really have a way into my apartment. At this point I thought it might be fun to try impromptu camping and tried to sleep outside my apartment.  I sit down on the floor and try to sleep but unfortunately its harder than I thought to get comfortable. I try for about an hour and 20 minutes but the cold and the weird angle I’m sitting at makes it quite hard. Ooh boy did the cold really bite me. I think if it wasn’t for the cold I may have actually been able to sleep outside. The other thing I was slightly worried about was someone thinking I ODd and trying to inject narcan. At this point I basically have 3 options Walk around all night until someone lets me in Go to the 24 hour happy donuts in Noe valley and camp out there Get a hotel room and sleep I choose option 3 because I really don’t wanna be cold anymore. This also teaches me that I may not be suited for camping if I can’t handle impromptu camping like this. I splurge and order a Waymo to the hotel so I can relax in a heated jaguar for a bit more. I stay at the Surf Motel over in the Marina for a few hours and get some sleep. Afterwards I go trash pickup and lo and behold I see “The Slosher” walk through. “The Slosher,” I am sorry I underestimated you. I was wrong and my intelligence is clearly on the level of a below average blueberry. Perhaps someday it will climb to the level of a below average raspberry. We pick up trash along with a new friend we met. The 3 of us have now made plans to go to a Cave rave at the end of September so we shall see how that goes. Afterwards I go back to my apartment and finally get a front door key from my apartment manager so now I don’t have to rely on someone else to let me in. Progress! Afterwards I do a bit of work and then invite “The Quant” and “The Taco” to come over for a chill hangout. I then take a nap which I generally hate doing but I was really tired. I then write this newsletter.

title: Episode 36
excerpt: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday In the morning before work I got a text from someone I hadn’t seen in two years asking if I was free to meetup for coffee. I was interested in seeing him so I set a plan…
content: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday In the morning before work I got a text from someone I hadn’t seen in two years asking if I was free to meetup for coffee. I was interested in seeing him so I set a plan to meet with him at Asha’s over lunch. Little did I know this would turn into one of the stranger experiences I would have. We set a plan to meet around 12. I get there right on the dot and ask what his ETA will be.  8 minutes later he replies that he's going to be late. I ask him how late and his response is “You tell me.” I didn’t really know what to say to that. He follows up a minute later by saying “Dude I have no idea what's going on here.” Following up with “I’m very tired. And slow.” I think he’s going through something and I do hope he is alright if so. Once we catch up I tell him a bit about how my life is going and he asks me to pick a number between 1 to 5. I pick a number and he writes it down in his notes app. I asked him what the number was for and he wouldn’t tell me. I ask him how law school is going and he says he doesn’t know if he should continue and asks me if he should or not. Remember that I haven’t seen him in two years and not since he started law school so it's not as if I have a whole lot of information to answer the question for him. I try to get a bit more information but the search proves … elusive. He then shows me his phone background which looks to be a lake of some sort with a mountain and a couple of boats in it. He asks me where I think it is. I suspect that it's Lake Tahoe based solely on vibes. I try to offer my guess but he then waives it away. At a couple other points in our meeting I ask if I should tell him my guess and he says no. Once we finish up at Asha’s we walk around a little bit before coming across an art gallery. He says he wants to go in so thats what we do. We get to the 4th floor of the building where they tell us everything on that floor is closed for the day but there should be stuff on the 5th floor. We take the stairs up and he mentions his legs hurting. I ask if we should go back and take the elevator and he says no. He then asks why we’re here before I reply “Uh … you said you wanted to come?” I truly am lost at this point and wonder what he wants to get out of this. We make it to the 5th floor and see some of the art I had what I thought was a cool interpretation for the 3rd one which I forgot. Maybe something about our inner dreams being manifested as shadows? We then leave the art gallery and I vaguely mention I should head out soon to go back to the python mines and he says “thanks for meeting” gives me a hug and then walks off. It seems like he may have been going through something or on drugs perhaps. Either way I hope he is ok. I don’t really know what to make of all of this. I go back and continue wrangling my workflows. Once that's done I go to the gym with “The Professor” and “The Quant”. I think I’m starting to get better with the dumbbell lifts. I still can’t lift a lot of weight but I don’t need to be reminded (as much) about my form. I remember to keep my shoulders back and tense up my abs. Unfortunately my pride does get the better of me as  I try to keep lifting despite my form breaking down. I don’t think I overdid it too hard but I may have gone a couple reps past where they suggested I stop. Oopsie poopsie. On the plus side I get a new PR in the plank of  2 minutes and 44 seconds. I’m pretty close to the 3 minute mark but I decided to listen to “The Professor” this time when he mentioned that my form is breaking down. Tuesday Today is mainly spewing my source code at the ol office space and then I head home and do nothing of particular interest. Wednesday Today after another pilgrimage into Python I go to run club with “La Tacqueira Royalty”. This is the first run where I can show off my new Midnight Runners shirt which is awesome. The bad news is that it is a bit cold out which means that my nip nips (also pronounced as nipples) in some cultures are quite cold. This improves somewhat as the run goes on but towards the end it certainly becomes an ordeal. Normally I’d stick around afterwards for a post run hang but instead decide to go to game night at “The Professor’s” place. The main game we play there is Exploding Kittens. For most of you who haven’t played with me I used to quite hate Exploding Kittens and found it quite boring. What changed was that whenever I play I decided to play my own game within the game where I try to die first by aggressively giving away my diffuses and proactively seeking bombs. I was able to do this pretty successfully for a while until “The Professor” decided to troll me by beating me to the punch and trying to die before me. This has turned our group Exploding Kittens dynamic into a game within a game where the two of us try to beat each other to the punch in dying while everyone else tries to win. I was all set up to play that way today until “The Professor” changed things up and gave me a deck with 4 diffuses and himself none. What then wound up happening was we played a “raid boss” variant of Exploding Kittens where everyone teamed up to keep me alive as long as possible to prolong my misery and everyone else trying to die. The win condition for them is that I’m in the final two players with the person who makes it to the end with me being the true winner. Since this is a raid boss variant I figured the funniest way to depict this game would be by using a manga fight with all of us substituted in as the characters. For context it will be “The Plower,” “The Quant,” “The Kpop dancer,” “The Professor,” and “Mirandom thoughts” all vs me. Since he rigged it so he has no diffuses he started things off by dying immediately and removing himself from the game. While this does mean he can’t win he definitely was the MVP in terms of defeating me with regards to setting up the plan, giving me a bunch of diffuses, and some posthumous contributions we shall get to later. My next opponent proved to be “The Plower”. She was a no nonsense nemesis to say the least. Her use of nopes proved vital in restricting my actions. At one point I knew there was a bomb on the bottom of the deck so I tried to use a draw from the bottom. This succeeds and I get the bomb I want to get rid of one of my diffuses but she then places a nope card. Normally this wouldn’t be allowed but “The Professor” intervenes posthumously with “house rules” to say that it is and I’m not allowed to draw the bomb. At this point “The Quant” also joins the fray and it quickly becomes a 2 v 1 showdown. Eventually “The Plower” goes down. I should also mention at this point that “The Kpop dancer” and “The Sparkle” don’t really participate in the fight and just play the game normally so they won’t be included in any of these pictures. They both die sometime around now but to be honest I don’t remember their order as its not particularly relevant to the main raid boss fight. Now its down to me vs “The Quant” and “Mirandom thoughts”. Throughout the fight I manage to burn off all my diffuses. At one point I use the ol trick of using a shuffle card and “happening” to shuffle a bomb right on top before I draw. Its pretty clear there are no rules at this point so you gotta do what you gotta do to win. Unfortunately “The Quant” and “Mirandom thoughts” collude with some more posthumous help from “The Professor”. They set up a gambit where “Mirandom thoughts” takes the diffuses from “The Quant” and then plays an attack card forcing “The Quant” to draw a bomb. With that its now down “Mirandom thoughts” and myself and “Mirandom thoughts” wins. Good game y’all. As blatantly rigged as it was it was certainly a lot more fun than the dreck that is normal Exploding Kittens. Thursday Today after another shift in the python mines I go to bar night hosted by “The Philosopher”. Its a fun time and I watch him hone his cocktail making skills. Unfortunately there isn’t really all that much to say here beyond that though. Friday Today I went to my daily code communal as per usual. On my way home from work I run into someone from a charity called Nature Conservatory asking me to donate money. Most people when faced with someone like this will look away, walk by quickly, and awkwardly mumble a “no thanks” when asked to donate money. From a social perspective that is indeed the safest course of action. I on the other hand choose not to play it safe and instead have some fun. When they approach me I talk with them and see how long it takes before they back away from me. When he talks about all the nature and protecting the Marin Headlands I mention that I love going there to throw my trash. I tell him I’m a huge polluter and love nothing more than making the world a little bit worse. To my surprise he doesn’t back down and commits to the bit. He mentions he loves polluting and if I donate to them they will help me pollute even more. This goes on for quite a bit and I was pleasantly surprised how much he committed. At first I wanted to get him to back away but it got to the point where I was enjoying the banter itself. I didn’t want this to end. Heck I was almost gonna donate if for nothing else than my sheer impressment. However I also thought that if I donated I’d lose the battle of pride and out of respect to the principles of the engagement I can’t back down. We then switch to me pretending to donate and getting my demographic info wrong. Apparently he could see through the fact that my DOB was not in fact 1910 or that my zip code somehow was not 6 digits. He then mentioned that he’d love to keep this going but he has an incentive to get people to sign up so he can go home so he was gonna focus on some others. I guess I won but it doesn’t feel like a real victory. I was hoping to be pushed more to my limits. To truly feel like I couldn’t keep committing to the bit anymore. To feel truly locked in. He then says next week will be his last week at the job and he’ll be out here for one more week. I hope I find him again. I want to continue our battle of pride properly. host what I originally intended to be a board game night but turned into me inheriting a bunch of “The Professor’s” furniture as he moves out followed by a board game night. I get an extra couch, a papasan chair, a trash can, a night stand, and a shoe rack. I’m told my place looks very different and much improved now. Big thanks to “The Quant,” “The Sparkle,” and “The Professor” for moving all this stuff over to my place. I can now comfortably seat somewhere around 10 people with no need for me to bring out the air purifier. Afterwards I headed over Madrones for “The Politican’s” bar crawl. Originally I intended board game night to last around 2 hours or so and end around 9 so I can go to this bar crawl. Fortunately / unfortunately we ended up having too much fun and the event that was supposed to end at 9 ended at 11:45. By the time I get there I realize that Madrones will be both very loud making it harder to talk to people and I need to pay a $10 cover. I don’t think tis worth it for a place like that so I wind up heading home. Saturday Today begins with trash pickup. Through the pickup I feel a bit down mentally. Forgive me as this next part will be hard to articulate and I debated putting it in here but it is important. I felt a bit down because I worry that I don’t bring enough value to my friends. I sometimes think that I’m not enough and those thoughts for whatever reason got to me now. Why now? Sadly I cant’ articulate this even to myself. Sometimes it just feels like the thoughts randomly come in. Its kinda like if you leave your mental door open and then they come in to your mental house and start harassing me. Whats worse is they didn’t even take their mental shoes off, those bad thoughts! Like if I’m not funny enough, helpful enough what is the point of me? I wish I could say there was a real resolution here other than I somehow just acknowledged those thoughts and then sorta accepted them and they went away for a while. Not permanently I suppose. Again this is not a well articulated point I know but my rule for these newsletters is to share anything I deem “interesting” for either better or worse regardless of how it makes me look and so I did. After that little episode I wrap up trash pickup and go to a food crawl for “The Professor,” “The Quant,” “The Pickleballer,” “The Taco,” “The Plower,” “The lawyer,” “High entropy,” “The sparkle,” “Mirandom thoughts” and other friends of “The Professor”. Since he is moving out a bunch of us do a food crawl where we go to all of his favorite food places. We go Bon Nene, Garden Creamery, Tartine, Five Star Truffles, Detour to play Killer Queen, and finally the Humza cave where we get some Dumpings from Dumpling House. I won’t go through all the details here and instead link you all to yelp reviews I wrote for each place. Since I wrote these Yelp reviews I naturally ordered the nothing at all of them so I can keep my bit of writing Yelp reviews at places I don’t’ eat at to become Yelp Elite going. Bon Nene review Garden Creamery review Tartine review Five Star Truffle review Dumpling House review Between Five Star Truffle and Dumpling House we go to Detour to play some Killer Queen which is quite fun. Big shoutout to “The Sparkle” for having a killer instinct and being quite good at aggressively attacking. From there we go back to The Humza cave and play more games and hangout. Around this time “The Shadow Brigade” comes as I manage to catch her on one of her monthly visits to the Bay. After a while we play game called Psycopath where everyone but me is aware of a “rule” that I have to guess. Everyone sits in a circle and the guesser (me) has to ask questions to one member at a time until I can figure out the rule. A past example of the rule is that when I ask a question to someone they answer as the person on their left and if they get the answer wrong (according to the person on the left) they say “psycopath” and they both switch places. In this case the rule is that there is no rule which I basically manage to get. One advantage I have in a game like this compared to most is I’m very good at battles of attrition. Usually when the game is played the person guessing the rule wants to give up but in my case I can keep going long enough that I make the people who know the rule want to give up. Sadly “The Professor” saw this coming and at one point nerfed me so I can ask at most 10 questions. I still managed to get it but I really want to test my stamina here and keep this up for a while. Perhaps an hour. The first time I played this game and I was the one figuring out the rule I figured it out part way through and kept going for another 10 minutes until they gave up. That was a while back when the group didn’t quite know my limits and naively assumed I’d crack first. They have certainly wisened since. Sunday The day begins with trash pickup as per usual without any of the random “mental breakins” from yesterday. I catch up with “The Raja of Rhythm” after his journeys to parts unknown and also see “Always causing a Racuqet”. The post trash hang today is fairly short and I go to a party hosted by one of my coworkers. My coworker has a bunch of friends who are very techy, more so than I would generally like to the point I was originally not going to go but decide I may as well. On my way to the party I meet some interesting people on the bus who like my custom “Mooni” hoodie. We talk for a bit and they encourage me to set up an online store and if I did that they’d buy them. I love meeting random people this way and I’m glad I got an interesting conversation because of my hoodie. One of the people I met had an art piece displayed in the world’s smallest children's art gallery (yes this apparently a thing). Afterwards I get off the bus and go the party. I was correct in my earlier assessment that the vibes of the party certainly weren’t what I’m used to. I meet this one guy whom when I ask “Whats something cool or interesting about you that people wouldn’t expect?” mentions that he’s unemployed (in my admittedly judgemental opinion I don’t think thats a good answer to the question) and then the conversation becomes a laborious effort of me trying to extract info out of him. He says that his startup exited and he is wondering what to do next. I ask him if he has been doing anything fun and he says no he is thinking about what to do next. Then I ask what he wants to do next and he says he wants to build something. “Build what?” I ask. He says he doesn’t know and wants to build something. Then he walks away. I also meet a guy who says he used to be a finance bro. I ask him what his recs are for the best places in SF are to get some cocaine and when he says he never had any I knew he must be a fake finance bro. Ok this interaction was actually pretty good but I found the joke too funny not to mention here. Most of the people there already know each other so its a bit hard for me to break in. I do have some actually normal conversations here but I had more conversations like the first than I would normally care to. Ie ones where people aren’t that interested in getting to know me and quickly walk away. All in all not my vibe. I then meet up with “The Professor” and “The Pickleballer” and hang out with them for a bit and take a bit more stuff from “The Professor” as he moves out. I take an old calculator of his that he had since high school that he wants to throw away but always kept taking regardless. I take it specifically so I can throw it away as soon as I get home. I then go home and write the newsletter.

title: Episode 35
excerpt: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Happy birthday “Always Causing a Racquet!” I haven’t known you super long but its been great having you here. Hope you stay after your internship! Monday Today I mainl…
content: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Happy birthday “Always Causing a Racquet!” I haven’t known you super long but its been great having you here. Hope you stay after your internship! Monday Today I mainly commune with the code and go home and chill. Tuesday Today after my daily code whispering I go to they gym with “The Quant” and “The Professor”. I manage to increase my plank PR from 1:40 to 2 minutes. I think I probably go even better next week. I do some back workouts which I’m surprisingly good at relative to the other workouts. I suspect this is because I use a machine for these as opposed to free weights which give me a greater margin of error without having to work on my form. When I do the free weights like dumbbell presses I’m never quite able to get the form right. I either forget to tighten my abs, keep my elbows right, or something else like that. I think I’m slowly getting better but still far from perfect. Wednesday Today after delving into the code I go to run club. The run itself is relatively straight forward. I was worried after skipping for two weeks post marathon I wouldn’t be able to run but I was happy to see that was false. After the run I hang out with “La Tacuqueria Royalty”, “The Climber”, and “Sergant Sassy”. We go to The Port of Peri Peri which has some great Portugese food. You can tell its delicious because I left a Yelp Review for it. We wound up spending pretty much the whole dinner talking about a variety of unhinged topics. Originally I wanted to go into detail but after telling some of my other friends IRL I decided not to here based on their reactions. Just know it was very amusing though and everyone there was a G. The one thing I can say though is that me and “The Climber” did some great improv around me having a pet duck by the name of Charles which was amazing. Also chunky milk is apparently more nutritious than non chunky from what I heard. The more you know right. Thursday Today before work I decide to go to Thursday morning run club. Generally I don’t actually run at this run club, instead I just show up for the post run hangout. However last week I promised tow of the people that I was running with there that I would run so I decided to this time.I was a bit nervous when I woke up because I felt some knee pain. Originally I told myself that it was nothing but about a quarter of a mile into the run I quickly realized it was not in fact nothing. My knee was searing and I had to call it quits. Thankfully this is the run club that I’m far less invested in but it was still annoying. It also turned out the people I made that promise to didn’t even show up so it was all for naught. Ah well. At this run club I meet someone who was friends with one of my college roomates. Truly a small world. After another day going to war with my code I go to bar night over at The Lark. I’m joined by “The Philosopher," “The Juggler” and “The Bartender” as per usual but also “Always causing a Racquet". Its his birthday today so I thought it would be fun to invite him! Bar night is fun as per usual. I do get an interesting piece of feedback that I tend to repeat jokes to the point of it being annoying. As someone who thinks my telling jokes is a key part of the value I bring I do spend some time ruminating on how I can fix this. One example which was brought up was that I tend to ask a common ice breaker question a lot “Whats something cool or interesting about you that people wouldn’t expect?” When I got home I spent some time thinking of other fun ice breakers I could use to break the monotony. I came up with some fun examples which I”m looking forward to testing out. Another consequence is I may need to retire some of my more common jokes that I use like my joke that goes something along the lines of “My jokes tend to bomb. Its ok though because I’m Muslim”. I do really like the joke but I guess if I’ve been telling it to the point of it being stale I may need to sunset it. I’m sure I’ll come up with new material but I was a bit bummed to hear that. Friday Today after wrestling my code into a chokehold I go to GGP and briefly hangout with “The Professor” and “The Pickleballer” at The Conservatory of Flowers. Unfortunately due to upcoming KBBQ plans I don’t spend a long time here but it was nice to chat amidst the background music of Outside Lands. On my way between Conservatory of Flowers and Kogi Gogi I get jumped by 3 small dogs. They don’t actually bite me but they all get very close. I was never a fan of small dogs and this definitely did not help. I audibly screamed for them to back off and tried to stand my ground. It really was a good thing those small rat bastards ar all bark and no bite. For completely unrelated reasons I briefly thought about the movie Old Yeller. Once that crisis was averted I make my way over to KBBQ where I meet up with “The Boxer,” “The Pasta Prince,” and “The Quant”. Kogi Gogi is great as usual. It turns out that a while back one of the waiters there who I know on a first name basis bought some Pokemon cards from “The Quant”. I was hoping to see him and ask how he was liking them but he wasn’t working there today. The KBBQ slapped as per usual. I learned that “The Pasta Prince’s” dad worked in Pakistan for a while and had an assistant by the name of Iqbal which I thought was pretty funny. Saturday The day begins with trash pickup as per usual. Nothing particularly surprising here. I would have liked to stay longer but I had a belated birthday party to go to for “The Plower!”. For this surprise party I do something a little sneaky. One of the interesting benefits to writing this newsletter is it gets me into the habit of sending a weekly text to everyone who gets it which proves useful for keeping up with friends who I may not see all the time. One such friend is “The Kpop dancer” who moved down to L.A a while ago. She told me she was planning to come up in Sepetember. Since “The Professor” will be leaving the Bay soon I convince her to move up her trip. Nobody knew she was coming other than me. I tell her to come to “The Plower”’s birthday party as a surprise to everyone. It was extra funny because she assumed I would have told everyone she was coming only to learn shortly before arriving that I did not in fact tell anyone as evidenced by this text exchange As I expected the surprise went great and everyone was excited to see her! When I catch up with her it was cool to see that she already knew a lot both about what I was up to and our friend group through my newsletter. We start off the birthday at Plow as would be expected for “The Plower’s” birthday party. When we get there we learn that the wait time will be 2 hours. I try my best to bribe the waiters with some Thai currency worth about $3 USD but sadly it doesn’t seem they are that interested in moving on up in the world as I don’t take my Thai money. I briefly contemplated bribing them with my fake money used solely as a movie prop but decided against it since anyone uncultured enough to decline Thai currency probably wouldn’t be swayed by this either. The old saying of casting pearls before swine is truly applicable here. We have a pretty large party so we don’t all get to sit at the same table. Since I wind up not sitting with After Plow we go to my place to play some Secret Hitler. Huge props to “The Quant” for helping out the fascists as a liberal by being an agent of chaos. I’m especially proud because that's exactly the sort of thing I’d do as a liberal. From there we all go down to Prime BBQ over in San Mateo. I went to this place before and while the meat was good it was overpriced as heck. Because of that I made a commitment to not eat there and instead write a Yelp Review. Since The Plower is into post cards I’ve been following a tradition for the last 3 birthdays of making one for her with photos of us from the time since her last birthday. This is this years! After a good hearty meal that I didn’t eat we go to the Hillsdale mall and enjoy the finest scenery one could find there which in all fairness was better than the Westfield mall over in SF. I felt like a teenybopper going to the Lego store and then the food court. Sunday Before the usual Sunday street sweep I have a call with my Mom. To be honest amidst all the stuff I’ve been doing I haven’t been calling home as much as I should. I generally call about once a week but because work got really busy that wound up being less. I feel bad because I do like talking to my Mom and its important to keep family close so I am going to make sure to make that more of a priority going forward. My Mom did say she missed my calls which was what prompted the call this morning and a goal to be more consistent with this. After that I go to trash pickup. I catch up with “The Hombre” and “The Yogi”. This also winds up being a quick trash pickup as I go to get brunch with “The Professor,” “The Kpop dancer,” “The Pickleballer,” “The Game master,” “The Attorney,” and “High Entropy” over in Duboce park. Between yesterday and today this weekend definitely takes me back to a couple years ago when this group of friends was my primary group of friends. It feels interesting looking back then vs now to see how things have changed. Due to life and all that we don’t all get to see each other as often as we’d like so I’m glad we got this chance today. We spend a while soaking up the sun over in Duboce. Part way into it we play Gomoku which in case y’all aren’t aware is kinda like Chinese connect 4 except its 5 in a row and you can connect diagonally as well as vertically and horizontally. I’m generally not very good at this game and quickly lose to “The Professor”. I then wind up playing against “The K-pop dancer” in a 15-20 minute long battle royale which I wind up eking out a win in. We then play a second game where she manages to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory. For context she was about to setup a 4 in a row that I couldn’t block but was just missing a single piece. This was explained to me and I was told I should concede. I decide not to and drag the game out and go for a 4 in a row that she could have blocked. Instead of blocking she decided to complete the 4 in a row not realizing I just needed to put my 5th piece and win the game. Had she blocked me she would have eventually been able to complete that 4 in a row I couldn’t block and win. She jokingly mentioned that she didn’t want to shame her Chinese ancestors and unfortunately that might have just done it. Considering my Paki ancestors never played the game I don’t think they really cared about my win. After hanging out more in the park we get dinner over at Nakama sushi which I decide to cheat on my diet and eat at. Afterwards I go home and write up the newsletter.

title: Episode 34
excerpt: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday Today is a fairly normal day in the Python mines. Nothing much really happens today other than work. I’ve made good progress on the project I’m working on but we need to…
content: Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday Today is a fairly normal day in the Python mines. Nothing much really happens today other than work. I’ve made good progress on the project I’m working on but we need to optimize it some more before its production ready. We’re almost at the finish line but still more to be done. Tuesday After the Python mines I go to the muscle mines aka the gym after work. I’ve got “The Professor” and “The Quant” helping me out. I’m doing a lot better than last time and I can actually start to see my form improve. Now I can actually start to do exercises without them correcting me *all* the time just *most* of the time. I get in some shoulder and arm workouts and despite feeling it at the time I’m surprisingly unsore the next couple days. Perhaps now that I’m getting better at form I need to up my weight. I also find I can hold a planck for a not terrible amount of time of 1 minute and 40 seconds. I probably could have gone longer but since I didn’t see the time it got hard for me to motivate myself. The next time I do it I want to keep the timer close to me and make games with myself to keep going for another minute, 2 minutes, and so on. I think if I can concretely see my time go up I’ll be more motivated to continue. I go home to find that my “Mooni” sweater finally came! I’ve been doing a lot to get into fashion lately and while this may not be the most  typically fashionable thing ever it has a special place in my heart because I really like both the design and the joke I came up with. Wednesday Another day working to deliver share holder value! Nothing particularly of note I keep on keeping on. The one notable thing is that one of my coworkers wanted her very own “Moonie” hoodie! This is really exciting for me as its the first time anyone was seriously interested in buying some of the custom clothes I made. After work I get dinner at Panchitas with “The Enabler,” “The Dentist,” and “La Tacqueria Royalty”. Panchitas holds a special place in my heart since its a corner stone of trash pickup and I’m glad that everyone else liked it as well. To folks’ surprise I did in fact eat there. Who would have guessed? Thursday Today is another day in the Python mines. One of my coworkers “The Pyramid schemer” said “Humza your drip game is fire” and I told her that quote was for sure going in the newsletter. After I finish in the mines  I head to bar night. Its a pretty normal bar night but considering the baseline is that their fun thats certainly not a bad thing! One super cool thing I learn is that a lot of thought goes into designing emergency siren noises. For context “The Juggler” works on designing drones and one of his projects right now is improving the system for crash landings. Part of that is figuring out what kind of noise you want when the system is landing. You want something that will make people want to clear the area without stopping to look at it. Apparently the siren system we use on ambulances is actually shockingly bad. If I remember correctly the best kind of noise is apparently something somewhat close to white noise. I also got a pair of Air Force Ones from “The Philosopher” for only $13 which proved to be quite the deal. I’ve been using them as my new shoes every day for the last few days and they have been quite nice! I decide to use today to try dealing with the FOMO that I mentioned last week and leave a bit earlier when I start feeling tired. Generally I’d try pushing through a bit more but I thought it might be good for me to realize that missing out on stuff won’t always be the end of the world. Friday Today after work I find myself with nothing really planned. Generally I have something planned on Friday nights but the plans I tried to make wound up falling through due to lack of interest. I take this as a sign that perhaps I’m in need of some solo time and decide to go on a meandering walk from my place to Hayes Valley. While hanging out with friends is always fun I have to admit that it is kinda nice to have a bit of walking time alone with my thoughts. Whenever I’m at home I’m always on my computer so its nice to have an environment where I can just think.  I try my best not to play any music and really just let my thoughts swirl around and think about them as they come. Maybe its the autist in me that likes public transit but I think about my thought process as riding a bunch of different trains for varying amount of times. Each train is a tangent I can go down. Some I ride for a number of stops. Some are one stop only. I think about what my life would have been like if the pandemic hadn’t happened. Maybe I still would have been doing Krav Maga and could have kicked some serious tooshie. Maybe I never would have never left my place in SOMA. Maybe I might have never discovered trash pickup. I also think a lot about what insecurities I have. Perhaps this may be something of a running theme in this newsletter but one thing I believe but haven’t really explicitly stated is that I think that knocking down mental walls and insecurities is probably one of the highest ROI things I can do for improving my overall happiness. The more of myself I can unshackle the freer I am to do anything and everything that I can think of.
