content: I made a character list detailing every character here. I got some feedback it can be hard to keep track. Let me know if this helps! Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Monday We have a work deadline coming up for a big project we want to ship by end of week so things are pretty intense. I don’t really do much after work as I am at the office longer than I usually am this week. And while I’m at work I’m much busier too with less time spent randomly chatting with co-workers. Tuesday The deadline draws ever nearer and unfortunately there are some problems with one of the parts of the project that I’m personally working on. I can’t say too much about it in the newsletter but this is unfortunately something that you have to get as close to perfect the first time without much room for errors. Generally one of the things with software engineering as opposed to other forms of engineering like say mechanical is that there is a lot more room for bugs (within reason). People are a lot less likely to be angry about a buggy web page than a buggy Golden Gate Bridge. Sadly thats not the case here and that coupled with a very large (and from our perspective expanding), surface area leads to what may well be described as type 2 fun once its all over. Wednesday Not much to say here other than the day continues and we realize that multiple parts of the project won’t be able to land on time so with my part we take a step back and figure out as a team what the best way is to fix all the bugs and come up with a more comprehensive test plan. Sadly I have to skip midnight runners but with how I’m working on these bugs I’m definitely sprinting :D. Thursday Not too much to add here honestly. Just gotta keep werkin. I go to bar night with “The Lads” for a bit only to find a particularly urgent bug that has to be fixed before tomorrow so I have no choice but to leave earl and head home and keep working. Friday I am starting to feel better about the project but its clear I gotta work over the weekend. At some point I reach my cognitive capacity for the day and I step out to go get KBBQ with “The Quant”. Its as delicious as it always is and a very welcome break from the week. Since I go to the KBBQ place I go to a lot the waiter and I start talking and towards the end of the meal he gives me a 5% coupon off my next meal I may have been slammed at work this week but I got 5% off Kogi Gogi so I’ll chalk this up as coming out ahead :D. Afterwards I go home and code for a couple more hours before crashing. Saturday My morning begins with trash pickup as per usual. Jk, it actually begins with me working, but then I go to trash pickup. Today we have “The Ravenkeeper,” “The Politician,” and “The Grandma” along with some others. A pretty solid group. After trash pickup we stop by Tacolicious and I add another Yelp review to my list of Yelp reviews at places I didn’t eat at. You can read it here if interested. After the restaurant I depart to what is undoubtedly the highlight of the week. The Amazing Race! “The Enabler” and a couple of his friends put on an Amazing Race esque event thorughout SF. The basic idea is that we have teams that we break into and we are given clues to go to different parts of the city and once there we have challenges to solve. Successfully completing the challenge will take us to our next clue. This goes on until the end. I’ll go through each phase of the race to give a sense of how it went down. Team formation and the pre race challenge When I get to the starting point of the race (“The Enabler”’s friends apartment in Hayes Valley), I meet my team for the race. Most people came up with teams beforehand but unfortunately the person  I was originally going to do it with couldn’t make it so I spent the morning before frantically calling my friends to see if any of them were down. Unfortunately  I couldn’t find anyone who was free for the entire afternoon as required. Additionally I don’t drink which poses a bit of a problem as the aforementioned challenges above come in drinking and non drinking variants and my not drinking reduces the options that teams have. Thankfully I find some people at the last minute (some of “The Enabler”’s other friends) who also aren’t drinking and we all become a team! They’re both really cool so I lucked out with a great team.  We also have the best team name!. Once thats settled we begin the pre race event. The hosts explain to us the rules. The basic gist is that we have the clue -> challenge format listed above, and when going between clue to clue you can only walk or take public transit with the exception of a one time Uber use. To stagger the start of the race there is a pre race trivia contest and the folks that do the best at that are allowed to leave earlier. The trivia is mostly Bay Area trivia ranging from pretty easy questions (“Where is Stanford located?”), to much harder questions (“What was the purpose of Alcatraz before it became a prison?”: The answer is military fort in case you are curious :D). Our team finishes roughly 5th in the trivia. We fumble a bit at the beginning but pickup towards the end so we’re feeling ready to go at it! Clue # 1. Once we’re off we get the first clue and head off. For those reading at home I invite you to think about this clue a bit before I talk about how we approached it. When I read the first part “cherry blossoms bloom”, I immediately thought JTown since its the most iconic place with those. For Korean food I thought Daeho since its the most well known Korean place there. We head there (while racing a bit to keep up with some other teams) and it turns out we’re right! We’re rewarded with our efforts with the next challenge Drinking Challenge: Find a place that lets you do sake bombs and do sake bombs. Take videos. Non drinking challenge: Buy group size + 1 bags of roasted edamame (100g) from nijiya market, and a food item with a big enough container to hold the edamame. On checking out ask for number of pairs of chopsticks for group. Hold onto these items until you get to the location of the next clue. You can eat the food item at any point. Make sure you always keep the edamame and chopsticks. Naturally we go with the Non drinking challenge and head to the market to buy our stuff. We almost mis read the instructions and got group size bags of roasted edamame as opposed to the +1. Good thing we remembered at the last min before buying. We buy some random mochi croissants because we think the container can hold the edamame but we don’t think too deeply about it.  Look how happy I look in this picture. So cute! Clue # 2 With this clue we immediately latch onto “SFs largest park” and make a beeline for GGP. At this point we use our one Uber figuring that thats probably the biggest distance we will have to traverse in the race. Whether thats the right decision is a question we will leave for later but for now we embark! The question then becomes what attraction in GGP do we go to? We’re really not sure so we decide to start over at The Conservatory of Flowers and work our way westward. Our thinking is that there are a lot of attractions densely populated together in that area like Conservatory of Flowers, Academy of Sciences, DeYoung Museum, and Botanical gardens. We try all of them to no success. We’re really not sure what to do here and have a bunch of random ideas for different attractions to go. One of us suggests Shakespeare gardens thinking that that might be related to “notable”. At this point we ask the hosts for help and they give a hint “get on the right track”. At this point I do a facepalm as I immediately realize we need to get to Kezar stadium! Astute readers may have noticed that the clue started with “On your mark. Get set. Go!”. Sadly we totally ignored that part and only realized once we knew where to go. From what we gathered a lot of teams struggled with this clue and they gave the hint likely because of that. Once we get to Kezar stadium we find the hosts and we get the next challenge. The non drinking challenge is to take the edamame that we got and use the chopsticks to pick it up and put it in the food container. If we spill any we have to pick it up and put it back. This is brutal. I am very bad with chopsticks and go at a snails pace. Eventually after a long and tedious process with hand cramps galore we manage to get them all in. I am definitely the slowest here. Props to one of my team mates for streamlining the process and giving us tips for doing it faster! The drinking folks on the other hand have to have someone do a beer mile while everyone else drinks the same number of shots. After this they are significantly inebriated to the point where they are allowed to go directly to the next clue while we have to do another challenge to nerf us a bit. This happens to be disc golf. We have to find a hole and each of us has to get a disc in the hole from 10m away.  There is a disc golf place north west of where we are so we go there as quickly as the 7 and 29 busses let us. Once there we disc golf and it is a bit of a struggle. I am not very good at this and it takes me about 7 minutes to get it in. My other teammates aren’t great but they are better than me at least. Eventually after much struggling I do get it in and we move onto the next clue. Clue # 3 With a “night to (not remember)” it clearly has to be a bar of some sort. When we get this clue my first thought is originally an Irish bar near by as I think of pot of gold with over the rainbow. Someone else wisely suggests Castro instead and after a bit of debating between Irish bar in GGP, a wizard bar in the Marina (its a long story), and going to Last Rite in the Castro we decide on Last rite. With “over the rainbow” we’re pretty convinced its Castro but we don’t know which bar in particular. We look for $10 deals in Castro bars and we can’t find any thats a strong candidate. Our basic strategy is to to Castro and try to brute force by finding popular bars and sending pictures until we are allowed to move on. Unfortunately our decision to use the Uber earlier comes back to bite us as we have to rely on the 5 + 22 public transit combination which is not in our favor when the 22 bus gets delayed and the 5 bus has a lot of stops. Eventually we make it to the Castro but we’re still not sold on which bar. We ask the hosts about Last Rite and they say no. We think about some others and decide to try Detour because there is some Amazing Race event called a Detour apparently. The hosts give us our next challenge. Drinking challenge: Find pride themed drinks with more than one color. Take a video of you drinking it. Non drinking challenge: Go to a karaoke lounge and order a (non alcoholic) drink. Sing a song and incorporate the drink’s name into the song. The moment you replace a word or phrase with the name you have to keep replacing that word or phrase for the rest of the song. Take videos. We decide to go to The Mint nearby. As we are walking there we wonder how other teams are doing. Apparently 3 teams already finished :O. At this point we are debating giving up and just getting food but we decide to press on. One other rule is that the top 6 teams get a prize and we think we are pretty close to last. But since The Mint is so close we figure we may as well finish. When we get to The Mint we think about what song we want to do. We figure it would be fun to do “I want it that way” and replace “that way” with “orange juice”. Unfortunately since this is a public karaoke lounge as opposed to a karaoke place with private rooms there is a long line to put on a song we decide to just use whatever song is already playing. I forget what the song is to be honest as I don’t think about it in the moment. We just pick a word in the chorus (it was “love” I think) and we replace it with orange juice. The challenge goes well and now we are into … the final clue. The last clue We speed walk back to the hosts apartment (about 14 mins from where we are). While there we aren’t sure what to expect. How many teams have finished? Whats our standing? We cast aside those questions and focus only on what we can do and get there as quickly as we can. We tie with another team for getting back. When we get up to the apartment we find that the final challenge is … Jenga. One detail I forgot to mention until now is that the hosts said the last challenge is one that is better done sober. Unlike before the drinking and non drinking challenge is exactly the same. Do jenga! We have to build a jenga tower up to 22 blocks high (it starts at 16). To increase the height you have to put 3 blocks on a given layer. That means we need to put 18 blocks total. And since there are 3 of us we all have to put 6 blocks on each. At this point 5 teams have finished  so to secure our spot in the top 6 we have to beat the team that just got back. Thankfully they’ve been drinking so we do have an advantage here. Like with everything else that required careful coordination I am not a good Jenga player but thankfully my teammates give me advice on which blocks I should pick. Its tense as we try to build our tower. One other rule is that if everyone in the group takes a shot the height of the tower gets reduced by 1. This means the drinking group only needs to get to 21 and they win if they take a shot. We slowly but steadily build our tower. As we get to the last few blocks the tower begins to lean so we can’t make any mistakes. It really becomes nervewracking picking blocks and moving them as slowly as possible while aware the other team is catching up.  I’d do a doodle here but I can’t draw a jenga tower to save my butt. We keep cool heads and don’t move any blocks too fast. We’re on the 22nd layer right as the drinking team is on the 21st. If they finish their shots before we finish our last blocks we lose. Thankfully we barely manage to finish before they finish the 21st. We anxiously call the refs over and we get our 6th place finish!! Post race This was a really fun event! Big thanks to “The Enabler” and friends for running. Afterward we have a debrief where I talk about the race with other teams and learn some interesting things. Apparently for the disc golf there was a place right near Kezar stadium where we did the edamame but its pretty obscure and they meant for us to go to the course further away to nerf us a bit more since we didn’t do the beer mile. Afterwards we all go out to some bars. Unfortunately one of the hosts is moving to NYC so this is also a farewell event for him. Bye Chris! It was great to have you here and hoping NYC is a lot of fun! I don’t stick around for long as I have more work to do. I go home and work for a few more hours and then go to bed. Sunday The day begins with some early morning work followed by a brunch at Plow. I meetup with “The Professor” and “The Pickeballer”. I get my usual nothing here which means I can leave a Yelp review that you can find here. After completing this review I earned a recognition :D. After Plow I go to trash pickup. Today  at trash pickup I met one of the more “interesting” people I ever came across there. I asked my usual ice breaker “whats something cool or interesting about you that people wouldn’t expect?” and she mentions that shes been vegan for 9 years. I’ve met a number of vegans (including some of you reading this newsletter) and my response to that is basically “ok cool.”. I later learn she doesn’t have a job and when asked what she likes to do since she doesn’t work she mentions she goes down to L.A and partakes in vegan protests. Ok, so at this point she isn’t vegan, she’s VEGAN, in that she makes it a large part of her personality which I can’t say for any of the other vegans I know. Interestingly despite not having a job she mentions she likes buying luxury goods and was debating buying a Channel handbag but didnt want to because it was 12K but the max she was willing to pay was 7K. Make of that what you will. After pickup we eat brunch. Well they all eat brunch and I don’t. She’s eating some pancakes and I ask if shes concerned about the dairy in them. She pauses for a moment, realizes that there is dairy and then a couple seconds later responds with “well I need to eat”. Considering the actually vegan options like the potatoes I truly don’t know what to say to this. I also meet a guy that has a youtube channel and had a viral video with Pokemon memes so that was cool!! After trash pickup I go home and work for a few more hours. From there I go to “The Professor”’s place and hang out with him, “The Plower,” “The Pickeballer,”  and “The Professor’s” mom. She is pretty cool and it was fun meeting her. She’s in town til tomorrow so she and “The Professor” and “The Pickleballer” (who is also “The Professor”’s sister) were hanging out. Not much to say here but it was a good time. From there I go home, finish work for the weekend and write up the newsletter!.

content: I made a character list detailing every character here. I got some feedback it can be hard to keep track. Let me know if this helps! Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Major shoutout to “The Doctor” for getting a faculty offer at the AITHYRA institute in Vienna! I’m now upgrading your nickname to be “The Professor”!! Super excited to see the cool stuff you do next! I know its been super stressful with all the traveling, interviewing, and of course the political climate being super sucky to sciences. In spite of all that though you have a prof job which is amazing!! Monday Today I just went to work and chilled at home. I debated going to chess club but decided against it this week. Tuesday See Monday. Wednesday Today after work was Midnight Runners. My throat was a bit sore so I opted to walk along the route and catch up with the runners at a couple of the stops. Afters we did the post run hang over at Kezar’s pub near GGP. I sit at a table with some of my friends and when the waitress comes by I don’t order anything which prompts her to ask me to not sit at a table. To get around this I stand by the table the whole time, with a part of me hoping she comes by again so I can explain this to her but unfortunately she doesn’t come back. Thursday I have the day off for Juneteenth so me and “The Quant” go on a hike from Crissy Fields up to Engagement Hill over in The Marin Headlands. “Granola Girlie”, since you said you wanted pictures here they are After the hike I walked around in Divisadero where I found this amazing poster Honestly I think it speaks for itself really. Friday Today after work I attempted to do one of the bits from my bit jar of finding every body of water in Golden Gate Park. I started East and worked my way West hitting Lily Pond -> The fountains near the Music Concourse -> The fountain near the DeYoung I was going to hit up a lake over in the Botanical Gardens next but by the time I got there they already closed. So I stopped and decided to finish the bit tomorrow. Saturday Today begins with trash pickup as per usual. Today we have “The notetaker”, “The writer”, and “Granola Girlie”. “Granola Girlie” brought her family with her which has now 4xd the number of people I’ve met from Wyoming. After trash pickup I resume my bit and go back to Golden Gate Park to find the other bodies of water. I go from Waterfowl pond -> Blue Heron lake -> Strawberry Hill lake -> Lloyd lake -> Elk Glen lake -> Mallard lake -> Metson lake -> The Golden Gate Angling and Casting club -> Spreckels lake -> North lake -> Middle lake -> South lake At one point when I’m going between Lloyd Lake and Elk Glen lake some woman stops me and asks me where Hellman Hollow is as she is trying to find a friends birthday party. After pointing it out to her she tells me that she lost her phone and wanted to use my phone to help find hers. I didn’t get suspicious vibes from her so I let her borrow it while I stared at the sky and thought about life. We get to talking after a little while and I learn that she grew up in the city and works at an Insurance company answering calls. I asked her if she is like a good neighbor and apparently she does work at State Farm. For whatever reason I try to see how much of her I can predict based off her vibes and I’m able to get the following correct She is an introvert with about 6-10 friends Her main hobbies are reading with a little bit of art She plays videogames (I thought she played more than she did though as she said shes starting to get into it) The friend whose birthday party it is is someone she met in highschool Shes not super active but does do something like the gym once a week (it was actually pilates but I’m counting this) Eventually she decides to just head home and skip her friends birthday party while she sorts out her whole phone situation. She did say she’d be down to hang out and we do exchange numbers so we shall see if I make a new friend from this. I order her an Uber since she can’t call one herself and as she leaves I ask her to “take a picture of me” (aka hand her a picture of me that I have) for the bit. Once I finish up my lake bit I head home and quickly get the Humza cave ready for boardgame night. For boardgame night I’m joined by “The Raja of Rhythm,” “The pickleballer,” “The Yogi,” “The Quant,” and one of “The Yogi’s” friends. We play a game called Munchkin which is quite fun. Essentially the idea is everyone is in a dungeon trying to level up by fighting monsters. When you kill a monster you gain a level and the first person to get to level 10 wins. What makes the game interesting is when you fight a monster other players can come in and either help you or help the monster. In the beginning players are more likely to help each other to split rewards and get stronger faster. But towards the endgame people will help the monster to ensure someone other than them doesn’t reach level 10. The endgame was absolutely brutal as we spent at least an hour with everyone on level 9 trying to stop whoevers turn it was from reaching level 10. I had one of the best characters for helping to drag everyone else down which turned the game into a battle of attrition. After around 3 hours of playing the game we were all pretty beat but eventually a pair of winners did emerge (a bit complicated to explain how multiple people can win but just know it can happen). I still think I deserve an honorary win for all I did to keep the game going for so long. Sunday Today is trash pickup, but its not just any trash pickup as I finally got to 200 trash pickups! Its hard to believe I’ve been doing this for over 2.5 years now. I’ve made so many friends and done quite a lot because of these pickups so it has quite a special place in my heart. This was also a special trash pickup because I got “The Pickeballer” to come out today which I wasn’t expecting! Today I was joined by “The Pickeballer”, “The Quant”, “The Ravenkeeper”, “Fortnight mocap dancer”, “The Yogi”, and of course “The notetaker”. Originally I had a goal after trash pickup of trying to redeem every reward I could get but unfortunately I failed this goal as I didn’t have the stomach space for all the free food. A more achievable version of this goal may have been to have a group of friends go and do it such that between the group every reward is redeemed. Between all of us though we do manage to get through Mannys brunch, Pupusa, Ritual, Boogaloo, Senor Sisig, and Beehive which isn’t bad. We would have done Arcana as well but they were closed. After a long post trash pickup hang I head home and do some work. Unfortunately I do have a deadline coming up relatively soon so I prioritized over the newsletter.

excerpt: I made a character list detailing every character here. I got some feedback it can be hard to keep track. Let me know if this helps! Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Have a couple folks I want to shou…
content: I made a character list detailing every character here. I got some feedback it can be hard to keep track. Let me know if this helps! Previous newsletters If you want to see any of the previous newsletters look here Shoutouts Have a couple folks I want to shout out this week! First is for “Olives” for going for what she wants and moving to N.Y! I will definitely miss you but really excited for all the cool stuff you’re gonna do in The Big Apple! When you come back in August we are doing karaoke and you’re gonna hear me do Rap God and WAP. The next is for “The Doctor”! Best of luck in Austria with your interview. We all know this will be the one and you will finally become “The Professor”. And enjoy you’re well earned trip across Europe! Monday Today I took the day off from work due to being under the weather. Didn’t do much except rewatch T.V Tuesday See Monday Wednesday Today I finally had some energy in me so I started to work from home. After work I got dinner with “La Tacuqeria Royalty” over at The Laundromat. Every Wednesday they have a smash burger. Heads up the line is pretty long. We wound up waiting for half an hour. The burger was pretty good (the fact I ate it of course means I can’t review it). But I’m glad I did it though. And it was my first time hanging with  “La Tacuqeria Royalty” 1:1. He’s a super cool guy, very down to earth and someone I think I vibe with more than I initially would have thought. I need to start hanging out with him more. He’s also very into One Piece! I think theres a handful of other folks reading this who are but its always cool to find another! Thursday Today I have even more energy so I do even more work but still from home. After work I go over to “The Doctor”’s place and play some games. Since he’ll be leaving for 2 weeks we all wanna wish him luck and eat his salmon (or in my case his shrimp). Nothing particularly notable here but its a great time as always. Friday Today I finally have the energy to go the office. The hardest part was explaining to the guy at MIXT why he hadn’t seen me all week since I usually pick up the office lunch orders. Other than that the day is fine. After work I go to poker night hosted by “Fortnite mocap dancer”. Unfortunately I can’t stay for too long this time so I only get a few rounds in. Here I decide to go the entire time without looking at my cards and raise the stakes dramatically. Unlike last time I win absolutely nothing but thats fine I expected as much. I did enjoy seeing the look on peoples faces when I raised the stakes from 10 cents to a dollar. And to my credit I did *almost* win 1 of the 3 rounds. “Mr. Socksessfull” did quite well though winning $36 dollars. I do learn that someone else here is Yelp Elite so once I get to my 20 Yelp reviews I may also ask this person to nominate me as well to increase my odds. From there I go to a North beach bar crawl hosted by “The Politician”. We start out over at a small place called Nik’s cafe. Its nice at first but as the soon to be 100+ crawlers start to swarm in we quickly outgrow it. Here though I do have some nice conversations with “The Writer”, “The Fisherman”, and others. The second bar we go to called The Savoy Tivoloi is absolute peak though. Of all the bars I’ve been to for the “The Politician”’s bar crawls this one was my absolute favorite. For one thing there was easily enough space for people to talk and  there was excellent music with a live band up front. Here I ran into an old coworker of mine who told me that things at Snorkel AI were actually doing pretty well. For the sake of my equity I hope he is right. Me and “The Fisherman” really go out on dancing when the live band plays “Pink Pony Club”, and “Mr. Brightside”. After this bar we go to “Tupelo”. To be honest the vibes here weren’t as good as they were at The Savoy Tivoloi. The main part was a space issue. It was too densely packed to really have good conversations at. I think it would be an ok bar if you just want to dance but I already danced quite a bit at The Savoy Tivoloi so at this point I decided to just head home. It was definitely quite fun overall though! “Olives” also comes through at the bar crawl so I see her for the last time before she moves to N.Y which was a nice touch. Bye Olives you will be missed! Saturday The day begins with trash pickup as per usual. Nothing particularly crazy here but good to see lots of people like “The Ravenkeeper”, “The Fisherman”, “The Writer”, “The Politician”, and others. Afterwards I meet up with “The Shadow Brigade” and we go on a walk from South Mission through Balboa Park, Ingleside, Ingleside Terraces, Lakeside, and finally Stonestown. I picked this route mainly because I hadn’t actually seen a lot of these random neighborhoods in the South west part of the city. Ultimately I can’t say they’re amazing but for residential neighborhoods they are at least somewhat nice. And now I can say I’ve seen more neighborhoods in the city so there is that. The coolest thing we saw on the walk was probably the Ingleside sundial which was the largest sundial in the world at the time it was built. For whatever reason Balboa park was the most disappointing to me as I did expect it to be a somewhat interesting park as opposed to just a flat stretch of green but perhaps thats what I get for not really looking up any pictures before hand and just going on vibes. While at Stonestown we go to fix “The Shadow Brigade”’s sunglasses over at The Sunglasses hut. On one of the chairs there they had a manual lying around for how to sell care kits for their sunglasses. They covered things like “What if people ask about it being expensive”, and “What if people already have one” and so on. Through this we learn that apparently you need to hydrate your sunglasses. I find one of the employees and feign interest in buying one of these kits and ask him a bunch of these questions to see how well he was able to memorize the answers here. Unfortunately the answer was not very and I did have to remind him of a couple of them. I guess its ok because on the front of the manual I learned that the training has to be done between 05/27-06/27 so I guess he still has a little bit to finish it up. Maybe I’ll come back after and see. I wanted to get a picture of the manual to show here but unfortunately by the time I thought of it he took it back and wouldn’t let me take a picture of it. After this I got dinner with one of my old coworkers over at my favorite AYCE KBBQ restaurant  Kogi Gogi. The waiter at Kogi Gogi knows me well enough at this point that he jokingly ribbed me for not really ordering any sides as I focus mainly on the meat. It was great catching up him and learning about the cool stuff he is up to at Meta and complaining about some of the people we hated at our old job. Unfortunately my old coworker can’t eat quite as much meat as I can so it was up to me to finish the job. I did at least live up to the waiters other comment that I can eat quite a bit of meat. The night ends with me going to a graduation party for one of my coworkers who we all call “The Chief Dog officer”. This was my first time really going to a party with a bunch of my coworkers and it was pretty fun!  One of my coworkers’ boyfriend is quite the troll with the energy to match even someone like me. At one point he asks about the trash pickup I do / how I heard about it and when I give the answer “my Parole officer” he really presses me for details. I spin up an elaborate story about how I went to prison in San Quentin followed by ADX Florence. Here there was a nice “family reunion” because I ran into my uncles who flew planes. Eventually I wind up escaping the prison by first getting a poster of a model and putting it in my cell and each night slowly drilling a hole behind the poster until the hole is big enough that I can escape through it. Unfortunately I don’t get to finish the story so I never got to explain how I would have a parole officer if I escaped prison but rest assured the explanation is quite splendiferous. Some folks were planning to do karaoke and I really wanted to join but my throat was still a bit sore so I couldn’t sing. Which was a real shame because I know some of my coworkers wanted to hear me do W.A.P and Rap God and I very much wanted to deliver. Instead I just head home. Sunday Today starts with Trash pickup. For those who may be unaware the place I do trash pickup was vandalized as part of some Anti Zionist protests. I don’t really want to get political in my newsletter but seeing a place that I come every week get smashed up definitely made me angry. I owe quite a bit to the trash pickup in terms of the community I’ve gathered around me and I do see Mannys as a core symbol of the trash pickup so this struck me in a way these sort of things don’t usually. Thankfully Mannys was open and operational by the time of the trash pickup wit the caveat that some windows were boarded up. Before we started picking up trash there was also a short speech by someone who experienced Anti Semetic violence over in the Marina a couple days ago. She mentioned that she heard someone saying “F the Jews” and she said she couldn’t let that slide and got into an argument with those folks which resulted in her getting shoved to the ground and her friend getting, in her own words, “the crap beaten out of him”. I definitely respect her courage for speaking out, and it makes me wonder what I would have done. Thankfully she seems ok now and I hope her friend is as well. After this we get back to normal trash pickup which I think is good because in times like this we need to come together at a community and remember why we still have reasons to smile. Todays trash pickup turnout also doesn’t disappoint when we have “The Ghostbuster”, “The Raja of Rhythm”, “The Yogi”, “Fortnite mocap dancer”, and … “Olives”. I was quite surprised since I already thought she moved on to the great city across the coast but apparently she decided to push back her flight at the last minute because she got too wrapped up in some existing plans. We make a spontaneous shopping trip to a pop on Valencia street where I get a new denim shirt and jacket We then go to Arcana where I do my bit of asking the bartender to “take a picture of me” wherein I hand her a photo of me. She takes this and hangs it up on the wall at Arcana which I thought was pretty cool at the end we head out and I say goodbye to “Olives” for realsies this time (as far as I know anyway). “Olives” if I find out you haven’t left yet I’m so rescinding that shoutout at the beginning. I go fishing with “The Fisherman” over by Pier 3. We don’t really catch anything but some older Chinese dudes next to us catch two bass while we’re there. As someone who watches fishing more so just to hang out I’m not bothered by not catching anything as it's just fun to hang out on a nice day by the pier. Since its Fathers day I get dinner with my Dad and my older sister over at Anatolian table. Its nice to catch up with them. My Dad asks me an interesting question “If your friends were to describe you in 3 words how would they do so?”. I think about this for a while and the answer I eventually come up with is “Outgoing”, “Funny”, “Approachable”. Shortly before this I actually see “The Raja of Rhythm” walking by across the street so I ask him and he in collaboration with “Fortnite Mocap dancer” and “The Ghostbuster” and someone else came up with the answer “Eccentric”, “Committed”, and “Thoughtful” which was honestly better than my answer. I ask my Dad and Sister the same question and my Dad says “Friendly”, “Approachable” and can’t quite come up with a 3rd word. My Sister says “Thoughtful”, “Extroverted”, and “Caring”. Once dinner ends and my Dad and Sister go back home to Marin I catch up with “The Raja of Rhtyhm”, “Fortnite Mocap dancer”, and “The Ghostbuster” over at Senor Sisig and watch them eat which is as great a time as always. I learn here that Rhode Island is where The Conjuring house is which makes me kinda want to go there. I never thought I’d have a reason to want to go to Rhode Island but here we are. Afterwards I head home to write up the newsletter.

content: Announcement Today marks the half year anniversary of me doing this newsletter. Whether you’ve been reading since the beginning or this is your first issue I want to thank you for being apart of this journey with me. When I started doing this a while ago I only started doing it as part of a bit (whose origins I will touch on below), and I didn’t expect people to really like it. The first time I did this I even prefaced it with a “You don’t have to read this if you don’t want to” because I was honestly pretty scared to send it now. Flash forward to now and I know that of the (currently 33 or so), people I send this to every week at least some of y’all quite like this and have found some of my anecdotes either funny, interesting, or touching and I really appreciate that! Also I know that this can be a lot if and you’d rather I don’t send it to you feel free to let me know and I won’t hold anything against you for it :D. Monday Today after work I go to chess club. In the past I played folks way above me who could effortlessly crush me, thankfully today I find someone who is at my same noobish level and we have a fair 40 minute long match. Unfortunately I’m still not good enough at chess to really be able to describe it yet but I do know roughly that chess follows an opening, middle, and endgame structure in terms of how folks talk about it so I’ll try to roughly do that here. Opening: In the beginning we both move very cautiously. Wherever any of our pieces are at risk we don’t dare do anything aggressive with defense being the name of the game. Occasionally we both falter and lose a couple pieces, him a bit worse than me. At this point I’m up roughly a knight and a couple of pawns. This early lead causes me to lower my guard and use my queen to capture a piece which leads to my queen being captured in turn. It was as brutal as it was swift. My arrogance was immediately punished and my eyebrows leaped up in horror. For a split second all I could do was sit in stunned silence as I was down my most valuable piece. Middle: A minute later after regaining my composure I realize that in capturing my queen he left his vulnerable as well and I retaliate. I’m thankful for this not so much for the fact that I took out his queen as much as the fact that now he doesn’t have such a huge piece lead over me. From here we cast aside our previous attitudes and much more aggressively capture pieces in the name of whittling down our opponents options. Theres a saying that to capture a King you must first capture his horse and that drives both of our strategies. While we each put each other in Check once or twice its nothing serious and the main deciding factor here is eliminating pieces. Its here where I start to gain the advantage as I strip away almost the entirety of his pawns. This is important as pawns run the risk of being promoted if they make it across the board. They aren’t the biggest problem immediately but if left unchecked unexpected issues can arise. Throughout this phase we both strip each other of most of the valuable pieces with a whole bunch of M.A.D. Eventually we get to a point where one of my pawns can become a queen and I have a few pawns, a new queen, king, and knight against his king, rook, and two pawns. At this point we both think I’m in the lead here but victory isn’t quite mine yet. Endgame: Here my main objective is to take out his rook while keeping his pawns from advancing, while his is to scramble to take down a bunch of my pieces and try to force a draw. Eventually I take out the rook which pretty much seals the game. It’s not a question of if I win so much as when I’ll win. If I remember correctly I think when it looks like victory is guaranteed the opponent is supposed to concede defeat but hes committed to seeing it through to the end which I definitely respect. If I want to win this I need to properly put his King in checkmate, none of this “check” nonsense. Its surprisingly difficult to completely trap his King as somehow there is always some point of escape. Sealing the deal requires cornering him into a progressively narrower part of the board using two queens and my knight. Eventually the deed is done and he truly has no moves left to play and the game is won. This was the first chess game I won in quite a while so I was quite pleased with the results. I could have played more but that first game went considerably longer than I thought it would so I decide now is a good time to call it and quit while I’m ahead Tuesday Today I go to work and then go home and chill. Nothing interesting here. Wednesday Today after work I go to Midnight Runners and I find once again to my surprise that “The Dentist” and “La Tacqueria royalty”. Its great to see rare pokemon twice in a row but I know I can’t get accustomed to such rarities being a common occurrence. The run today isn’t too bad overall only being 3 miles but my slight sore throat definitely doesn’t do me any favors here. I mostly manage to keep up with those two rascally rabbits except at the very end. As the run comes to a close and the finish line is in sight “The Dentist” jets full speed toward the finish line with “La Tacqueria Royalty” not too far behind. I try to match but I feel a pain in my upper ribs I don’t usually feel when running. I try but today my body can’t keep up with what I want to do mentally and I help myself to a full course meal of their dust. Don’t fear though, I may have lost the race but I won a much bigger prize immediately after! I’m talking about another bit being completed! One of the bits I got was “Ask someone to take a picture of you and then hand them one”. And thats just what I did. Specifically I handed them something like this. People found the bit to be quite funny and now I think I may try to keep pictures of myself on hand so that I can do this bit now and again. It could serve as a nice compliment to my deck of cards. Because this run took place on worldwide running day we were treated to a barbeque afterwards which would have been great if not for the incredibly long line. As one might expect at an event with 150+ people service can’t exactly be fast for everybody. By the time I get to the line I ask what meat the hotdogs are made of and the guy grilling them says “meat”. Given that incredibly helpful response I opt not to eat them since I have no idea if they are beef or pork. Afterwards there is a raffle for different items like Sports Basement giftcards and Nalgene water bottles. Originally I go into this thinking I have zero hoots to give and don’t care about the raffle until I realize the golden opportunity in front of me. If I win the raffle I can go up to the announcer and ask her to “take a picture of me”. How funny that would be! Now that I have a reason to care about the raffle I eagerly await for the results only to find I don't’ win and my opportunity to do this bit just disappeared. Ah well. At the same time I got a last minute invite to “The Juggler”’s birthday party but since I got the invite while MR was happening I unfortunately can’t make it. Nevertheless I wish you a very happy birthday and I love your enthusiasm, energy, and good natured spirit! You’re such a fun guy to hang out with! And of course you’re no hasbean. Thursday Originally after work I was gonna go to a speed dating event with “The Doctor” and “The Quant” but it got cancelled at the last minute. Instead the 3 of us get dinner. Today is “The Quant’s” birthday so we turn this into a celebration dinner for him over at Abu Salim! Happy birthday Quant! Thanks for being such a great friend these last couple years. I’m glad you’re interested in all the events I’ve dragged you to over the years from long walks (props again for surviving most of the perimeter trail!), to KBBQ, Midnight Runners, Trash pickup and a lot more. Also congrats again on passing the level 3 exam for becoming a Chartered Financial Analyst. Can’t wait to dabble into more hijinks with you and perhaps even some shenanigans as well. And of course I know you have that dog in you! Thankfully since I know the Salim of Abu Salim I’m able to arrange a little birthday surprise for him as well via some Baklava cake! From there I go home to my parents place to celebrate Eid. Friday Eid Mubarak to all who celebrate! (Although given the demographics of the newsletter this may just be me here). For those unaware Eid actually occurs twice a year, once to celebrate the end of Ramadan, or in this case to celebrate the end of Hajj. Hajj is a 7 day long pilgrimage to Makkah that Muslims are expected to do once in their lifetimes. As is traditional for Eid my Dad and I go to the masjid for an Eid prayer. Before the prayer starts the imam gives a rather sassy lecture on people not embracing the traditions of Eid. He notes that nobody from Marin actually went to Hajj and that many people today especially the youth have never actually slaughtered a goat as is customary. Typically a lot of people (like myself), will pay to have one slaughtered in Pakistan or another such country rather than doing it themselves. He tells us a story of some people who raised a goat for 2 months and bonded with it before slaughtering which sounds quite tough but at the same time I respect the heck out of that commitment. He also pointedly tells off some folks having a side conversation just one row behind me. The whole lecture was dripping with “I’m not mad I’m just disappointed” vibes. After this I go to family lunch and spend some 1:1 time with my Dad. He asks me if I’ve “found anybody yet”, and since I don’t feel like telling him all my escapades from the posters to the speed dating events I just told him that I’m working on it. I ask my Dad whats new with him and he says not much, he’s just doing the same ol same old. I briefly try to convince him to try something different from what he normally does since I know given his semi retired state he has the time but sadly this doesn’t quite go anywhere. After another prayer at the Mosque I head back to SF. I get dinner with “The Quant” and “The Raja of Rhythm” over at an AYCE Brazillian steakhouse Espetus. Its not quite as good as Kogi Gogi but its nice to try something different every now and again. Unfortunately since I ate here its not eligible for a yelp review. “The Raja of Rhythm” has been getting really into motorcycles since completing his course and it was super cool to hear him explain all the different aspects of motorcycles to me. I’m pretty excited for this arc of his, anything that can get someone to nerd out for 15+minutes straight in a convo is great for a person. Saturday The day begins with Trash pickup. Its fun but not too much in particular to note here. Originally I was going to keep the twin brother bit  with “The Ravenkeeper” going by getting “The Doctor” to pretend to be me but eventually I decide to cancel the bit and just tell her. It was a fun bit while it lasted tho! From there its time for “The Quant”’s birthday party. We start off by rock climbing over at Mission Cliffs. For climbing we have “The Quant”, “The Plower”, “The Doctor”, “The Doctor’s sister” (who I will henceforth by request refer to as “The Pickleballer”), and “Mirandom thoughts”. As usual climbing proves to be a very humbling experience for me as I’m only able to do 1 of the 4 V0s I attempt. Unfortunately my fear of heights  starts kicking in and I’m worried that I’m going to fall. I’ve had friends get bad injuries from climbing and I don’t like it enough that it feels worth the risk, but this is for “The Quant” so I try my best. And my best is terrible. This is me at the end I’m left an empty husk of a man. After climbing we split off and me “The Plower”, “The Quant”, and “The Plower” go to see the new John Wick movie while the others take a little break. “The Doctor” has to work on a big presentation for next week which I’ll go into when I use that as an excuse to praise him so look forward to that in next weeks issue … or not I’ll be doing it anyway 🤷. The new John Wick movie  was pretty good! Since I know some of y’all will be seeing it soon I’ll divide my thoughts here into the Spoiler and Non spoiler review Non spoiler review John Wick Brap brap pew pew. People are dead. There are lots of fights. It’s a John Wick movie. And the ending is straight fire (iykyk). Spoiler Review Overall the movie was quite good! It nails what people want which are the fight scenes. There is a plot in the movie but its not what we really come for but its not bad, its just standard. Unfortunately there is a bit of a lull between the setup and the first major fight which is where I took a nap. I missed about 2 paragraphs of the Wikipedia article worth of the movie. This doesn’t really factor into my ability to follow the action so who cares. The plot is a fairly simple revenge story about a girl trying to kill the cult who killed her parents. Since this takes place between 3 and 4 we do get to see John Wick himself for a brief cameo which was pretty cool. After the movie we go to dinner over at Funky Elephant, a Thai place in the Mission! The food is quite good! See here for a full Yelp Review. As a sidenote once I get to 20 Yelp Reviews I’m gonna enlist “The Dentist” to nominate me for Yelp Elite and then I’ll try my luck at prying open the doors of Valhalla. Here at the dinner we have the full force of the birthday party. We’ve got “The Quant”, “The Plower”, “The Taco”, “The Shadow Brigade”, “Mirandom thoughts”, “The Pickleballer”, “The Doctor”, “From the loin”, and some other schmuck. We got “The Quant” a custom Pokemon card as a gift which I was quite proud of. The first ability in the card is a reference to him being a “Chartered Finanaical Analysit”, though me and “The Doctor” always like to troll by calling him a “Financial Accountant”. If any of y’all see him in person I highly encourage you to do the same its great fun! The second ability is more of an inside joke whose explanation is outside the scope of the newsletter. After we pay I try getting the waiter to come and do a joke where they say there is an irregularity with the bill and ask if any of us is a financial accountant and while their attempt gets an A for effort the joke doesn’t quite stick. From there we go to the Humza cave and play some board games including Secret Hitler and Coup. For the people who haven’t been to my place before I get some great reviews “I’m appalled” - “The Shadow Brigade” “Wow … just wow” - “Mirandom thoughts”. Thanks, love y’all too :D! But in all seriousness I’ll admit my apartment is a tad bare bones right now and perhaps another improvement arc I might enter is to add some decorations for the walls as opposed to the nothing thats hanging there right now. “The Plower” and “The Doctor” even offered that if I give them $100 they will buy and hang up stuff for me. So look forward to a version of The Humza cave with stuff on the walls in the future. Sunday The day starts off with trash pickup as per usual. One of the smaller ones in terms of people I know so I meet some new folks who seem cool but their not “The Shadow Brigade” level where I’ll drag them to come defeat the shopping goliath with me the same day, but thats cool they can’t all be.It's not just new people though as we have “The Avocado” with us as well which is always a great time. One of the new folks I meet is a 34 year old woman who complains about men on Hinge and says “Everyone on Hinge is the ugliest male I’ve ever met”. After seeing her reject people I’m like “damn, if those guys are ugly I don’t wanna know what that says about me”. From there I go to a moving out party hosted by “Mr. Green flag”. Its great catching up with friends here that I don’t see as much as I’d like these days like “The fisherman”, “The Plant Prince”, and “The Trash Queen”.  I also meet some new folks who seem cool. I ask my usual ice breaker “Whats something cool or interesting about you that people wouldn’t expect?” and I get a couple pretty interesting answers. One girl is *really* good at singing. She says she has pipes like some celebrity singer whose name I forgot. Apparently when she went to L.A and did karaoke at a public bar some guy dropped to his knee and kissed her hand. Damn now I want to hear her sing sometime I’m quite curious. Another guy has aphantasia which is a condition where you can’t picture images in your minds eye. I’ve heard of the condition before but I’ve never met anyone with it so it was interesting to hear him talk about his experiences. He is also a super talented artist who showed some of the stuff he draws and it was really good!! I mentioned before that “Mr. Green flag” is hosting this as a moving out party but thats not quite right. The party is more meant to be a celebration of being grateful for things today that may not always be there and to remember the phrase ‘its nice while it lasted’. I won’t go into full detail since this is my newsletter not his but I’ll just say iykyk. Also I understand that last sentence might sound a bit gloomy but thats not how he would want it to be thought, this is a happy party and the mood definitely reflects such! Amusingly enough a lot of people sort of missed the point and thought it was just a moving out party and assumed he was moving out of the Bay completely when really he is going to go travel for like a month and then just moving apartments. As part of the party one of “Mr. Green flag”’s friends made a jar where we could write our favorite memories with him. Its hard to pick one particular memory but given the timing I’ll pick this. It was at a party of his a half a year ago where the idea for the newsletter was born. The full story is that “Mr. Green flag” was having a party and since a lot of people were coming who he hadn’t seen in a while he posted a Partiful update with major life events that happened to him over the last half a year. I was talking with him about this at his party because I thought it was an interesting idea. He does it so that he doesn’t have to repeat the same status updates to everyone he talks to and can focus on getting to know what the guests are up to. I liked that perspective and he and “The Plant Prince” jokingly suggested I write a newsletter about my life. I don’t think at the time they thought I would actually do it or that it would turn out quite like this but here we are! Thanks for being where this all started!! “Mr. Green flag”, you’re a very gentle soul and certainly a very thoughtful and introspective person. I told you this in person but I’d love to see you write a newsletter :D. Hope your travels are really fun and looking forward to seeing all the new stuff you’ll be up to when you’re back! From there I go home and write up the newsletter.

title: Episode 25
excerpt: Previous chapters If this is your first newsletter and you’re interested in reading previous ones I’ve compiled a list of them here Shoutouts I’m starting a new section called Shout outs. The inspiration for this is someone once likened this newsletter to a s…
content: Previous chapters If this is your first newsletter and you’re interested in reading previous ones I’ve compiled a list of them here Shoutouts I’m starting a new section called Shout outs. The inspiration for this is someone once likened this newsletter to a social network where only I post. Given that I thought it would be great to shout out people who have done cool / interesting stuff this week so I can brag about how awesome y’all are to my other friends. Starting off we have “The Raja of Rhythm” who is doing a class this weekend to get his Motorcycle license. I think thats pretty sick and deserves a shoutout. Monday For Memorial Day I did the “Breakers to Bay” walk. This is essentially doing the reverse of “Bay to Breakers” where I walked from Lands End to the Ferry Building. I was joined on this endeavor by “The Quant” and “The Raja of Rhythm”. It was a beautiful day out and really nice to go for a long walk like this. Afterwards a long walk like that we go to Kogi Gogi to get some good meat in and as always it meats if not exceeds expectations. As we were waiting outside before we got our table we struck up conversation with someone painting a building nearby. He told us about how he came to the U.S from Mexico when he was 19 and has been painting buildings for over 15 years. I don’t talk to a lot of people like this generally so it was quite unique. He’s planning to go back to Mexico soon and do the same thing over there where the money he has saved up goes a lot further. Tuesday Today during work I make a spontaneous decision to throw away my unicorn hat, also affectionately dubbed “The Chastity Hat”. I like the hat and think its fun but if I want to reach my goal of being more fashionable sacrifices do need to be made and this is one of them. Goodbye chastity hat, you were great fun and I’m wishing you all the best on your new travels in trashland but its time for improvement. Onwards and upwards! After work I keep my momentum from above and go shopping.I start off with socks as I figure that would be low hanging fruit. I actually quite enjoy getting fun socks and it requires less effort than the other parts of the wardrobe. I go to “Sockshop Haight Street” and pickup quite the haul Afterwards  I go to Buffalo Exchange to try to pick up jackets only to be met with abject failure. Here my lack of fashion sense means that I need to recruit help from one of the group chats with “The Doctor”, “The Plower”, “The Quant”, and “The Taco” on hand to provide advice on the items I pick. And it turns out everything I pick sucked. Heres a selection in case y’all want to roast my terrible ability to pick clothes as well. Fair warning since this involves many pictures of me I recommend having some ibuprofen on hand if you don’t have any before looking at the next section. You’ve been warned. The feedback I got on every outfit basically boiled down to “No”. It was incredibly exhausting trying on outfit after outfit, sending it to the groupchat, and being met with a no. I generally pride myself on having high energy levels but 20 minutes of this broke me. I’ve walked 45 miles over 19 continuous hours, ran 5 miles with an air purifier , and wore down Garden Creamery until they brought back the Mujicha ice cream flavor. At this point I thought I could face any challenge that came my way with a smile on my face. I had no idea how wrong I was. I felt crushed mentally and spiritually. I had flashbacks to when I was a kid going to the outlet malls with my family taking solace in the PSP that I brought to keep myself entertained while everyone else went to slay the shopping beast. But now I have to try to slay the beast myself and I failed. It was clear to me that the next time I do this I can’t go alone and need reinforcements. I somberly walk out of the thrift store and try my best to recoup my morale by playing some spikeball over in PanHandle. It helps but I was definitely off my game today due to the damage I incurred. Wednesday Today after work I go to Midnight Runners. I must have rolled a d20 before coming to run club today because 3 rare Pokemon came to run club being “The Dentist”, “La Taqueria Royalty”, and rarest of all “The Enabler”. I wonder if this is what it feels like to get that super rare Charizard Pokemon card. Of course “The Quant” is there as reliably as usual :D. Without an air purifier to carry today the run was pretty straightforward. Afterwards we go to Tony’s Pizza which is great. In case anyone is interested I wrote a full yelp review of it here as part of my quest to become Yelp Elite. Thursday Today at work I learn that one of my coworkers is going on a yacht party that her and her boyfriend were invited to and the boyfriend unfortunately couldn’t make it. I think it would be hilarious if I pretend to be her boyfriend and go but sadly she shoots me down. I’m not even really that interested in a yacht party, I just think the idea of pretending to be someone else so  I can crash a yacht party would be fun. The main reason I bring this up is I told her that in response I’d mention it in the newsletter and I am nothing if not a man of my word. Instead of that I meet up with “The Raja of Rhythm” and one of his friends over at Fermentation Lab and have a chill night. While we’re talking she mentions wanting to get a tattoo of a big cat on her back. I was hoping it would be a Cougar so I could make a Cougar joke but it winds up being a Jaguar. Friday Today after work I do some emergency shopping. I’m trying to convince someone that I have a twin brother by the name of Imran so I quickly cobble together a Goodwill outfit thats different from what I would wear. Thankfully since I’m not worried about this looking good I can just by stuff quickly and circumvent facing the shopping beast. This is the outfit I wind up with I give the outfit a test drive as I go to poker. “The filmmaker” is hosting it and I’m joined by “John Wick”, “The Raja of Rhythm”, and many others. Originally I walk into this game thinking that I’ll be charitably donating my $5 buy in from the less fortunate to the more fortunate. I had absolutely zero expectations that I’d win. Surprisingly lady luck actually smiled on me more than I thought. My golden rule for playing poker was to not focus on winning or losing but instead doing whatever I found interesting. For example I would not look at my cards and instead opt to go based on vibes. I reasoned that winning or losing a few bucks pales in comparison to the fun of just assuming I had really good cards sometimes and play accordingly. It was pretty funny whether I won or lost this way and sometimes I won big with multiple straights, and 3s of a kind that I only knew about after I had to reveal. In the end I wound up winning $16 which means I’ve now officially entered the 1%. So you know, bow down peons. The nice thing was that everyone left with chips in the end. Some left with chips on their pockets while others left with chips on their shoulders but hey, a chip is a chip. “Enabler”, if you’re reading this I know you play poker sometimes so lets play together. Also “The Philosopher”, next time I come to poker night I’ll actually play. Saturday The day begins with Trash Pickup. I mentioned before I’m trying to convince “The Ravenkeeper” I have a twin and this is where I put it to the test. I go to trash pickup not as Humza but as “Imran” my twin brother. Humza was supposed to come but he “was out drinking last night and wound up sleeping in til 11:30”. I’m pretty sure she doesn’t believe me one bit throughout this but as someone who commits to the bit I can’t just back down. I keep the charade up for about 2 hours. It gets tricky as she asks me more and more questions like “Whats something about Humza he would never tell us”. I have to create a whole fictitious backstory while keeping in mind everything I had already made up in the past. Essentially it was the longest and trickiest improv I had ever done. Supposedly Imran works at Google and she asked for a referral. I came up with a Google Voice number just in case she ever asked for a phone number but she wanted to tap phones instead. Truly sneaky indeed.  Due to various circumstances the backstory wound up involving me pushing “Imran” down some stairs when we were 7 giving him a scar that I still make fun of to this day. He also lives in the Marina, hates trash, and loves playing soccer. He wasn’t even going to come to trash pickup except for the fact that he wanted to prove his existence and that his friends cancelled on him for the usual post hangover Brunch. Eventually we part ways after Imran promising to refer her to Google ..,. Somehow. I learn from “Granola Girlie” that she reads my newsletter with breakfast so if anyone ever asks about I can now say that the newsletter is a key part of a balanced breakfast. From there I go to Chinatown. As part of my birthday present I got a jar of bits to try and achieve and one of them is the following For the item to be mysterious I set the rule that I should have no idea what it is because the label is written only in Chinese. I walk through multiple shops and eventually I find this It looks about as good as any other mystery item I could find so I decide to buy some and eat it. I buy roughly a quarter of a pound of the stuff only to find that it tastes incredibly mulchy and I give up after a couple of bites. My mouth feels dirty after eating this and I wouldn’t recommend it to almost anyone (except one person who we will talk about soon). After throwing the rest of “mystery item” away I learn from a Chinese friend I ran into that this is apparently called Polygonatum and its used to make soups. Apparently its also toxic to consume in large quantities. Guess its a good thing I didn’t eat the whole quarter of a pound. I’m sure the slight queasiness I felt in my stomach immediately after eating it was probably unrelated. I go to Dolores Park to try another bit that I got I went around shouting “Life advice … 25 cents” and “A quarter now is worth a quarter life crisis”. As expected nobody took me up on it. To be fair I didn’t adequately prepare this bit. I just did it because I happened to be nearby. In the future when I make a more solid attempt of it I’m gonna get a table and make a sign advertising my life advice services. Maybe somebody will come by, probably nobody will but at least then I can say I truly tried. Afterwards I meet up with “The Doctor” and we play Gomoku in Dolores for a while. The man is truly a god of Gomoku. For those unaware Gomoku is a game where you try to place 5 tiles of the same color in a row on a Go board before your opponent does. I play multiple rounds and lose against him every time. I do improve as the games progress though. Our last game is a six minute long battle of pure intensity. Its pitch silent as we’re both concentrating on our moves. My brows inch deeper and deeper down with each passing move as I try my best to block his relentless onslaught. I try to give myself mental strength by mentally replaying intense fights I’ve seen in Shounen anime as the protagonist boldly tries to beat the overpowered Antagonist. This was it. This was gonna be my moment of glory. Sadly towards the end my greed gets the best of me and I think I have an opportunity to go for 5 in a row only to play right into his hands. I immediately crash onto my back and sigh in defeat. From there we meet up with “The Plower” and play Dune Imperium. After a few months of not playing its refreshing to play again. I was worried I would still be burnt out after all the online Dune we played while “The Doctor” was travelling but as the game goes on the old joy I used to feel slowly comes back. I’m still not as into the game as I used to be but it nevertheless feels a bit like the good ol days of Dune. Sunday The day begins with trash pickup. There are surprisingly few people here this time. I wind up pairing up with someone I don’t know called “The Shadow Brigade”. She tells me shes in the Army reserves doing signal processing transmitting signals and intercepting enemy signals which is super cool. I almost decide to give her the nickname “Mixed Signals” but realize thats easy to misinterpret so “The Shadow Brigade” it is. Rarely do I make friends with / vibe with someone so quickly, it reminds me of when I met “The Enabler”, and “The Dentist. Also, its a good thing that shes in the Army as well because I need all that strength for the upcoming fight ahead. After trash pickup we along with “The Plower”, “The Doctor”, and “The Quant” go to Stonestown to face the shopping beast once more. I learned from Tuesday that I can’t face it alone so I bring a whole squad to take down the goliath. My objective here is to get as many things I can that look good and that will help me face an upcoming trial that will be discussed next week. I hope y’all still have the ibuprofen handy as there will be a lot more pictures of SF’s ugliest shopper inbound. We first start with Zara where I have surprising success buying a jacket and shirt that the group likes I leave Zaras feeling a bit tired but still energized and ready for the next fight. Little do I know how bad this would be. We then go to the main boss Uniqlo. To say Uniqlo was overwhelming was an understatement. It really forced me to use every bit of willpower I had left. Everyone in the group presented me a bunch of different options to try on. Each option was both a blessing and a curse as I had to go through the ordeal of changing, sending a picture, and asking for feedback. It was like Tuesday but much worse. Of course that all assumes I can even get to the changing room in the first place. I first have to deal with a 10 minute line which already provides significant strain. Whoever made Uniqlo so popular that I have to wait in line for 10 FLIPPIN MINUTES TO CHANGE deserves a whole bunch of Polygonatum down the throat. Eventually I make it to the changing room and try on a whole bunch of things. After all these outfit changes I feel like a broken husk of a human being. Barely being able to think about more than the next step I take. Thankfully we find some stuff thats good. The pants from the third photo and the jacket from the 5th photo wind up being winners. I get one more jacket like that but in black. Below are some outfits I made with what I bought Theres one last stop before calling it done and thats shoes. Thankfully “The quant” really takes over here and just gives me shoes to try on and we see what we all like while I’m disassociating mentally. Eventually we decide on these And the outfit is complete. Mission accomplished! Thanks to everyone involved who helped me take down the goliath. Especially “The Shadow Brigade” who I only just met that day but managed to rope into such a perilous undertaking. I really hope I don’t have to face this gauntlet of horrors again for a while. AFterwards we all head to “The Doctor”’s place to play some board games. And then I go home and write up the newsletter.

title: Episode 24
excerpt: Monday Today is a pretty ordinary day in the bucket. I go to work, go home, and write up the newsletter that I procrastinated on last week. Pretty standard stuff. Tuesday Today after work I go to play spikeball over in the Pan Handle. Unfortunately I don’t ge…
content: Monday Today is a pretty ordinary day in the bucket. I go to work, go home, and write up the newsletter that I procrastinated on last week. Pretty standard stuff. Tuesday Today after work I go to play spikeball over in the Pan Handle. Unfortunately I don’t get to play quite as many games as I’d like so instead I decide to practice my serves. I have this one serve I do where I hit the ball between my legs so it hits the net real low. I can do it at least 30% of the time but want to get it higher so its more useable I have another serve I do where I hit the ball from the side and chop it towards the net rather than hitting it directly on. I tried for all of a minute to draw this but my limited stick figure skills have failed me here. Hopefully if not y’all can visualize this in your head and if not well idk man sahwee. Wednesday During work today I come to the realization that I”m not really using my MIXT points well enough. For those unaware Mixt is a salad chain in SF and it happens to be where I get lunch every day. Because I pay for a bunch of orders on the company credit card I’ve accumulated a whole bunch of reward points with nothing to use them on. Today I think to myself that it would be cool if I can get the custom salad I order every day as a permanent menu item (“The Iqballer”). I figure the best way to do that would be to message the CEO since Twitter taught me you can sometimes get good results by doing that. It turns out the CEO is on LinkedIn Since she is out of my network I need LinkedIn premium to message her. Shoutout to “The Plower” and “The Plower”’s boyfriend for getting me free LinkedIn premium so I can do so. I shoot her a message and unfortuantely she hasn’t responded yet. I need to follow up with her later Today after work is Midnight Runners. But this isn’t just any ordinary MR. THis is the one where I do the air purifier challenge. This is essentially where I do the whole 5 mile run while carrying my air purifier. Some of you may wisely be wondering why I would do something like this. Its because someone at Bay 2 Breakers jokingly suggested I do it and well you all know me at this point. When I see a bit to commit to I’m gonna do it. To be honest this was harder than I thought it would be. I don’t think it was so much the weight as it was the clunkiness of carrying it. The weight wasn’t too bad (probably between 10-20 pounds), but it wasn’t easy to carry and I did have to shift it around a bunch to get it to keep my arms from getting too sore. Also I noticed I was definitely expending more effort. Even going at a slower pace I was much more winded cardio wise than normal. So evidently its doing something. One other thing I didn’t expect while doing this is how many people would ask why I’m doing it. I’m not kidding when I say that somewhere between 10-20 different people asked me why I’m carrying an air purifier. Many people thought I was doing this because I just bought it and didn’t want to leave it there, or that I lost a bet of some sort. I’m surprised this is so much of a curiosity for folks but apparently it was. Afterwards is the post MR hang which is great as always. Thursday Today I start the morning with a little stroll before work since the weather is absolutely amazing. I catch the tail end of the Almost Friday Run club as part of this. By tail end I specifically mean the part where people are socializing and have already finished running. I figured I’d rather enjoy the nice weather with a leisurely walk then try to run. One hack I’ve realized is that if you join them just for the socializing they don’t really care if you actually did the running or not. Its even funnier if before revealing I didn’t run I crack a little smirk and mention how I didn’t even break a sweat. At this run club I met somebody who is actually a professional musician. I’ve never met one before so it was pretty cool hearing about her experiences. Apparently the job has you contract out to different harmonics for short stints and move around. She said she did it so then even if it fails she will have cool stories to tell and evidently she did. From there I go to work. Some of my coworkers make me a fruit birthday cake since they know I’m on a diet It was really nice and very much appreciated!! After work I go to a dating event. This isn’t quite like the Shuffledating events I’ve gone to in the past. Instead this is an event run by some Stanford students doing an AI matchmaking company. The whole premise here is that before the event you have a conversation with an AI model describing your personality along with what you’re looking for in a partner and they use that to match you up with someone. It seemed intriguing so I decided “why not”. When I get there it turns out the event starts with a bunch of regular mingling with the AI match part coming later. The mingling part is essentially a couple hundred people chatting each other up. I guess its just like a bar except you know everyone there is single. I have a bunch of conversations with people many of whom seem cool but nobody I really vibe with. I meet one person who did research on cows in undergrad trying to figure out what environmental factors lead them to being the happiest and it turns out the way you brush them had the biggest impact.I have a bunch of other miscellaneous conversations that don’t really go anywhere. One interesting quirk of an event like this with so many people is that a lot of conversations feel very ephemeral with very quick turnaround times if you’re not vibing. I guess the emphasis here is on vibing quick and early which I’m not always sure is realistic. Usually on a first date at people generally have at least an hour to get to know each other but oh well. During one of my conversations I brought up my weekly newsletter and she said “Do your friends actually read it?”. I was a bit taken aback and said yes and she said “Oh thats really sweet of them.”. I’ll admit that definitely threw me for a loop. Its rare to meet someone so openly condescending towards a hobby of mine. Usually people would at least keep that thought to themselves and say some sort of empty phrase peppered with a hint of plausible deniabilty if they really didn’t care for it. I’m not sure whether to be impressed by the honesty or put off by it. Suffice to say that conversation didn’t really go anywhere. As I left the conversation I was more on the taken aback side and silently hoped the middle school students she taught would be extra annoying the next day. Interestingly I meet as many current coworkers as former at this event with both of those numbers being greater than 0 which reminds me just how small a world this truly is. After 40 minutes of this we finally get the AI matches. We’re told there are envelopes in the back and we need to go to the table thats been designated for us. I match with one “Molly M” at one “Table 53”. Thats all well and good except for the fact that I don’t see a Table 53 as the tables only go up to 32. I pace back and forth throughout the bar looking for this supposed Table 53 only to find that its as real as me not committing to the bit. Eventually the organizers send out a text blast saying they messed up and anyone with a higher table number should congregate over by the pool table. While on my way there I trip over a metal grate and quickly grab a woman’s shoulder instinctively to balance myself. I always know how to make myself look good. Eventually after a while I do wind up meeting this “Molly M” and we chat for a few minutes. Shes a genetic councilor specifically in the area of cancer. I didn’t know that certain kinds of cancer were hereditary so that was interesting to learn. She seemed fun but I guess she didn’t feel the same way when I got the “it was nice to meet you” just 3 minutes in. I’ve learned that “its nice to meet you” is not the same thing as “its nice to talk to you” I decide to head out shortly after this and go to bar night with “The Lad’s”. We go to the usual spot of Fermentation Lab and just chill for a while. I talk with “The Mosher”, “The Orchestra captain”, “The juggler”, and “Thats nuts”. It was a a fun time but nothing overly memorable. Friday Today after work I host a board game night over at The Humza cave. I’m joined by “The organizer”, “The Doctor”, “The Mosher”, “The Boxer”, and “John Wick”. Interestingly “The Mosher” and “John Wick” have the same actual first name so I do wind up using these character names to help distinguish them. We play a few rounds of Secret Hitler where the fascists get their butts kicked all 3 times without it even being close (I trust you all to make your own jokes about how this relates to the current political climate and insert it in here). Naturally of course I’m also the only person who was fascist all 3 times as well. We also play Coup where I introduce a new house rule of not teaching new people how to play and having them figure it out for themselves which leads to some pretty funny results. Saturday Today starts off with Trash Pickup over in The Mission. The crowd is smaller than usual (likely due to Memorial day weekend) but its no less fun.
