While there me and “The writer” meet a guy who is *REALLY* good at impressions. He can do all sorts from “Thor”, to different nationality accents, and a lot more. It was super interesting seeing him do all these impressions. After trash pickup its time for my party in GGP! We start off over by The Conservatory of Flowers and dance our way through GGP. We make our way from the Conservatory of Flowers roughly to the rollerskating ring and then back. Huge thanks to everyone coming to dance with me! I know many of y’all weren’t comfortable dancing but even just walking with me while I danced was still appreciated. Props to “The fisherman” and “The Doctor” for your killer moves. One especially nice touch is that some of my friends got a bunch of toy unicorn hats from Amazon like this and everyone wore them which was very touching! We then picknicked in GGP for a while and did presents. A bunch of y’all contributed to some pretty awesome group gifts! I’m really touched by the gifts, they’re incredibly funny! I can’t wait to start going through the bit jar and doing some of these bits! And to wear my new shirt! :D We picknicked in GGP for a while and enjoyed the nice day. It was really great getting to just hang out and catch up with a bunch of friends especially those who I don’t get to see too often these days. After the picnic we went to Volcano Curry over in Richmond for dinner. Its one of my favorite restaurants here, the beef tendon curry is really good! The night ends with karaoke over at K-Box. We have some really good singers in the group espeically “The Raja of Rhythm” and “Farz”. Its a really grand time! The one downside is that they don’t quite have every song we want. It’d be nice if these karaoke places let us connect our phones or something so we can pick out different songs. The night ends with me doing Rap God because you know, I gotta do Rap God. Unfortunately it wasn’t on the K-Box’s list of songs so we hack our away around it by connecting my phone to the speaker that I brought for dancing and use one of the mics as an amp. It ain’t much but its an honest song. Huge thanks again to everyone who came today! Y’all are what make SF such a special place to me!! Sunday Today begins with Trash pickup as per usual. At the same time there is also Carnivale happening which is pretty fun to see! “Olives” is Jamaica so we wanted to find any Jamaican representation but unfortunately we couldn’t see any. Interestingly Jamaican Carnivale is actually bigger than South American Carnivale but thats not well advertised here. Incidentally at the trash pickup I wind up meeting someone who looks just like the person from Thursday who commented on the Newsletter. She has the exact same as well but when I ask if she’d seen me somewhere before or if she’s a middle school teacher she says no to both of those. After  all the festivities I head over to a birthday party for one of my old coworkers. I catch up with a few of my old coworkers there and what I hear doesn’t exactly make me regret my decision to leave. Interestingly this old coworkers is about to leave herself to become a full time LinkedIn influencer. I’ve never heard of anyone trying to be an influencer over there and while I have a general disdain for LinkedIN as a platform in general I wish her luck and I respect her conviction to go full time on something like this. For whatever reason at this party in particular I get bored of introducing myself to a whole bunch of people and decide to leave a bit early which is pretty unusual for me. From there I go to dinner with my family. We do a joint birthday dinner as both me and my younger sister had birthdays recently. For a while I didn’t really tell my parents about me doing trash pickup because in the past they expressed their disapproval of it but I figured I may as well tell them. This was inspired by what happened back in episode 16 when I realized that in order to feel closer to my family I should tell them more about the kinds of things that I do. My Mom wasn’t the happiest at first but it wasn’t as bad as I thought it would be. My family all found it funny when I told them my “Thank the courts” joke and the fact that I was able to get us 30% off on a pretty big meal at Anatolian table didn’t hurt either. From there I head home. Unfortunately I have a bad headache at this point so I’m not able to finish up the newsletter quite on time

title: Episode 23
excerpt: Monday The day starts off with work as per usual. After work I decide to go to chess club. I’m terrible at chess but I heard about it and it seemed interesting. I played two games and got my butt kicked times. Unfortunately I don’t even know chess well enough…
content: Monday The day starts off with work as per usual. After work I decide to go to chess club. I’m terrible at chess but I heard about it and it seemed interesting. I played two games and got my butt kicked times. Unfortunately I don’t even know chess well enough that I can properly describe the game to give a breakdown of the dynamics so instead I’ll say the game started off as ok, became sad and ended as a big sad. The second game actually started off ok, became happy, became slightly sad before sharply turning into big big sad. After playing these games I think that chess could be a fun thing to try and pickup so I’ll come back again sometime and maybe not end a game as big sad. Tuesday Today after work I go to the Panhandle to try to play spikeball with some friends. Originally I was going to go to a speed dating event with “The philosopher” but it got cancelled due to low signup. Unfortunately when I get there all the spikeball nets are taken so I’m forced to play hacky sack instead. For those who may be unaware hacky sack is a game in which you kick a small beanbag like thing with a group of people and try to keep it from touching the ground. After playing it once I can unironically say that it REALLY SUCKS. I mean seriously its like if you take the combined terribleness of Catan, Dune 2, and Hadestown and combine them into an absolute abomination of a game. Unlike chess which I was bad at but want to improve at, I instead seek to improve hacky sack by burning it to the ground. Wednesday Today after work I go to Midnight Runners. The run itself is perfectly fine with not much to really say. While at the run I ask several people my new icebreaker question “Whats something cool or interesting about you that people wouldn’t expect?”. One person said that they are actually passionate about coding which they noted as a rarity in the Bay. I quite appreciated that answer as I personally would agree with that persons sentiment. Another said that there is nothing about them people wouldn’t expect and that they are a boring person. I would have liked to pry more because I think there is something interesting in almost everyone but many are just bad at bringing it to the surface but I didn’t quite have the time to do so. Thursday Today *before* work I go to an early morning run club over in Golden Gate Park. They call this the Almost Friday run club which wins the prize for most accurately named run club I’ve ever been to. But when the competition is called “Midnight runners’ and you meet at 630PM thats not exactly a stiff fight here. The poster I found this club through said they “don’t run fast”. I found this to be a lie as they were running at a 9-9:30 pace which meant I had to actually try to keep up with them. Unfortunately my legs were a bit sore from yesterdays run so I bow out early on and instead decide to enjoy a nice morning in GGP and catchup with the rascals later. Naturally the fact that I didn’t run with them didn’t stop me from joining their group picture. We head over to Flywheel afterwards where I watch them get coffee. They seem like a cool bunch but I didn’t get to know them super well. I may go again and see if I can keep up. After work I go to a dating event designed to help men with any dating issues they may have. For me I’m nervous about asking women out in person which is kinda funny considering that in almost every other aspect of my life I’m pretty confident and can say almost whatever to anyone more so than almost anyone I’ve met. But I do have my weaknesses and this is one of them. At the event I meet some real characters. There is this one guy who is pseudonymous and only goes by his twitter name rather than his government name. I also meet someone who brought a bunch of pens for people to borrow for a group journaling activity and they said that they greatly value the pens and took a picture so they know exactly which pens are returned by the end. Even I have to admit they were a tad out there. The event itself is interesting. It starts with us journaling about our issues and why we think we have them. I mention my lack of confidence and that I’m scared of rejection turning things awkward. After this they ask us to imagine a situation in which we lacked confidence to do something we wanted. I thought back to a girl I met at trash pickup last year who was quite attractive and I would have liked to ask out but ultimately never did. I knew for a fact she was single because I saw her on Hinge but I never quite did anything with that. The host then asked us to imagine how a version 2.0 of us would have acted and how that could have played out for both better or worse. I imagined myself having done it and went through some scenarios both good and bad. I think the key takeaway of this was supposed to be you mentally acclimating yourself to doing the thing in question. This then turns into people asking the host a bunch of questions. He mentions that he met his current girlfriend at an event he ran called “awkward flirting” and that they had both read each others blogs. Like I said this event had a pretty high density of characters. I unfortunately need to leave early because I have another thing to do tonight. From there I go to a bar in Lower Haight because “The hombre” is moving out of his apartment and having a party to celebrate. This party was cool because it was a crossover of many different folks including “The fisher”, “Green flag”, “Granola girlie”, “The pasta prince”, and many others. As it turns out at the same time “The lads” are having a bar night as is typical on a Thursday so I decide to invite them over making this a real crossover episode between all walks of life. This also means that I’m actually the one who knows the most folks at this party. Its great catching up with a bunch of these folks and excited for “The hombre” to progress on the next step of his apartment journey. Turns out he is also going to Argentina for 6 weeks which is super exciting! Once things wrap up I rope “The philosopher” into walking me home and we chat more about this and that. One thing he brought up since I talked about the dating event is attractiveness and that I’m not really any women’s type based on physical looks. I won’t deny that physical attractiveness isn’t exactly my strong suit and I can definitely improve here. Two key area are probably my fashion sense and lack of upper body. I can probably do a better job being more fashionable my main problem is the fact that I don’t really care. I’m perfectly happy with my own fashion in and of itself and maybe I can do better there. Also I can definitely do a better job with my upper body strength and should really go to the gym. The problem here is that I don’t intrinsically like going to a gym and doing exercise, I much prefer going outdoors and doing more dynamic stuff like walking or running but sadly that alone isn’t enough. Friday Today after work I quickly go to the Midnight runners 6th birthday run. Well to be more precise I go to the pre party run and grab some stuff and take some pictures I would have liked to stick around for the run but I already made dinner plans to get dinner with “The historian”. Its been a while since I caught up with him so its a great time getting Korean food and walking around. Fun fact: “The historian” was the first person I ever got KBBQ with and the one who inspired my passion in it. He’s also one of the few friends I can go for really long walks with 1:1 so its truly a retreat to walk around from Nob hill to Pac Heights, to the loin, to Fidi, to Duboce with. Along the way I briefly saw “The dentist” who did the Midnight runners run and even won a massive group game of Rock Paper Scissors. Congrats dentist that is truly impressive! So impressive I’d almost change your name in this to “The rock paper scissors” champion if I didn’t value consistency so much. Saturday The day starts off with trash pickup which is great as usual. After trash pickup I go to a hangout organized by “The Doctor”.  “The Doctor” and I are both part of an extended friend group that doesn’t hang out as much these days so today was kinda a reunion for that group. I got to see lots of faces I hadn’t seen in a while including “The lawyer”, “High entropy”, “Mr. Marvelous Mushroom”, and “The Wrestling Wizard”. Much like with Thursday I bring some folks from trash pickup to the hangout including “The Ravenkeeper”, “The philosopher”, “The writer”, some of “The philosopher”’s friends (one of whom will come up later), and some others who admittedly I forgot their names. Its a grand ol time with equal parts mischief as hijinks. Afterwards we splinter off and its just me, “The plower”, “The doctor”, “The doctor’s sister”, and “The quant”. We go back to “The doctor”’s place and play some games and learn some gene sequencing. “The doctor” gives us a whole lecture on gene sequencing which is pretty cool. From my understanding the way it works is there are two methods of gene sequencing (in the scope of this lecture anyway). First some setup. Lets say you have a segment of DNA and you want to find out its genetic makeup (aka what sequence of (A)denine, (G)uanine, (C)ytosine, (T)hymine  its made up of). The first method he brought up is Nanopore sequencing. The way this method works is by voltage analysis. Specifically we take the fragment of DNA in question and pass it through a nanopore. When we do this we can measure the voltage through the pore to understand what the underlying components are. From my understanding I don’t think you can get down to the individual sequence of A, G, C, T here. Instead what you can do is take the voltages and map them to sequences may something like AGGCT or something like that. Whats cool here is that you can actually use ML techniques to learn a model between voltages and the different subsequences. The way he explained this to me reminded me a lot of ML in that if you start from scratch you first bootstrap with either synthetic compounds whose genetic makeup you know or simple sequencing algorithms to give a rough set of initial labels which you can then use as a basis for more nuanced algorithms. The second algorithm is called Illumina sequencing which works by taking a strand of DNA and dividing it up into chunks of a bunch of base pairs and instead attaching special colored blocks to them. The trick here is that only one colored block can attach to a chunk and that will tell us what the make up of the chunk is. The machine takes a picture and we can do a color analysis to figure out the chunk. One tricky thing here is that this process can be error prone so rather than just doing this once, for each chunk you make a bunch of copies and do this whole process and look at the aggregate to figure out the makeup of the chunk. Apparently the underlying process can be rather noisy and there is an upper bound to how clean it can be meaning no matter what you always have to do this with some redundancy.  Here too I’m reminded of ML and its really cool to me to see how gene sequencing uses a lot of the same ideas from ML :D .One of the cons with this method is that you can only do it on shorter base pairs at a time whereas with the Nanopore method you can do this on much longer ones. I think there were some pros to this method but unfortunately I don’t remember them (Illumina: higher accuracy, but shorter reads. Nanopore: generally lower accuracy, but super long reads). Note: I’m giving “The doctor” edit permission for this newsletter so feel free to correct me here :D After this “The philosopher” and “The juggler” are hosting a birthday party  for one of their friends. The twist here is that we’re all playing a prank on this guy where we all pretended we met him back in college. I actually kicked off this prank earlier at trash pickup since he came there (I told you that one of the friends with “The philosopher” from earlier would come back later). The party itself goes quite well and the prank goes well (too well). The guy said he felt bad that he forgot all these people and I’m almost tempted to tell him. But thats not my prank to tell. While at this party I ask another guy the question “Whats something cool or interesting about you that people wouldn’t expect” and he replies “My dark past”. Out of respect I won’t go into the details he told me but I have to admit I certainly wasn’t expecting that reply to the question. At one point I get really tired and try to sleep a bit on the floor which works as well as you think. Interestingly the fatigue lowers my inhibition in a similar way that drinking does. I’m almost to the point where I text one of my group chats how much I appreciate them but after dozing off for 15 minutes I exit that state. We then leave “The juggler’s” house and go to El Farlito. I decide to bow out at this point because of Bay 2 Breakers the next day. Sunday Today is Bay 2 Breakers! One of SF’s best days! Originally I was planning on running it but we instead decide to join up with the MR cheer squad over in Hayes valley. Today I meet up with several of “The enablers” incluing “The dentist”, “La Tacuqeria royalty”, and “Ray of sunshine”. We all hang out and watch the festivities which are truly a blast. The MR theme was Club Penguin so we all wear Penguin onesies. While at B2B I see quite some interesting costumes including several pope costumes, a Caltrain costumes, and of course the naked people. After cheering for a while all us penguins walk along and spontaneously break into a flash mob at multiple points which is amazing and is getting me even more excited for my dance party next Saturday (which by the way if you haven’t marked yourself as attending you definitely should 😤). After walking along for a while we decide to grab brunch at Che Fico. I grab my usual there which is great! And I wrote a yelp review for anyone interested. I part ways with “The enablers” here and hang out in Panhandle enjoying the festivities a bit more. I try a sliding activity they have where you slide across a soaped up mat and it goes about as well as I expected it to. WhatsApp Video 2025-05-18 at 13.17.24.mp4 After enjoying the ambiance of B2B for a couple more hours I head over to Terra Mia for “The taco”’s birthday party. We decide on pottery and its an experience. While I don’t love it it certainly isn’t anything like the horrors of hacky sack. I try painting an owl like thing and I guess it didn’t come out terribly To be honest I have no idea what I’m gonna do with this thing considering how I usually feel about decorations like this. Maybe I’ll leave it somewhere interesting. I got “The taco” a custom compass :D. I got this for her both because her love for “El Rancho Grande” is matched only by her ineptitude with directions (so much so I almost used “Magellan” as her name in this newsletter ironically). Afterwards I went to go get dinner with “The enablers” over at the Public Izakaya. Unfortunately since I did eat at this place I can’t give it a yelp review as part of my yelp elite goal. I hadn’t seen “the enabler” himself ina  while so it was great catching up with him again. I also saw “the dentist” and “La Tacqueria royalty” after the not quite as long time of a few hours. At the place I got a beef tongue Japanese curry which really sucked unfortunately. I love beef tongue and Japanese curry normally so I thought the combo would really hit. Sadly it didn’t. I was debating catching up with the birthday party crew from earlier but at this point I was too tired and needed to go home and work

title: Episode 22
excerpt: If this is your first time here and want to read previous newsletters they are all in this folder Monday Today before work I run into one of my old coworkers from my past job on the MUNI. We catch up for a bit and I wind up going to go see my old company’s of…
content: If this is your first time here and want to read previous newsletters they are all in this folder Monday Today before work I run into one of my old coworkers from my past job on the MUNI. We catch up for a bit and I wind up going to go see my old company’s office. It turns out my old company moved offices and their new office is quite nice. On top of that this is the first day of the new office so to celebrate they have a huge breakfast spread. I liberally help myself to some turkey bacon and fruit while catching up with some old coworkers (and writing “Humza was here” on a bunch of the whiteboards). It was fun to see those guys again! Before I leave I liberate some of the pistachios and take them with me as a souvenir. Just like old times! After that I go back to my actual office and my workday proceeds as normal. Its a really nice evening out so I go for a walk. My friend “Green flag” tells me about a moon howling event where you can go and howl at the moon with a bunch of people over in Dolores park. It sounded pretty interesting and I’d have loved to go but unfortunately I had to write last weeks newsletter which I was behind on and I had other miscellaneous work so I skipped out. Hopefully I’ll go next time! Tuesday Today is a pretty normal day. I go to work. I work. I go home and chill. Wednesday Today after work I finally go back to Midnight Runners. Its really nice having my knee recovered so I don’t feel like a fat slug anymore (I’m just a regular slug now). I’m joined on this run by “The Quant” and together we kick ass and take names. Amusingly I forgot my run clothes so I did the whole 5 miles in jeans which surprised my coworkers (little do they know I’ve done it in jeans + backpack with laptop in it). The run itself goes quite well. I really felt myself getting into my stride after the 2nd mile and I think I definitely have been approving. During the run me and “The quant” are talking with a guy and “The quant” makes up a story about how I supposedly walk 25 miles every day. Since he isn’t usually the type to do so I’m caught off guard by this but play along. I’m really proud of the fact that now he is the one making up the bit and I follow along with it rather than the other way around. In my head I thought to myself “Thats my quant.” Also really proud of the fact that he has taken a lot more social initiative than he has in the past which is something he said he wants to work on. Love that self improvement! After the run I talk with some folks over at the bar. Lately I’ve been borrowing an icebreaker question from “The philosopher” which is “Whats something unexpected about you people wouldn’t guess?”. I quite like the question as it catches people off guard and can lead to some pretty interesting stories. One of the people I talk with says that one night when was living in Manhattan she decided to become an Uber driver out of boredom. She went out from 8PM to 3AM and did Uber eats on a bike. She said she wouldn’t recommend it and she wound up sloshing some food. But it made for a fun story! Another guy said thats not the sort of question he would answer sober and left it at that. From there I go home and chill. When I get home I try something I learned about on Twitter. Apparently the o3 model from OpenAI is very good at predicting vibes based on photos and I wanted it to see what my vibe was. The tldr was that it told me I’m excited but awkward. To be honest this isn’t surprising to me as I realize I’m pretty bad at taking photos and I can never quite smile right. I wanna try to be better at taking photos (ideally starting with not having my eyebrows raised and my tongue out). Thursday Today I go to work and then go to bar night with some of my friends. Mainly its “The philosopher” and some of his friends. While at the bar we strike up conversation with an interesting guy who is apparently an indoor ski instructor around here. To be honest I’m not a big fan of winter sports and the idea doesn’t really appeal to me but it was interesting to find an indoor ski instructor around here. We then chit chat for a while about nothing of particular interest until I get tired and tap out around 9:30 and go home and sleep. Before I sleep I come across an interesting essay on receiving compliments. Like many people I can sometimes squirm and feel uncomfortable receiving compliments depending on the complement. The essay talks about this and goes into a bit more detail about why it can be. A lot of times people care more about compliments in things they have invested in and not so much about things that they don’t. I really like these paragraphs in particular Is someone complimenting something you don't care really meaningless? Could it not still be a moment of warmth?Personally, just because I don’t value a certain trait in myself doesn’t mean no one else should. It doesn’t mean their appreciation is fake. Letting something land, especially something nice, means dropping your guard. It’s like stepping into a light and letting yourself be seen. You have to stop rationalizing, stop minimizing, and just be there with it. I wonder: if your perception of self is built on staying in motion, on self-improvement or humility or keeping your edge, even a second of that can feel... like you might let them down? Or giving something up. Or that you don’t deserve it. But it's a false trade-off. Receiving doesn't make you arrogant. It makes you reachable. One of the big points here being that receiving compliments can counterintuitively be a sign of vulnerability. There have definitely been times where I’ve received compliments in a rather ungraceful manner. Part of why I write this newsletter is to help myself be more vulnerable and I think another good step would be being better at receiving compliments in areas I may not be as invested in myself. Friday Today after work I go and get all you can eat KBBQ with “The quant” and “The yogi”. We go to Kogi Gogi naturally.  Its as good as it always is. And its always fun finding new people to get AYCE with! After walking around GGP at night I head home and hop on a call with “The doctor”, “The plower”, and “The taco”. I hadn’t seen “The taco” in a while so it was quite nice to talk with her again. Saturday Today I leave early to go run an AAPI heritage month 5K over at the Marina that “The dentist” invited me to. I go there around 8 only to find nobody there. Unfortunately after checking with “The dentist” I learn that I went to the wrong place as there are multiple AAPI 5Ks and the one I’m actually supposed to go to starts at 10AM over in Japantown. This puts me in a bit of a bind as I was supposed to lead volunteer trash pickup around 10. My initial plan was to run the 5K that I thought would be at 8:30 and then head over to the Mission to pickup at Trash. For a little while I debate what I want to do as I really wanted to do this 5K but at the same time I don’t want to let trash pickup down. This is extra tricky since the regular leads are out of town so I have to scramble to find a replacement. Eventually I reach out to “The writer” who comes in clutch and agrees to lead trash pickup despite never doing it before. Major shoutout “The writer”, you’re a real one! With trash pickup leadership secure I walk over from The Marina to Japantown to start this 5k. When I get there I meet up with “The dentist” and two of her friends who I’ll call “The other yelp elite” and “The girl who is moving to London in a week” (yeah I’ll admit these are among the worse nicknames I’ve come up with but I don’t expect them to read this or be recurring characters). The first hurdle of the event comes before any of the running in that there are a bunch of boring AAPI heritage speeches I have to listen to. I don’t like these during trash pickup and I don’t like them here either. Thankfully in due time we clear the first hurdle and the actual race starts. This is the route we wind up running The group I’m running with is definitely faster than the typical Midnight runners pace. I’m not totally out of my depth but I definitely have to put in the work to keep up with the others. I’m at a bit of a disadvantage here as I have my backpack with me and a couple times during the race my backpack unzips open and some of the content comes flying out. Thankfully I don’t have anything particularly valuable but I did have to stop and pick up the tape that came out at one point. One recurring theme is that people here clearly don’t care much about traffic lights as we run a surprisingly large number of red lights. I guess AAPI heritage stops for nothing. At a couple points “The dentist” tries to be a voice of reason and calls out that we’re running these but eventually I guess we all just decide to go with the crowd here. Most of the race is flat or downhill. The only hill we knew would be coming was the one when we go up Grant to get to Chinatown. That one wasn’t too bad and afterwards we think we’re in the clear and should be smooth sailing. Turns out before the event ends we have a final boss we need to clear and that is these two blocks here These were two blocks of very brutal uphill. Before this point I was able to run everything even if I did have to exert myself to do so but this really wrecked me. I was able to run up 95% of it or so but I did need to stop once or twice to catch my breathe. Only “The dentist” was able to run up all of it without stopping. “The other yelp elite” and “The girl who is moving to London in a week” decide to walk up the hill. And keep in mind they’re both really athletic soccer players so that should say how bad the hill is After clearing the hill the heat definitely starts getting to me, but thankfully the last bit isn’t too bad. We clear the final stretch and finish over at Plymouth Park! We run at roughly a 9min/mile pace so now I think I can upgrade myself from a slug to a 3-toed sloth. To celebrate heres some concept art reflecting this important evolution in me. After the run we get some Chinese food from a place near by and hang out over in Washington square park. Interestingly this place had us wait for 40 min which was longer than it took for us to actually run this 5k. While at the park I get to to know “The other yelp elite” and “The girl moving to London next week” and they’re both pretty cool. I ask them the same question I asked on Wednesday “Whats something unexpected about you people wouldn’t guess?”. I learn from this that they were both biotech majors in college which you wouldn’t guess from the fact that they work in finance / consulting. From there I head over to GGP and hang out with “The doctor” and “The doctor’s sister”. We come up with a card game that combines Coup with Exploding kittens which works as follows You start with two coup cards just like in regular coup On your turn you can draw a card from the pile of cards or spend a card to do an action (adding Exploding kittens mechanics to Coup) You can do as many actions as you want (like in Exploding kittens) but your turn ends when you draw a card or take money from the treasury You can lie about what actions you are performing but can be called out with same penalties as Coup Winner is last one standing The idea is interesting but the game ultimately winds up being pretty imbalance as the optimal strategy is to horde cards. It was a noble attempt and I think we’re on to something but the game isn't quite there yet. After hanging out in GGP for a while we go to play ping pong. “The doctor” and “The doctor’s sister” are both really good at ping pong as it turns out and I”m starting to get a feel for how it works. I’m pretty ok at hand eye coordination and backhand but my front hand and top spin still need quite a bit of work. From there we go to Sanppo restaurant in SF and have some food which is kinda meh. Thankfully since I didn’t eat here I can leave a Yelp review to help me reach my goal of becoming Yelp elite while not eating at the places I review which can be found here for  any interested reader After that I walk home and chill before going to bed Sunday The day starts with trash pickup. Its a smaller than normal crowd today with “The yogi”, “The frog” and “The raven keeper” joining me. Turns out today for trash pickup the mayor himself Daniel Lurie comes to pickup trash with us which doesn’t really change things except we get more boring speeches before picking up trash than normal, my favorite. After trash pickup “The quant” swings by to join for the post trash pickup hang. While there we decide to ask Daniel Lurie some questions. I start off by asking him how he would feel about changing the expression “wearing the pants” to “wearing the Levi’s”. In case you don’t know Daniel Lurie comes from the Levi family and a lot of his fortune (which he used to fund his campaign race), comes from there. He was genuinely startled by the question at first and then cobbles together a “sounds good to me” while laughing. I thought it was pretty funny. I kinda wished I led this trash pickup so I can make the joke that between the Levi family stuff and being the mayor Daniel Lurie truly wears the pants in the city. At the request of “The yogi” I also ask what his agenda is for changing SF. He gives a very political answer in which he says the same thing in 5 different ways none of which are particularly helpful. I don’t mind since I got to ask my original question but I wasn’t impressed by this answer. Afterwards me, “The quant”, and “The frog” go to Garden Creamery where we meet up with “The doctor”. Unfortunately it looks like they stopped serving Mujicha which is a darn shame. Interestingly the folks at Garden creamery now recognize me and immediately tell me such when I walk in which is funny. From there we go to Dolores park and chill for a bit. Afterwards I go home and chill and then writeup the newsletter

title: Episode 21
excerpt: If this is your first time here and want to read previous newsletters they are all in this folder Monday Today I went to work and went home. Nothing too interesting. Tuesday Today I went to work and went home. Originally I had wanted to go play squash but it…
content: If this is your first time here and want to read previous newsletters they are all in this folder Monday Today I went to work and went home. Nothing too interesting. Tuesday Today I went to work and went home. Originally I had wanted to go play squash but it turns out my knee hadn’t fully recovered yet. In lieu of that I did play spikeball with some folks in Panhandle which was fun. Wednesday Today after work I really wanted to go to run club but unfortunately the knee vetoed this. At this point I feel like a slug. A sluggy slug slug that slugs. This is what I feel like right now. Instead I went to a friends going away party. Turns out one of my friends quit his job and is gonna go be a monk in China for month along with some other assorted Asia travels. So to celebrate this he had a Shaolin movie night where he ordered a bunch of Chinese food. In the background we had Drunken Master and Shaolin Soccer playing. Drunken Master was made back in 1978 and admittedly its age did show a bit with regards to the sound effects. It sounded like all the martial arts effects were someone bending a big piece of paper, but in a funny way! Thursday Today after work I went to go see the Minecraft movie with some coworkers and it was quite good! I didn’t walk out or fall asleep once! This may sound small, dare I say normal but those who know me and my history with movies understand that in and of itself is high praise. I don’t have a letterboxd or anything like that but I’ll write a review of the movie here as if I did The Minecraft movie is very honest in what it tries to do. Is it gonna be the next Titanic, Everywhere all at Once, or some other movie where I’m deeply invested in the character development, themes, or societal commentary? Hell no. Its a fun comedy about people hanging out in the minecraft world. It speeds past the initial character setup not even pretending to give anything close to a compelling setup. This itself is actually a charm in a so bad its good kinda way. The jokes of the movie were overall quite good and I laughed quite a bit. My favorite was when a character called the garbageman was flirting with a middle aged principle and she said “you can bag me and take me to the curb anytime”. Jack Black brought his usual brand of goofy entertainment and Jason Mamoa was also on point. There were some other kid actors there who were perfectly adequate. As someone who generally likes great antagonists I’ll be the first to say that the antagonist of this movie wasn’t great by any traditional means of judging antagonists but she worked for the movie. There was a fun joke in how she was defeated which I won’t spoil in case anyone reading this is gonna go see the movie. All in all a solid shameless comedy and so far its my pick for movie of the year. The fact I haven’t seen other movies this year is irrelevant. Friday Today after work I hosted a board game night with “The Raja of Rhythm”, “The Plower”, “The Doctor”, “The Quant”, and “The Doctor”’s sister. We wound up playing a lot of Coup and Chameleon. I think I need to start making a Partiful for these because I realize I’m very inconsistent with inviting people mainly because I go off of who I can remember whenever I make these events only to rush invite people on the last day and naturally many folks are busy then. Unfortunately while playing Chameleon I faced some (read this part in Trump’s voice) “nasty nasty allegations” from “The Plower” that I cheated in Chameleon by giving myself whatever role I wanted when shuffling the cards. Naturally these allegations were completely unfounded and I beat them but I suppose its worth mentioning. We play Coup for a while and our games slowly become more and more cursed. We continually remove such trifles as rules restricting when you can take coins and when you can take turns. Our pent up chaos demons truly take the wheel here in the funniest way possible. Once the game night ended I went with “The Raja” to check out one of the local bars in my neighborhood. He hadn’t really checked out any around here and was interested to see what the scene was like. We went into a bar that had a lot of older people in it. This bar had been around for a while (I think 100 years or so) and they had some old pictures from back in the day. I had walked by this bar quite a bit but hadn’t actually been in it until now. Saturday The day starts as it generally does with trash pickup which is a smashing hit as usual. After trash pickup I hang out in Golden Gate Park for a while. Initially I came there for a wrestling event only to learn that the wrestling event was actually tomorrow instead. I wander around the park for a while only to come across a pickup Volleyball area in the park. I recently rewatched some Haikyuu and figured I could pull off an epic jump serve or something like that. Unfortunately these games take a while and it seems there are a good number of people in line already so after waiting for like half an hour I give up and decide to resume my wandering. After a while of that I go over to “The Doctor”’s place for a movie night. When I get there we wind up pivoting to a game night with a movie in the background. In terms of games we play Exploding Kittens, Resistance, and Coup. I don’t do well at many of the games today which isn’t a big deal in and of itself but I do notice it triggered my competitive side which I don’t like. This happened before during an intense Dune game a while back and its something I want to try to work on and improve. The best way to do so is probably to acknowledge it before I start playing any board game with folks so I can mentally tell myself its just a game and to relax. It doesn’t help that the movie playing in the background does distract folks from the game which led to a couple hiccups but that aside I want to get better here. From there I wind up going to a friends birthday party. When I get there it turns out the birthday party was just 3 people with me being the 4th. To be fair the birthday boy did plan this at the last minute but I do feel a bit bad for the small turnout and kinda wished I had come earlier but given the last minute nature of the whole thing I did want to go to the movie / game night I had already committed to as well. We hang out and talk for about half an hour before the party dies down. I hang out with “The Philosopher” for a while as we walk around and go to The Geary Club to talk with strangers. On the way there “The Philosopher” asks me what I value in life. I think about this for a bit and ultimately land on the following. I value friends and family I value religion I value doing interesting things without radically changing my life I value health The 3rd one is interesting since he mentions that I wouldn’t do anything too crazy like quit my job and go to China to be a monk (he is also friends with the guy from Wednesday). I realize that thats true and I’m largely happy with my life and am not really looking to make any major changes, moreso try new things that fit into my existing life structure. I flip the question back around on him and he says that its impossible to determine values in life directly and instead they are derived from actions. In other words he didn’t answer the question. Big sad! We get to The Geary Club and start talking with a couple of the people there. For context The Geary Club is a dive bar over in The Tenderloin so the people I talk with are definitely outside my normal distribution. The main guy we end up talking with is a 30 year old going to college dealing with some relationship trouble. To be honest I realize shortly after starting to talk with him that I don’t really vibe with him all that much. Because of this I give him a fake name and lie about pretty much every aspect of my life. I tell him I’m “Frank” a former gardener who is just bumming around not really doing anything with my life. The only true things he learns about me are because “The Philosopher” tells him a couple true things before I make it clear I intend to improvise my way through this entire conversation. Shoutout to “The Philosopher” this thing is much more his scene and I do applaud his ability to talk with a wide variety of people. I consider myself pretty outgoing but its clear there are some folks I’m less inclined to talk to and I do want to get better at that. Perhaps I start going to The Geary Club with “The Philosopher” more often. Another factor that makes it difficult is that I start getting tired and around midnight I give up and head home. Sunday Today I go to trash pickup and leave before picking up trash. The reason I go is because I have two friends who I really want to introduce to each other. “The Raja of Rhythm” has played guitar for a while and wants to get more into writing and “The Writer” is writing a book series right now and is picking up guitar for the first time. And they are both very kind / thoughtful people so I think they’d go great together! Unfortunately I don’t get the chance to do this today but mark my words it will happen, and the crossover episode will go great! The reason I skip trash pickup is to go on a run with “The Enablers”. I’m a bit nervous since my knee just started feeling a bit better but thankfully I actually manage to keep up them and even wind up leading a good chunk of the run! Way back in episode 4 I go for a run with some of these guys and massively struggle to keep up, so this is a huge improvement! Granted they may have been going slower but still! The weather was great so got some great pics along The Embarcadero and Fort Mason. Thankfully it wasn’t a long run, only a few miles. After the run we go to brunch over at Board and Drink. Naturally I don’t get anything because the airlines are still asking me if I need two seats. However that doesn’t stop me from writing a yelp review anyway. The reason I’m doing this is because I want to try to make Yelp Elite without actually eating at any of the restaurants I review. I think it will be really funny. After brunch I go and wrestle in GGP. I found this event by looking at Partiful and seeing open invite events. I saw this and it seemed interesting. To be honest wrestling isn’t really my forte and I struggle a lot. But the whole point of this event is to struggle rather than to win. To return to what its like to be a monkey struggling in the jungle. Well I definitely accomplished the mission there.  We play a variety of games including one where you  try to push the opponent until they lose their footing, one where you try to lock hands and poke your opponent, and one where you try to take your opponents sock off. That last one threw me to the ground and made me give up rather quickly. \ It was fun though and I’m glad I did it despite what the pictures above indicate! Definitely something I hadn’t done before. After this I hang out in GGP with “The Doctor” and “The Doctor’s sister”. We hang out in the park for a bit and then go to a Japanese place. Unfortunately since I ate there I can’t write a Yelp review for it  but the lamb chop was actually good! From there I go to a bonfire with “The Philosopher” and “The Juggler”. Turns out some of “The Juggler”’s friends are in town so they have a bonfire over by Ocean Beach. They have some kosher beef sausages which are great, some turkey sausages which are meh, and some oysters which are like the Dune 2 of food. Unfortunately I get a bit of a headache and I get really cold so I call it about an hour in. I then go home and I’m too tired to write the newsletter unfortunately so I save that task for tomorrow.

title: Episode 20
excerpt: Monday Today I worked and chilled afterwards. Tuesday Same as Tuesday (I’m very exciting and original). Wednesday Today i had to skip Midnight Runners and it wasn’t because of anything cool like The Dan’s birthday or being in Hawaii. Does anyone wanna throw o…
content: Monday Today I worked and chilled afterwards. Tuesday Same as Tuesday (I’m very exciting and original). Wednesday Today i had to skip Midnight Runners and it wasn’t because of anything cool like The Dan’s birthday or being in Hawaii. Does anyone wanna throw out their wildest guess as to why I skipped this week? If you said its because my legs were still sore then you win 5 imaginary dollars. If you win 10 more imaginary dollars I’ll give you a custom prize. Thursday Today after work I stay late to do some work and after dinner I wind up playing Smash with some of my coworkers. While playing the topic of Pokemon comes up and we talk about how some pokemon like Lopunny are very sexualized. While talking with them I learn that some people made smash or pass tierlists for pokemon. Apparently Vaporeon is ranked as A tier and I said “Makes sense because Vaporeon can get you wet”. I know thats a messed up joke but I’m proud of it so its going in the newsletter 😤 Friday Today after work I hang around the office and chat with some of my coworkers for a while. We just kinda chat for a while about random things. My coworkers are pretty cool and I’m usually pretty busy friday nights so perhaps it was a good thing I got this chance even if by this point in the week I was hoping I’d have more content for y’all. Saturday Today starts with trash pickup as per usual. Unfortunately since the organizer is out of town I have to step in from the shadows and help out with leading today. Every time I lead it makes it that much harder for me to lie to people and say its my first time doing it which is less than ideal. Nevertheless duty calls so I do what I can. After trash pickup I head over to Round One in Stonestown. For those unaware Round One is a Japanese arcade chain that found its way over to America. I go with a group of friends and we play a variety of games. The game I spend the most time playing a rhythm game called Taiko no Tatsujin. Its a drum game where you have to hit the right notes on either the center or edge of the drum as well as the right side. One of my friends who spent a lot of time playing rhythm games winds up being really good at this. So good in fact that going forward in the newsletter I’ll refer to him solely as the “Raja of Rhythm” or “The Raja” for short. The main reason we go to Round One is because one of my friends “The Quant”, finally passed level 3 of the CFA. He was studying really hard for it over many months so a huge congrats again to “The Quant” for passing. After Round One we go back to “The Doctors” place and play some boardgames. While there we are joined by “The Plower”. At point we wind up trying to play One Night werewolf with 3 people. Through this we develop a better appreciation of why you play this game with more people but also find some pretty fun edge cases in the game that only arise in these sorts of situations. It was pretty cursed but in my honest opinion more fun than regular One Night werewolf. While this is happening the Warriors are playing the Rockets over at Chase center (The Doctor lives right near there). Funnily enough we wind up rooting against The Warriors because the sooner they get eliminated from the bracket the more quiet Chase Center will be and the less noise pollution The Doctor will have to live with (it can get pretty loud there). Sunday A couple hours before trash pickup I see a message in the organizers group chat saying we have no leads today so once again I have to come out of obscurity and help lead some wayward souls. Because of the nature of the Sunday trash pickup I wind up needing to give a speech before to organize people. If I’m gonna come out of obscurity I figure I may as well have some fun with it. I put my usual card trick to good use and referred to everyone as “Munchkins” which felt right in the moment. I also taught people a new word. During the speech its customary to have folks take a picture and usually during the picture the organizer says something pedestrian like “on 3 say trash”. But I figured as organizer I ought educate the masses so I said “on 3 say collywobbles”. Yes thats a real word and I highly encourage people to use it more. It means stomach pain or queasiness. After trash pickup we do our post trash pickup hang and a day I have long been waiting for. As part of the hang we go to Garden Creamery and they finally have a flavor known as Mugicha!! For those unaware Mugicha is roasted barley. Its a flavor of ice cream that Garden Creamery used to carry a couple years ago but stopped having. Astute readers might be wondering why I care about ice cream flavors since I’m a self professed lactose racist. Well astute reader (and the others who I’ll still tell anyway), the answer is because The Doctor really loves this flavor of ice cream and has wanted to see it back for quite a while. Now it wasn’t just a coincidence that it happened to be back today. Its because of a long standing effort on my part. Back in episode 16 I mentioned reading about high agency and was thinking about how I could be more agentic. After I read the essay I set myself a goal of coming up with a task I could do to assert my own agency over the world. The goal I came up with was getting Garden Creamery to bring back the Mugicha. I started off back then by messaging Garden Creamery on instagram asking if they could bring back the flavor. As you can see … no response :(. The next Saturday I go in person and ask them about it. They mention having gotten my message and promise to bring it back sometime in the next week or two. To keep an eye on things I follow Garden Creamery on instagram. I wanted to be ready the moment they announced it was coming back so I could alert The Doctor. Throughout this time I subject myself to a whole bunch of random stories on the Garden Creamery instagram feed that I give precisely zero hoots about. They talk and talk about different flavors they have each day and since none of them are the Mugicha … I don’t care. Apparently they have another instagram called “Dogs of garden creamery” and guess what … I don’t care! But I still gotta check every story *just in case* they feature the gosh darn Mugicha. After a couple weeks I go back again and this time the workers there are even *less* helpful and just vaguely say they may bring it back again at some point. Gotta love that hedging! On Saturday I was originally planning to go and ask them again until I realize I need a different approach. And then I had it! What if instead of one person messaging them on instagram I get a whole bunch of people messaging them on instagram! So I get a whole bunch of my friends including several people at trash pickup, The Quant, and The Plower to message them. I do this on Saturday and then they finally respond with a video that they are making it! Big thanks to all my friends who messaged Garden Creamery on my behalf and helping me bring back the Mugicha! I wonder how it is? Truthfully I’m not much of a barley guy. As soon as I message The Doctor he Ubers over to Garden Creamery. Since this is special I ask the Garden creamery staff to greet him when he comes in with a “Welcome <insert real name here>! Would you like the Mugicha?”. I figured if I’m going through all this effort why not really go all out! I made sure to video the whole thing and while I won’t be sharing the video here here is an abstract art rendition of the moment While seeing the look on The Doctor’s face may have been the best part I think the below is a close second. Now I’m wondering what my next Agency project will be. I’m not entirely sure yet but if any of you have thoughts I’d love to hear them. I’m toying with the idea of trying to be a Yelp elite. Originally I never really thought about it much as I didn’t think of myself as a foodie and didn’t have a high opinion of people who called themselves foodies. But after meeting “The Dentist” whose a Yelp elite I realize perhaps if other Yelp elites are also like “The Dentist” maybe it could be worthwhile after all. After making history I resume my post trash pickup hang. It turns out its a friends birthday today and he is having a birthday party. Unfortunately I can’t make it but I do get him this card He is a big fan of both cooking and film so I thought this would be fun. At this point I’ve gotten good enough at making custom birthday cards that I can do the whole process entirely on my phone now. After wandering around in the Mission we go back to “The Raja’s” place and do some workouts. The Raja does a lot of home workouts so we do a variety of things ranging from pushes, curls, legs, and core. By far core is my strongest area for whatever reason and pushes my weakest. When doing a plank I’m pleasantly surprised by my ability to hold a plank for over 2 and a half minutes and longer than the others. When doing pushes I’m unpleastantly unsurprsied by my ineptitude to do anything  of merit. I would have been ok on legs if I wasn’t still somewhat sore from last week. After that I go home and write up the newsletter.

title: Episode 19
excerpt: Monday Today is a pretty ordinary day. I go to work, I go home, and I chill. Thats about that Tuesday Today after work I go to play squash over at the Mission Rec center for the first time. I had never played squash before but one of my friends was thinking a…
content: Monday Today is a pretty ordinary day.  I go to work, I go home, and I chill. Thats about that Tuesday Today after work I go to play squash over at the Mission Rec center for the first time. I had never played squash before but one of my friends was thinking about it so I said I was down to play. For those who have never played squash before its a racquet sport kinda like tennis or badminton except instead of hitting over a net instead both sides hit towards a wall and once the ball hits the wall the other side hits it back. Playing squash was super fun even if I was pretty bad at it. I certainly didn’t realize how much wrist strength it required to hit the ball back each time. While there we found a couple other folks who invited us to a squash group chat so I may be playing more squash in the not too distant future Wednesday Today after work I go to run club. The run was fun but not particularly noteworthy. After the run I meet a guy who apparently has 50 pairs of shoes. I gotta admit this was definitely unusual. Thursday Today at work I’m talking about run club with a coworker of mine and she asked me if I’m in the marina run club and I said no. I asked if she was and she said “I’m not that single … yet”. It took me a moment to recognize the implication she thought I was *that* single but perhaps given that I told her about the posters perhaps that was obvious. After work I go to bar night. This bar is great because it let me blatantly eat my Mixt salad there which is always appreciated. While at the bar we meet a couple of interesting characters. Some people who we suspect are a bit less than homed. One of whom bears a striking resemblance to a friend of mine there and tries to get me to invite her to karaoke. In theory I’m not opposed to inviting people I just met that day to do karaoke with me but in practice the people I invite should be a bit less sketchy than she was. The other person asked for investment advice, got defensive, and left to go look for a “golden shovel” in the streets. Theres probably a lesson in there somewhere Friday Today after work one of my friends has a sea shanty party. Think of it like group karaoke with songs where nobody really takes the lead and everybody sings in union to very repeatable and easy to remember lyrics. This taught me something important about myself that I’m not the biggest shanty fan. I liked the company of course but I can’t say shanties are necessarily my favorite songs. During the party I ask for a spoon to eat some guacamole and the host jokingly gives me a straw. The expectation would naturally be that I ask for / get a spoon instead but I took it as a challenge and ate guacamole out of  a straw. It went better than I thought. Not easily mind you but still more manageable than I thought. I duck out of this party for a while and go to my coworkers visa celebration party. She recently got her visa updated so she can continue being here which is awesome! I go to her party only to find that I’m the first person there and that they weren’t expecting me to come so early (8 minutes past the start time on partiful). I forgot that most parties operate that way. I spend quite a bit of time talking with her boyfriend and one of his friends and the boyfriend in particular proves to be a troll on about my level which is a pretty rare find. Somehow the topic of work gets brought up and I mention that by default I assume he’s a software engineer. He then tries to sell me a bunch of spiels about how he is actually a marketer, nay a soap opera actor. Its quite hilarious and refreshing to meet someone who responds to my trolling in a similar style. We then spend a lot of time getting into Latin American geography and I learn some interesting factoids like that Nicaragua is roughly 10x the size of El Salvador. Around this time some of their other friends come to the party. At this point we’ve reached the always fun situation where everyone their knows each other and I’m the only one who doesn’t. They talk a lot about different people who aren’t here and since I don’t know who these people are I’m forced to come up with my own headcannon. They mention someone named Rhythm who I’ll assume was named because the moment he was born he could immediately play the drums and his parents wanted to lock in his destiny. They also mentioned someone named Yash who I assume likes cats. I don’t really have something specific to point to as to why but more so a subtext thing. After this some of my coworkers come and I finally feel like I know people again. Interestingly at this point the room splits with me and my coworkers on one half and boyfriend and his friends in the other half. At this point I go back to the shanties. By the time I come back to the shanties the main shantying is done and I chill and talk with people there for a bit. It seems like they’re planning to go out afterwards but I’m too tired so I just hit the bed Saturday & Sunday You might be wondering why I put Saturday and Sunday in one heading here … well we’ll get to that later. Saturday starts off as usual with trash pickup. Today the automatic route assigning system I mentioned a few issues back actually works without hitch. I get some requests for feedback for a next version which I may or may not implement. After trash pickup I go to put up v2 of my date me posters. Interestingly enough at the same time one of the trash pickup organizers is putting up fliers for an upcoming trash pickup so we wind up doing this together. Having another person was pretty useful as we were both doing a lot of the same basic stuff so working together we could streamline the process. From there I get ready for the powerpoint party I’m hosting. In case anyone hasn’t been (and made the poor choice not to go to this one  🙄) a powerpoint party is a party where everyone makes a powerpoint on a topic they are passionate about and presents it in front of the group. I added a twist where everyone presents someone elses powerpoint which proved to be quite fun. We had quite the unique array of presentations including A pasta tier list A guide on what makes good flag design Citing the cryptid known as “Trash Tales” Writing a weekly newsletter Cool flags around the world (yup two separate people made presentations on flags :D) A “plowerpoint” on the restaurant Plow A presentation that truly can’t be contained by such things as a summary title How to speak Cantonese like a local (naturally I made sure not to give another Chinese person this one) It was really fun seeing all presentations! There was a great synergy where I swapped both the flag people and had them present each others presentations. After that we played a bunch of Secret Hitler and Chameleon. From there two of my other friends came over to start our next big thing which is a 45 mile walk around the city. Yeah you heard that right the original plan was  to do this Starting at around 10PM saturday night and go through the night til Sunday and finish the walk. I was the one who originally came up with the idea and roped my two friends into this only to find that at around 9:30 I was getting pretty sleepy. Before we leave I get some feedback that perhaps going through Bayview in the late night is not the best idea so I decide to change the route. How? Well we will get to that. Also they brought a bunch of supplies like food and water while I didn’t really pack much for this walk. And by much I mean anything. Maybe in retrospect I should have naped throughout the day and not hosted a party before going off on this walk but ya know it is what it is. Eventually my two friends are able to drag me from my house and after getting some provisions from a Mexican place and a corner store we set off. What winds up happening is a pretty complicated series of events so we’ll break this up into specific story arcs. Overcoming fatigue We start off with what winds up being either the hardest or second hardest part of this walk for me which is overcoming my fatigue. We start off at Lands End and make our way through it over to the presidio and down to Golden Gate park I struggle to keep up with my friends and their rambunctious energy. One of them jokes that this is a field trip and they’re young children with lots of energy and I’m the reluctant dad along for the ride. Towards the end of this stage I reach one of my lower points. I want to use the restroom and since its close enough by I lead the group so that we go towards my apartment so I can use the restroom there. Once they realize what I’m doing they basically tell me thats not really in the sprit of such walks and after conceding I use “the nature” instead. Somehow at this point I magically start feeling more awake and we enter stage 2 of the walk Hills, hills everywhere As I mentioned earlier the original route I had planned would have us go through Hunter’s point at about 2AM and after consulting with the people at Powerpoint party I decide to make a strategic pivot. The goal is to try to get to 45 miles but using a different more freeform route. I decide it may be fun to have us go through a whole bunch of hills at once so I take us on a route that goes through Tank Hill Twin Peaks Bernal Heights Holly Park Billy Goat Hill Glen Canyon Mt. Davison (tallest natural point in the city) Throughout this phase I start gaining more energy and things become a lot more fun! At one point we found a 24/7 donut store at 2AM that sold Ito Ens and I got all the Ito Ens they had. It may have only been 3 but I got them. The Ito Ens undoubtedly played a vital role in keeping me up. We go through all sorts of different views which are quite nice but as one of my friends noted tend to look relatively similar early in the day (or very late in the day I suppose). After getting to Mt. Davison the sun started coming up and things became much brighter. We watch the sunrise over at Mt. Davidson. After the sunrise the lack of sleep catches up with my friends. At this point I’m not really sure what I should do. Initially I think that I’m going to bow out but then I decide to go to a couple more hills. In the back of my mind I think that maybe I can still get to 45 miles. Originally my goal was to just do Granview and Corona heights and call it there since the weather wasn’t even good anyway. Starting off strong solo After parting ways with my friends I decide to go up north to Grandview park and then go over to Buena Vista and Corona heights I’m still feeling quite strong at this point and quite enjoying everything so far A trashy detour Since I’m the only one doing the walk I decide to take a detour and go to trash pickup. When I get to Mannys I decide to pace around for a while to keep my mileage going up even while I was at the cafe. For once I’m actually thankful that trash pickup was a relatively small crew today as I don’t feel the pressure to a whole bunch of trash friends. The friends who are there are for the most part going to Dolores park but since its 420 a bunch of people would be smoking there which I would hate anyway so I continue on Embarcadero After trash pickup the sun comes out and I have a renewed motivation. I walk from Mannys over to the Embarcadero and then along the Embarcadero to Coit Tower. This is a really nice part of the walk as the weather is great and my motivation is still strong! After Coit Tower I go down through Fishermans Wharf and the Marina. While at the Marina I check my Strava and realize that its seriously off.I realized later its because I accidentally paused it and didn’t resume it. Thankfully my health app is still a reliable mileage indicator. Where it stops being fun Once I get to the Marina the walk really starts taking its toll on me. At this point I’m roughly 34 miles in and I definitely am not enjoying it as much as I was at the beginning. I’m still able to keep going but the spark I had earlier was lost. The last really nice view I had on this walk was here by Inspiration point. I walk up from the Marina over to the Presidio and get to Golden Gate Park which brings us to … The final 5 miles At this point in the walk I am pretty ready to be done. I’m still going only out of a desire to finish. I’ve come this far and I want to meet my original goal. Around here I think the mental fatigue really takes its toll as well. Its not that I’m tired (aka from the lack of sleep), moreso just the desire to talk with someone. I now understand how powerful having people cheer you on can be when running a marathon or something like that. I always used to think “why do people need to sign up for these fancy races to run when they can just run a marathon around them”, but I totally understand how that can be helpful towards the end. Thankfully I do have a groupchat I’m texting and their encouragement is of course greatly appreciated I was hoping I’d run into somebody, anybody that I happened to know in GGP. And surprisingly enough I did. I ran into a bunch of people I knew from highschool over there. This was in the pre newsletter era but I did know a bunch of them lived in SF and I did talk with them before so it wasn’t totally unexpected but still definitely a nice surprise. Having someone to talk to did definitely help. I only walked with them for like a quarter of a mile or so as they needed to leave the park but it did give me just enough to see it through. For the final part of the walk I walk across GGP and walk back. Never has a walk through GGP felt like such a slog to me but at this point this is how it is. I try my best to finish. I need to take more breaks to make sure I don’t overdo it with my legs. But somehow against all odds I get through GGP, go to Gus’s to get some berries, and as I leave Gus’s the walk finishes. As soon as I finish I send this to the aforementioned group chat At 5:11 PM after about 19 hours the walk comes to an end. In total the walk was pretty much exactly 45 miles . Above is my relevant mileage from the relevant parts of Saturday and Sunday. In total I walked almost exactly 100K steps for this walk. It was truly a beast. And frankly I’m not sure I want to attempt anything like this again. It did help me to learn what my limits for walking truly are. At this point I have basically no energy in the tank and wind up crashing. I start writing up the newsletter but I don’t finish until Monday. I wind up sleeping for 10 hours which is unheard of for me as I usually do 6-7

title: Episode 18
excerpt: Monday Today is a pretty normal day. I go to work, I go home and chill. Really starting off the week strong here :D Tuesday Today is also a pretty normal day. The one slightly interesting thing is that after work I finalize v2 of the “date me” posters I want…
content: Monday Today is a pretty normal day. I go to work, I go home and chill. Really starting off the week strong here :D Tuesday Today is also a pretty normal day. The one slightly interesting thing is that after work I finalize v2 of the “date me” posters I want to put up. This is what I end up with Wednesday Today after work instead of going to run club as per usual I go a friends birthday dinner. We go to Doobu over in Japantown. As per usual I don’t really eat, especially since everything is cheese based but it was a great time! My friend is really into Capybaras so I wound up getting him a plush capybara We also got him a birthday cake! Since Doobu uses blowtorches for finishing up the food we have them try to light the candles using a blowtorch which was an interesting experience but admittedly not very effective. Unfortunately I have yet to deliver it to him but I’m making a custom birthday card that looks something like this! Thursday Today during work I surprise some of my coworkers by accurately being able to guess where they live / would live based on their personality and vibes. For example one of my coworkers who is an Account Executive very  into Berry’s  and has a dog I could immediately peg as a Marina girl. I also predicted that one of my coworkers would stay in the Bay long term and settle down probably around Piedmont with kids in around a decade and he said I was pretty accurate. After work me and some of my coworkers go out and have dinner. My coworkers are great so the vibes are great despite the grilled chicken being pretty mid. At one point one of my coworkers steps out to take a relatively long phonecall and we are able to surmise that she spent more of it listening than talking based only on the back of her head. Also it turns out one of my other coworkers also writes a newsletter! His is different from mine though in that he thinks more from the perspective “If I’m catching up with a friend I haven’t seen in 6 months what are some of the big updates I’d give them.”. Its really cool to see other people doing something like this! Friday Today after work me and some coworkers hang out for a while and grab drinks / dinner. Between drinks and dinner one of my coworkers (the newsletter one), said he’d make the decision as to whether he’d stay or leave by flipping a coin on his phone. I found that pretty funny and told him it would wind up in the newsletter so here it is :D. The place we go to dinner is in the Marina but despite that its still a fun time! Interestingly one of the servers there is someone I went to high school with. I didn’t know her all that well and I didn’t really feel like having a reunion right then and there but its still a thing that happened. After that I go and catch up with one of my old friends who I hadn’t seen in about 6 months. It turns out during the 6 month timeskip he is starting a new job and throwing a party to celebrate! His old job was being a MechE at a farm company so the whole party wound up being farm themed with farming videos playing on tv and farm themed drinks. It was a fun time! At one point I wind up meeting someone and decide to mess with her a little bit. She asked me what I do for fun and I told her “On Monday I wake up, go to work, think about my imminent death and go to sleep. Tuesday through Friday are the same as Monday. Over the weekend I wake up, think about my imminent death, and go to sleep.” Thanks to my deadpan delivery she didn’t know whether I was joking or not. I figure I could either introduce myself to her by saying I like to tell jokes but I figured this would both be more effective and more fun. Saturday Today starts off with trash pickup as per usual. We have a pretty big turnout today with 42 people! On the one hand I do really like having a big turnout but on the other it means I can’t talk to everyone I want to :(. There is only so much time in a trash pickup and with so many cool people like your Blairs, your Sohams, your Kaylynns, your Seabasses, your Tommys and many many more it becomes a real pain :(. I juggle through as best as I can but I’m never able to get it quite optimally. During trash pickup I also get some advice on v2 of my date me poster and at the same time I also get advice from someone where she tells me I should consider also asking my parents if they know anybody. Like in the family friend sense. Haven’t really considered that before but who knows. After that I go to GGP and hang out with some friends. We play Coup for a while and despite my best attempts I’m only ever able to come close to winning and being the one everyone tries to get rid of rather than the winner. We also play Exploding Kittens. Sunday Today I made trash pickup history by being the first person ever to wear a suit to trash pickup! The reason I did so was because of an event that I’ll describe slightly later that required formal attire. I figured that my options were to either skip trash pickup or do it in a suit and if you know me you’d probably guess that only one of those was a real option for me. Also during trash pickup I get to meet not one but two of my friends’ Moms which is pretty cool. Perfect time for the suit! After trash pickup I go to this event which is a “funeral for the forgotten”. Its not a real funeral, its more that one of my friends who was gone traveling for a year is coming back! Originally this was meant to be a surprise but she made a key mistake of making herself (albeit using an alias), as a host on the partiful. Originally her coming back was meant to be a surprise but because of the key mistake above everyone coming already realized anyway. On Monday when I first got the partiful I decided to not so subtly let her know that I knew she was a host It was really good seeing my old friend again! She had some pretty interesting adventures going to Turkey, Saudi Arabia, India (where she stayed most of the time), China, and Malaysia. Apparently at one point she briefly joined a cult (emphasis on briefly here). The one downside was that I definitely took the dress code requirement more seriously most and was probably the best dressed person there. I don’t regret this mind you as I think showing up to trash pickup in a suit makes it all worth it but I was a little bit surprised to be best dressed. Also I forgot that not everyone is as punctual me when I show up at the time the event is supposed to start and the host is still in PJs which was extra funny to contrast against my suit. We hang out for a while, catch up on life, and play some ping pong. Its my first time really playing ping pong and I was surprised I managed to hold my own relatively well against my friends who played it more (I also played in the suit which I think gave me a bit of a debuff). After that I go to get KBBQ at good ol Kogi Gogi and then I head home and write the newsletter!

title: Episode 17
excerpt: Tuesday Today is a pretty ordinary day. After work I work on v2 of the date me flyers I hung up last week Wednesday After work I go to run club. This run club is a bit special as its a Holi run. More specifically we celebrate Holi by throwing color packets at…
content: Tuesday Today is a pretty ordinary day. After work I work on v2 of the date me flyers I hung up last week Wednesday After work I go to run club. This run club is a bit special as its a Holi run. More specifically we celebrate Holi by throwing color packets at each other for a while before doing the run. During run club I make the bold choice to try running a mile backwards. In the past I’ve tried running short bursts backwards on the order of 30-40 feet but this time I decided to try running backwards for a whole mile. It turns out humans are naturally built to run forwards and running backwards expends a lot more energy and uses completely different muscles I’m not used to exercising. At this point I’ve run enough that running a mile at Midnight Runners wouldn’t be enough to make me tired but running backwards the whole time manages to do the trick. On top of that I finish near the bottom of the pack (only one or two people were behind me which is much worse than my usual performance). I was hoping I could do another mile backwards as well but my calves weren’t feeling it. I did finish the run backwards though which is something. I may try doing this more to get to the point where running backwards isn’t too bad for me and perhaps I could finish middle of the pack while still running backwards. After the run I hang out with folks at the bar. Unfortunately its pretty loud and at one point I mean to tell someone that she looks really sold on something but it came out as she looks “so old”. This leads her to shove her ID in my face which I found kinda funny. Thursday After work I hang out at The Crafty Fox with some friends. Unfortunately I get really hungry and proceed to order some food. I wanted to hold out and eat when I got home but the pressure was too much. I then proceed to have some of the worst Korean Fried Chicken I’ve ever had. It was absolutely terrible. So terrible I left a Google Maps review of The Crafty Fox After that we play a card game called Durak.
